| [THEORY-1114](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1114.md) v3 | Which self-category a person uses, what it means and who in it is most typical vary lawfully with the comparative frame of reference: a grouping of self with others becomes salient as the differences within it shrink relative to the differences between it and the rest of the frame (metacontrast) and as those differences match expectations about the category, and as it does, self-perception is depersonalized | Self-categorization theory as restated by Turner, Oakes, Haslam and McGarty (1994), [LIT-1794](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1794.md), and reviewed by Hornsey (2008), [LIT-1742](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1742.md). Personal and social identity are levels of self-categorization. Salience is perceiver readiness times fit, comparative fit being the metacontrast ratio. The level, kind, content and prototype structure of self-categories shift with the comparison set: Americans read as less aggressive beside Iraq than beside the Soviet Union, and a group's extreme members become more prototypical in an intergroup context. Proposed: every result in the record comes through the theory's authors, reported without data, and the account's stronger claim, that the self is generated rather than stored, is not part of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1115](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1115.md) v2 | A we-identity, being one of us, can arise through mutual individualization, in which members grasp one another as non-substitutable and complementary, without depersonalization, as in long friendships and romantic partnerships; so depersonalization is not necessary for a we-identity | León (2023), [LIT-1721](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1721.md). Self-categorization theory claims depersonalization as "the basic process underlying group phenomena", for groups of any size, friendship groups included (Turner et al. 1987, pp. 50, 103, as quoted), and phenomenologists have taken it as the account of the "we". But close relationships yield we-identities while their members grasp each other as non-substitutable, and relationship research on couple resilience finds the "we" more adaptive the more differentiated the "I". Proposed: the argument is conceptual, and the cited evidence was not analysed by the source or read here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1116](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1116.md) | Football fans can identify with a superordinate community of fans across clubs and countries, a European fan community, alongside their club identity rather than in place of it; that identification goes with particularized trust in foreign fans and cross-border viewing, and is independent of attitudes to the sport's governing institutions | Biel (2026), [LIT-1133](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1133.md): a four-country quota survey of 3,685 fans. Club, national and European fan-community identification average 6.1, 5.6 and 5.3 of 10. The European item loads on its own factor in a two-factor solution. It goes with trust in a European fan from elsewhere (b = .34), viewing of foreign leagues, positive views of fans and attachment to Europe, and not with critique of football governance. Proposed: single items, a Heywood case in the factor solution, percentages whose denominator does not match the analysed n, and cross-sectional associations. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1124](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1124.md) | Normalized log co-occurrences of words in large corpora behave as distances in a Euclidean semantic space: they correlate with human similarity ratings (r = 0.75 against MEN) and their nearest-neighbour centrality and reciprocity fall in the range expected of points sampled in a Euclidean space, apart from superordinate and function words | Hashimoto, Alvarez-Melis and Jaakkola (2016), [LIT-1801](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1801.md), §3, read in [NOTE-1329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1329.md). The correlation follows a normalization chosen to maximize it; the two nearest-neighbour statistics are necessary conditions, the corpora exceed the asymptotic centrality bound and pass only a non-asymptotic range, and the free-association data fail the reciprocity criterion the paper states. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1126](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1126.md) | In animal development the organ-level outcome is reproducible while the trajectories of individual cells differ between embryos raised alike, so developmental regularity is imposed on variable cell behaviour rather than read out from a fixed sequence of cellular events (Weiss, as Nicholson reconstructs him), with invariant lineages such as that of C. elegans the conceded exception | Nicholson (2026), [LIT-1821](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1821.md), read in [NOTE-1340](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1340.md). Weiss's "determinacy in the gross despite demonstrable indeterminacy in the small", shown as a redrawn schematic (Fig. 5) and supported by citations to work on stochastic gene expression and cell-fate decisions. This is the only one of the paper's four critiques that rests on evidence, and the paper presents none of the evidence itself. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1127](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1127.md) | A CycleGAN trained to translate aerial photographs to maps and back satisfies its cycle-consistency loss by encoding details of the photograph in a low-amplitude, high-frequency signal in the generated map: the reconstruction recovers details the visible map lacks, is destroyed by noise of three 8-bit levels or by JPEG compression and survives low-frequency change, and the same sensitivity lets an imperceptible perturbation of almost any map make the reverse generator output any chosen photograph | Chu, Zhmoginov and Sandler (2017), [LIT-1800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1800.md), §§2–4, read in [NOTE-1346](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1346.md). One trained model on one dataset. The noise curve (Fig. 3, 50 photographs) is the only quantitative result; the hidden details, the composing edits and the attack are shown by examples. Proposed: an empirical finding about one model, said by the authors to recur on other datasets, not shown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1131](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1131.md) | On native-authored pragmatic items in Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil and Malayalam, current multilingual LLMs pick the right reading from four options more often than they label it unaided, and when wrong they lean toward the literal reading | Singh et al. (2026), [LIT-1817](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1817.md), read in [NOTE-1345](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1345.md) from the Findings of EMNLP 2026 PDF. MCQ beat NLI in 20 of 20 model–language pairs (recomputed). 59.1% of wrong MCQ answers took the literal distractor, against 33.3% by chance, and 53.8% of Contradiction items were labelled Entailment. The gold answers are each language's one item author's reading, cells hold 5–16 items, and the MCQ and NLI sets are different items. So "recognizing and reasoning about pragmatic meaning are distinct competencies" is the authors' gloss, not a finding. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1136](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1136.md) | Poincaré embeddings of one hierarchy from different random seeds differ by more than an isometry of the hyperbolic ball, with branches placed differently and pairwise distances changed, so aligners that allow only a global orthogonal or Möbius map recover almost none of the correspondence, while a non-linear registration by a hyperbolic neural network, trained through a Sinkhorn divergence and started from a pretraining step, recovers a substantial part of it but finds the exact match for under a quarter of items even when the two hierarchies are identical | Alvarez-Melis, Mroueh and Jaakkola (2020), [LIT-1808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1808.md), §§5–7, Figs. 1–2, Tables 1–2; read in [NOTE-1323](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1323.md). Proposed: single runs, one embedding method for the matching experiments, and GW, the obvious isometry-free baseline, is not run. It does not say why seeds disagree (the paper conjectures negative sampling), nor that the matching preserves the hierarchy's direction, which it does not enforce. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1137](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1137.md) | When an abstraction map between two causal models is learned by optimal transport from paired interventional distributions, a transport cost that rewards pairs of states compatible with the same paired interventions gives much lower held-out abstraction error than a Hamming cost when the intervention set is rich, and higher error when it holds only a few, because with few interventions the compatibility cost is nearly uniform | Felekis et al. (CLeaR 2024), [LIT-1806](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1806.md), §§4.2 and 6 and Appendices C and E, read in [NOTE-1342](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1342.md). Two synthetic models (STC, LUCAS) and one real two-lab dataset (EBM), all discrete, evaluated by leaving one intervention pair out. The ω-cost wins on STC with parent-free interventions and on LUCAS, loses on STC with two interventions on tar and on EBM. The explanation, a nearly uniform cost when interventions are few, is argued and fits the four cases. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1143](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1143.md) | When one domain carries more information than the other, a translation trained only to make the round trip close cannot meet that requirement through a correspondence in the intermediate's visible code, so the round trip closes through a channel the intermediate's audience does not read; agreement of the round trip with its source therefore says nothing about whether the intermediate renders the source's content for that audience | Chu, Zhmoginov and Sandler (2017), [LIT-1800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1800.md), §2 and §5, read in [NOTE-1346](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1346.md). The authors argue it from the many photographs a single map stands for, and support it with [THEORY-1127](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1127.md)'s evidence on one model; they propose, and do not run, the test of adding capacity to the smaller domain. Proposed. It is the converse of the record's collapse case for [CLAIM-496](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-496.md): there routes agree because nothing travels, here because everything does, out of sight. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1144](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1144.md) | A multilingual classifier trained only on English politeness ratings separates the most from the least polite requests in nine other languages at about 81% accuracy, without translation, yet stays about 10 points below one native judge's agreement with two others in most of them | Srinivasan and Choi (2022), [LIT-1799](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1799.md), read in [NOTE-1339](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1339.md). XLM-R fine-tuned on 1,926 English requests reaches 0.808 mean accuracy on the balanced top/bottom-quartile sets (250 per language), 0.801 on Google Translate input; GPT-3 zero-shot 0.706 (Table 3). Leave-one-out human accuracy is around 90% (Fig. 3). The judges were screened for agreeing with this classifier, and the extreme items were chosen on a mean that includes the held-out judge, so the gap and the transfer are both measured on favourable ground. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1145](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1145.md) | Unsupervised alignment of two monolingual word-embedding spaces recovers translations only where the spaces are close to isometric, and the distance from isometry depends on the corpora and the embedding algorithm as well as on the languages: adversarial alignment fails for English with Estonian or Finnish, across corpus domains, and between skip-gram and CBOW spaces of the same language pair, GW alignment is weakest on the same Finnish pair, and a spectral dissimilarity of small nearest-neighbour graphs tracks success | Søgaard, Ruder and Vulić (2018), [LIT-1819](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1819.md), read in [NOTE-1337](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1337.md), with the GW results of Alvarez-Melis and Jaakkola (2018), [LIT-1818](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1818.md), read in [NOTE-1336](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1336.md). Proposed: the evidence is single runs of one adversarial method, plus one GW table, and the authors themselves report that some seeds succeed where the method otherwise fails. What it does not support is a typological law about dependent marking, or the reading that a good fit establishes that the matched words mean the same. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1148](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1148.md) | Single judges agree moderately on how pragmatically similar two spoken utterances are, mean pairwise correlation 0.45 to 0.72 by session, less when the utterances differ in words, so a mean over six to nine judges is much more reliable than any one judge | Ward and Marco (2024), [LIT-1812](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1812.md), read in [NOTE-1338](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1338.md) from the LREC-COLING 2024 PDF. Over 693 seed/re-enactment pairs in three sessions, mean pairwise Pearson agreement was 0.45, 0.72 and 0.66 (Table 2), and 0.80 in Session 2 when lexically different pairs were left out (p. 160). The Spearman–Brown reliability of the panel means, 0.88–0.96, is my computation. The judges talked during the session and knew each other, and all pairs are within one language, so the figure is neither a floor for a panel nor a value for translations. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1154](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1154.md) | People interpreting an analogy carry relations from base to target and drop the attributes of objects, and among the relations they prefer those bound into a system by higher-order relations, such as causal or mathematical constraints, over isolated ones (structure-mapping and its systematicity principle) | Gentner (1983), [LIT-1810](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1810.md), read in [NOTE-1349](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1349.md). Argued from worked examples (the Rutherford analogy, heat and water) with one study, summarized without statistics, showing relational content dominating interpretations of analogies but not descriptions of objects. The systematicity principle is stated as a likelihood on p. 163 and as determination in the abstract and summary. The rules work on a predicate structure the theory takes as given, which its footnote 4 concedes is a modelling choice. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1157](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1157.md) | Native-speaker crowd judges agree only modestly on the graded politeness of written requests in their own language, mean pairwise Spearman about 0.46 across nine languages, and the same bilinguals agree less on English requests, about 0.36 | Srinivasan and Choi (2022), [LIT-1799](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1799.md), read in [NOTE-1339](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1339.md) from the Findings of EMNLP 2022 PDF. Three Prolific annotators per item rated Wikipedia requests −3 to +3; mean pairwise Spearman within 20-item tasks was 0.46 on the 15 target-language items and 0.36 on the 5 English items (Table 2). The paper says own-language agreement is higher "across all nine languages"; Tamil (0.33 against 0.38) is the exception. The annotators had been screened for agreeing with an XLM-R classifier. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1160](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1160.md) | Choosing which source objects to have an oracle match, by the derivative of a proxy utility of the entropic transport plan (its nearness to a permutation, or its consistency with the graphs) with respect to supervising each candidate match, averaged over matches by the current plan, raises held-out alignment accuracy more than uncertainty, centrality and matching-sampling query rules at the same label budget, by up to about three points on network alignment and less on image–text tasks; the gain depends on weighting by the current plan, without which the rule does worse than random | Yu et al. (2026), [LIT-1807](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1807.md), Tables 3–5 and 7, read in [NOTE-1327](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1327.md). Eight datasets, four aligners, a budget of 20% of true pairs in ten rounds after a random 20%, five runs, no variances. Proposed: an empirical result with small margins, on benchmarks where the truth is near one-to-one, so a coherence proxy and accuracy agree. It chooses among fixed questions; it does not extend what can be asked. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1170](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1170.md) | A convex map between two scenarios' model sets is induced by a classical adaptive procedure exactly when some non-contextual model of the corresponding adaptive hom scenario induces it | The adaptive analogue of Theorem 44 that Barbosa, Karvonen and Mansfield assert in Closing Bell ([LIT-845](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-845.md), §6.2) without proof, split from [THEORY-174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md) when the fifteenth status review narrowed that entry to the non-adaptive procedures its re-derivation covers and promoted it ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1: a dropped clause the source asserts). The non-adaptive route does not transfer as it stands, since Lemma 39 fails for adaptive procedures. Proposed until a proof is read or re-derived. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1171](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1171.md) | In groups that build a new communication system, larger groups make it more systematic, and the greater variety of input they face drives the effect | The wide form of Raviv, Meyer and Lev-Ari (2019), [LIT-825](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-825.md), kept here when the fifteenth status review narrowed [THEORY-164](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-164.md) to what their experiment showed and promoted it ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). The paper asserts that larger groups make an emerging language more systematic and that the greater variety of input they face drives the effect. One laboratory study with two group sizes found the size effect, and the mechanism rests on lagged association within its data; whether the effect replicates, and whether variability causes it, is open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1172.md) | Linear mode connectivity emerges during training, not at initialization: copies trained from a shared state become stable to SGD noise after 1.5–20% of training, and independently trained networks become linearly connected after alignment only gradually | The wide form [THEORY-114](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-114.md) held before the tenth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-114](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-114.md), Active, is its evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1173](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1173.md) | Testimonial injustice is an ingenuous misjudgement of a speaker's credibility caused by prejudice, not a deliberate manipulation of it, and it can be structural and pre-emptive, when a speaker's word is never sought because of a structural prejudice that is no one's fault | The wide form [THEORY-327](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-327.md) held before the twelfth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-327](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-327.md), Active, is its evidence. Fricker states the account as what testimonial injustice is, not only as her usage; the record holds it as hers, in two papers read in full. Whether the book states it so, and whether it is right about the wrong, is open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1174.md) | Industry can bias a scientific community toward a worse treatment without corrupting any individual, by selectively funding researchers whose methods already favour its product, provided researchers differ in method and both influence and the training of newcomers follow productivity; an independent funder that discounts industry-funded work counteracts this, and one that funds on productivity alone makes it worse | The wide form [THEORY-146](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-146.md) held before the eleventh status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-146](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-146.md), Active, is its evidence. The old title's "counteracts this only if it discounts" is restated as "that discounts ... counteracts this": the paper compares two funder policies and asserts no necessity, a mis-statement left with [THEORY-146](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-146.md)'s note. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1175.md) | Between tests, implementation intentions in the contingent if-then format had larger effects than plans that schedule when, where and what without linking cue to response (d = .43 against .29); rehearsing the plan once raised the effect, keeping a copy to revisit lowered it (.31 against .44), and adding how or for how long to a time-and-place cue roughly halved it | The wide form [THEORY-908](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-908.md) held before the tenth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-908](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-908.md), Active, is its evidence. Sheeran, Listrom & Gollwitzer (2024), [LIT-1488](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1488.md), conclude that the if-then format leads to superior impact, that rehearsal helps and that revisiting a kept copy makes plans less effective; their evidence is between-test moderator contrasts, uncorrected for bias. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1176](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1176.md) | Implementation intentions affect performance only when the goal intention they serve is strong and activated, so the cue-triggered response is gated by the goal and does not fire on the cue alone | The wide form [THEORY-904](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-904.md) held before the tenth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-904](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-904.md), Active, is its evidence. The title is the old title's general clause; its evidence clause read the 2024 moderator (d = .79) as a plan effect, a mis-statement left with [THEORY-904](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-904.md)'s note. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1177](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1177.md) | For experiments on a finite parameter set, being at least as informative for every decision problem is the same as being able to simulate the other by a randomisation | The wide form [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) held before the twelfth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md), Active, is its evidence. Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), claims the equivalence for any outcome space, through Theorem 2, quoted from his 1951 paper. The record's re-derivation reaches only outcome spaces that are standard Borel, since its last step needs a regular conditional distribution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1178](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1178.md) | In slices of striatum, visual and prefrontal cortex and hippocampus, Hebbian co-activation leaves a synaptic eligibility trace, lasting about 1 s in striatum, 3 to 10 s in cortex and about 2 s in CA1, that a later neuromodulator or plateau potential converts into a weight change and whose sign it can set: experimental support for three-factor learning rules on behavioural time scales | The wide form [THEORY-909](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-909.md) held before the tenth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-909](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-909.md), Active, is its evidence. Gerstner, Lehmann, Liakoni, Corneil & Brea (2018), [LIT-1494](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1494.md), read five experimental papers as a decaying eligibility trace whose conversion, and direction, a third factor sets, and as support for three-factor rules on behavioural time scales; the evidence is mostly slices, one laboratory per region, and the reviewers grant that other mechanisms could bridge the gap. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1179](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1179.md) | In an active-inference model of post-traumatic context inference, an overly precise prior that one is in a harmful context makes exploratory sampling look uninformative, so the agent attenuates the periphery, never receives the evidence that would correct the prior, and the belief sustains itself; lowering precision removes the symptoms without correcting the prior | The wide form [THEORY-285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md) held before the eighth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md), Active, is its evidence. Linson et al. (2025), [LIT-983](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-983.md), recast post-traumatic stress as lost context disambiguation and offer the loop as its mechanism; their simulations show it once per phenotype, with unreported parameters, and fit no patient data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1180](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1180.md) | In foraging tasks, higher stress or anxiety goes consistently with less exploration, and in one task with a predator to check for, people higher in somatic anxiety checked less and did worse, a reduction associated with greater aversion to detecting the predator | The wide form [THEORY-907](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-907.md) held before the thirteenth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-907](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-907.md), Active, is its evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1181](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1181.md) | The content of a crowd-built r/place artwork is decided off the canvas, in negotiation through shared design images, where a few central members admit or refuse additions, and carried out by placers who mostly never join the discussion, so the placement record shows the outcome of coordination but not who directed it or who cooperated | The wide form [THEORY-218](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-218.md) held before the tenth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-218](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-218.md), Active, is its evidence. Litherland & Mørch (2021), [LIT-1037](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1037.md), give a framework in which the image on the canvas carries out a design decided in the forum, and argue that placement data cannot show cooperation, conflict or affiliation; they studied one artwork, and call the link from forum power to placements unclear. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1182](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1182.md) | Across seven computational learning studies selected without a systematic search, anxiety goes with altered adjustment of learning rate to uncertainty, mostly for aversive outcomes, while overall learning rate, choice consistency and outcome valuation show little relation to it | The wide form [THEORY-897](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-897.md) held before the thirteenth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-897](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-897.md), Active, is its evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1183](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1183.md) | Crowd-maintained r/place images persist as an equilibrium of attack and repair, and their abrupt overthrow is preceded by several distinct precursors, including the defenders' own conduct, rather than by one generic warning signal, while many overthrows give no warning | The wide form [THEORY-214](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-214.md) held before the twelfth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-214](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-214.md), Active, is its evidence. Falmagne, Stephenson and Levin (2026), [LIT-1025](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1025.md), frame a defended image as an equilibrium of attack and repair and read several of the precursors of its overthrow as the defending community's conduct. The framing is presupposed by their state variable, and the social reading is their own conjecture from SHAP curves. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-1190](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1190.md) | In a Markov decision process, an agent that evaluates actions as if it will fail to avoid danger at later steps, while in fact choosing optimally at each step, spreads threat value to states far from the danger and avoids early and widely, which reproduces qualitatively exaggerated threat appraisal, fear generalization and several laboratory findings associated with anxiety | The wide form [THEORY-915](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-915.md) held before the thirteenth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-915](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-915.md), Active, is its evidence. | [THEORY-1216](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1216.md) | Ill structured problems can be handled by an alternation between a solver working on a problem that is well structured at each moment and a recognition and retrieval system that keeps modifying the problem space from memory or the environment, a serial solver gains nothing by assembling the problem space at the outset, and nothing but the size of the knowledge base may separate ill from well structured problems, so that no qualitatively new mechanisms are needed | The thesis Simon (1973), [LIT-1634](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1634.md), proposes, kept here when the twenty-second status review promoted [THEORY-1084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1084.md) as a report of the proposal ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). The paper describes the architecture, matches it to an architect, to battleship design and to a chess program, and argues from the seriality of the solver; nothing is built or tested, and Simon states the last part as what his analysis "suggests". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1217](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1217.md) | Both owner ideology and favor exchange drove the Hungarian portal Origo's reduced coverage of corruption in 2013–2016: favor exchange alone cut it by 29–44%, the new owner's ideology alone by 63% after 2016, and the two together by 74%, so they are substitutes; and a ban on targeted government advertising would have raised it by 41–79% | The finding of Szeidl and Szucs (2021), [LIT-1315](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1315.md), without the condition on their identifying assumptions, which the authors call "arguably strong" for print and weaker for online. (2017), [LIT-1507](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1507.md), p. 5, stated and not tested. Kept here when the twenty-second status review promoted [THEORY-927](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-927.md) as the report ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). | Proposed |

| [THEORY-1220](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1220.md) | A graph network that learns its sheaf restriction maps from node features succeeds on heterophilic graphs because it learns the class-aligned transports its separation theory prescribes: sign flips or rotations across classes, identity within them | The wider thesis of Bodnar et al. (2022), [LIT-1811](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1811.md), kept here when the twenty-second status review promoted [THEORY-1139](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1139.md), the reading of what was measured ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). | [THEORY-1222](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1222.md) | In relational quantum mechanics as stated in Rovelli (1996), rules (i) and (ii), that there is no state except within a further observer's information and no information without interaction, exclude any contradiction between observers' views: what a third system predicts of two observers' information always agrees with what it finds on interacting with them | Rovelli's general consistency claim (1996), [LIT-1635](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1635.md), §III.D, p. 15, kept here when the twenty-second status review promoted [THEORY-1080](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1080.md) as a report ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). | [THEORY-1224](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1224.md) | In Claude language models, projecting out the most active J-space directions in early workspace layers lowers the rate of felt, first-person, sensory language in the models' narrations of their own processing and in their descriptions of another person's experience, while norm-matched perturbations along other directions do not and the text stays coherent; so in these models the experiential register of report depends on the access-like workspace and is not specific to self-report | The wide form of Gurnee, Sofroniew et al. | [THEORY-1225](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1225.md) | Among white Southerners today, those living in counties where a larger share of the 1860 population was enslaved are somewhat less Democratic, less supportive of affirmative action and more racially resentful, by about a tenth of a standard deviation per standard deviation of slave share, and colder toward black Americans, by about a third; the difference is not accounted for by the present black share of the population, and in voting it appeared after Reconstruction rather than before the war, which supports its origin in the incentives that emancipation gave planters to repress black labor and votes, and its local transmission thereafter | The wide form of Acharya, Blackwell and Sen (2016), [LIT-1388](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1388.md), kept here when the status review of 2026-10-30 narrowed [THEORY-889](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-889.md) to what the analysis measured and promoted it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). | [THEORY-1226](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1226.md) | In Claude language models, a sparse set of residual-stream directions that a corpus-averaged Jacobian lens identifies as verbalizable (the J-space) is causally privileged for verbal report, for holding instructed concepts, for unspoken intermediate steps of reasoning and for passing one argument to many functions, while continuation, anomaly detection and line wrapping use the same information without routing through it; it carries workspace-like content only in a middle band of layers, holds on the order of tens of active directions and under a tenth of activation variance, and is amplified and relayed by the weights more than other directions | The wide form of Gurnee, Sofroniew et al. | [THEORY-1231](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1231.md) | When each agent's Q-function is approximated as an average of pairwise terms and expanded about the mean action of its neighbours, the first-order term vanishes and the approximation error is a second-order remainder bounded by the curvature of the pairwise Q-function, leaving a two-body problem between an agent and its neighbours' average; with homogeneous agents, mean field Q-learning converges to the Nash Q-value under assumptions the authors call strong, and learned tasks of 500 and 1000 agents where independent and centralized-critic baselines failed | The wide form of Yang et al. | [THEORY-1239](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1239.md) | No logistic system, one that separates propositions from general laws of inference, can carry commonsense knowledge, whose defaults later evidence displaces: attempts to repair its monotonicity will continue to fail | Minsky's (1974) further claim against logic, from the frames memo's appendix ([LIT-410](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-410.md), read in [NOTE-337](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-337.md), C7). It argues tractability from pruning and sparsity and counts evaluations for one maze (C3). It tries no problem where many outcomes stay plausible, and runs no Bayes-adaptive planner beside it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1246](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1246.md) | The so-called contentless goal-states of Shamatha, Transcendental and Stillness Meditation are neither truly contentless nor identical: they lack thoughts, perceptions, images and memories but keep wakefulness, calm, stillness, a non-conceptual knowing and the like, and they differ across the practices in attentional stability | Woods, Windt and Carter's thesis about the experiences, filed beside [THEORY-866](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-866.md) by the twenty-fourth status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-866](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-866.md), Active, holds what the teachers' texts describe; whether practitioners' experience is so is this entry's question, with [THEORY-866](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-866.md)'s old condition. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1251](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1251.md) | Mossio, Montévil and Longo take organization, as closure of constraints, to be a theoretical principle of biology, posited a priori as physics posits its phase space and defining the domain together with variation, so that every system meeting both is biological by definition and organisms are one class of such systems; on this reading "organisms are organized" is constitutive, not an empirical finding, and the principle is to be judged by what it makes intelligible | Mossio, Montévil and Longo (2016), [LIT-1888](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1888.md), §§1 and 4, read in [NOTE-1461](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1461.md); the definitions are Montévil and Mossio's ([LIT-582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-582.md), [TERM-070](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-070.md)). The paper states the principle's status and scope and supports it by history and analogy; it derives nothing from it here. Proposed: what the principle buys is untested in this paper. It does not say that closure is observed in every organism, nor that only organisms realize it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1262](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1262.md) | In multi-token-prediction pre-training at 167M to 1.2B parameters, the part of the MTP gradient that pulls toward the sampled target carries about four-fifths of the MTP gradient reaching the shared trunk with roughly a quarter of the signal-to-noise ratio of the self-distillation part, and removing it from the trunk improves next-token loss, speculative decoding and zero-shot accuracy by small margins | Teoh (2026), [LIT-1896](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1896.md), §6 Figs. 3–4 and Tables 2–6; read in [NOTE-1470](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1470.md). Proposed: one run per scale, four scales, no seeds or variances, margins of one to two percent. It does not show that data-anchored correction is dispensable: the output head keeps it, and the paper attributes the explicit-KL variant's weaker head to its absence there. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1263](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1263.md) | In on-policy self-distillation of language-model reasoning, a privileged-context teacher's advantage is concentrated on the student's failed trajectories and is smaller at larger scale, and restricting supervision to the student's verified trajectories, with the student's own failed attempt as the teacher's context, keeps the gain over the base model where standard on-policy self-distillation loses it | Hossain, Kousar and Tourni (2026), [LIT-1883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1883.md), Tables 1, 2 and 5; read in [NOTE-1479](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1479.md). Proposed: single training runs, Qwen3 only, the teacher's advantage measured at two of three scales, and a second candidate cause, per-entry clipping, left in every run. It does not show that the teacher's privileged knowledge is useless; it shows that it is hard to transmit where the student cannot see what it rests on. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1271](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1271.md) | Mossio, Montévil and Longo argue that closure of constraints both stabilizes and propagates variation: it regenerates each constraint beyond the time scale at which it is conserved, and removes a variation only if the variation does not reach the constraints that regenerate the varied one; when it does reach them, the variation propagates and the system either loses closure and disintegrates or comes to realize a new closure, which they say a rock, a flame or a table cannot do | Mossio, Montévil and Longo (2016), [LIT-1888](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1888.md), §5, read in [NOTE-1461](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1461.md). The conditional is close to definitional. That regeneration actually recovers is a dynamical claim the paper does not model, and the contrast with non-organized systems rests on three examples. Proposed. It does not say how large a variation closure can absorb, nor that recovery follows whenever the structural condition holds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1272](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1272.md) | Late in training, SGD weights drift sub-diffusively, with displacement growing as a power of training time set by a spectral dimension and the local learning coefficient | Hennick and De Baerdemacker (2025; ICLR 2026), [LIT-1879](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1879.md), read in [NOTE-1467](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1467.md). Late-training displacement fits R(t) ∝ t^α with α below ½ on MNIST MLPs, TinyStories models and ImageNet convnets fine-tuned with SGD, read through the Alexander–Orbach relation as α = d_s/(2λ) with d_s ≤ λ. Proposed: d_s is obtained by fitting that same relation, so the fits test the power law and not its link to the LLC; Kunin et al. report super-diffusion in another regime. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1277.md) | Persons and organizations can be described not as successive stages, with the collective built up from individuals, but as coexisting levels of ordering through which one action propagates, each preserving its components; on that description the problem of scaling up from individual to organizational action does not arise | Bencherki & Iliadis (2021), [LIT-1922](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1922.md), read in [NOTE-1483](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1483.md), with Bencherki (2017), [LIT-1901](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1901.md). The claim behind the parent paper's dissolution of the scaling-up problem ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), p. 1364). Proposed: a conceptual proposal, illustrated by one meeting excerpt, with no criterion that fixes a level independently of the analyst. It redescribes the problem; it does not show that aggregation never occurs. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1278.md) | Communication can be treated as transduction, the continuity of an action through processes that it transforms, rather than as exchange between parties; meaning is then the contribution an action makes, in retrospect, to a joint individuation, coexisting meanings mark concurrent individuations, and the problem of scaling agency from individual to collective is claimed to dissolve | Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024), [LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), read in [NOTE-1484](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1484.md), pp. 1355–1358 and 1363–1365. Simondon's transduction made into a theory of organizational communication. Proposed: argued from examples, with the dissolution of scaling up asserted. The examples (a synapse, a hunger pang, a piston) show the notion applies to any change, which is its strength as a vocabulary and its weakness as a theory. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1279](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1279.md) | Organizational categories are radially structured, so applying them to nonprototypical cases extends and changes them; this is one source of continuous change in routine organizational action | Tsoukas & Chia (2002), [LIT-1913](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1913.md), pp. 573–575, read in [NOTE-1489](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1489.md). The paper's mechanism for organizational becoming, built on Lakoff's and Johnson's prototype theory and Hart's penumbra of legal rules. Proposed: it is supported by illustrative cases, not tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1280](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1280.md) | Agency can be redescribed without agents, as the affective force by which one individuation process takes up another's excess action in a communicative event and both pass from a lesser to an augmented ability to act; agents are then effects of such events, and the absence of the force is disindividuation | Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024), [LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), read in [NOTE-1484](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1484.md), pp. 1349–1357. The paper's central proposal, after the Spinozan formula for affect that Massumi offers as a proposition, not a definition, and Simondon's individuation. Proposed: argued, and illustrated by one reanalysed meeting. It has no criterion that would let an observation count against it, and it builds the augmenting direction into the definition of agency. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1281](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1281.md) | Montréal School CCO's commitment to interaction as the basis of organizing makes conversation analysis its method of choice, and that commitment keeps ventriloquism from serving as an open metamodel for communication theory | Wilhoit (2016), [LIT-1923](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1923.md), read in [NOTE-1487](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1487.md). An argument about method in a five-page reply to Cooren. It is not a claim that ventriloquial analyses entify agents, which is what Bencherki, Brummans & Vézy ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), pp. 1363–1364) cite it for. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1283](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1283.md) | Micropolitics is the modulation of a relational field toward a maximally inclusive co-patterning of contrasting tendencies, in which each realizes itself without curtailing the others; the co-patterning is aesthetic, an affirmation of discord rather than its resolution | Massumi (2017), [LIT-1910](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1910.md), p. 64, read in [NOTE-1486](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1486.md); anticipated in the 2009 interview ([LIT-1905](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1905.md), p. 12) as "a symbiosis: a cross-fertilization of capacitations". It is an aim, which Massumi grants "sounds utopic" and calls "always-as-yet unknowable". Bencherki et al. ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), p. 1358) quote it exactly and use it to say what organizational becoming is constituted by. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1284](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1284.md) | Organization is a secondary accomplishment of change: change in organizations is continuous, as actors reweave their webs of beliefs and habits to accommodate new experience, and organization is both the attempt to stabilize that flux and the pattern that emerges from it | Tsoukas & Chia (2002), [LIT-1913](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1913.md), read in [NOTE-1489](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1489.md). The thesis of organizational becoming, which Bencherki, Brummans & Vézy 2024 ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md)) say their theory parallels. Proposed: it is argued from process philosophy and illustrated from others' ethnographies. The change it describes is carried by human actors, not agent-free. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1285.md) | Organizational action can be described as pre-individual, so that whose action it is, a person's or an organization's, is an outcome of the individuations it is allowed to contribute to rather than a given; an action then has as many significations as the individuations it takes part in, and a person whose action is refused a collective's recognition experiences that as disindividuation | Bencherki (2017), [LIT-1901](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1901.md), read in [NOTE-1482](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1482.md), with Bencherki & Iliadis (2021), [LIT-1922](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1922.md). The proposal of which Bencherki, Brummans & Vézy's "agency without agents" ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md)) is a development. Proposed: argued, and illustrated by three excerpts from one documentary. Nothing identifies disindividuation apart from the affect it is inferred from, and the account needs, but disclaims, a standard of whose action it rightly was. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1286.md) | Affect is not transmitted from one body or event to another; it is reactivated anew in each event, and bodies cued by the same event are attuned to it differentially rather than made alike | Massumi (2009), [LIT-1905](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1905.md), read in [NOTE-1488](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1488.md), pp. 6 and 9: affect "is not a content that can be transported from one event to another ... an event logic, not a logic of transmission or communication", and there is "affective difference in the same event". This sits uneasily with the "excess action" that Bencherki et al. ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md)) have passing between individuation processes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1291](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1291.md) | Within levels of mechanisms, apparent top-down and bottom-up causes can be read as mechanistically mediated effects, intralevel causation among components together with the constitution of the whole by them, so that the relation between levels is constitution and not causation; Craver and Bechtel show the translation for six cases, on the assumption, not argued, that every higher-level cause has a mechanistic explanation | Craver and Bechtel (2007), [LIT-1928](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1928.md), read in [NOTE-1491](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1491.md). Parts and wholes are not distinct events. So, given transmission, distinctness or asymmetry views of causation, they cannot be cause and effect, and the symmetry of interlevel experiments is explained by constitution. The six worked cases translate. The account says nothing about whether a feedback loop crossing the mechanism's boundary changes the analysis, and its generality is assumed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1292](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1292.md) | Whether a coupled oscillator sustains its own rhythm or is a damped oscillator driven from outside is settled directly by removing the drive, and, because the two arrangements are not dynamically equivalent, may also show in how they respond to a shift of phase: in Leise and Siegelmann's model, damped peripheral clocks regain their phase relation to the central clock quickly, while self-sustained ones take longer, need strong coupling, and sometimes resynchronize by a long delay instead of an advance | Bechtel and Abrahamsen (2010), [LIT-1936](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1936.md), §3.6, p. 328, read in [NOTE-1492](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1492.md). Peripheral clocks were once taken for "slaves" of the SCN, damping without it. Later evidence suggested they keep oscillating and lose synchrony, so the SCN is "a conductor" rather than "a ringmaster". The paper's reading is that models of both kinds "can reveal the empirical signatures that each may leave". This is a biological instance of the record's question where maintenance is realized. It is also a case outside [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s ideal limit: the outside drive does not reproduce the inside law, so a perturbation of state may tell them apart. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1294.md) | Constitution is best inferred, and only abductively, from the failure to break a coupling: a set of parts constitutes a phenomenon when every cause of the phenomenon is also a cause of some member of the set, no smaller set does as much, and no expansion of the variables studied turns up a cause of the phenomenon that spares them all, so constitutive relevance is fixed by the set a part belongs to and no finite series of experiments settles it | Baumgartner & Casini (2017), [LIT-1939](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1939.md), §§4–5, their No De-Coupling account, developing the fat-handedness criterion of Baumgartner & Gebharter (2016), [LIT-1934](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1934.md), pp. 20–22. Read in [NOTE-1490](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1490.md) and [NOTE-1493](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1493.md). Proposed: a definition offered with no operationalization and no case from practice, which the authors say themselves. It does not say how far a variable set must be expanded, and it takes parthood as given. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1296](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1296.md) v2 | Deliberate thought selects and sustains candidates from a stream of unintended thoughts that mind-wandering generates, and whether the conscious model of oneself as a knower that accompanies the selection causes it, enables it or only accompanies it is undecided by current evidence | Metzinger (2017), [LIT-1945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1945.md), pp. 11–17, read in [NOTE-1496](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1496.md). The "cognitive affordance hypothesis": mind-wandering is "mental sleep-walking" that "sets up the inner world" of candidate mental actions, and frontal control "latch[es] onto the best candidate". Offered as a hypothesis after Clark and Cisek's affordance competition, with no data. The second clause is the chapter's own statement that the data "do not help to decide" what the epistemic agent model does, which takes back the principle the 2015 paper stated. "Best" is not defined, so the hypothesis does not say whether selection is by the candidates' content or by relations that govern them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1297](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1297.md) v2 | Mind-wandering is a recurring loss of M-autonomy, the veto-centred ability to suspend or end one's own ongoing mental processes; on the figures Metzinger uses, it takes about half of conscious time, not the two thirds he states | Metzinger (2013), [LIT-1942](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1942.md), restated in 2015, [LIT-1941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1941.md); read in [NOTE-1495](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1495.md) and [NOTE-1497](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1497.md). The identification is conceptual: an episode of unintentional mind-wandering cannot, while it runs, be suspended or ended at will, and veto is what M-autonomy turns on. The share is computed from others' figures, and recomputed here: 631 of 1207 conscious minutes, 52%, against the "roughly two thirds" both papers state. Proposed: no measure of veto during episodes is reported, and the 30–50% figures count task-unrelated thought, which includes deliberate daydreaming the definition excludes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1298](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1298.md) v2 | When mental control returns after mind-wandering, the self-model represents the return as the person's own act whether or not the person's control system caused it, because it must bridge to earlier control to keep the autobiographical self-model continuous | Metzinger (2015), [LIT-1941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1941.md), pp. 289–292, read in [NOTE-1497](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1497.md); first in 2013 ([LIT-1942](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1942.md), pp. 4, 11) and widened in 2017 ([LIT-1945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1945.md), pp. 20–21) to the sense of origination in agency generally. It rests on Schooler et al. (2011) and Wegner (2002), neither read, and on the argument that a self-model which must represent itself as always having had the ability cannot represent its return as caused from outside. A hypothesis: no episode is reported in which the cause of a return and the report of it were recorded apart. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1299](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1299.md) v2 | Pure awareness, on Metzinger's account, is the content of a temporally thin model of the organism's own tonic alertness, its capacity to know; experience in this minimal form lacks an egoic self-model, a first-person perspective, time, space and even phenomenal oneness, but not self-modelling, and tonic alertness that is not so modelled is not experienced | Metzinger (2020), [LIT-1946](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1946.md), read in full in [NOTE-1498](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1498.md), and Metzinger (2024), [LIT-1943](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1943.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1499](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1499.md). MPE is "an inner representation of tonic alertness", "non-egoic self-modelling" that "definitely has representational content". In the 2024 sketch it is "a highest-level but nonegoic self-model" of the system's epistemic openness, which "really endows the content generated on all lower-order levels with phenomenality". It is a hypothesis fitted to retrospective reports. It does not say that consciousness needs no model of the system, only that it needs no model of a knowing self. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1300](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1300.md) | In mind-wandering the capacity for veto over one's own mental processes is kept and its representation in the self-model is lost, and on Metzinger's principle a capacity can be deliberately exercised only while it is so represented; the loss of M-autonomy is then the loss of a condition of the capacity's efficacy, not of the capacity | Metzinger (2015), [LIT-1941](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1941.md), pp. 280–283 and 296, read in [NOTE-1497](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1497.md); anticipated in 2013 ([LIT-1942](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1942.md), p. 3, note 4). The "moderate, nuanced position": what is lost is "not the ability itself" but "conscious knowledge of our potential for second-order mental action", with the "principle of 'Autonomy by Phenomenal Self-Representation'". Both are stated, not argued, and neither is tested. Metzinger's 2017 chapter ([LIT-1945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1945.md), pp. 13–14) says the data cannot decide whether the self-model constitutes, enables or only accompanies control, which withholds the principle's causal reading. "Deliberately" also does work: inhibition can be wholly subpersonal. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1302](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1302.md) | Sánchez-Cañizares reinterprets Irruption Theory for binary decisions (IAT*): irruption is the onset of a landscape with one attractor per option and absorption the passage to a single attractor, both correlated in mind and brain, reversing the sign of Froese's variance hypothesis; the mind's causal role is to set the landscape's control parameters by "selecting the relevant physical coarse-graining", not to push the state, so on this account the mind controls which outcomes exist and not which one the state reaches | Sánchez-Cañizares (2026), [LIT-1992](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1992.md), read in full in [NOTE-1506](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1506.md). The interpretation is the paper's (pp. 6–7, 18–20); the last clause is this reading's description of the control architecture it implies, from the model and simulation of pp. 8–12, in which the choice between wells is settled by initial condition and noise. Proposed: the paper says IAT* "cannot be tested with empirical results without further assumptions" (p. 7). Bears on [CLAIM-533](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-533.md) and [QUESTION-071](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-071.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1308](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1308.md) | In Chen et al.'s student samples from Belgium, China, the USA and Peru, need satisfaction related to life satisfaction and vitality and need frustration to depressive symptoms with no detectable difference across countries, and neither relation was moderated by how much a person valued or desired the need | Chen et al. (2015), [LIT-2000](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2000.md), read in [NOTE-1527](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1527.md). Two cross-sectional studies, N = 683 and 1,051. The relations and the null moderations are as reported. Proposed because universality is inferred from failures to reject, with fewer than 150 per country in the test half, and because explicit valuation and desire are the only measures of need strength. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1311](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1311.md) | The BPNSFS frustration scales measure low need satisfaction in negatively keyed form, not need frustration in the sense of active thwarting, so the separation of frustration from low satisfaction in BPNSFS data, and frustration's stronger link to ill-being there, is largely a keying artefact | Murphy et al. (2023), [LIT-1978](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1978.md), read in [NOTE-1530](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1530.md); Kermavnar et al. (2024), [LIT-1988](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1988.md), read in [NOTE-1509](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1509.md), adopt it. The item content and the keying structure ([THEORY-1316](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1316.md)) are shown. That the frustration scales are therefore low satisfaction is the authors' conclusion, held "probably" and "likely primarily", and by their own account cannot be decided with data in which keying and construct are confounded. Proposed for that step. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1314](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1314.md) | Contextual emergence, on which an emergent phenomenon's parts are necessary but not sufficient, needs a functional boundary between the phenomenon and its context, without which the context could be folded into the base and the account collapse into weak emergence or global supervenience; and the subject of attention is contextually emergent in this sense, its boundary being the skull, meninges and brain stem, so that its macro-level patterns constrain micro-level activity with a power that is not reducible to the parts and needs neither downward nor circular causation | Jennings (2026), [LIT-1963](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1963.md), §§4–6, read in [NOTE-1508](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1508.md), with Bishop and Atmanspacher 2006 ([LIT-1987](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1987.md)) and Bishop, Silberstein and Pexton 2022 ([LIT-1993](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1993.md)), both unread, for contextual emergence. The boundary condition is the paper's own addition (fn. 15). Proposed, with a sharp edge: the paper's reason that the boundary resists micro redescription is that its properties "are macro-level ones" (p. 20), which is the point at issue, and its neural evidence fits weak emergence too. Bears on [CLAIM-334](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-334.md), whose supervenience premise it denies. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1319](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1319.md) | In Niemiec, Ryan and Deci's post-college sample, attaining intrinsic aspirations went with more well-being and less ill-being, and attaining extrinsic aspirations, entered alongside it, added nothing to well-being and went with more ill-being; the extrinsic null is a unique-variance result, since alone extrinsic attainment correlated positively with well-being and need satisfaction | Niemiec, Ryan and Deci (2009), [LIT-1960](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1960.md), read in [NOTE-1520](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1520.md) from the PMC author manuscript. N = 147 at two years post-college; latent SEM and residualized-change models, all self-report. The intrinsic result and the extrinsic null are as reported; the null holds only with intrinsic attainment in the model. Proposed because one small correlational sample cannot show that extrinsic success fails to raise well-being. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1321](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1321.md) | Froese proposes that irruptions combined with attunement, modelled on Watson et al.'s self-optimization of a Hopfield network by occasional resets to arbitrary states plus Hebbian learning, answer the libertarian's randomness challenge, how behaviour can be effective though underdetermined; but in the model offered the resets are arbitrary, so what makes the behaviour effective is the learned attractor landscape, and nothing in it distinguishes a motivated irruption from noise | Froese (2023), [LIT-1950](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1950.md), read in full in [NOTE-1521](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1521.md). The first half is the paper's proposal (§§4, 5.2.3, 6); the second half is this reading's observation about the model it cites, from the paper's own description of it ("reset to an arbitrary configuration"). Proposed because the proposal is stated as potential ("holds potential to provide") and no model with motivated irruptions is given. It bears directly on [CLAIM-533](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-533.md) and on the luck objection ([THEORY-328](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-328.md), [THEORY-040](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-040.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1324](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1324.md) v2 | In Ryan, Mims and Koestner's experiment, the same expected reward for doing well left less later free-choice engagement when given with controlling feedback than with informational feedback, and in both styles less than no reward with the same feedback: the interpersonal style of a performance-contingent reward changes its effect, and the reward lowers intrinsic motivation even when the information it carries is held fixed | Ryan, Mims and Koestner (1983), [LIT-1970](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1970.md), read in [NOTE-1522](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1522.md) from the scan on the SDT site. One experiment, N = 96, n = 16 per cell, ANCOVA on initial interest. The framing effect is F(1, 89) = 4.25 and the reward effect against feedback-matched controls F(1, 89) = 4.34; recomputed from the cell means without the covariate, about 4.9 and 3.4 (p ≈ .07). Felt pressure was higher under controlling conditions; mediation was not tested. Proposed for replication and mediation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1325](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1325.md) | In Chirkov et al.'s student samples from South Korea, Russia, Turkey and the USA, the more autonomous people's reasons for engaging in practices of any cultural orientation, collectivist and vertical included, the higher their well-being, with no detectable difference across countries or genders; and vertical practices were much less internalized than horizontal ones | Chirkov, Ryan, Kim and Kaplan (2003), [LIT-1989](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1989.md), read in [NOTE-1513](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1513.md) from the published PDF on selfdeterminationtheory.org. N = 559, cross-sectional self-report. The positive relation held in every country and for every type of practice (β = .15–.42 within country); "no moderation" is twelve non-significant interactions in samples of 94–195. The primary study for SDT's claim that autonomy is not individualism, which it supports empirically only in this form. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1326](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1326.md) | In Voigt's model of hard decisions, when two options are valued equally the value differential is too small to choose (conflict, dACC), and the tie is broken during the choice by fixation: precuneus allocates spatial attention bottom-up to the salient item and dlPFC holds it in working memory, which both settles the choice and raises that item's value, a change that lasts only if the choice is remembered (hippocampus) | Voigt (2022), [LIT-1976](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1976.md), an Opinion article read in [NOTE-1517](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1517.md). The model is the author's "tentative" synthesis, resting mainly on Voigt et al. 2019 (not held) in which fixation duration and dlPFC and precuneus activity predicted later preference change; the causal role of gaze is imported from other studies. Proposed. The sharp edge for its use by Jennings ([THEORY-1341](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1341.md)): the attentional step is bottom-up capture by salience, not top-down prefrontal feedback. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1328](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1328.md) | Kane answers the luck objection by making indeterminism a hindrance inside goal-directed effort rather than a cause on its own: in a self-forming action the agent makes two competing efforts, each meeting the indeterminacy as interference from the other, so whichever succeeds is a willed success for which the agent is responsible; indeterminism lessens the agent's control but not its responsibility, and what responsibility needs is macro-control of processes involving many neurons, not control of each | Kane (2009), [LIT-1984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1984.md), pp. 39–44, read in [NOTE-1518](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1518.md). Proposed: the reply rests on analogies whose structure differs from the self-forming case (one aim and an outside obstacle against two aims, each the other's obstacle), and it does not meet the rollback form of the luck objection ([THEORY-328](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-328.md) is the record's nearest neighbour). Its concession, that indeterminism lessens control, is what [CLAIM-533](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-533.md) turns on. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1329](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1329.md) | On Kane's account, self-forming actions occur under motivational conflict, when tension moves the relevant brain regions away from thermodynamic equilibrium, "a kind of stirring up of chaos" that makes them sensitive to micro-indeterminacy at the neuronal level, so that the choice is undetermined | Kane (2009), [LIT-1984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1984.md), p. 39, read in [NOTE-1518](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1518.md). Kane's neural hypothesis, stated without evidence in this paper. Proposed: it is an empirical claim about brains for which the paper gives none, and the record holds nothing that measures it. It is the attribution [CLAIM-533](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-533.md) makes to Kane, now checked against his text. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1334](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1334.md) | Persona shifts induced by prompting and by finetuning are mediated by the same linear trait directions, so finetuning on data that implies a trait moves the model along the trait's persona vector as a system prompt would; Chen et al. suspect personas are latent factors that persist across many tokens | Chen et al. (2025), [LIT-1998](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1998.md), read in [NOTE-1524](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1524.md). The mediating reading is the authors' framing and PSM's use of the paper ([LIT-1952](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1952.md): training-time shifts "can be regarded as conditioning"). What the paper shows is correlation of shift with expression, and steering effects in both directions; that the regularizer against the shift fails, with the trait moving to other directions, counts against a single direction being the carrier. Proposed for that gap. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1336](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1336.md) | In a cart-pole whose only given utility is 10-step empowerment, a controller that greedily picks the action leading to the more empowered successor balances the pole upright, though the states of highest empowerment lie off-centre and cannot be reached or sustained under the agent's own dynamics; what the agent can keep is not where empowerment is highest | Klyubin, Polani and Nehaniv (2008), [LIT-1951](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1951.md), pp. 4–7, read in [NOTE-1514](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1514.md). A single simulation of one model with two actions, computed by the authors; the robustness of the off-centre maxima is stated, not shown. Proposed for want of a reproduction and a second system. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1343](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1343.md) | The first-order picture in which a small integral of motion Q of a many-body Hamiltonian is, under weak local noise, the slowest Lindbladian eigenoperator holds at large system size whenever its leak ε out of span{Q} satisfies ε ≲ γ ≪ 1, because the gap controlling the perturbation is not the exponentially small level spacing but one of order min(γL, √(v_Bγ)), set by the ballistic growth of the operators Q leaks into | Yang and Abanin (2025), [LIT-1958](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1958.md), §IV, read in [NOTE-1534](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1534.md). Proposed because the argument assumes fully chaotic operator growth for the complement, is checked numerically only at nine sites, and is qualified by the authors themselves: hydrodynamic modes give a continuum of slow modes in the Mori limit, so the gap "might not exist at all" outside sectors orthogonal to them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1351](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1351.md) v2 | In West, Fisher, Gardner and Kiers's account, a transition in individuality is defined by two separable conditions, mutual dependence (parts that once replicated alone can replicate only within the larger unit) and negligible within-group conflict, and proceeds by forming a cooperative group and then transforming it, with no clear border between the steps; across transitions what explains them is an ecological benefit to cooperation together with group formation that unites the members' interests (clonal bottlenecks, lifetime monogamy, vertical transmission of clonal symbionts), while kin discrimination and the repression of competition played relatively minor roles | West et al. (2015), [LIT-2003](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2003.md), read in [NOTE-1538](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1538.md). A colloquium review: the definition and the two steps are the authors' framework, and the explanatory claim is drawn from the comparative literature they cite. Proposed because they call it "tentative", and because the theory for transitions between species is missing on their own account. It differs from [THEORY-141](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-141.md) on mechanism: group formation, not policing, does the work. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1353](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1353.md) | In transformer language models to about 1B parameters, a conjunction circuit forms when its last missing parts align together in one stochastic attempt, with no credit for partial alignment, so its formation time depends on how many parts are missing and not on its size, and ablating one part collapses the capability; plasticity loss is the same law read backward, a depletion of uncommitted attention heads that more data cannot undo and re-initializing query–key weights can | Dong (2026), read in [NOTE-1540](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1540.md). One rate equation, sites × attempts × drive × e^(−βK) minus destruction, with K the missing parts. Forward, a capability ignites above a data-concentration floor that is a saddle–node; backward, plasticity loss is site depletion, silent in the loss and repaired by a query–key reset; and no native SGD knob is a temperature. Evidence: a toy grid, ablation on Pythia (32 of 32 cells below partial credit, 22 of 32 on the preregistered criterion) and six seeds for the reset. Proposed: single-author, unreplicated, mixing unproved. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1354](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1354.md) | Lucas and Griffiths propose that people learn the functional form of causal relationships, such as whether causes act disjunctively or conjunctively and how reliably, as abstract theories in a hierarchical Bayesian model, and transfer them to new objects of the same kind, so that evidence about one set of objects changes their causal judgments about a different set | Lucas & Griffiths (2010), [LIT-2018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2018.md), read in full in [NOTE-1543](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1543.md). Five blicket-meter experiments: training that suggests a conjunctive, noisy-disjunctive or deterministic form changes judgments of new objects in an identical test block, and more within a domain than across; a two-parameter sigmoid model fits the mean ratings (r = 0.98–0.99). Proposed: small samples, in-sample fits against rivals that cannot vary between conditions, one reversed prediction, one marginal effect, and no preregistered replication read. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1355](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1355.md) v2 | Gershman, Blei and Niv propose that animals in conditioning experiments assign trials to latent causes under a prior admitting an unbounded number of causes, so that extinction is learned as a new cause rather than erasing the conditioned one, and that renewal and the context-dependence of latent inhibition follow from this inference while hippocampal lesions and immaturity abolish them by preventing new causes from being inferred | Gershman, Blei & Niv (2010), [LIT-2011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2011.md), read in [NOTE-1547](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1547.md). A Chinese restaurant process mixture over trials, inferred online by a particle filter, reproduces acquisition, extinction, ABA and ABC renewal and context-specific latent inhibition in simulation; with the concentration set to zero it reproduces the loss of context-dependence after hippocampal lesions and in young rats. Proposed: the support is qualitative simulation beside replotted data from other labs, with no fitted parameters and no quantitative comparison with rival models. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1356](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1356.md) | Collins and Frank propose that people learning stimulus–action rules by reinforcement spontaneously build latent task-sets cued by one input dimension, even when that structure gives no advantage during learning, so that a new context signalling an old task-set is learned faster (positive transfer) while a new context whose rule partly overlaps old task-sets draws errors that would be correct under an old task-set (negative transfer) | Collins and Frank (2013), [LIT-2012](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2012.md), read in [NOTE-1545](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1545.md).
