Proposed: positive transfer replicated across the paper's two experiments (N = 33, N = 35) but is modest (t = 2.37, p = .024 in Experiment 1), and the negative-transfer interaction was significant over the whole group only in Experiment 1, a trend in Experiment 2. The EEG follow-up re-analyses Experiment 2's participants, so it is no independent replication. The account is behavioural; it does not say people perform Bayesian inference over task-sets, which the authors disclaim, nor that the Chinese-restaurant reuse prior is what people use, which they leave untested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1358](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1358.md) | In Kemp, Goodman and Tenenbaum's account, people learn to learn causal models by inferring a causal schema, a partition of objects into categories with category-level causal powers, characteristic features and between-category interactions, from contingency and feature data, and the schema lets a causal model for a new object be learned from one trial or from its features alone while still being overruled when the object proves unlike any category | Kemp, Goodman & Tenenbaum (2010), [LIT-2008](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2008.md), read in [NOTE-1551](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1551.md). A causal schema, a CRP partition of objects with category-level causal models, features and pairwise interactions, sits above object-level causal Bayes nets; four adult experiments in one paradigm show one-shot and zero-shot causal learning and overruling, matched qualitatively better than two baselines, with two misfits. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1359](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1359.md) | Jiang and Lucas propose that, when people choose interventions across a series of related causal-learning tasks, they seek information about overhypotheses about how causes combine as well as about which objects are causes in the task at hand, carry the overhypotheses they learn into later tasks, and accept less information about the immediate causal structure in exchange | Jiang & Lucas (2024), [LIT-2014](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2014.md), read in [NOTE-1546](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1546.md) (appendices not read). Two preregistered online blicket experiments. Learners that ignore form information or hold one fixed form barely beat random at predicting interventions; the model that does not transfer edges the full model on average (.059 against .055), while per participant the full model is best for the largest group, whose fitted weights mostly favour form information. Proposed: the transfer clause is the weakest, failing at the group level. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1360](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1360.md) | Körding, Beierholm, Ma, Quartz, Tenenbaum and Shams propose that in auditory-visual localization the observer infers whether the two cues share a cause and weights fused against separate estimates by the posterior probability of a common cause, so that an ideal observer of this kind predicts human localization responses and the fall of crossmodal bias with disparity better than forced fusion, segregation or interaction-prior models | Körding et al. (2007), [LIT-2010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2010.md), read in full in [NOTE-1541](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1541.md). Proposed: one experiment of the authors' own (19 subjects) and a refit of Wallace et al.'s (2004) published data support it, against forced fusion, segregation, a MAP rule and two interaction priors, but the rule that commits to the more probable structure was not compared and only a split-half check tests held-out prediction. It does not say how the prior over causal structure is learned, that the inference is automatic, or that the model is hierarchical; that word is A's, from the owner's pasted synthesis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1361](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1361.md) | Baker, Jara-Ettinger, Saxe and Tenenbaum propose that people attribute beliefs, desires and percepts to an agent moving through a spatial scene by jointly inverting a model of it as an approximately rational planner that perceives by line of sight and updates its beliefs, so that such a model predicts adults' graded mental-state and world-state judgements better than versions lacking action costs or uncertain beliefs and better than motion-feature heuristics | Baker, Jara-Ettinger, Saxe and Tenenbaum (2017), [LIT-2013](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2013.md), read in full in [NOTE-1549](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1549.md). Proposed: two experiments (16 and 176 adults) support it against the lesioned models, but the motion heuristic tied on Experiment 1 beliefs, the desire fit carries no information within scenario type, and the test is cross-validation over the authors' own scenarios. It is a computational-level claim, not an account of the algorithm; it does not say the model is hierarchical, a word that is A's, from the owner's pasted synthesis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1362](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1362.md) | Mathys and colleagues show that a hierarchy of any number of Gaussian random walks, each level setting the log-variance of the one below, inverts under a mean-field variational approximation to one-step updates of the same form at every level above the first; each mean update is a prediction error weighted by the ratio of the precision of the prediction below to the posterior precision, a value prediction error at the first level and a volatility prediction error above it | Mathys et al. (2014), [LIT-2015](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2015.md), read in [NOTE-1548](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1548.md). The Hierarchical Gaussian Filter's update equations for n levels: the same precision-weighted prediction-error form at every level above the first, a value prediction error at level 1 and a volatility prediction error above. Proposed until the updates are re-derived. It says nothing about how close the approximation is to exact inversion, whether the parameters can be recovered, or whether people learn this way. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1363](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1363.md) | In Kemp, Perfors and Tenenbaum's account, abstract inductive constraints such as the shape bias are higher-level parameters of a hierarchical Bayesian model, here the within-category variability and population feature distribution of a Dirichlet-multinomial, learned from a few labelled exemplars per category at the same time as the categories' own feature distributions, and once learned they let a single exemplar of a new category license generalization by shape | Kemp, Perfors & Tenenbaum (2007), [LIT-2017](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2017.md), read in [NOTE-1544](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1544.md). Learning a constraint is inference over a hierarchy's higher-level parameters (α, β): low within-category variability of shape is the shape bias. The model reproduces Smith et al.'s first- and second-order generalization qualitatively, with no new experiments, and misses the no-name condition. Computational level; the structure and top prior are given. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1364](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1364.md) | Collins, Cavanagh and Frank propose that the latent task-set structure people build incidentally during simple reinforcement learning shows in prefrontal EEG: a switch of the dimension a participant treats as context, but not of the other dimension, evokes task-switch potentials over lateral prefrontal cortex, and the size of the early switch positivity and the decoded attention to that dimension each covary across participants with how much they later transfer learned rules to new contexts | Collins, Cavanagh and Frank (2014), [LIT-2007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2007.md), read in [NOTE-1550](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1550.md). Proposed: one sample, the participants of Collins and Frank's (2013) Experiment 2 (N = 35; 33 for ERP, 32 for classification), with several uncorrected topographic tests and an early-positivity window chosen from the grand average. The late switch negativity tracked the context dimension but did not predict transfer; the early positivity, absent at group level, and the decoder did (ρ = 0.5, ρ = 0.35), and agreed with each other only marginally. The context dimension is assigned from behavioural switch-costs, so the EEG does not read out the structure independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1365](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1365.md) | Mathys, Daunizeau, Friston and Stephan derive, by a mean-field variational approximation with each variational energy expanded to second order at the previous posterior mean, closed-form one-step updates for a hierarchy of Gaussian random walks whose step sizes are set by the level above; the updates take the Rescorla–Wagner form, their learning rate rises with the inferred volatility, and individual differences are carried by fixed coupling parameters | Mathys et al. (2011), [LIT-2016](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2016.md), read in [NOTE-1552](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1552.md). A derivation with illustrative simulations: closed-form trial-by-trial updates for a three-level hierarchy of volatility, of Rescorla–Wagner form, with a learning rate that is the agent's posterior variance and grows with its volatility estimate, and with per-agent coupling parameters standing for individual differences. Proposed until the updates are re-derived. It says nothing about how close the approximation is to exact inversion, or about whether people learn this way. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1366](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1366.md) | Freidlin and Wentzell hold that for a dynamical system under small random perturbations, the behaviour over long times, exit from a domain of attraction and which stable set the stationary distribution concentrates on, is decided by the logarithmic asymptotics of the probabilities of rare events on finite intervals, given by the infimum of an action functional over the relevant paths | Freidlin and Wentzell (3rd ed. 2012; Russian original 1979), [LIT-2035](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2035.md), read in [NOTE-1562](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1562.md) from the front matter only, where the Introduction outlines this programme (pp. xix–xxi). Proposed: the theorems are in chapters not read. Berglund's survey, [LIT-2037](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2037.md), restates the exit-time theorem but not the stationary-distribution result. It does not give sharp times, only logarithmic ones, and it is about diffusions, not about organizations or capabilities. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1367](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1367.md) | Dollar and Howe report that a four-fingered hand with compliant polymer joints and an adaptive tendon transmission, driven by one actuator under open-loop control, grasped household and test objects despite positioning errors comparable to the object's size, so that passive mechanics did work usually assigned to sensing and control | Dollar and Howe (2010), [LIT-2040](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2040.md), read in [NOTE-1575](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1575.md). Proposed: the experiments are small, success was judged by eye, and no fully actuated hand was tested alongside. It is about power grasps of medium objects; the hand cannot pinch. It does not say that the hand computes, or has goals, or that one actuator suffices for dexterous manipulation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1368](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1368.md) v2 | Chen, Choi and Mahadevan show that in a quad kirigami sheet read as a linkage the fewest links that rigidify the sheet always outnumber the fewest that connect it, and that under random links the maximum of internal mechanisms, connectivity percolation and rigidity percolation fall at distinct link densities in that order | Chen, Choi & Mahadevan (2020), [LIT-2064](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2064.md), read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1574](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1574.md) (main text; the SI with the proofs was not read). Proposed: the minimal counts are proved by construction in the SI, which was not read; the thresholds are numerical, and the rigidity threshold is a peak of a second derivative with a heuristic explanation. Planar quad kirigami and infinitesimal rigidity only; no experiments. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1369](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1369.md) v2 | Chen and colleagues show that marginally rigid origami and kirigami carry a topological polarization, so that a quasi-1D origami strip folds at the edge its pattern angles select and a domain wall between kirigami of different polarizations is flexible though constraints locally match the degrees of freedom, while periodic triangulated origami appears always to have zero polarization | Chen, Liu, Evans, Paulose, Cohen, Vitelli and Santangelo (2016; arXiv 2015), [LIT-2049](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2049.md), read in full in [NOTE-1624](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1624.md). Proposed: the strip result has the authors' own experiment, but the domain-wall result is numerical and the 2D origami claim is a conjecture on numerics. It does not say that joining rigid parts creates freedom in general: equal polarizations give no wall mode, and walls of the other orientation are stressed lines that carry load. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1370](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1370.md) v2 | Berglund holds that large-deviation theory fixes only the exponential order of the mean time for a small-noise diffusion to leave a potential well, while the Eyring–Kramers prefactor needs other methods, fails at degenerate saddles, and can fail to have a limit for irreversible dynamics | Berglund (2011), [LIT-2037](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2037.md), read in [NOTE-1590](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1590.md), a review registered as a stand-in for Freidlin and Wentzell ([LIT-2035](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2035.md)). Proposed: the survey sketches and cites the proofs rather than giving them. It does not say the prefactor is unknowable for non-gradient systems in general, only that large deviations do not deliver it and that in the cycling case it has no limit. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1371](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1371.md) | Ratliff, Dong, Sekar and Fiez hold that economics, control theory and online learning each solve only part of incentive design, so that designing incentives for returning agents whose behaviour changes with the principal's own past incentives, under hidden types or hidden actions, remains open | Ratliff, Dong, Sekar and Fiez (2019), [LIT-2097](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2097.md), read in full in [NOTE-1566](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1566.md) from the authors' manuscript. A perspective's judgement of the state of three literatures, not a theorem; Proposed until a later review states the same. It does not say the problem is unsolvable, and it leaves out the economics of dynamic contracting with limited commitment, which treats one case of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1373](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1373.md) v2 | Combinational logic built from flat-foldable origami switches can be reconfigured by moving the switching elements rather than rewiring them, by rotating the two elements of a gate between series and parallel or by permuting elements among the blocks of a Rubik's-cube arrangement, and so reaches more functions per element than a rewired gate array | Hu, Tan, Chen and Yan (2025), [LIT-2082](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2082.md), read in [NOTE-1608](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1608.md). The rotatable gate, the 30-gate array and a third-order cube switching between full adder and full subtractor were built and tested over all inputs; the densities per cube order and the gate savings are counts against the authors' own baselines. It does not say that the computation is purely mechanical, since outputs and inter-gate signals are electrical, or that the material reconfigures itself. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1374](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1374.md) v2 | Hopkins (2013) holds that a flexure system's freedom space is the intersection of its parallel limbs' freedom spaces and the span of its serial stages' freedom spaces, so the same finite library of freedom–constraint space types suffices to analyse and synthesize any combination of parallel and serial flexures, and comparing constraint orders with the system's constraint space classifies a design as exactly, over- or under-constrained | Hopkins (2013), [LIT-2069](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2069.md), read in full in [NOTE-1580](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1580.md). Proposed: the rules follow from linear reciprocity of screw spaces and are stated with design examples, but there is no experiment and no independent check, and the library's completeness rests on Hopkins (2010), [LIT-2042](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2042.md). It excludes interconnected limbs, is kinematic only, and its over-constraint test says nothing of misfit stress. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1377](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1377.md) v2 | Li and Choi show that the rigidity of general origami patterns can be tuned by enforcing or relaxing the planarity of selected facets, and that the critical density at which a pattern reaches its minimum number of degrees of freedom depends on the facet-selection rule, the number of candidates sampled per step and the fraction of triangular facets | Li & Choi (2026), [LIT-2068](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2068.md), read in [NOTE-1564](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1564.md) (main text; the Supplementary Notes were not read). Proposed: one group's simulations on ten patterns. The n − 3 count is proved; the dependence of the critical density on rule, pool size and triangular-facet ratio is numerical, and the formula for it is fitted, not derived. Rigidity is infinitesimal at one folded configuration, and the "critical density" is a fixed-size statistic, not a thermodynamic threshold. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1380](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1380.md) v2 | Zhuk shows, independently of Bulatov, that for a finite set of relations on a finite domain, deciding satisfiability is solvable in polynomial time if a weak near-unanimity operation preserves every relation and is NP-complete otherwise, by an algorithm that combines local consistency with linear algebra over prime fields | Zhuk (2017; J. ACM 2020), [LIT-2023](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2023.md), read in part in [NOTE-1555](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1555.md) (the introduction, outline, definitions, Theorem 5.1 with proof and the conclusions). Proposed: the main proofs were not read. It is about deciding existence of a solution, for fixed finite languages on finite domains. It does not say anything about infinite domains, where the author shows CSPs can be undecidable, about quantified CSPs, or about the connectivity of the solution space. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1382](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1382.md) v2 | Bulatov shows that for every finite constraint language over a finite domain, deciding satisfiability is solvable in polynomial time when the language has a weak near-unanimity polymorphism, and with the hardness already known this makes every such problem polynomial-time solvable or NP-complete | Bulatov (2017), [LIT-2115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2115.md), read in part in [NOTE-1572](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1572.md) (§§1–2 and the opening of §3; the proofs not read). Proposed: the tractability algorithm and its 80 pages of proof were not checked. It concerns decision problems over a fixed finite language on a finite domain. It does not classify systems or single instances, and says nothing about infinite domains or about moving between solutions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1383](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1383.md) | Obayashi, Aoi, Tsuchiya and Kokubu explain the small, thin, fractal-like basin of attraction of the simplest passive walking model by the saddle-type instability of its upright equilibrium: pulled back through the swing phase, the set of states that take a step is thinned along the saddle's stable manifold and folded into a V with nested slits | Obayashi, Aoi, Tsuchiya and Kokubu (2016), [LIT-2110](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2110.md), read in [NOTE-1586](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1586.md), as a neighbour of McGeer (1990), [LIT-2108](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2108.md). Proposed: the figures were read by caption, and the mechanism is argued, not proved. It is about one idealised model; it does not say that every passive walker's basin is shaped this way, nor anything about McGeer's own walkers. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1384](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1384.md) | Erkut, Ingolfsson and Erdoğan show that locating ambulances to maximize expected cardiac-arrest survivors, rather than coverage within a time standard or average response time, saves more lives in deterministic models, with the advantage shrinking once random response times or ambulance busy probabilities enter the coverage model | Erkut, Ingolfsson and Erdoğan (2008), [LIT-2089](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2089.md), read in [NOTE-1556](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1556.md). Proposed: the comparisons are the paper's own, on one city's data, with survival functions for cardiac arrest assumed for all urgent calls and a non-optimal heuristic for the richest models. The account is about expected survivors under the authors' survival functions and evaluation model; it does not say coverage is useless, since by the paper's Table 6 coverage with either source of uncertainty reaches the best-known value. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1385](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1385.md) | Martinengo and colleagues find that spaced digital education for health professionals improves post-intervention knowledge more than massed digital education does, with a small effect, and promotes clinical behaviour change, while the evidence for spaced over massed digital simulation for skills rests on two studies of low certainty | Martinengo, Ng, Ng, Ang, Jabir, Kyaw & Tudor Car (2024), [LIT-2102](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2102.md), read in [NOTE-1610](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1610.md): 23 trials, immediate post-intervention outcomes. It does not say that spacing improves retention of skills over months, nor anything about long non-use; and for simulation the abstract and body give different pooled estimates (SMD 1.15 and 1.24). Proposed: one meta-analysis over studies mostly at unclear or high risk of bias. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1386](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1386.md) | A neural network trained only on the equilibrium and energy conditions of a truss model of conical Kresling origami recovers its energy curve and inverts it to geometries with prescribed stable heights and barrier, and stacks of such cells with ascending barriers fold in the designed order under compression | Kang, Kim, Yang and Ryu (2025), [LIT-2086](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2086.md), read in [NOTE-1619](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1619.md). Forward and inverse results are checked against a beam-truss FEA that shares the network's truss abstraction; the folding order is checked also in one scaled PET prototype, where barriers differ from prediction and are compared after normalizing to the bottom layer. It does not say the truss model captures the mechanics of real cells. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1387](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1387.md) | Asano shows that a passive rimless wheel's gravity-powered gait on a slope is asymptotically stable and period-1 because its impact posture and the energy gravity restores each step are fixed by geometry, so the return map's eigenvalue is cos²α, independent of the step period, and the gait exists only above a minimum slope tan²(α/2) | Asano (2012), [LIT-2050](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2050.md), read in [NOTE-1578](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1578.md), as a neighbour of McGeer (1990), [LIT-2108](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2108.md). Proposed: the derivations were read, not redone. The eigenvalue and the minimum slope come from a linearised stance phase. It is about the rimless wheel alone; it does not say that walkers with a swing leg are stable for the same reason, or where on steep slopes walking ends. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1391](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1391.md) | Rockafellar and Uryasev show that the conditional value-at-risk of a loss at level β equals the minimum over α of α + (1−β)⁻¹E[loss − α]⁺, so minimizing it over decisions is a joint minimization that also yields the value-at-risk, convex when the loss is convex in the decision and a linear program on sampled scenarios when the loss is linear | Rockafellar and Uryasev (2000), [LIT-2052](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2052.md), read in full in [NOTE-1623](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1623.md) from the authors' 1999 manuscript (Theorems 1 and 2 with their proofs, §3). Proposed until a second source states the same. It holds for loss distributions without atoms, at a fixed β, in one period; it says nothing about how large a sample the rare scenarios need, which the paper's own examples show can be large. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1393](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1393.md) | Abel and colleagues prove that a single-vertex crease pattern with a mountain–valley assignment folds rigidly from flat exactly when it contains a bird's foot, a same-parity tripod or cross together with one crease of the opposite parity | Abel, Cantarella, Demaine, Eppstein, Hull, Ku, Lang and Tachi (2016), [LIT-2093](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2093.md), read in full in [NOTE-1589](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1589.md) (arXiv v1). Proposed: the proofs were followed in one reading but not checked against the journal version or reproduced. It does not say anything about multi-vertex crease patterns, about folds far from flat, or about motions in which the paper passes through itself. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1397](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1397.md) | Coecke, Fritz and Spekkens propose that a resource theory is a symmetric monoidal category of resources and free transformations, that partitioning a process theory into free and costly processes generates such theories of states and of processes, and that the questions usually asked of a resource theory depend only on its preordered commutative monoid of convertibility, whose combination law can vary independently of its order | Coecke, Fritz & Spekkens (2014; Information and Computation 2016), [LIT-2032](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2032.md), read in [NOTE-1591](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1591.md) (main text; Examples 3.13–3.18 and Appendix A skimmed). Proposed: the appendix proof and the sketched lemmas were not checked. The morphisms of such a theory are free: it says nothing about costs attached to transformations, which the authors leave open as "epsilonification", and nothing about time, rates or a free set that changes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1399](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1399.md) v2 | Silverberg and colleagues show that the square-twist origami, whose crease pattern admits no rigid folding motion, folds by bending its facets, and that the ratio of bending to crease stiffness, together with the plane angle, sets a critical transition between monostable and bistable folding | Silverberg et al. (2015), [LIT-2100](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2100.md), read in [NOTE-1554](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1554.md) (the letter in full; SI pp. 1–2 skimmed). Proposed: one group's experiments on paper and gel with matching simulations, on a single unit cell. The general thesis that the number of degrees of freedom changes with the energy scale probed is the authors' framing; what was shown is this one structure. Tessellations are proposed, not tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1400](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1400.md) v2 | An array of non-volatile bistable origami switches laid out one module per minterm can be programmed to any combinational function of its inputs by a mobile actuator that sets the modules it passes, so programmability moves from rewiring into an addressing path that origami logic itself steers | Chen, Tan and Yan (2025), [LIT-2030](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2030.md), read in [NOTE-1559](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1559.md). Built and tested for 2- to 4-input arrays (half and full adder and subtractor, 2-bit adder or multiplier); generality to any function is by construction over pre-built minterm modules. It does not say that the device programs itself: the address path is fixed by a magnet layout designed outside it, and the robot runs on electric motors. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1402](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1402.md) | Akitaya, Demaine, Horiyama, Hull, Ku and Tachi prove that deciding whether a crease pattern can fold rigidly from flat is NP-hard: weakly when every crease must fold, and strongly when creases are optional | Akitaya et al. (2020), [LIT-2071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2071.md), read in [NOTE-1579](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1579.md) (model and main text in full, reduction gadgets skimmed). Proposed: the gadget constructions behind Theorems 15 and 16 were not checked line by line. It does not say that the problem is in NP in general, which is open, or anything about the mechanics of folding a real sheet. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1403](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1403.md) | Deng and colleagues show that a soft composite whose magnetic particles are held in a meltable polymer can have its magnetization pattern rewritten by local laser melting under a programming field and fixed again on cooling, so one film can be given many different shape responses to the same actuation field | Deng, Sattari, Xie, Liao, Yan and Lin (2020), [LIT-2034](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2034.md), read in [NOTE-1565](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1565.md), as a neighbour of Yeow, Yang and Ren (2024), [LIT-2113](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2113.md). Proposed: the figures were read by caption, and the supplement on cycling only by its caption. It does not say that the film can be rewritten in place without an external laser and field, nor anything about an actuator coupling to and decoupling from a separate structure. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1405](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1405.md) | Kinoshita and Ohsaki show that a bistable compliant truss mechanism, whose second stable state comes from snap-through stopped by contact with an obstacle, can be converted into a single-piece frame mechanism with the same function by optimizing thin pseudo-joints at its former pin joints under a strain cap, without lumping deformation into a point hinge | Kinoshita and Ohsaki (2009), [LIT-2029](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2029.md), read in full in [NOTE-1597](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1597.md). Proposed: the conversion is shown on one seven-node example, in simulation, with equivalence judged by overlaid force–displacement curves. It does not say that the frame is bistable without the obstacle, that the method finds frames without a truss to start from, or that a fabricated frame behaves as computed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1408](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1408.md) | Kane and Lubensky show that in isostatic lattices the number of zero modes in a region equals a local count of sites and bonds plus a topological count fixed by winding numbers of the bulk equilibrium matrix, so that gapped phases of different topological polarization carry protected floppy modes or states of self-stress at their boundaries and interfaces even where degrees of freedom and constraints locally balance | Kane and Lubensky (2014; arXiv 2013), [LIT-2078](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2078.md), read in full in [NOTE-1601](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1601.md), the supplementary proof included. Proposed: the theorem is proved and the two models agree with it; an independent case is what promotion asks. Chen et al. ([LIT-2049](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2049.md)), read in this batch, apply the topological polarization to an origami strip and to kirigami and are a candidate. It does not say that every boundary mode is topological, or that the linear zero modes extend to finite motions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1409](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1409.md) | Hull and Tachi show that the Miura-ori and Chicken Wire origami tessellations cannot be uniquely self-folded by crease-local driving forces, while generic quadrilateral tessellations rotationally symmetric about the midpoints of the tile's sides, which have only two folding modes, can be | Hull and Tachi (2018), [LIT-2033](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2033.md), read in full in [NOTE-1603](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1603.md) (arXiv v1). Proposed: the theorems were read with their proofs, which rest on the authors' 2016 criteria, not checked here. It does not say anything about stiffness, bending energy or noisy actuators, which the model leaves out, or about tessellations beyond monohedral quadrilateral ones. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1410](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1410.md) | Siemroth shows that when an agent privately knows its organization's spending needs and gains from spending above them, a principal who commits in advance does weakly better by letting the agent roll over some share of unused funds than none, effective only when the share exceeds the agent's marginal gain from misuse and sometimes best below full roll-over, while auditing only spending above a threshold under a punishment large enough that it is never imposed | Siemroth (SSRN 2021; IER 2024), [LIT-2103](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2103.md), read in [NOTE-1594](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1594.md) from the February 2022 working paper. Proposed: the results are the paper's propositions, whose proofs (in the appendix) were not read, and the version of record, which may differ, was not reached. Within the model they are stated for two periods, risk-neutral parties and uniform needs; the threshold audit holds in year 2 and in year 1 absent saving, an interval rule otherwise. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1411](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1411.md) v2 | Stern, Arinze, Perez, Palmer and Murugan show in simulation that a creased thin sheet trained by repeatedly folding it under example force patterns, with each crease softening when a supervisor judges the fold correct and stiffening otherwise, comes to fold unseen test force patterns into the correct class's structure, because the heterogeneous stiffness it acquires eliminates most folded structures and enlarges the basins of a few | Stern, Arinze, Perez, Palmer and Murugan (2020; arXiv 2019), [LIT-2116](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2116.md), read in [NOTE-1615](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1615.md) from the arXiv v1 preprint, titled differently; the PNAS text and the Supplementary Notes were not read. Proposed for that reason. It is a result about a model: it does not say that any physical sheet has been trained, that the sheet learns without an external supervisor, or that it scales beyond small two-class tasks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1415](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1415.md) v2 | A series stack of decoupled bistable Kresling barrels is a Preisach memory whose reachable states are fixed by the order of the switching thresholds, while hidden elastic degrees of freedom admit defect states that the loading protocol cannot reach and can leave only irreversibly | Jules, Reid, Daniels, Mungan and Lechenault (2022), [LIT-2072](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2072.md), read in [NOTE-1617](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1617.md). Shown in experiment on one four-barrel stack and its softer twin, with the Preisach graph confirmed and defect states found by twisting by hand. It does not say that the 64 counted states were all observed (39 of 48 single-defect states were), that the readout identifies every state, or that loading alone can create a defect in a decoupled stack. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1419](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1419.md) v2 | Damavandi, Hagh, Santangelo and Manning show that, for elastic energies quadratic in their constraints, constraint counting predicts energetic rigidity only when the system has no states of self-stress, and that when it has them the spectrum of the prestress matrix decides whether second-order rigidity implies energetic rigidity, with no general result when that matrix has negative eigenvalues | Damavandi, Hagh, Santangelo and Manning (2022; arXiv 2021), [LIT-2041](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2041.md), read in full in [NOTE-1570](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1570.md). Proposed: a single paper's derivations, with the hardest case left open by the authors. It does not say that a system with states of self-stress is never energetically rigid, nor that the shear modulus measures rigidity; and it covers Hookean energies only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1420](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1420.md) v3 | The sublevelset persistent homology of an energy landscape contains its disconnectivity graph as the zero-dimensional part and also records alternative transition paths and higher critical points, and for the alkane torsional landscape it has a closed form in every dimension | Mirth, Zhai, Bush, Alvarado, Jordan, Heim, Krishnamoorthy, Pflaum, Clark, Zhang and Adams (2021), [LIT-2047](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2047.md), read in [NOTE-1616](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1616.md), appendices with the full proofs skimmed. The first two parts are standard correspondences the paper states and illustrates; the closed form is its Theorems 1 and 2. It treats one scalar energy only: nothing here covers several resources at once, which would need multi-parameter persistence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1421](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1421.md) | Liebman and Mahoney hold that when an organization's budget expires at year-end and the value of its spending is uncertain, it holds a precautionary buffer through the year and spends it on low-value projects at the deadline, so that spending spikes and quality drops at year-end, and that letting unused funds roll over, given the budget-setter's commitment not to claw them back, removes most of the waste | Liebman and Mahoney (NBER 2013; AER 2017), [LIT-2028](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2028.md), read in [NOTE-1553](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1553.md). Proposed: the model derives the mechanism; the spike and the quality drop are shown in US federal procurement only, the quality drop on rated I.T. projects only; the rollover effect on volume rests on one agency's authority, its effect on quality on one project; and the title's most of the waste is a calibrated welfare share, not a measurement. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1425](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1425.md) | Rocks and colleagues show that in disordered spring networks a chosen linear strain response between a distant pair of target nodes and a pair of source nodes, and several such responses at once, can be produced with near-total success by removing about one percent of the bonds, chosen greedily with an analytic update built from the network's states of self-stress and compatible stress | Rocks, Pashine, Bischofberger, Goodrich, Liu and Nagel (2017; arXiv 2016), [LIT-2060](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2060.md), read in [NOTE-1607](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1607.md) from the arXiv v1 preprint; the PNAS text was not reached. Proposed for that reason and because the Supporting Information was not read. It is a linear, athermal result for central-force networks made rigid first: it does not say why the chosen bonds work, that the network could find them itself, or that allostery in proteins works this way. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1429](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1429.md) | Kuehn holds that a critical transition is the point where a slowly drifting system leaves an attracting, normally hyperbolic slow manifold for a fast jump, that fold, transcritical and subcritical Hopf and pitchfork bifurcations are such points while supercritical ones are not, and that the slowing down before them scales with the distance to the bifurcation with exponent ½ for the fold and 1 for the others | Kuehn (2011), [LIT-2048](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2048.md), read in [NOTE-1598](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1598.md) from the arXiv v2. Proposed: the propositions' proofs are short normal-form computations that were read but not redone here. It is about one slow variable and one-dimensional (planar for Hopf) fast normal forms; it does not say when the jump comes, which drift delays and noise can advance, nor that observed indicators reliably reveal the exponent. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1431](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1431.md) v2 | A multistable origami metamaterial driven by a fixed sequence of tension and compression can serve as the reservoir of a reservoir computer: a trained linear readout of its sequence of stable configurations classifies inputs better than the same readout of the raw inputs, and a retained buffer of cells carries input history | Liu, Fang, Xu and Wang (2023), [LIT-2026](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2026.md), read in [NOTE-1600](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1600.md). The comparison with the raw inputs (90.4% against 87.2% on binarized MNIST) and the memory result are simulations with a least-action model; the experiment covers ten 5×4-pixel digits on a 4×2-cell prototype. It does not say that the material learns: only the linear readout is trained. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1433](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1433.md) v2 | Krishnakumar and Suresh show that compliant mechanisms can be designed by topology optimization without pseudo-densities, by removing material where the topological derivative of a mutual-to-weighted-input-and-output strain-energy objective is lowest, which yields designs without point hinges and lets one parameter trade geometric against mechanical advantage | Krishnakumar and Suresh (2015), [LIT-2099](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2099.md), read in full in [NOTE-1582](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1582.md) from a lab-posted manuscript, as a stand-in for Sigmund (1997). Proposed: hinge-freedom is shown by pictures of a handful of coarse-mesh designs, and the η trade-off on one example. It is the authors' account of their own method, not of Sigmund's; it does not say that the designs stay hinge-free under stress constraints or large deformation, or that they were built. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1436](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1436.md) | Liu, Zhang and Fang show that an origami spring, modelled as a chain of one-degree-of-freedom cells by adding virtual creases, can be fitted to a range of 3D curves when its cells are grouped to share a few actuators, with fitting error falling as actuators are added and each added actuator gaining less | Liu, Zhang and Fang (2023), [LIT-2077](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2077.md), read in [NOTE-1558](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1558.md) (the main text; the supplement skipped). Proposed: the figures were read by caption and text, and the experimental comparisons are in the unread supplement. It is kinematic and about static shapes. It does not say how good the virtual-crease model is for a flexible spring, that the grouping found is optimal or unique, or anything about moving between shapes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1438](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1438.md) | Marras, Zhou, Su and Castro show that DNA origami joints made of stiff double-stranded bundles connected only by single-stranded scaffold restrict thermal motion to one designed degree of freedom whose range and stiffness are set by connection length, that a crank–slider and a Bennett linkage assembled from such joints follow their rigid-body motion paths, and that the Bennett linkage, rarely found unaided in its higher-energy compacted state, is held there by added bridging strands and released by toehold-mediated strand displacement, each move taking about a minute | Marras, Zhou, Su and Castro (2015), [LIT-2118](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2118.md), read in [NOTE-1635](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1635.md) (main text and figure captions; the Supporting Information unread). Proposed: the conformational statistics are negative-stain TEM fractions on a surface, which the authors call upper bounds, over 52 to 918 particles with misfolds excluded, and one actuation cycle is reported. It does not say that the mechanisms fold with high yield, that switching survives repeated cycles, or that the grid fractions are those in solution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1439](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1439.md) | Dunn and colleagues show that a DNA origami template with several approximately degenerate well-folded shapes can be annealed to different distributions of those shapes by changing only which staples stabilize intermediates: weakening the cooperative long-range seam staples shifts the products strongly toward the fold that short-range staples favour, and strengthening short-range staples suppresses the fold in which one of them must bridge long range, while in their kinetic model strong early seam contacts trap about half of folding runs | Dunn, Dannenberg, Ouldridge, Kwiatkowska, Turberfield and Bath (2015), [LIT-2135](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2135.md), read in [NOTE-1643](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1643.md). The shift is shown by AFM shape counts on one tile, one anneal ramp and one buffer, with 36-62% of candidate objects fitted; the trapping figure (52% misfolds with full seams, 1% with broken ones) is the model's. The equal stability of the final folds is the authors' design argument, not a measurement, and the model is not thermodynamically self-consistent. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1459](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1459.md) | The source of a state's revenue shapes its capacity and accountability: revenue earned by taxing citizens obliges the state to build a bureaucracy, stay present on the ground and bargain with taxpayers, while unearned income from natural-resource rents or aid does not, and lets those capacities decay | Moore (2004), [LIT-2182](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2182.md), read in [NOTE-1663](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1663.md): the fiscal (social) contract proposition and its rentier-state converse, with aid counted as a strategic rent, and the further point that easy concessional finance turns governments from negotiating with taxpayers. Proposed: a review that argues from European history and others' cross-national evidence, convincing for oil and, by the author's own account, weak and possibly reverse-caused for aid. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1460](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1460.md) | Large aid sustained over decades can weaken a recipient state's institutions: it substitutes for taxation, grants and not loans going with lower revenue, and it decouples the state's revenue from its performance, weakening its accountability to citizens | Moss, Pettersson & van de Walle (2006), [LIT-2144](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2144.md), read in [NOTE-1661](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1661.md): a review of the tax-effort and state-building literatures. Besides the two mechanisms in the title they name a third, fragmented donor practice drawing capacity from the civil service, and hold that a state becomes self-sufficient by learning to tax. Proposed: the authors call the aid–revenue evidence negative on balance but "not a conclusive result", and their own analysis is bivariate. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1475](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1475.md) | On Mauss's comparative account, gifts in archaic societies are voluntary in form but obligatory to give, to receive and to return. In Maori law the return is compelled by the hau of the thing given, which seeks its origin through every holder. In the Northwest-coast potlatch a gift accepted without a return, or without a larger one, costs the receiver face, rank and in the limit his freedom (debt slavery). Mauss holds that the same morality survives in modern societies, where an unreturned gift still makes its acceptor inferior and charity wounds. He argues that social insurance is right as a return owed to the worker for labour already given, beside a duty to rely on oneself. | Mauss (1925), [LIT-2191](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2191.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1658](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1658.md) with the introduction, chapter I, the Northwest-coast section and the conclusion read in full. Proposed: the ethnographic half is Mauss's reading of others' fieldwork, and the hau half rests on one informant's text in a translation Mauss calls abridged; the modern half is moral and political argument. It does not say that an unconditional gift exists, that reciprocity needs lost capability, or anything about aid. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1476](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1476.md) | LaVoice finds that, among similarly blighted census tracts in 28 large US cities, black neighbourhoods were two to three times as likely to be cleared under Title I of the Housing Act of 1949, that cleared tracts kept about 12–13% lower population and housing density and a 16% lower black share for decades with rents up about a quarter, and, because rents in uncleared low-income tracts rose with them, reads a spatial-equilibrium model as showing the lowest-income households city-wide made worse off | LaVoice (2024), [LIT-2142](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2142.md), read from a 24-page 2021 draft in [NOTE-1680](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1680.md), not from the version of record. Proposed: the draft defers its complete results to the full paper; its income gain is given as 18% and as 16% without reconciliation, so no income figure is asserted here; controls are slums in other cities, with black-share pre-trends that differ; and the welfare result is the model's, not a measurement. It does not track the displaced or measure the social ties the clearances broke. It complements the city-level [THEORY-1470](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1470.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1477](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1477.md) v2 | Planted tree nuclei facilitate forest recovery because, once established, they keep attracting seed dispersers and improving microsites, whereas bird perches and bat boxes leave no improved conditions and decay within years; nuclei must also spread, which is slow, unpredictable and rarely measured, and in tropical moist forest a nucleus needs about 64 m² to attract birds and shade out grass | Holl, Reid, Zahawi, de Siqueira & Brancalion (2024), [LIT-2172](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2172.md), read in [NOTE-1676](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1676.md): an opinion article by the senior author of the unread Corbin & Holl (2012), [LIT-2179](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2179.md), read as its stand-in for mechanism and nucleus size. A planted tree is support that becomes the capacity; a perch stands in for that capacity and then rots. Proposed: the article argues from the literature rather than showing data, its 64 m² minimum is cited from Zahawi & Augspurger (2006) and Holl et al. (2020), and it says itself that spread is rarely measured. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1483](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1483.md) | In Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's model, where the cost of taxing falls with depreciating revenue-collecting experience and grant aid fills the fiscal gap, aid that ignores this learning drives a country whose initial institutions are weaker than a threshold to aid financing the whole budget and the loss of its tax capacity, while one with stronger institutions converges to a low-aid state; a planner who internalizes the learning still has a stable high-aid, low-capacity equilibrium beside the efficient saddle path, which is reached only by an up-front cut in aid | Azam, Devarajan & O'Connell (1999), [LIT-2156](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2156.md), read in full in [NOTE-1682](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1682.md). Proposed: the derivation of the dynamics and of the steady-state roots was rechecked symbolically for this reading, but the stability of the two points and the myopic threshold rest on the paper's phase diagrams, which were not re-derived. It is a model with unit slopes, tax inefficiency the reciprocal of experience and fixed spending; it says nothing measured about any country. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1500](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1500.md) | Temporal dissipative solitons in a continuously pumped Kerr microresonator, held by the pump against cavity loss, exist only in a window of normalized detuning between √3 and π²f²/8, form spontaneously from noise-seeded modulation when the pump laser is swept from the upper onto the lower branch of the Kerr-bistable resonance, show as discrete steps in transmission, one per soliton number, whose number varied between simulated scans with the random seeding, and persist with a shape fixed by resonator and pump until the pump is switched off or the detuning is pushed beyond the small thermal triangles | Herr, Brasch, Jost, Wang, Kondratiev, Gorodetsky and Kippenberg (2014), [LIT-2204](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2204.md), read in [NOTE-1692](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1692.md) from arXiv v3; experiment in one MgF2 resonator, simulation of the coupled-mode (Lugiato-Lefever) equations without thermal effects, and approximate analytics. Proposed: the window rests on an infinite-domain analysis the record has not read, and the equations were read from a page image because extraction drops square roots. It does not say that formation shows hysteresis (no reverse sweep is reported), how fast a soliton vanishes after switch-off (not measured), or how the number of solitons varies between experimental runs (reported for simulations only). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1501](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1501.md) | In a conservative system a soliton is a solitary wave, held by a balance between nonlinearity and dispersion, that keeps its shape at constant speed and emerges from a collision with another soliton with its amplitude, shape and velocity unchanged except for a phase shift; the name and the numerical discovery come from Zabusky and Kruskal's 1965 solutions of the KdV equation, in which solitons arose from a sine-wave initial condition | Zabusky & Porter (2010), [LIT-2208](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2208.md), read in full in [NOTE-1689](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1689.md), an encyclopedia article by the co-author of the 1965 letter. Filed as the read neighbour of Zabusky & Kruskal (1965), which was not reached. The definition is the article's, after Scott (2005); the collision property is illustrated by the article's own simulation, not proved there; the history is Zabusky's later account of his own work. It holds for integrable equations: the article says the relatives do not in general share the interaction property. The wording is the filer's, from the reader's report; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1506](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1506.md) | In a spherically symmetric real scalar field with a double-well potential in 3+1 dimensions, subcritical bubbles with energy above a plateau value, core field beyond the inflection point and initial radius in a window shed part of their energy and settle into oscillons of nearly constant energy and radius whatever their initial radius, which radiate almost nothing for 10^3 to 10^4 m^-1, against about 5 to 10 m^-1 in the linear theory, and then decay quickly once slow radiation has lowered the core amplitude below the value at which its fluctuations stop being unstable; no topological invariant or conserved charge protects them | Copeland, Gleiser & Müller (1995), [LIT-2200](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2200.md), read in full in [NOTE-1699](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1699.md). Shown by numerical simulation, with a one-degree-of-freedom Gaussian ansatz explaining the lower radius bound and the end; spherical symmetry throughout, stability tested only against radial perturbations. It does not explain the upper radius bound, give an analytic lifetime, or define the plateau's endpoints formally. The wording of the title is the reader's condensation of the paper's §§III–IV and VII. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1507](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1507.md) v2 | A configuration of finite energy must approach a vacuum at spatial infinity, and the map from the boundary into the vacua falls into homotopy classes that cannot be continuously deformed into one another, so the space of configurations splits into sectors labelled by a topological charge measured at the boundary; the energy, action or tension in a sector is bounded below by that charge and the soliton saturates the bound, and a kink, which interpolates between distinct vacua at its two ends, has its charge fixed by that boundary data | Tong (2005), [LIT-2207](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2207.md), read in NOTE-1694 for the topological charge and the kinks (§1.1, §2.1, §§3.1–3.2, §3.8.3, §§4.1–4.3.2). Standard topological soliton theory, stated by Tong for instantons, monopoles, vortices and domain walls in gauge theories. The thesis that a topological soliton cannot decay except by annihilation with an opposite charge or by a change at the boundary is the reader's inference from these points, not Tong's statement, and is not part of this account. A neighbour of Copeland, Gleiser & Müller (1995), [LIT-2200](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2200.md), for the protection oscillons lack. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1509](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1509.md) v2 | A soliton of an integrable wave equation under weak loss does not break up but shrinks along its family of shapes at a rate set by energy balance, exponentially under linear damping and algebraically under viscous, Landau, boundary-layer and friction losses, while a shelf of non-soliton wave forms behind it wherever the loss does not conserve mass | Grimshaw, Smyth & Stepanyants (2018), [LIT-2198](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2198.md), read in full in [NOTE-1687](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1687.md), for the Benjamin–Ono equation with six kinds of weak loss, by first-order adiabatic theory checked against direct numerics. Filed as the read neighbour of Kivshar & Malomed (1989), whose central method for damped solitons it carries in one equation. The KdV laws, which make the title's "integrable wave equation" more than one case, are quoted in the paper from earlier work, not derived, and so are not shown here. It says nothing of NLS, of gain or supply, or of strong loss. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1524](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1524.md) | When external funding and legitimacy are granted for adopting the forms of capable states (best-practice laws, agencies and procedures) rather than for demonstrated performance, recipient organizations engage in isomorphic mimicry, producing a capability trap in which state capability stagnates or declines while reform and aid continue, and it is escaped by locally defined problem-solving through authorized experimentation, tight feedback and broad engagement (PDIA) | The thesis the authors assert, split from [THEORY-1481](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1481.md) when the twenty-fifth status review promoted the report of their argument ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1481](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1481.md) holds that they argue it; whether it is true is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1481](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1481.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1525](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1525.md) | Many low-capability states, at their measured pace of improvement, would take centuries to millennia to reach high state capability, and the persistence is sustained by two techniques: isomorphic mimicry, keeping legitimacy by imitating the forms of functional organizations without their function, and premature load bearing, loading fledgling organizations with tasks too complex too soon | The thesis the authors assert, split from [THEORY-1463](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1463.md) when the twenty-fifth status review promoted the report of their argument ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1463](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1463.md) holds that they argue it; whether it is true is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1463](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1463.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1526](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1526.md) | Near the flat state a non-intersecting rigid origami vertex with small positive Gaussian curvature has a configuration space split into two components (popped up and popped down) that no rigid, non-tearing motion joins, while for small negative curvature the two are joined by a neck, except at degree four | The thesis Berry, Lee-Trimble and Santangelo (2020), [LIT-2024](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2024.md), assert, filed beside [THEORY-1423](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1423.md), the Active report that they find it, at the twenty-fifth status review ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). It keeps [THEORY-1423](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1423.md)'s old condition word for word. The authors call the quadratic-order proof "somewhat involved" and confirm it numerically on one symmetric 5-fold vertex. The inherited condition does not name degree four, which the title excepts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1527](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1527.md) v2 | Every endomorphism in Marsden and Zwart's categories of quantale-enriched profunctors generates a free internal monad, its reflexive–transitive closure (Proposition 37, Corollary 38) | The closure result of Marsden & Zwart (CSL 2018), [LIT-2054](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2054.md), read in full in [NOTE-1602](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1602.md), whose proofs the paper sketches. Split from [THEORY-1435](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1435.md) by the status review of 2026-11-06 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1, [ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3): that entry reports the proposal and is Active; this one asserts the result and keeps the old condition word for word. A re-derivation of Proposition 37 for Q-profunctors is below, awaiting a second checker ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §5); Corollary 38's wider scope is not re-derived. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1528](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1528.md) | Crease patterns designed with one folding motion inevitably have exponentially many distractor branches meeting at the flat state, created by frustrated loops of two-branch vertices, and the spatial placement of actuators, read through the cover of their folding islands, predicts folding success better than their number | The generalization Stern, Pinson & Murugan (2017), [LIT-2074](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2074.md), read in [NOTE-1571](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1571.md), assert: in their abstract, that "even crease patterns with only one designed folding motion inevitably contain an exponential number of ‘distractor’ folding branches", and in their results, that the union of folding islands is "a much better predictor of folding success than just the number of actuators". Split from [THEORY-1418](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1418.md) at its narrowing by the status review of 2026-11-06 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1), keeping its old promote_when. One study: idealized rigid panels, zero-temperature descent, meshes up to 6 × 6, actuation on one 4 × 4 pattern. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1529](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1529.md) | Human cooperation is readily sustained between individuals, above all in dyads, through precise reciprocity, empathy and a partner who cannot be excluded at no cost, and is fragile between groups: categorization alone yields mistrust and in-group favouritism by bounded reciprocity, observed out-group favouritism hardens it into distrust, and chiefly negative interdependence, real or perceived, turns that into costly competition, aggression and hate, so that the processes that build in-group cooperation can fuel intergroup conflict | The thesis Van Lange and Bergmann (2026), [LIT-2002](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2002.md), propose, filed beside the Active report [THEORY-1352](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1352.md) by the twenty-seventh status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md), [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). Assembled from the authors' selection of laboratory and field work, with no new data and no pooled effect sizes; the stages are not tested together. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1530](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1530.md) | Attention is prioritization of processing by a subject that is the whole collection of an organism's fixed, formed and fluid interests, separated from filtering by whether selection answers to that collection, marked by feedback from dorsolateral prefrontal cortex; when interests are equally weighted, attention breaks the stalemate and updates the chosen option's value, so that a fluid interest becomes a formed one | The account Jennings (2026), [LIT-1963](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1963.md), proposes, filed beside the Active report [THEORY-1341](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1341.md) by the twenty-seventh status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md), [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). The criterion is inferred, not tested, and the stalemate mechanism is taken from one model, Voigt 2022. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1532](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1532.md) | A flat triangulated rigid origami sits at a singular point of its configuration space where generically 2^Vi folding branches meet, one pair for each pattern of vertex popping states, so folding from flat is exponentially ambiguous | The generalization Chen and Santangelo (2018), [LIT-2021](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2021.md), assert from numerics, split from [THEORY-1427](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1427.md) when the twenty-seventh status review narrowed that reading to what was computed and proven ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1, [ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md)). Proven only for Henneberg-1 triangulations, a vanishing fraction of all. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1533](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1533.md) | Affect is the felt transition of a body's power to affect and be affected toward a diminished or augmented capacitation | The wide form of [THEORY-1282](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1282.md), kept when the twenty-seventh status review promoted that entry as a report ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1): Massumi's account of affect taken as true, not as reported. He offers it as a proposition, after Spinoza and Deleuze, with no evidence, and refuses its use as a criterion; whether it picks out anything an account of emotion or appraisal does not is open. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1534](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1534.md) v2 | In Simondon's ontology, information is not a signal transmitted between finished entities but a disparity between two differently ordered domains of a metastable system, and its meaning is the new structure that transduction produces in resolving it | The wide form of the reading in [THEORY-1276](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1276.md), kept when the twenty-seventh status review promoted that entry as a report ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). Iliadis (2013) and Bencherki & Iliadis (2021) assert that this is Simondon's view. Whether it is turns on his own text, which the record holds only as Unavailable ([LIT-1648](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1648.md), [LIT-1900](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1900.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1536](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1536.md) | Readiness to come off invasive ventilation is tested by withdrawing support for a spontaneous breathing trial of 30 to 120 minutes, since predictors of readiness have low power; patients are classed as simple, difficult or prolonged weaning by whether the first attempt succeeds and, if not, whether up to three trials or seven days suffice; and outcomes worsen across these groups, about half of patients whose weaning fails remaining on invasive ventilation at one year | The thesis the source asserts, split from [THEORY-1515](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1515.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1515](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1515.md) holds that the authors assert it; whether it is true is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1515](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1515.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1537](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1537.md) | Mechanical ventilation harms the diaphragm at both ends of effort, atrophy following low effort from over-assistance or sedation and injury possibly following excessive effort, so that ventilation and sedation should be titrated to keep an effort close to that of quiet breathing; that support proportional to the patient's own neural drive makes disuse from over-assistance unlikely, since assist falls as diaphragm activity falls | The thesis the source asserts, split from [THEORY-1514](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1514.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1514](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1514.md) holds that the authors assert it; whether it is true is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1514](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1514.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1538](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1538.md) | Supplying individuals by translocation while the habitat threat persists gives only ambiguous or transitory gains and perpetuates conservation reliance, which can fall below a reliance threshold only if extrinsic threats and intrinsic small-population limits are relieved together | The thesis Mussmann and colleagues (2017), [LIT-2183](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2183.md), assert, split from [THEORY-1467](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1467.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of their argument ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1467](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1467.md) holds that they argue it; whether it is true is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1467](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1467.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1539](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1539.md) | Poverty causes stress and negative affect, and these in turn make people more present-biased and risk-averse independent of credit constraints and background risk, so that behaviour taken as the poor's own preference may partly be an effect of poverty and may help perpetuate it | The thesis Haushofer and Fehr (2014), [LIT-2152](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2152.md), assert, split from [THEORY-1462](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1462.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of their account ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1462](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1462.md) holds that they hold it; whether it is true outside the laboratory is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1462](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1462.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1540](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1540.md) | Without perpetual active management of invasive plants, predators and water levels in Hawai'i's wetlands, the endangered Coot, Stilt and Gallinule would decline | The thesis the authors assert, split from [THEORY-1489](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1489.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of their findings ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1489](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1489.md) holds that they report the trends and hold this; whether it is true is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1489](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1489.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1541](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1541.md) | Fully controlled mechanical ventilation weakens, shrinks and injures the human diaphragm as it does in animals: biopsies from brain-dead organ donors ventilated for hours to days show diaphragm fibre atrophy and injury with oxidative stress and raised proteolysis markers, not seen in the pectoralis, the changes growing with the duration of ventilation, and diaphragm twitch pressure in ventilated patients falls by about a third in six days; in animals, keeping spontaneous effort lessens the loss but leaves a residual deficit | The thesis the source asserts, split from [THEORY-1511](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1511.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1511](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1511.md) holds that the authors assert it; whether it is true is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1511](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1511.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1542](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1542.md) | Restoring the pressure-free conditions of a degraded ecosystem can fail because the degraded phase leaves a reinforcing legacy of its own, such as hardwoods that stop fire spreading, sludge that favours a floating competitor, or eroded beaver sites, so recovery needs direct biotic manipulation, by removal or by reintroduction in the right order, besides abiotic restoration | The thesis Kadowaki and colleagues (2018), [LIT-2165](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2165.md), assert, split from [THEORY-1468](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1468.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of their account ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1468](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1468.md) holds that it is their account; whether the cases they cite bear it out is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1468](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1468.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1543](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1543.md) | A firm's ability to recognize, assimilate and apply outside knowledge rests on its prior related knowledge, built largely as a byproduct of its own R&D and not quickly bought, and because this capacity accumulates and shapes what the firm expects of a field, a firm that stops investing in a fast-moving field may be locked out of it even after major advances | The thesis the source asserts, split from [THEORY-1518](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1518.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1518](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1518.md) holds that the authors assert it; whether it is true is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1518](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1518.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1544](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1544.md) | Where degradation has built biotic–abiotic feedbacks that hold the degraded state, such as invader-driven fire and nitrogen cycles, herbivory on regenerating plants, lost seed sources or bare soil that sheds rain, restoring the historical disturbance regime or abiotic conditions does not return the community; restoration must first disrupt those feedbacks or move the state directly, often by several actions together, before restored conditions suffice | The thesis Suding, Gross and Houseman (2004), [LIT-2169](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2169.md), assert, split from [THEORY-1510](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1510.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1510](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1510.md) holds that they assert it; whether it is true is this entry's question. [THEORY-1510](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1510.md)'s old condition asked only for a second reader of the paper, so this entry's condition is new, drafted at that review: the authors concede that rigorous tests of alternative stable states are beyond most restoration efforts, and [THEORY-136](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-136.md)'s bar applies. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1545](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1545.md) | When automation performs a subtask while the operator goes on doing the task, the operator's skill at that subtask decays from disuse, the cognitive part more than the procedural part, and out of the operator's awareness, because the task itself is still done and still succeeds | The thesis the source asserts, split from [THEORY-1521](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1521.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1521](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1521.md) holds that the authors assert it; whether it is true is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1521](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1521.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1546](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1546.md) | Burning Man's gifting carries no obligation on the recipient to reciprocate, yet sustains circulation through gratitude that recipients return to the community in later labour, a generalized rather than bilateral reciprocity; non-participation is the most pressing threat to it, and the organization answered it in part by reforming how theme camps are registered and placed | The thesis St John asserts, split from [THEORY-1497](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1497.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of his account ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1497](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1497.md) holds that he holds it; whether it is true is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1497](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1497.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
