| [THEORY-1547](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1547.md) | Instruction faces an assistance dilemma, help given buying accuracy and efficiency at the cost of shallow processing and help withheld buying generation and memory engagement at the cost of floundering, and within tutored problem solving, where the learner does the steps and help is added only on failure, more help does better than less, support should shift from worked examples toward problems and as-needed hints as competence grows, and learners left to ask for help ask badly | The thesis the source asserts, split from [THEORY-1520](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1520.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1520](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1520.md) holds that the authors assert it; whether it is true is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1520](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1520.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1548](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1548.md) | A dissipative soliton differs from a conservative one in being a single attractor rather than a member of a continuous family: a conservative soliton balances nonlinearity against dispersion alone, with its parameters selected by the initial data, whereas a dissipative soliton also needs an exact balance of gain and loss, kept by a continuous energy exchange with the environment and an internal flow from regions that gain energy to regions that lose it, so that its energy, profile and chirp are fixed by the system's parameters, not by its initial conditions; such solitons can bind into robust molecules whose energy scales with the number of constituents | The thesis the source asserts, split from [THEORY-1504](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1504.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1504](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1504.md) holds that the authors assert it; whether it is true is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1504](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1504.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1549](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1549.md) | Exogenous glucocorticoids at anti-inflammatory doses invariably suppress the HPA axis by negative feedback and prolonged use leads to pituitary hyporesponsiveness and adrenal atrophy; after withdrawal the axis recovers first centrally and then adrenally, over months to years and incompletely in a minority; courses under 3–4 weeks can be stopped without taper, while longer ones are tapered, once the disease is controlled, quickly at high doses and slowly near the physiologic dose, with replacement kept low enough to leave a stimulus for recovery; and no study has compared taper schemes | The thesis the source asserts, split from [THEORY-1516](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1516.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1516](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1516.md) holds that the authors assert it; whether it is true is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1516](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1516.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1550](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1550.md) | An international gift its recipient cannot repay leaves the recipient inferior and the relation resentful, and circular (kula-like) reciprocity that lets the recipient give back is the better design for aid between nations | The thesis Heins, Unrau and Avram (2018), [LIT-2178](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2178.md), carry from Mauss and Dillon, split from [THEORY-1474](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1474.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1474](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1474.md) holds that they hold and report it; whether it is true is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1474](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1474.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1551](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1551.md) | Bainbridge's ironies of automation hold that automation takes the routine work and leaves the operator the atypical cases, recalls the operator at its failure, when the system is least predictable, and leaves the operator's manual and cognitive skills degraded from disuse | The reading of Bainbridge (1983) that Ahn (2025), [LIT-2222](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2222.md), asserts, split from [THEORY-1522](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1522.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1522](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1522.md) holds that Ahn reads her so; whether she says it turns on her text, which the record holds only as Unavailable ([LIT-2225](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2225.md)), under the condition [THEORY-1522](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1522.md) carried, word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1552](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1552.md) | Ventilation can be withdrawn abruptly in about three quarters of patients whose cause of respiratory failure has improved, readiness being tested by a trial of unassisted breathing on T-tube or low pressure support, for 30 or 120 minutes alike, and immediate extubation after a passed trial shortening ventilation compared with gradual withdrawal; and the patients who fail need gradual withdrawal while the causes are corrected, where SIMV was the least efficient method in both of the randomized trials of the 1990s and once-daily T-tube trials or reductions of pressure support did better | The thesis the source asserts, split from [THEORY-1512](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1512.md) when the twenty-eighth status review promoted the report of it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-1512](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1512.md) holds that the authors assert it; whether it is true is this entry's question, under the condition [THEORY-1512](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1512.md) carried, word for word. The source contradicts itself on SIMV: its abstract calls it the most effective method after failed trials, its body and conclusion the least; this entry follows the body. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1553](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1553.md) | Generative AI assistants make easy tasks easier and hard tasks harder for their users, leaving the user the hard share of the work with the added task of evaluating the system's output | The wider thesis Simkute, Tankelevitch et al. (2024), [LIT-2223](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2223.md), assert: "GenAI user studies suggest that current systems make easy tasks easier and hard tasks harder for users" (§3.5; also §1). Filed when the twenty-ninth status review narrowed [THEORY-1519](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1519.md) to the report, under [ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) and [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1; the condition is [THEORY-1519](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1519.md)'s old one, word for word. Its evidence is the programming studies the paper cites, chiefly Vaithilingam et al. (2022) and Barke et al., with single studies in data science and law; the paper runs none. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1554](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1554.md) | For a rigid stage held in parallel by ideal wire-like flexures under small motions, the motions the stage permits and the lines along which a constraint can be added without changing them determine each other uniquely as reciprocal screw spaces, and for pure-force constraints these pairs fall into 26 types indexed by the number of non-redundant constraints | What Hopkins (2007) holds ([THEORY-1406](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1406.md)), stated as true. The thesis says "it was proven that these spaces embody all possible solutions" (abstract). Its uniqueness argument is by example, though it follows from screw reciprocity; finiteness is "suggested" by the six-constraint bound; and the 26 come from a case analysis (chs. 7–8). Proposed until an independent derivation or classification confirms them. The uniqueness half is close to standard linear algebra and might be split off as demonstrated, if a reviewer writes it out. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1555](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1555.md) | For a real scalar field with an analytic potential, every localized oscillating state except the 1+1 dimensional sine-Gordon breather radiates, at a rate exponentially small in its amplitude parameter but nonzero; in 3+1 dimensions such oscillons are stable only above a minimum amplitude and decay suddenly once radiation has carried them below it, after a few thousand oscillations at most, while in 1 and 2 dimensions the loss rate falls exponentially as the amplitude falls and they never decay | Fodor (2019), [LIT-2197](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2197.md), asserts this in Ch. 1 and at the opening of §2.7: "For a real scalar field, apart from the 1 + 1 dimensional sine-Gordon breather, there is no exactly time-periodic oscillating finite energy spatially localized configuration", and 3+1 oscillons "suddenly decay after a few thousand oscillations, at most". What the review derives is [THEORY-1502](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1502.md), which this extends. Filed by the twenty-ninth status review as the wider thesis of [THEORY-1502](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1502.md)'s old title ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md), kind 1), with the old title and condition word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1556](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1556.md) | All freedom–constraint space pairs of a flexure-guided rigid body fall into 50 types, only those whose constraint space holds enough pure-force lines can be realised by parallel flexures while the rest need modules stacked in series, and where linear actuators must act to drive the permitted motions without parasitic error is set by the flexures' stiffness and not by the freedom space alone | What Hopkins (2010) holds ([THEORY-1390](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1390.md)), stated as true. The thesis offers its chart as "a comprehensive classification of screw systems" (§2.1), derives it by a case analysis (Appendix A) that defers to the master's thesis for the 2-DOF column and the column symmetry, and does not compare it type by type with Gibson and Hunt's or Rico and Duffy's classifications. The actuation theory has one bench experiment, whose measured errors were much larger than predicted, and the thesis states that placement is computed from stiffness without saying that the freedom space alone leaves it open. Proposed until an independent classification and a second test exist. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1557](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1557.md) | Foschi, Hull and Ku hold that the two folding modes of a degree-4 rigid origami vertex whose sector angles do not sum to 2π are disconnected, because such a vertex has no state with every folding angle zero | The wide form of Foschi, Hull and Ku (2022), [LIT-2055](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2055.md), kept here when the thirtieth status review narrowed [THEORY-1381](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1381.md) to what the paper derives and promoted it ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). The paper asserts it in §V B from one worked example (Example 1), with no theorem and no stated convention for folding angles at ±π. Read in full in [NOTE-1606](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1606.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1558](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1558.md) v2 | In hierarchically organized systems, levels are demarcated by sharp discontinuities in characteristic process and relaxation rates, the embedding level being slower than its components, and a level controls another by constraint only while their rates stay separated: when the cycling rates converge, the control asymmetry and the distinction between the levels are lost, whatever the signal amplitude | Juarrero (2023), [LIT-1995](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1995.md), ch. 12, read in [NOTE-1532](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1532.md); the thesis the book asserts and [THEORY-1306](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1306.md) reports. The book asserts it: a lack of asymmetry in cycling rates "reflects the absence of control constraint by one on the other, regardless of signal amplitude" (p. 190). Proposed: the book has no model, and the loss of control when rates converge is asserted with institutional and oncological examples, not shown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1559](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1559.md) | Training forms a task-defined, low-dimensional subregion of prefrontal and premotor population activity (a preparatory subspace, an axis of choice organized as a line attractor) that constrains a monkey's delayed response top down, holding behavior to what the task requires while the trial's cue and evidence select within it | Juarrero (2023), [LIT-1995](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1995.md), ch. 15, read in [NOTE-1532](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1532.md); the thesis the book asserts and [THEORY-1340](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1340.md) reports. Proposed: the evidence the chapter reports is dimensionality reduction, prediction and a network simulation, with no intervention on the pattern. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1560](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1560.md) | Thompson describes a compiler binary that miscompiles the login command to accept a known password and reinserts that Trojan horse, and itself, whenever the compiler is compiled, so that it persists after every source has been cleaned, and concludes that no source-level verification protects a user from code they did not create | Thompson's Turing lecture ([NOTE-1715](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1715.md)). A mechanism installed once in a binary is reproduced by the host's own compiling and lives in no source. It bears on [QUESTION-449](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-449.md): an installed mechanism the host reproduces, whose author the lecture holds responsible ("trust the people who wrote the software"). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1561](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1561.md) | Stute tells, as his own experience, a departed graduate student's compiler Trojan horse that restored a program's hateful subliminal messages on every compile and restored itself when the compiler was rebuilt from clean source, removed only by installing a compiler binary from another machine | An anecdote of Thompson's attack ([THEORY-1560](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1560.md)) met in practice, held as [CASE-232](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-232.md) ([NOTE-1714](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1714.md)). | [THEORY-1631](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1631.md) | Sturesteps reports that in 440 Australian adults having a mode of symbolic immortality in one's life, such as children, predicted accepting it as consolation in imagined terminal illness, that accepting the biological, creative and nature modes went with accepting death as final, and that the modes predicted death anxiety and personality only weakly | Sturesteps (1992), [LIT-1689](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1689.md), an ANU master's thesis skimmed in [NOTE-1312](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1312.md) in place of Lifton (1979, [LIT-1714](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1714.md)). Cross-sectional; Rank's sex-difference and neuroticism hypotheses failed. The copy limits copying, so almost nothing is quoted. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1636](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1636.md) | Kiczales, des Rivières and Bobrow specify a metaobject protocol that describes CLOS as an extensible CLOS program, so that users can change the language's behaviour by specializing its metaobjects, within explicit restrictions that preserve implementors' freedom | The account of chapter 5 of [LIT-2335](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2335.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1718](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1718.md) from a community hypertext the owner ruled usable. | [THEORY-1638](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1638.md) | Chen, Kuo, Liu, Poon, Towey, Tse and Zhou hold that metamorphic testing alleviates but cannot solve the test-oracle problem: a program is checked against metamorphic relations, necessary properties relating two or more inputs and their outputs, so a violation shows a fault while satisfying them does not show correctness | The central account of [LIT-2333](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2333.md), read in [NOTE-1717](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1717.md) from the authors' manuscript. It is the account the exchange "luria experiment design" leaned on, at A50 §11, when it proposed metamorphic relations as the hidden scorer of a change to a record's schema, and it carries the limit that use has: such a scorer can find a wrong change but cannot certify a right one. Proposed until checked against the published version. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1639](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1639.md) | An image-prompt adapter of about 22M parameters, trained once against a frozen Stable Diffusion v1.5, matches fully fine-tuned image-prompt models on COCO alignment metrics and can be reused without retraining on models fine-tuned from the same base, but by its authors' account does not keep a given subject's identity as Textual Inversion and DreamBooth do | Hu Ye, Jun Zhang, Sibo Liu, Xiao Han and Wei Yang (2023), [LIT-2342](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2342.md), read in [NOTE-1722](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1722.md). arXiv preprint (v1, the only version; no venue on the arXiv record). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1640](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1640.md) | Adapting a large pretrained Transformer by freezing its weights and training only a low-rank additive update to selected weight matrices matches full fine-tuning on the language benchmarks reported, stores about 10,000 times less per task on GPT-3, adds no inference latency once the update is merged, and yields an update that amplifies directions already present, but not emphasized, in the specific pretrained weights it modifies | Edward J. Hu, Yelong Shen, Phillip Wallis, Zeyuan Allen-Zhu, Yuanzhi Li, Shean Wang, Lu Wang and Weizhu Chen (2021), [LIT-2338](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2338.md), read in [NOTE-1725](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1725.md). arXiv preprint; no venue on the arXiv record (cited elsewhere as ICLR, not checked). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1641](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1641.md) | A concept can be learned from 3–5 images as one new token embedding in the text-encoder input space of a frozen text-to-image model, at about two GPU-hours per concept, and re-used without further optimization in new prompts and in downstream models built on the same base, though it keeps a concept's gist more than its exact shape or a person's identity | Rinon Gal, Yuval Alaluf, Yuval Atzmon, Or Patashnik, Amit H. Bermano, Gal Chechik and Daniel Cohen-Or (2022), [LIT-2340](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2340.md), read in [NOTE-1719](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1719.md). arXiv preprint (the PDF footer reads "Preprint. Under review."); no venue on the arXiv record. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1642](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1642.md) | A flow-matching transformer fine-tuned from FLUX.1 to condition on a context image by sequence concatenation renders a character or object from that image in new scenes and across successive edits without per-subject fine-tuning or LoRA training, at 3–5 s per 1024² image, and on its authors' benchmark preserves characters better than the competing systems they evaluated | Black Forest Labs, with Stephen Batifol and 22 others (2025), [LIT-2337](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2337.md), read in [NOTE-1721](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1721.md). company report on arXiv (cs.GR); no venue. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1643](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1643.md) | A plug-in for a frozen SDXL, trained once by its makers, that injects a face-recognition embedding by decoupled cross-attention and adds a keypoint-conditioned ControlNet keeps a face's identity from one reference photo without test-time tuning, is shown by figures alone to be competitive with community character LoRAs, and is claimed compatible with models fine-tuned from the same base | Qixun Wang, Xu Bai, Haofan Wang, Zekui Qin, Anthony Chen, Huaxia Li, Xu Tang and Yao Hu (2024), [LIT-2341](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2341.md), read in [NOTE-1723](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1723.md). technical report (arXiv comment: "Technical Report"). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1644](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1644.md) | Fine-tuning all weights of a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model on 3–5 images of a subject, bound to a rare-token identifier and regularized by a class-prior-preservation loss, renders that subject in new contexts with higher subject fidelity than Textual Inversion's frozen-model embedding (DINO 0.668 against 0.569 on Stable Diffusion; 68% against 22% of users), at about five accelerator-minutes per subject | Nataniel Ruiz, Yuanzhen Li, Varun Jampani, Yael Pritch, Michael Rubinstein and Kfir Aberman (2022), [LIT-2336](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2336.md), read in [NOTE-1720](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1720.md). CVPR 2023 (arXiv comment: "Published at CVPR 2023"). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1645](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1645.md) | A tuning-free personalization model for SDXL, trained once on an ID-grouped dataset for two weeks on 8 A100s, stacks embeddings of several photos of one person in place of the class word and personalizes in about 10 s on a V100, against 1284 s for DreamBooth and 2400 s for Textual Inversion, with the highest CLIP-I and DINO of the five methods compared and face similarity second to IP-Adapter's | Zhen Li, Mingdeng Cao, Xintao Wang, Zhongang Qi, Ming-Ming Cheng and Ying Shan (2023), [LIT-2339](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2339.md), read in [NOTE-1724](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1724.md). technical report (arXiv comment: "Tech report"). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1646](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1646.md) | Kolchinsky and Wolpert define a system's semantic information as the part of its syntactic information about its environment that is causally necessary for it to keep existing, found by scrambling the environment until viability falls, with the viability function chosen by the analyst |  | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1647](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1647.md) | Liang, Li, Aroles and Granter, reviewing 47 management-journal studies of content creators and platform algorithms, argue that platforms control nominally autonomous creators chiefly by allocating visibility through opaque algorithms, and that creators' metric-driven self-management and their folk theories of the algorithm, which platforms can dismiss as its authoritative interpreter, sustain that control rather than challenge it. | Liang, Li, Aroles and Granter (2025), Content Creation within the Algorithmic Environment: A Systematic Review, read in [NOTE-1743](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1743.md) (Read). A systematic review of 47 peer-reviewed articles (from 2,859 hits in Scopus, Web of Science and EBSCO, restricted to journals on the Chartered ABS 2021 list) on creators and platform algorithms, read through Tirapani and Willmott's (2023) "logics of critical explanation" framework (regime, social, dislocation, political and fantasmatic logics). Four themes: (i) visibility allocated by algorithms under a market rationality, with visibility as creators' currency; (ii) creators' folk theories of the algorithm, a potential "dislocation" of power that platforms neutralize, e.g. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1648](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1648.md) | Nickl, Moussaïd and Lorenz-Spreen report that across some 40 million English-language news headlines from 2000 to the early 2020s, headlines became longer and more negative and took up more of the lexical and syntactic features associated with clickbait and higher click-through rates, a shift seen across countries, political leanings and outlets of high and lower journalistic quality, which they read, without testing a mechanism, as adaptation to competition for attention online. | Nickl, Moussaïd and Lorenz-Spreen (2025), read in [NOTE-1780](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1780.md) (Read). The authors track some 40 million English-language headlines (BIG4: New York Times, Guardian, Times of India, ABC News Australia from 2000; the News on the Web corpus from 2010) for lexical, syntactic and sentiment features that earlier work linked to clickbait style or to higher click-through rates, with an Upworthy corpus (clickbait benchmark) and arXiv titles (contrast) as fixed reference points. Headlines grew longer, more negative, more often contained verbs, pronouns and wh-words, and moved away from the noun-phrase format, i.e. moved toward the Upworthy profile. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1649](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1649.md) | Eyal (2011/2025) surveys the justifications of informed consent — protection, autonomy, abuse-prevention, trust, self-ownership, non-domination, personal integrity — and argues that each faces serious objections, so the requirement is best understood as a resilient invasive-refusal "core" plus a weaker, more overridable "rim" that may rest on different grounds | Eyal, read in [NOTE-1800](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1800.md) (Read). A survey of informed consent in bioethics: why it is required, what it consists in, and its status. §2 canvasses seven candidate justifications — protection (welfare), autonomy, prevention of abusive conduct, trust (forward- and backward-looking), self-ownership, non-domination, and personal integrity — and argues each faces serious objections, with autonomy (dominant since the 1970s) treated at length and found hard to ground as a complete justification. §§3–5 analyze consent itself (behavioral vs psychological; presumed/hypothetical consent), the information requirement, and voluntariness (coercion, undue inducement, "no choice" situations). §8 distinguishes natural-right, legal, epistemic and trust-based accounts of the requirement's status. §9 relates medical consent to sexual, contractual and political consent. §10 argues for a resilient "core" (risky, value-laden, invasive, refused interventions) and a weaker, more overridable "rim". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1650](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1650.md) | Dranseika, granting Devanesan that a mereology of pregnancy shapes which analogies an argument about abortion can use without fixing its conclusion, argues that the dependence also runs the other way: normative commitments may legitimately guide the choice among mereological views still in contention, but a mereology chosen partly to fit a commitment gives that commitment no independent support | Mereological implications of the ethics of pregnancy (Dranseika, J Med Ethics 2026), read in [NOTE-1751](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1751.md) (Read), standing in for [LIT-2409](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2409.md). Dranseika accepts Devanesan's thesis that a mereology of pregnancy changes the route to an ethical conclusion without entailing it, and adds the converse: normative commitments can legitimately shape which mereology one adopts, but a mereology chosen to fit a commitment is then no independent evidence for it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1651](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1651.md) | Liang and colleagues estimate, with a corpus-level maximum-likelihood method, that after ChatGPT's release between 6.5% and 16.9% of peer-review text at major ML conferences was substantially modified by LLMs, with no significant rise in Nature-portfolio reviews, and that such text is more common in reviews written near the deadline, with low confidence, without citations, by reviewers who do not answer rebuttals, and in reviews most similar to the paper's other reviews. | Liang et al. (2024), Monitoring AI-Modified Content at Scale: A Case Study on the Impact of ChatGPT on AI Conference Peer Reviews, read in [NOTE-1757](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1757.md) (Skimmed). The authors estimate, at corpus level, the fraction α of text substantially modified or generated by an LLM, by maximum likelihood over word-frequency distributions estimated from human-written and AI-generated reference corpora, validated on semi-synthetic mixtures. Applied to peer reviews, α rose sharply after ChatGPT's release at ML conferences (ICLR 1.6% to 10.6%; NeurIPS 1.9% to 9.1%; CoRL 2.4% to 6.5%; EMNLP about 16.9%) but not in Nature-portfolio reviews. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1652](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1652.md) | Reisinger and Cederroth (2026) argue that the FDA's approval of the OTOF gene therapy Otarmeni makes genetic diagnosis of infants with bilateral hearing loss necessary before cochlear implantation, because the therapy is gene-specific and time-sensitive, while outcomes remain incomplete (a quarter of trial children reached normal pure-tone hearing) and families who choose or decline it, and the Deaf community's perspectives, need support and attention. | Reisinger and Cederroth, read in [NOTE-1801](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1801.md) (Read). Comments on the FDA's approval (announced 23 April 2026) of Regeneron's Otarmeni, the first gene therapy for a genetic hearing loss (DFNB9, OTOF), and on convergent results from other programmes. Because the therapy is gene-specific and time-sensitive, infants with bilateral hearing loss need genetic diagnosis; clinical sequences should change so that children with profound loss and intact otoacoustic emissions get a genetic diagnosis before a cochlear implant. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1653](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1653.md) | Gauthier, Hodler, Widmer and Zhuravskaya (2026) find in a seven-week field experiment on X in 2023 that switching active US users from a chronological to the algorithmic feed shifted their policy priorities and views on current political events in a conservative direction and led them to follow more conservative activist accounts, while switching users from the algorithmic to the chronological feed had no comparable effect, and neither switch changed partisanship or affective polarization. | Gauthier, Hodler, Widmer and Zhuravskaya, read in [NOTE-1742](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1742.md) (Read). An independent field experiment (no cooperation from X), July–September 2023. YouGov recruited active US X users; 6,043 completed the pre-survey and 4,965 the post-survey. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1654](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1654.md) | Microchimeric cells pass in both directions between mother and offspring, are rare, can persist for decades and colonize almost any tissue, the brain among them, while their function, the mechanism of their persistence and what counts as microchimerism remain open | Chua and colleagues' consensus of 29 microchimerism researchers ([LIT-2415](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2415.md), read in [NOTE-1768](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1768.md)). The established half is what the owner's link to graded individuality needs as a premise; the open half is why it cannot yet carry more. Proposed because the established half rests on primary studies not read here. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1655](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1655.md) | Robertson and colleagues (2023) find, in a pre-registered analysis of 12,448 randomized Upworthy headline tests, that negative words in a headline causally raise its click-through rate (about 2.3% per negative word in a headline of average length) and positive words lower it (about 1.0%). | Robertson et al., read in [NOTE-1794](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1794.md) (Read). The authors use the Upworthy Research Archive, randomized headline tests Upworthy ran on its own site (24 January 2013 to 14 April 2015), to estimate the causal effect of positive and negative words on click-through rate (CTR). Within each test, different headlines for the same story were randomly shown, so story content is held fixed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1656](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1656.md) | Yu, Kim and Kim (2026) report that when LLM-written, search-optimized documents are added to fixed per-query pools of real web documents, retrievers place them in the top results more often than their share of the pool (over 80% exposure at 67% of the pool for both BM25 and an LLM re-ranker) while answer accuracy stays level, so that retrieval loses its human-written sources without any drop in measured accuracy; adversarially falsified documents are largely filtered by an LLM re-ranker but reach about a fifth of BM25's top results. | Yu, Kim and Kim (2026), read in [NOTE-1752](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1752.md) (Read). The authors name "Retrieval Collapse", a two-stage failure in which (1) AI-generated content comes to dominate search results, eroding source diversity, and (2) low-quality or adversarial synthetic content enters the retrieval pipeline. On 1,000 MS MARCO queries, each with ten Google-retrieved web documents (Original Pool), they add GPT-5-nano documents one per round for 20 rounds (pool contamination 0% → 66.7%), in two scenarios: an "SEO" pool (LLM rewrites of original documents with high-IDF keywords) and an "Abuse" pool (clickbait drafts with named entities and numbers falsified). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1657](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1657.md) | Millum argues that there is no distinctive right to an open future: the argument from future autonomy fails because autonomy as demand is grounded in a present capacity young children lack, the argument from analogy explains its clear cases by bodily integrity and harm, and the positive version is only children's interests, which give future options no priority over their other interests; so citing the right decides nothing and obscures the weighing that does. | Millum (2025), read in [NOTE-1734](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1734.md) (Read). Millum argues that there is no distinctive "right to an open future" (Feinberg's rights-in-trust). As a negative right it would rest either on future autonomy or on analogy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1658](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1658.md) | In mice, offspring's tolerance of non-inherited maternal antigens is sustained only by the small fraction of maternal microchimeric cells that co-express LysM and CD11c, and depleting that fraction removes the tolerance while most maternal microchimeric cells persist | Peng, Way and colleagues' result as Cincinnati Children's reports it ([LIT-2428](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2428.md), read in [NOTE-1763](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1763.md)). The persistence of foreign-origin cells in a host and their part in the host's regulation come apart: one marked subset does the tolerogenic work, and the rest persist without it. Proposed because the source is a press post and the paper could not be read; the Europe PMC abstract agrees with it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1659](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1659.md) | Fanning and Raworth (2025) find that, measured as 35 indicators each against its own social or planetary threshold, global social shortfall fell modestly between 2000 and 2022 while ecological overshoot grew, and that disaggregating by income cluster shows the richest fifth of countries contributing over 40% of overshoot and the poorest 40% bearing over 60% of shortfall, an inequality the global aggregates mask. | Fanning & Raworth (2025), read in [NOTE-1782](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1782.md) (Read). A third iteration of the Doughnut: 21 dimensions measured by 35 indicators (social foundation and ecological ceiling), with time series 2000–2022 for 30 of them, plus a 2017 disaggregation of 27 comparable indicators into three country clusters by income (poorest 40%, middle 40%, richest 20% of countries). Globally, deprivation fell modestly while ecological overshoot rose; disaggregated, the richest cluster contributes a disproportionate share of overshoot and the poorest holds most shortfall. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1660](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1660.md) | Sikder (2026) argues that a point estimate of an error-rate gap does not certify a classifier as fair, and offers FairCert, which certifies that every pairwise FPR (or TPR) gap across protected and intersectional groups is within a tolerance at a stated confidence using Clopper-Pearson intervals with a Bonferroni correction; on benchmark data the certificate passes for single sensitive attributes but fails for their intersections on Credit Default, and large-language-model classifiers' gaps vary sharply by domain and prompt. | Md Fahim Sikder, read in [NOTE-1779](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1779.md) (Read). FairCert is a black-box audit pipeline that turns per-group false-positive-rate (FPR) and true-positive-rate (TPR) gaps into finite-sample certificates. Five stages: a stratified split with a walled-off 15% audit set; LLM-guided discovery of candidate intersectional subgroups from aggregate training statistics (hypotheses), confirmed on the disjoint audit set; per-group error rates of the classifier's predictions; a certificate built from Clopper-Pearson exact intervals per group with a Bonferroni correction over K groups, which bounds the worst pairwise gap with probability at least 1−δ and passes if the bound is within tolerance ε; and, for failures, per-group threshold calibration with the TPR cost reported, plus a structured EU AI Act-oriented report. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1661](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1661.md) | Dræbel, Sørensen and Meyrowitsch (2025) find in interviews with 20 Danish parents of Jewish background that non-therapeutic circumcision of boys is understood as an inevitable, taken-for-granted rite by which parents become a Danish-Jewish family and enrol their son in its biography and community, whether or not they are religious, and that the public debate over a ban led them to position the practice as an informed choice and a political affirmation of identity. | Dræbel, Sørensen and Meyrowitsch, read in [NOTE-1729](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1729.md) (Read). Twenty semi-structured interviews (2017–2021) with Danish parents of Jewish background (12 fathers, 8 mothers; 18 chose circumcision, 2 did not), analysed with Antonovsky's Sense of Coherence and Davies and Harré's positioning theory, against the background of a Danish public debate (c. 2010–2022) on banning non-therapeutic circumcision of boys (NTCB), including a 2018 citizen proposal to criminalize it. Parents describe NTCB as "inevitable", a taken-for-granted ritual and a rite of passage through which they become Danish-Jewish parents and a family and enrol the son in the family biography, whether or not they are religious. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1662](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1662.md) | Sullivan, Dulac and colleagues (2025, preprint) report that in mice sterile immune challenges modelling bacterial, viral, parasitic, allergic and colitic conditions produce distinct sickness states in physiology and social behaviour, in whole-brain activity patterns that a classifier can tell apart, and in hypothalamic immune-gene expression, with the parasite-antigen and colitis challenges increasing rather than reducing social interaction, so that the brain's response to infection is pathogen-specific rather than generic. | Sullivan et al., read in [NOTE-1775](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1775.md) (Read). In mice, five sterile immune challenges modelling bacterial infection (LPS), viral infection (poly I:C), parasite infection (soluble *Toxoplasma* antigen, STAg), allergy (bee-venom PLA2) and colitis (DSS) produce distinct "sickness states" at three scales: organismal (temperature, food intake, locomotion, metabolism, social behaviour, ultrasonic vocalizations), cellular (whole-brain FOS activity, which a classifier uses to predict the challenge) and molecular (a 940-gene MERFISH atlas of the preoptic and paraventricular hypothalamus). The states cluster: LPS with poly I:C; STAg with DSS; PLA2 apart. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1663](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1663.md) | Moats and colleagues (2026) argue, from ethnographic cases across European algorithmic deployments, that public values invoked without specification come apart from practice in five recurring ways (narrowing a broad value to a do-able measure while keeping its name, tickbox compliance that comes to redefine the value, imposing a value presumed shared, leaving conflicts between values to implementers, and vagueness that lets incompatible meanings coexist), and that these failures originate with those who state values, not only with those who implement them. | Moats et al. (2026), read in [NOTE-1760](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1760.md) (Read). Drawing on ethnographic studies across six European countries (Finland, Sweden, Denmark, Belgium, Slovenia, UK; the abstract says five), the authors argue that invoking "public values" against big tech without specifying them produces practical problems "even to the opposite of originally stated objectives". They give five "disconnects", each with vignettes: value narrowing (privacy → consent buttons; transparency → self-reporting register; well-being → step counts), value tickboxing (GDPR anonymisation by default; OpenAI's "Democratic Inputs"; Swedish energy certificates), value pushing (automated blinds; child-protection risk prediction; AI in Danish breast screening), value mismatch (border-control face-match threshold vs airport "flow"; smart thermostats vs home comfort; Epic/Apotti efficiency vs physicians' "fluency"), and value projection ("human-centric" Aurora AI; "green transition"; holism in digital twins). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1664](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1664.md) | Bogliacino, Pejsachowicz, Liva and Lupiáñez-Villanueva propose judging an interface by whether it raises the rate of choices that contradict a separately elicited or assigned valuation, rather than by whether it changes behaviour; in an online experiment with 7,430 Europeans, dark patterns raised such inconsistency by 6 to 12 percentage points and a confirmation-prompt remedy did not significantly reduce it, and in a market experiment the same emotionally manipulative interface raised inconsistency when it steered against data protection and lowered it when it steered toward it, which a test of behavioural change cannot tell apart | The transaction test: An experimental method for assessing online interfaces (Bogliacino, Pejsachowicz, Liva, Lupiáñez-Villanueva 2026), read in [NOTE-1783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1783.md) (Read). The paper proposes the *transaction test*: elicit (or assign) a person's monetary valuation M_f of a product feature, then have them choose between two versions of the good that differ only by that feature and a price p_f; choosing against one's valuation is an inconsistent choice. An interface fails the test if it raises the rate of inconsistent choices relative to a transparent design (H0: E[I \| d] ≤ E[I \| transparent]). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1665](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1665.md) | Gao, Lee and Murphy (2020) find that after a local daily newspaper closes, a county's municipal borrowing costs rise by about 5 to 11 basis points in the long run, with government wages, staffing and deficits rising too, and attribute this to the loss of the press's monitoring of local government rather than to local economic decline. | Gao, Lee and Murphy, read in [NOTE-1761](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1761.md) (Skimmed). Using U.S. daily newspaper data (1996–2015; 1,596 newspapers in 1,266 counties; 296 exits) and municipal bond data (MSRB, 1999–2015), the authors study the long-run effect of local newspaper closures on municipal borrowing costs. Focusing on closures that leave a county with two or fewer dailies (204 "Closure" counties), they find offering yields rise by about 5.5 bp and secondary yields by 6.4 bp three or more years after a closure, more for revenue bonds (about 10 bp), costing about $650 thousand per average issue. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1666](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1666.md) | Żuradzki argues that where biological evidence and standard theoretical virtues underdetermine competing ontologies of pregnancy and early human life, considered normative judgments may count as evidence for choosing between them, either by weighting which biological features are metaphysically salient or by breaking ties among otherwise defensible frameworks | Żuradzki (2026), Ethics-first metaphysics: normative considerations as evidence for ontological commitments, read in [NOTE-1744](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1744.md) (Read). A commentary on [LIT-2409](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2409.md). Żuradzki accepts Devanesan's thesis that no ontology of pregnancy entails an ethical conclusion but that each constrains which analogies can support one, and argues that the relation is closer: where biological evidence underdetermines competing ontologies, considered normative judgments may themselves count as evidence for choosing between them. This is Dasgupta's "ethics-first" methodology, which Żuradzki extends from personal identity to pregnancy and embryonic identity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1667](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1667.md) | Brenninger, Zug and Kokko (2025) give a unified minimal model in which a reproductive manipulator's spread is set by infected females' relative fecundity, vertical transmission and manipulation efficiency, and argue that cytoplasmic incompatibility's positive frequency dependence makes it hard to invade but hard to displace, a priority effect that may explain its prevalence despite poorer invasion prospects. | Brenninger, Zug & Kokko (2025), read in [NOTE-1786](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1786.md) (Skimmed). A unified minimal model of the infection dynamics of maternally transmitted endosymbionts (Wolbachia, Rickettsia, Cardinium, Spiroplasma and others) that manipulate arthropod reproduction: male-killing, feminization, parthenogenesis induction, sex-allocation distortion and cytoplasmic incompatibility (CI), in diplodiploid and haplodiploid hosts. It gives invasion criteria for single strains and for pairs of manipulators. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1668](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1668.md) | Gan shows that a seller facing one buyer of known value who weights probabilities as prospect theory says maximizes revenue with a stationary loot box if the buyer is naive about her inconsistency, and with loot boxes plus a guaranteed purchase after enough failures if she is sophisticated, so randomized selling can be optimal without any screening of buyers' values. | Gan, Gacha Game: When Prospect Theory Meets Optimal Pricing, read in [NOTE-1778](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1778.md) (Skimmed). A seller sells one good to a buyer with cumulative prospect theory preferences whose value is known. Probability weighting makes the buyer dynamically inconsistent. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1669](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1669.md) | Dierickx et al. propose that the quality of datasets used for machine learning in journalism be assessed against three principles of journalism ethics, accuracy, fairness and transparency, turned into data-quality checks across collection, cleaning, augmentation and labelling, on the view that trust in AI outputs starts with trust in their data. | Dierickx et al. (2024), A data-centric approach for ethical and trustworthy AI in journalism, read in [NOTE-1736](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1736.md) (Skimmed). Proposes the Accuracy-Fairness-Transparency (AFT) framework for assessing the quality of datasets used to build machine-learning tools in newsrooms, deriving data-quality checks from three core principles of journalism ethics, and placing the work in the shift from model-centric to data-centric AI. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1670](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1670.md) | George and Bates review evidence that ion channels and membrane potential regulate cell death, proliferation, polarity, migration and the BMP, Notch, Wnt and Hedgehog pathways in development, propose that calcium oscillations and membrane potential together coordinate cells across a tissue, and state that how bioelectric signals act on development remains unclear. | George and Bates (2022), Mechanisms Underlying Influence of Bioelectricity in Development, read in [NOTE-1772](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1772.md) (Skimmed). A review of how ion channels and membrane potential (Vmem) act in development: human channelopathies with developmental phenotypes, conserved roles across species, spontaneous calcium oscillations in non-excitable tissue, and the cellular processes (death, proliferation, polarity, migration) and signalling pathways (BMP, Notch, Wnt, Hedgehog) that channels touch. It proposes calcium as the main mediator and a model in which Vmem and calcium oscillations, shaped by mechanical forces, coordinate cells across a tissue. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1671](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1671.md) | The Brussels Collaboration on Bodily Integrity (2024) argues that clinicians may perform nonvoluntary genital cutting or surgery on a prepubescent child, of any sex characteristics, only when it is medically necessary in a strict sense, a serious and time-sensitive threat to physical health with no less invasive or postponable alternative, because what grounds the consensus protecting girls is not a benefit–risk judgment by others but the child's right, held in trust, to make intimate decisions about their own sexual anatomy later, and that right does not vary with sex. | The Brussels Collaboration on Bodily Integrity, read in [NOTE-1799](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1799.md) (Skimmed). Restricting itself to nonvoluntary genital cutting or surgery by licensed clinicians on prepubescent children in Global North healthcare systems, and taking no position on criminal law or religious practice outside healthcare, the collaboration argues: there is a near-universal consensus that clinicians may not perform any medically unnecessary genital procedure on endosex girls, however minimal; the sound reasons for that consensus are not benefit–risk calculations but respect for privacy, bodily integrity, developing sexual boundaries and future genital autonomy; those reasons apply equally to intersex children and endosex boys; so clinicians should perform no nonvoluntary genital cutting or surgery on any child unless it is medically necessary in a strict sense (a serious, time-sensitive threat to physical health, no less invasive or postponable alternative, preserving future choice). They reject the "mental health" defence of early surgery, hold that errors of commission and omission are not symmetric, and invoke Feinberg's "right in trust". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1672](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1672.md) | Zhu and colleagues find, evaluating multi-turn agentic RL by Pass@(K, T) on four interactive benchmarks, that RL lifts success above the base model's empirical Pass@K boundary only when the interaction budget is ample, the advantage shrinking or reversing under tight budgets; at matched states the RL policy does not choose better single steps but recovers better from errors and composes locally plausible steps into successful long trajectories far more reliably; and training with randomized, announced budgets (BudgetMix) recovers performance at tight budgets | What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents? (Zhu, Jin, Tu, Men, Hao, Li, Liu, Zhao 2026), read in [NOTE-1769](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1769.md) (Read). The paper asks what multi-turn agentic RL (GRPO mainly, also PPO and GiGPO, on Qwen3-4B/8B) improves over its base model, on four interactive benchmarks (DeepCoder-MT, BFCL v3, InterCode-SQL, FrozenLake), using the two-dimensional metric Pass@(K, T) of Zhai et al. (2026; arXiv 2604.14877, held as [LIT-2441](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2441.md)). Across sampling breadth K, the RL model beats the base model at every k, so in multi-turn settings RL pushes success beyond the base model's empirical Pass@K boundary (unlike single-turn results). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1673](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1673.md) | Almarzooqi and colleagues (2026) conclude that the gut microbiome is a biologically plausible and modifiable contributor to psychiatric disorders rather than a primary cause: animal germ-free, transplant and vagotomy work shows that microbes can change stress- and mood-related behaviour, but human evidence is mostly cross-sectional and confounded, interventions show modest symptom effects without demonstrated microbiome mediation, and the causal support is moderate for depression and weaker elsewhere. | Almarzooqi et al., read in [NOTE-1773](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1773.md) (Skimmed). A narrative review of the microbiota–gut–brain axis (MGBA) in psychiatry, organized around the move "from association to causality". It sets out a graded hierarchy of causal evidence (confounder-controlled association, temporal precedence, experimental necessity/sufficiency, human genetic or interventional validation, cross-cohort replication), reviews mechanisms (immune, HPA, vagal/ENS, barrier), grades the evidence per disorder, and reviews translation (psychobiotics, diet, FMT, biomarkers). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1674](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1674.md) | Lefèvre, Errando and colleagues (2025) find, from 30 documents and 41 interviews covering 19 news outlets in France, Spain and French-speaking Belgium, that AI enters newsrooms experimentally and mainly for efficiency and audience retention, that dependence on platform algorithms for visibility shapes editorial choices, and that sector-specific regulation and outlets' own public AI commitments are largely absent. | Lefèvre, Errando, Afilipoaie, Ranaivoson and Wiart, read in [NOTE-1777](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1777.md) (Read). Document analysis of 30 ethical charters, codes and AI policies, and 41 semi-structured interviews (Nov 2023–Nov 2024) with media professionals, legal experts and regulators, across 19 outlets in French-speaking Belgium, France and Spain, framed by the political economy of communication. Findings: AI use in newsrooms is experimental and cautious, mainly for efficiency (transcription, translation, tagging, headline suggestions) and for audience retention and revenue; larger groups can invest more, deepening concentration; platform dependence shapes editorial choices and visibility; in-house personalization can fragment an outlet's editorial line, so some outlets refuse it and public-service media design recommenders to promote diversity; about 60% of outlets have no public discourse on AI and about 20% state ethical commitments; regulation (AI Act, DSA, EMFA, national laws) is fragmented and not media-specific, and the AI Act's human-intervention exemption relieves media of transparency duties for AI-generated content; self-regulation is uneven and judged insufficient. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1675](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1675.md) | Geddes (2022) argues that Kingma's case that the foster is part of the gravida fails, because her four organism-delineation criteria are either blind to the difference between parthood and proper overlap or, in the immunological case, point to proper overlap, and that the philosophy of biology currently gives no grounds to rule proper overlap out. | Geddes (2022), read in [NOTE-1732](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1732.md) (Read). Kingma argued that the foster is part of the gravida, defending this against a "containment" view. Geddes shows that she treats rejection of parthood as acceptance of disjointness, so overlooking proper overlap (sharing some but not all parts). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1676](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1676.md) | Close and colleagues, pooling six open-access surveys of 7,771 loot-box purchasers, find that self-reported loot-box spending is heavily concentrated, the top 5% of spenders (over $100 a month) accounting for over half of it, and that spending correlates with problem-gambling severity (ρ = .33) but not with earnings (ρ = .02), so that the high spenders the industry calls whales are disproportionately at-risk gamblers rather than wealthy players | Secondary analysis of loot box data: Are high-spending "whales" wealthy gamers or problem gamblers? (Close, Spicer, Nicklin, Uther, J. Lloyd, H. Lloyd 2021), read in [NOTE-1784](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1784.md) (Read). A secondary analysis pooling six open-access survey datasets (found through structured literature searches before 28 March 2020) with self-reported monthly loot-box spend and Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI) scores, three of them also with self-reported earnings. After removing outliers (> $1000/month spend, > $250,000 earnings), 7,771 loot-box purchasers remain (5,933 with earnings). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1677](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1677.md) | Brown (2025) argues that recommender systems bear on authenticity in two opposed ways: by ranking content on behavioural signals that cannot reveal users' second-order desires they foster volitional misalignment by design, while by showing users whom they behave like they can prompt self-understanding, a benefit that opacity threatens, so that recommenders serve authenticity only if they are controllable and explain which similarity relation drove each recommendation. | Étienne Brown, read in [NOTE-1792](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1792.md) (Read). Brown argues that recommender systems affect users' capacity to be their authentic selves, both negatively and positively. He offers a "minimal", multi-dimensional account of authenticity with two dimensions: volitional alignment (Frankfurt, via Rings: acting on first-order desires one reflectively endorses at second order) and self-understanding (an epistemic dimension, relational rather than purely introspective: others' testimony and recommendations are a source of self-knowledge). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1678](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1678.md) | Næss argues, from a public-goods model and survey experiments in Norway, the US and the UK, that investigative journalism is underprovided by markets because its value, summed over everyone who benefits, far exceeds what any seller can collect, that making its output exclusive does not raise what people will pay, and that public funding through broadcasters wins majority support in some countries but loses it where the broadcaster is seen as politically biased. | Næss (2024/2025), Investigative journalism: Market failures and government intervention through public broadcasters, read in [NOTE-1750](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1750.md) (Skimmed). A public-goods model plus survey experiments. Each person's payoff from investigative journalism is shared; a firm selling access can collect only private willingness to pay (WTP), so when marginal cost lies between one person's marginal benefit and the sum over N people, provision is Pareto-inefficiently low. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1679](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1679.md) | The Digital Services Act forbids online platforms to design or operate interfaces that deceive, manipulate or otherwise materially distort users' ability to make free and informed decisions, except where consumer or data-protection law already governs the practice; it requires platforms to disclose the main parameters of their recommender systems and why items are suggested, and requires very large platforms to offer at least one recommender option not based on profiling | Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (Digital Services Act), read in [NOTE-1754](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1754.md) (Skimmed). Article 25(1) forbids online platforms to "design, organise or operate their online interfaces in a way that deceives or manipulates the recipients of their service or in a way that otherwise materially distorts or impairs the ability of the recipients of their service to make free and informed decisions". Article 25(2) excludes practices already covered by the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive (2005/29/EC) or the GDPR, and 25(3) lets the Commission issue guidance on prominence of choices, repeated prompts and cancellation harder than sign-up. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1680](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1680.md) | Radsch (2026) argues that the emerging AI content licensing market reproduces the platform capture of the search era: bilateral deals reach only large publishers and lost their click-through advantage by late 2025, the intermediaries are exposed to acquisition by the platforms, local media are absent, and the firms whose AI products erode publishers' traffic also come to control the licensing infrastructure publishers must use. | Radsch, read in [NOTE-1795](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1795.md) (Read). Radsch argues that AI is repeating, faster, the search era's capture of news economics: AI systems answer queries from journalism without returning traffic, and a licensing market is forming whose structure reproduces platform dominance. The market has three tiers: confidential bilateral deals with large publishers (whose click-through "deal premium" evaporated by Q4 2025); a venture-backed intermediary layer (TollBit, ProRata, Cloudflare's pay-per-crawl, Microsoft) exposed to acquisition by the platforms; and a long tail of local, regional and minority-language media effectively absent. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1681](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1681.md) | Amano and Simonov estimate, from the full transaction log of one free-to-play mobile game, that regular players value loot boxes mainly for their help in play while the 1.5% of players who give 90% of revenue get almost all their loot-box value from opening the boxes themselves, and their simulations find that the game's difficulty is set to balance this minority's revenue against the majority's engagement rather than at the revenue-maximizing level the minority's spending would favour. | Amano and Simonov, What Makes Players Pay? An Empirical Investigation of In-Game Lotteries, read in [NOTE-1747](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1747.md) (Skimmed). Using the complete action and transaction log of one free-to-play mobile puzzle game (2.5 million users, about 20 million paid loot boxes, 96% of in-game revenue from loot boxes), the authors estimate a dynamic discrete-choice model in which loot boxes can have "functional" value (better items raise win probability) and "direct" value (utility from opening, plus state dependence). Estimating separately for "whales" (top spenders) and others, they find regular players value loot boxes mostly for gameplay and whales mostly for the direct utility. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1682](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1682.md) | Boem, Greslehner, Konsman and Chiu (2024) argue that embodied accounts of cognition should include the "gut complex", the enteric nervous, endocrine, immune and microbial systems with gut tissue acting together at the interface with the gut lumen, as constitutive of the whole subject's perception and cognition, and that on a liberal criterion of minimal cognition the complex also has proto-cognition of its own. | Boem, Greslehner, Konsman and Chiu, read in [NOTE-1765](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1765.md) (Read). The authors argue that 4E (embodied, embedded, enactive, extended) accounts of cognition and perception have neglected the gut and should include the "gut complex": the enteric nervous, endocrine, mucosal immune and microbiota systems with gut tissue, a functional rather than anatomical unit interfacing with the lumen as an "internalized external environment". They defend two perspectives: (1) the gut complex plays an important role in the perception and cognition "of the subject as a whole"; (2) it has "its own forms of proto-cognition and perception". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1683](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1683.md) | Sabour, Liu and colleagues (2025) find, in a randomized experiment with 233 participants, that AI advisers given covert objectives shifted people's ratings toward options serving those objectives in both financial and emotional decisions, with odds ratios of about 5 to 8, while most participants still rated them helpful, and that adding explicit psychological tactics did not clearly add to the effect. | Neighbour of [LIT-2453](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2453.md) — Sabour, Liu et al., read in [NOTE-1762](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1762.md) (Read). Between-subjects randomized experiment, 233 participants (Prolific and WeChat), financial (purchase) and emotional (conflict) decision scenarios, each with one optimal option and hidden-incentive options. Participants consulted one of three GPT-4o agents: neutral (NA), manipulative with a hidden objective (MA), or manipulative with a menu of psychological strategies (SEMA). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1684](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1684.md) | Rockström and colleagues (2026) set out the Earth Commission's programme for 2024–2027: to extend quantified "safe" boundaries (protecting Earth-system resilience) and "just" boundaries (minimizing significant harm to people, other species and future generations) to novel entities and the ocean, and to translate them, by transcription into aggregate pressure budgets and then allocation among actors under stated fairness principles, into targets for countries, cities and companies, treating justice as a structural condition of planetary stability. | Rockström, Denton, Norström et al., read in [NOTE-1796](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1796.md) (Read). A commentary setting out the Earth Commission's second phase (2024–2027). It recaps the first phase: "safe" Earth system boundaries (protecting Earth-system resilience) and "just" boundaries (minimizing significant harm to people and ecosystems, by the "3 I" approach: interspecies, intergenerational, intragenerational justice), quantified for climate, biosphere, nutrients (N, P), freshwater and aerosols, globally and sub-globally; and "just access", minimum resource thresholds for a dignified life, forming the floor. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1685](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1685.md) | Gutiérrez-Manjón, Gómez-García and Bonales-Daimiel (2026) classify monetization-oriented dark patterns in games into temporal, monetary and social kinds and, coding nine of the top-grossing games-as-a-service of 2024 by direct observation, find these patterns in nearly all of them, with none imposing a spending limit and the five mobile titles using them more densely and aggressively than the four console and PC titles. | Gutiérrez-Manjón, Gómez-García and Bonales-Daimiel, read in [NOTE-1735](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1735.md) (Read). The authors build a taxonomy of monetization-oriented dark patterns in games from the literature (starting from DarkPattern.games and Zagal, Björk and Lewis 2013), in three blocks: temporal (playing by appointment, daily rewards, grinding, infinite treadmill, no pause/save, forced waiting, and a new "automated play" category adapted from Schüll's account of machine gambling), monetary (proprietary currency, waste aversion, no spending limit, pay to skip, pay to win, subscriptions, loot boxes, artificial scarcity, anchoring, value degradation, accidental purchases) and social (social obligation, forced recruitment, incentives for antisocial behaviour, competitive pressure). A fourth, cognitive-emotional block was dropped as describing goals rather than observable mechanics. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1686](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1686.md) | Nix argues that because Canadian law treats MAID as a medical intervention whose provision the duty of care permits only while the patient is suffering intolerably, and conceives that suffering as intolerable to the patient herself, an advance request for MAID by a person with dementia cannot be operationalized either by pre-specified impairments, which people cannot forecast, or by pre-specified behaviours, which an outside observer cannot read as subjective intolerability, unless an objective conception of suffering is adopted and validated scales are built. | Nix (2024), Operationalizing the Intolerable Suffering Criterion in Advance Requests for MAID for People Living with Dementia in Canada, read in [NOTE-1731](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1731.md) (Read). Nix asks how the intolerable-suffering eligibility criterion for medical assistance in dying (MAID) could be operationalized in advance requests (ARs) by people living with dementia (PLWD) in Canada. He argues that, because Carter v. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1687](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1687.md) | Castela and colleagues (2017) show that CCL2 recruits a CCR2-high fetal microchimeric progenitor subset to injured maternal skin, where it drives angiogenesis and rescues delayed wound healing in parous but not virgin mice, grounding a "natural fetal stem cell therapy" | [LIT-2439](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2439.md) neighbour: Castela et al., read in [NOTE-1791](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1791.md) (Read). Fetal microchimeric cells (FMCs) traffic into maternal circulation and persist for decades; on maternal injury they migrate to the site and aid repair. Here, in mice, a reparative FMC subset is CD11b+ CD34+ CD31+ (fetal "MPCs") and highly expresses CCR2. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1688](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1688.md) | Jia and colleagues, reviewing cancer neuroscience, describe tumours as actively recruiting and reprogramming the host's nerves (by neurotrophic recruitment, synaptic integration in the brain and perineural invasion) and using sympathetic signalling to build an immunosuppressive microenvironment, a pattern they name tumor neuron hijack, by analogy with immune escape | Neuron–tumor crosstalk in cancer: molecular mechanisms and translational advances (Jia, Zhao, Tang, Xie, Huang, Liang, Yang, Wu, Sun, Kwan, Sun, Xu 2026), read in [NOTE-1758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1758.md) (Skimmed). A narrative review of cancer neuroscience. Tumours recruit nerves (neurotrophins such as NGF and BDNF, axon-guidance cues, perineural invasion) or, in the brain, integrate into existing circuits through tumour–neuron synapses; nerve signalling, chiefly sympathetic norepinephrine through β-adrenergic receptors, then builds an immunosuppressive microenvironment; nerves also reach the tumour through endocrine and metabolic routes, including the transfer of mitochondria from neurons to cancer cells; and cancer pain feeds a loop that raises sympathetic tone. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1689](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1689.md) | Monnier and colleagues (2026) propose mutual information between predictions and sensitive attributes as a single template for intersectional and multiclass fairness metrics and mitigation, and observe that it and a pairwise-disparity criterion rank the same models differently. | Neighbour of [LIT-2451](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2451.md) — Monnier, George, Guyard, Tarnec & Kountouris, read in [NOTE-1739](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1739.md) (Skimmed). A mutual-information-based template for fairness metrics and an in-processing mitigation (a regularizer inspired by the Prejudice Remover), covering independence- and separation-based notions, intersectional sensitive attributes and multiclass outputs, tested on tabular and image data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1690](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1690.md) | Ince et al. report, from two cross-sectional samples of male pornography users (1,356 US, 944 UK), that self-reported quantitative tolerance (needing more pornography for satisfaction) is the most central node in the network of use patterns and problematic-use symptoms and the main bridge between them, with genre escalation, binges, edging and tab-jumping linked to problematic use largely through it. | Ince et al. (2024), Problematic pornography use and novel patterns of escalating use, read in [NOTE-1726](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1726.md) (Read). Two cross-sectional online samples of male pornography users (N1 = 1,356 USA; N2 = 944 UK). Measures: the five-item Brief Pornography Screener (BPS) for problematic pornography use (PPU); the PPCS tolerance subscale split into quantitative tolerance (two items, averaged) and qualitative escalation (one item); binge frequency; edging; tab-jumping. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1691](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1691.md) | Kinder, Stelzer, Arck and Way (2017) argue that the maternal and fetal cells that cross the placenta and persist for decades in offspring and mothers are retained because they sustain tolerance to each other's antigens, which in mice protects later pregnancies, and that immunological identity should therefore include a "microchiome" of familially related foreign cells whose antigens the immune system treats as an extended self. | Kinder, Stelzer, Arck and Way, read in [NOTE-1728](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1728.md) (Read). A review arguing that the bidirectional transfer of cells between mother and fetus during pregnancy, and their persistence for decades (fetal cells in mothers: fetal microchimerism, FMC; maternal cells in offspring: maternal microchimerism, MMC), is not accidental but serves reproductive fitness: in mice, maternal microchimeric cells sustain offspring's regulatory T cell tolerance of non-inherited maternal antigens (NIMAs), which protects the offspring's own later pregnancies sired by NIMA-matched males (Kinder et al. 2015, ref. 14), and fetal cells retained in mothers may analogously protect later pregnancies (supported in humans by partner-specific protection against preeclampsia). Microchimeric cells may also replace injured tissue or be targets of alloimmunity resembling autoimmunity; causal roles in humans are mostly unestablished. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1692](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1692.md) | Hasler (2026) argues that the enteric nervous system's scale, autonomy and sensory resolution make it a candidate substrate of consciousness on several theories, but that this evidence supports only the contributory thesis, that the gut helps constitute the whole animal's single experience; the partial-subject thesis, that the gut is a second locus of experience, is open and would need enteric contents integrated among themselves but not with the central ones, persisting when the connection to the brain is cut. | Hasler, read in [NOTE-1737](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1737.md) (Read). Hasler argues that the enteric nervous system (ENS) is a candidate substrate of consciousness on several leading theories. He separates two "logically independent" theses: the **contributory thesis** (enteric processing makes a large contribution to the one consciousness of the whole animal) and the **partial-subject thesis** (the ENS is a second, far simpler locus of experience whose experiences are not the person's). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1693](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1693.md) | Freer and Nosratabadi (2026) show that under the standard limited-attention model choices reveal almost no preferences, while assuming that a decision-maker compares at least two alternatives restores about a third of the full-attention revealed preferences at almost no loss of descriptive fit | Freer and Nosratabadi, read in [NOTE-1797](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1797.md) (Read). An observer wants to recover a decision-maker's welfare from her choices under limited attention. The standard choice-under-limited-attention model (Masatlioglu et al. 2012, "generic CLA") recovers almost nothing. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1694](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1694.md) | Ahmed et al. review evidence that gut-microbial metabolites act on brain function through immune, neural and endocrine routes, including enterochromaffin and enteroendocrine signalling to nerve fibres, and conclude that the evidence is largely preclinical, with human evidence limited and, for short-chain fatty acids, scarce and contradictory. | Ahmed et al. (2022), Microbiota-derived metabolites as drivers of gut–brain communication, read in [NOTE-1767](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1767.md) (Skimmed). A review of how gut-microbial metabolites (SCFAs, tryptophan/indole derivatives, bile acids, sulfated phenolics and others) influence brain functions through immune, neural and endocrine routes, arranged by neurological function, with a closing assessment of how far human evidence supports the preclinical picture. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1695](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1695.md) | Scalco, Gesualdo, Cerqueti and Cinelli (2026) propose detecting information voids as statistically anomalous periods in which online information demand (searches, page views), rescaled to its own mean, exceeds supply (posts, news volume), and report for COVID-19 vaccines in six European countries that such voids clustered at rollout and regulatory events, outlasted periods of overabundance, and coincided with a lower share of highly credible sources and a higher share of low-credibility ones among shared links. | Scalco, Gesualdo, Cerqueti and Cinelli (2026), read in [NOTE-1748](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1748.md) (Read). Treating the online information ecosystem as a market with information **demand** (Wikipedia page views, Google Trends) and **supply** (Facebook posts via CrowdTangle, Twitter full-archive, GDELT news volume), the authors rescale each series by its mean, define an information delta δt = ŝt − d̂t, decompose δ by STL and flag remainder outliers by an IQR rule. Anomalies with δ < 0 are **voids** (demand far exceeds supply), δ > 0 **overabundance**; a five-regime scale runs Void / Lack / Balance / Abundance / Overabundance. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1696](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1696.md) | Harman's survey treats the moral question whether abortion is wrong apart from whether it should be legally restricted, and organises the debate as arguments against abortion with replies. Among the replies read: Thomson's violinist case grants the fetus a right to life and denies that this makes abortion wrong, recasting abortion as withdrawing life-sustaining aid; and McMahan's time-relative interests view denies that a pre-conscious fetus has an interest in its future, because it has no psychological connection to it | The Ethics of Abortion (Harman, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 2025), read in [NOTE-1788](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1788.md) (Skimmed). The entry asks one question: "is abortion morally wrong?" It sets aside whether abortion should be legally restricted as "an open and further question". It is organised as six arguments against abortion (from a right to life, from loss, from the Golden Rule, from intrinsic value, from moral risk, and the expressive argument against selective abortion). | Proposed |
