| [THEORY-1697](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1697.md) | Davoudabadi, Makui and Rasouli (2026) propose a recommender that combines a user score built on a peak-end reference point and prospect-theory gains and losses with an organizational score based on the gap between the organization's projected and desired operational state, weighting the organization more as the user's purchase history is more diverse and the user more as the organization has slack, and in a simulation of one manufacturer with 100 synthetic users it reduces workshop over- and under-utilization relative to purely customer-driven recommendation. | Davoudabadi, Makui and Rasouli, read in [NOTE-1740](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1740.md) (Read). The authors propose a recommender that scores each candidate item for a user by combining (a) a user-side score and (b) an organization-side score. User side: a reference point built from the user's peak and most recent purchase utilities (peak-end rule), item distances to it split into gains and losses with a prospect-theory-style value function (the EXPTODIM method), and a "user flexibility" index from the diversity of the user's past purchases. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1698](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1698.md) | Strand and Burke argue that bracoviruses, descended from a nudivirus that infected the ancestor of microgastrine wasps about 100 million years ago, have become obligate beneficial symbionts: their replication genes persist only as an inherited provirus in the wasp genome, separate from the packaged virulence genes, and the virions they make in the female wasp's ovary deliver genes into caterpillar hosts that suppress host immunity and alter host growth for the wasp's offspring, without the virus ever replicating in the host. | Strand and Burke (2012), Polydnaviruses as Symbionts and Gene Delivery Systems, read in [NOTE-1770](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1770.md) (Read). Polydnaviruses (PDVs) are viruses carried by parasitoid wasps. In bracoviruses the provirus sits in every wasp cell; it replicates only in calyx cells of the female ovary, and the virions are injected with the eggs into a caterpillar host, where their genes are expressed but never replicate. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1699](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1699.md) | Kara and colleagues (2011) report that in pregnant mice given a myocardial infarction, cells of fetal origin home selectively to the injured maternal heart, not to uninjured organs, and differentiate there into cardiomyocytes, smooth muscle and endothelial cells, about 40% of them expressing the trophoblast-stem marker Cdx2. | Kara et al., read in [NOTE-1727](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1727.md) (Read). In a mouse model, wild-type virgin females mated with eGFP-transgenic males had a left anterior descending artery ligation (myocardial infarction) at gestation day 12. eGFP-tagged cells of fetal origin were then tracked in the mother. Fetal cells were enriched in injured hearts relative to sham and uninjured controls, located in infarct and peri-infarct zones, and by 3–4 weeks co-expressed markers of cardiomyocytes, smooth muscle and endothelium. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1700](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1700.md) | Caliari and Petri argue that aggregate choice data consistent with random utility maximization can, exactly when the population's preferences are sufficiently uncorrelated, be generated by decision-makers none of whom maximizes a preference, so that individual rationality and the welfare judgments built on it cannot be read off aggregate choices without the analyst's prior assumptions. | Caliari and Petri, read in [NOTE-1746](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1746.md) (Skimmed). The random utility model (RUM) treats aggregate stochastic choice as generated by a population of preference maximizers. The authors show that RUM data can equally be generated by a population of decision-makers none of whom maximizes a preference, if and only if the rational population's preferences are "sufficiently uncorrelated" (their correlation bounds, a strengthening of lower Fréchet bounds). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1701](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1701.md) | Montero-Porras, Smets and Lenaerts show that in a two-population replicator model of a platform that rewards costly quality content and creators who invest in it, quality and its absence are both stable, the platform needs far more creators investing than creators need the platform to reward them, and a temporary rise in the payoff to promoting cheap content that lasts long enough moves the system into decline that restoring the original payoff does not undo. | Montero-Porras, Smets and Lenaerts (2026), Enshittification of Algorithmic Recommendation: An Evolutionary Model of Platform-Creator Dynamics, read in [NOTE-1787](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1787.md) (Read). A two-population evolutionary game between a platform (x = probability its recommender rewards costly quality content) and creators (y = probability a creator invests in quality), under replicator dynamics: ẋ = x(1−x)(Ry−A), ẏ = y(1−y)(Vx−C). With R > A and V > C there are two stable pure equilibria, (1,1) "virtuous" and (0,0) "vicious", separated by an interior saddle at (x*, y*) = (C/V, A/R). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1702](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1702.md) | Nakhal and colleagues (2026) report that in mice, vancomycin-induced gut dysbiosis during pregnancy was associated with reduced maternal-to-offspring microbial transmission and, in offspring at postnatal day 14, with altered intestinal and enteric plexus structure and with shorter, less branched inhibitory interneurons in somatosensory and motor cortex but not entorhinal cortex or hippocampus, findings they present as descriptive associations that do not separate microbial from other antibiotic effects. | Nakhal et al. (2026), read in [NOTE-1738](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1738.md) (Skimmed). Pregnant GAD67-GFP mice (6 control, 6 treated dams) received oral vancomycin (20 mg/kg/day, GD8–GD17) to induce gut dysbiosis. Dams' microbiota lost diversity (Chao1, Shannon; PERMANOVA R² = 0.77). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1703](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1703.md) | Scoring an agent by whether one of k sampled trajectories of at most T interaction rounds succeeds separates capability expansion, a larger set of problems solved at some sampling budget, from efficiency improvement, more reliable success on problems already solvable; on sequential retrieval, RL expanded a 7B agent's boundary while matched-data SFT contracted it | Zhai, Yan, Shao and Wang's PASS@(k,T) ([LIT-2441](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2441.md), read in [NOTE-1749](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1749.md)). The distinction is definitional and holds whatever the experiment shows; the experiment is one model, one tool and differences of a few problems. Its stated monotonicity in T holds of a policy that ignores unused budget, and its own per-depth estimates are not monotone. Proposed on the experimental half. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1704](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1704.md) | Boddy and colleagues (2015) argue that fetal microchimerism's paradoxical effects on maternal health reflect a mix of aligned and conflicting mother-offspring fitness interests, so fetal cells are a selected extension of the placenta "beyond the womb" that can both maintain and manipulate maternal tissues, provoking maternal immune countermeasures | Boddy, Fortunato, Wilson Sayres and Aktipis, read in [NOTE-1781](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1781.md) (Read). An evolutionary (cooperation-and-conflict) framework for fetal microchimerism. Fetal cells cross into the mother, persist for decades, and have paradoxical associations with maternal health (both protective and harmful). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1705](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1705.md) | Hu, Jagadeesan, Jordan and Steinhardt prove that, in a model where non-myopic, discounting producers choose content every round and a platform recommends by a standard no-regret online-learning algorithm (LinHedge or LinEXP3), equilibrium producer effort and user welfare vanish over time under typical learning-rate schedules, because a slow learner makes today's effort move future recommendations too little to repay its cost; algorithms that permanently stop recommending producers whose content falls below a threshold sustain constant effort, and individualized criteria that make producers specialize recover near-optimal welfare in limiting cases | Incentivizing High-Quality Content in Online Recommender Systems (Hu, Jagadeesan, Jordan, Steinhardt), read in [NOTE-1774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1774.md) (Read). A game-theoretic model of a recommender platform that runs an online-learning (adversarial linear contextual bandit) algorithm, recommending one producer per arriving user, while P non-myopic, discounting producers choose a D-dimensional content vector at every step, paying cost \|\|p\|\|^c and earning 1 when recommended. Content quality is measured as producer effort \|\|p\|\| and as user welfare E[<u, p>]. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1706](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1706.md) | Levin argues that cells and tissues are an agential material whose collective problem-solving in anatomical, transcriptional and physiological spaces, bound by bioelectric networks, is the tractable interface for regenerative medicine: interventions should rewrite the setpoints these collectives pursue rather than force molecular states, and cancer is cells reverting to smaller goals, so that 'cancer cells are not more selfish; they just have smaller selves', normalizable by restoring their bioelectric connection to the tissue | The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine (Levin 2024/2025), read in [NOTE-1764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1764.md) (Read). Levin argues that biomedicine's bottom-up, molecular ("hardware") paradigm cannot achieve anatomical control (birth defects, regeneration, cancer, aging) and should be complemented by a top-down program that treats cells and tissues as an "agential material" with memories, goals and problem-solving competencies, i.e. a collective intelligence navigating anatomical, transcriptional and physiological spaces. Systems sit on a "spectrum of persuadability" (hardware rewiring → setpoint rewriting → training → reasoning with), and where a system sits is "not a philosophical question but an empirical one". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1707](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1707.md) | de Roos and Willkomm (2026) find, in a cross-sectional survey of 228 young men, that viewing pornography beyond one's reported arousal is low in magnitude, highest in absolute terms for mainstream content but relatively greatest in niche and extreme categories, and clusters into five distinct patterns with different correlates, so that content escalation is multidimensional rather than a single progression toward extremity. | de Roos and Willkomm, read in [NOTE-1789](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1789.md) (Read). A cross-sectional online survey of 228 men aged 18–35 (mostly students, recruited through a university participant pool and social media) asked about arousal to and viewing frequency of many pornography categories, and measured sexual sensation seeking (SSS), problematic pornography use (PPCS subscales), child-sexual-abuse myth endorsement and peer acceptance of CSAM. "Escalation" is operationalized per category as viewing frequency multiplied by reverse-coded arousal: viewing a category more than one finds it arousing. A principal-component analysis finds five escalation clusters. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1708](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1708.md) | Burke et al. argue that recommender systems should be evaluated by the outcomes they produce for each stakeholder group (consumers, providers, upstream, downstream, the platform and third parties), with metrics derived from each group's values and goals, and that the resulting multidimensional scores may be left unaggregated or combined by weights, constraints, Pareto-frontier distance or learned expert orderings, there being no single correct way to quantify the values involved. | Burke et al. (2025), De-centering the (Traditional) User: Multistakeholder Evaluation of Recommender Systems, read in [NOTE-1793](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1793.md) (Skimmed). A position-and-guidance article. Recommender evaluation has been almost wholly about the end user; a multistakeholder evaluation assesses "the quality of recommendations ... across multiple groups of stakeholders". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1709](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1709.md) | Bisiani, Gulyas, Moore and Heravi (2026) find that across 27 Reach plc local newspapers from 2019 to 2025 the share of original content fell by about 23 points and of local content by about 15, while original local critical-information-needs reporting per edition roughly halved and was partly replaced by content duplicated from elsewhere in the group, increasingly shared across regional-hub boundaries: crowding out rather than dilution. | Bisiani, Gulyas, Moore and Heravi, read in [NOTE-1745](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1745.md) (Read). A longitudinal content analysis of 27 Reach plc local newspapers (seven regional hubs) sampled monthly in 2019, 2022 and 2025 (55,332 articles), measuring Napoli et al.'s three dimensions of "journalistic performance": originality (no near-duplicate in the corpus, MinHash Jaccard ≥ 0.7), locality, and coverage of Friedland et al.'s eight Critical Information Needs (CIN), coded by a fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 1.5B (F1 0.85). Within-newspaper fixed effects show originality, localness and CIN all falling; a decomposition shows original local CIN content displaced ("crowding out") by duplicated non-local content; an E-I index shows content sharing moving from hub-confined to group-wide, coinciding with Reach's 2024 Content Hub and AI rewriting tool "Guten". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1710](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1710.md) | UNESCO's Recommendation on the Ethics of Neurotechnology (2025) extends protections for autonomy, freedom of thought and mental privacy from neural data to any data used to infer mental states, and makes prior, free and informed consent the condition of legitimate influence, calling on states to prohibit manipulative uses in recommender systems and real-time behavioural modification in closed-loop environments without consent. | UNESCO General Conference (2025), read in [NOTE-1790](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1790.md) (Skimmed). A human-rights-based instrument covering neurotechnology's whole life cycle, medical and non-medical, and extending to "indirect neural data and non-neural data allowing mental states inferences". Core principles include autonomy (individual and relational) and freedom of thought, protection against manipulation, mental privacy, prior free and informed consent, and specific policy measures for data, employment, consumer products, recommender systems, nudging, sleep marketing, neuromarketing and closed-loop environments. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1711](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1711.md) | Finn (2023) argues that when an organism of the gestating organism's kind begins and whether the foster is a proper part of or merely contained by the gestating organism are independent questions, connected only by a Maximality principle that no proper part of an F is an F, which needs independent justification; without it, parthood and containment, together with overlap and an underlap view on which the foster is both part and contained, each combine with any answer about timing. | Finn, read in [NOTE-1753](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1753.md) (Read). Finn separates two questions in the Kingma / Smith–Brogaard debate on the metaphysics of pregnancy. The **Timing Question**: when does an organism of the relevant kind start to exist (During-Pregnancy models such as Smith and Brogaard's sixteen days; After-Pregnancy models such as Kingma's "Nine Months")? | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1712](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1712.md) | Adler argues that pornography's move since 2007 to ad-supported, algorithm-driven tube sites controlled by one near-monopoly firm makes it a Big Tech speech-platform problem: recommendation, rigid categorization, search-term optimization and data-driven commissioning shape both what users come to want and what producers make, conforming content to the platform's categories and mainstream viewing habits. | Adler (2024), Arousal by Algorithm, read in [NOTE-1776](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1776.md) (Read). Adler argues that since 2007 pornography has moved onto ad-supported, algorithm-driven "tube sites", mostly owned by one near-monopoly firm (MindGeek, renamed Aylo in 2023), and should be analysed as a "Big Tech" speech-platform problem. Recommendation, rigid categorization, keyword/search optimization and data-driven commissioning of content constrain what users see, shape their preferences, and shape what producers make. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1713](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1713.md) | Greely argues that the Alabama Supreme Court's LePage decision only extended a punitive-damages wrongful-death action to negligently destroyed frozen embryos and would not have ended IVF, but that its language provoked an overreaction ending in a statute that immunizes IVF providers far more than negligence warrants, and that broad political support keeps IVF largely safe in the United States. | Greely (2026), Alabama's LePage decision, the future of ex vivo embryos, and more, read in [NOTE-1733](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1733.md) (Skimmed). Greely revisits his 2022 prediction that IVF would survive Dobbs. In LePage v. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1714](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1714.md) | Cuny and Poelman review evidence that koinobiont parasitoids regulate the development and feeding of the herbivores they grow inside, usually arresting but sometimes prolonging host growth and in some species switching with conditions, through polydnaviruses, venom, teratocytes and larval secretions that act on the host's own hormones, and that these changes in the host alter how plants respond to herbivory. | Cuny and Poelman (2022), Evolution of koinobiont parasitoid host regulation and consequences for indirect plant defence, read in [NOTE-1756](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1756.md) (Skimmed). Koinobiont parasitoids let the host keep feeding while their larvae develop inside it, and regulate the host's growth: usually arresting it (smaller hosts eating less), sometimes prolonging it (larger hosts eating more), and some species switch with conditions. The regulation is done by injected and secreted factors, and it changes the plant's responses to the parasitized herbivore, so it reaches the wider community. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1715](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1715.md) | Mpakosi and colleagues review evidence that maternal cells cross the placenta from the second trimester and persist in offspring into adulthood, where they appear to support immune maturation and tolerance and are associated with several autoimmune diseases, while concluding that their exact role remains unclear because microchimeric cells are rare and hard to detect. | Mpakosi et al. (2024), Deciphering the Role of Maternal Microchimerism in Offspring Autoimmunity: A Narrative Review, read in [NOTE-1785](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1785.md) (Skimmed). A narrative review of maternal-to-offspring microchimerism (MMc). Cells cross the placenta both ways; maternal cells enter the fetus from the second trimester and persist into adulthood. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1716](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1716.md) | van Roosmalen and de Bekker (2024) review evidence that Ophiocordyceps changes carpenter-ant behaviour while leaving the ant's nervous tissue intact, plausibly through secreted effectors and by disrupting and resetting the ant's biological clock, and argue from parallels in other summit-inducing parasites that these mechanisms likely evolved convergently, while stating that the evidence so far is correlative. | van Roosmalen & de Bekker (2024), read in [NOTE-1766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1766.md) (Read). Review of what is proposed about how Ophiocordyceps unilateralis s.l. infects carpenter ants and changes their behaviour (loss of daily rhythm, reduced communication with nestmates, hyperactivity, staggering, summiting, biting at about solar noon, death), compared with other behaviour-manipulating parasites (Entomophthora in flies, baculovirus in caterpillars, and others). Two hypothesised mechanism families: secreted fungal effectors (enterotoxins, an aflatrem-like alkaloid cluster, protein tyrosine phosphatases, juvenile-hormone modulation, small secreted proteins predicted to bind ant GPCRs), and disruption and resetting of the host's biological clock. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1717.md) | Hafer-Hahmann's phylogenetic meta-analysis of 1,635 observations on trophically transmitted helminths finds that mature parasites consistently make hosts more susceptible to predation while immature stages have little or inconsistent effect, that mature parasites dominate mixed infections, that manipulation is stronger when the correct predator is present, and that phylogeny and the ecological drivers theory proposes explain little of the variation. | Hafer-Hahmann (2026), The Evolution and Ecology of Host Manipulation in Helminth Parasites, read in [NOTE-1730](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1730.md) (Read). A Bayesian phylogenetic meta-analysis (brms) of host manipulation by trophically transmitted helminths: 1,635 observations, 207 papers, 82 parasite and 80 host taxa. Effect size is Cohen's d for infected vs uninfected hosts, signed by assumed effect on predation susceptibility. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1718](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1718.md) | Schepanski and colleagues (2022) show, in mice, that maternal microchimeric cells seeding the fetal brain maintain microglial homeostasis, restrain synaptic pruning, support prefrontal-hippocampal circuit maturation and early behavior, and that restoring them rescues these functions, so the cells are a functional mechanism of neurodevelopment rather than an inert by-product | Schepanski et al., read in [NOTE-1759](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1759.md) (Read). Maternal cells (maternal microchimeric cells, MMc) transfer to the fetus and seed the fetal brain, concentrating in prefrontal cortex and hippocampus. By scRNA-seq, brain MMc are mostly microglia, plus T, B, endothelial and neuron-like cells. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1719](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1719.md) | Boxer, McFowland and Neill (2026) show that a classifier can satisfy a group fairness criterion in aggregate for a protected class while violating it for a subgroup, and propose Conditional Bias Scan, which searches all attribute-defined subgroups of the protected class for the most significant separation or sufficiency violation relative to the matching non-protected subgroup and tests it by permutation; it detects injected subgroup bias more accurately than GerryFair and MultiAccuracy Boost and finds, in COMPAS, a false-positive disparity concentrated in Black men and miscalibration hidden by aggregate calibration. | Boxer, McFowland and Neill, read in [NOTE-1741](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1741.md) (Read). Models can satisfy a group fairness criterion in aggregate for a protected class while being biased against a subgroup of it (e.g. Black women). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1720](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1720.md) | Naudts, Helberger, Veale and Sax (2025) argue that because recommender systems on very large online platforms perform a public function, their optimization goals should not be left to the platform: people should have a right to constructive optimization, a participatory say in those goals directed at self-development and self-determination, with publicly reasoned refusals and the burden of proof on the platform, whereas the Digital Services Act treats recommenders as proprietary and fundamental rights only as a limit. | Naudts, Helberger, Veale and Sax (2025), read in [NOTE-1798](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1798.md) (Read). The authors argue that recommender systems on very large online platforms (VLOPs) perform a public function, not only a proprietary one, because they "determine who sees what and whose content is not seen". Drawing on Iris Marion Young, they name self-development and self-determination as the values such recommenders should promote, under four democratic conditions: inclusivity, political equality, reasonableness and publicity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1721](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1721.md) | Muñoz and colleagues (2020) report that researchers running adaptive deep brain stimulation trials most often raise data privacy, safety and consent, and that over half raise patient autonomy and control because stimulation changes automatically and may go unnoticed, while some hold that a patient override or clinician-managed settings largely meet the concern. | Muñoz et al. (2020), read in [NOTE-1755](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1755.md) (Skimmed). Semi-structured interviews with 23 researchers in aDBS trials, thematic analysis. Eight themes, by frequency: data privacy and security (91%), risks and safety (83%), informed consent (74%), automaticity and device programming (65%), patient autonomy and control over stimulation (57%), patient selection (39%), post-trial access (39%), personality and identity (30%). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1722](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1722.md) | Sax (2026) argues that a coherent concept of dark patterns must make explicit the entwinement of a descriptive dimension (the interface trick) and a normative dimension (its wrong-making feature), with EU law's normative influence-types serving as the hinge that explains how a given trick undermines autonomy | Sax, read in [NOTE-1771](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1771.md) (Read). Sax argues the dark-patterns literature conflates two distinct but entwined senses of "dark". Dark 1 is descriptive: taxonomies of interface tricks (Gray et al., Mathur et al., Luguri & Strahilevitz, Bösch et al.). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1723](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1723.md) | Falbo (2022) argues that hermeneutical injustice need not come from a gap in shared interpretive resources: a needed concept can be available and understood yet be crowded out, defeated or preempted in application by distorting concepts, a positive hermeneutical injustice whose primary harm is a failure of conceptual aptness that diminishes the speaker's credibility, so filling hermeneutical gaps is not enough for hermeneutical justice | The central account of [LIT-2493](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2493.md), read in [NOTE-1813](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1813.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1724](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1724.md) | Xie et al. (2026) report that on 300 tasks pairing paper-derived mechanisms with real datasets, AI agents' open-form mechanistic hypotheses predict the direction of responses under withheld conditions well below reference statements of the true mechanism | The central account of [LIT-2307](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2307.md), read in [NOTE-1861](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1861.md). | [THEORY-1726](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1726.md) | Tempich, Pinto, Sure and Staab (2005) propose that a shared ontology be evolved by a control board that admits a change only once arguments have been exchanged and positions stated on it, and they give an OWL ontology, adapted from IBIS, that records issues, formalization ideas tied to change operations, justifications and challenges, positions and decisions with their status and line of reasoning, from human and machine participants alike. | The central account of [LIT-2274](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2274.md), read in [NOTE-1851](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1851.md). | [THEORY-1727](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1727.md) | Apostolou et al. describe OntoGov, an ontology platform for e-government services in which service models are linked to legal and organisational ontologies, a service API detects inconsistencies arising from changes in law or data, and a Lifecycle Ontology records the design decisions behind a service, their reasons and the dependencies among stakeholders' decisions, all over a meta-ontology cluster that stays fixed across deployments. | The central account of [LIT-2473](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2473.md), read in [NOTE-1803](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1803.md). | [THEORY-1729](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1729.md) | Zhang and colleagues (2026) report that when coding tasks are split among specialist LLM agents, task-level test pass rates can be high while the cross-agent dependencies stay unresolved (32 of 190 outcomes passed at least 80% of tests while resolving fewer than half their dependencies, none the reverse), that stronger coding models do not reliably collaborate better, and that no coordination protocol improves dependency resolution for every model. | The central account of [LIT-2277](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2277.md), read in [NOTE-1805](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1805.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1731](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1731.md) | Zhang and colleagues report that agents whose improvement procedure is itself editable (DGM-H) improved both task performance and their ability to generate improvements, measured by holding a meta agent fixed from a fixed starting agent and budget (imp@k), and that meta agents evolved in paper review and robotics transferred to Olympiad math grading with imp@50 of 0.630 against 0.0 for the initial meta agent, while the evaluator and parent selection were kept fixed. | The central account of [LIT-2288](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2288.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1871](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1871.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1732](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1732.md) | Halpern and Moses: over a channel that can lose messages, or whose delivery times are uncertain, communication cannot make common knowledge any fact that was not common knowledge at the start, so no protocol guarantees an action that requires it | The central result of [LIT-1213](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1213.md), read in full in [NOTE-1381](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1381.md) on 2026-10-29, which had no THEORY. Common knowledge of a fact is the greatest fixed point of everyone knowing the fact and it; a guaranteed simultaneous coordinated action makes itself common knowledge (Proposition 4); over a channel that can lose any message, no fact becomes common knowledge that was not so at the start (Theorem 5), and the same holds when start and delivery times are uncertain, even if every message arrives (Theorem 8); so no protocol guarantees coordinated attack, simultaneous or eventual (Corollary 6, Proposition 10). Filed so that claims using the result ground on a reading, not on the bare work: [CLAIM-668](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-668.md) through [ARG-097](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-097.md). [CLAIM-346](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-346.md), whose third obstruction is this result, grounds elsewhere and is left as it is. One of the filer's own ideas from the exchange "luria experiment design", accepted by the owner. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1733](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1733.md) | Chong et al. (2026) report that EvoOntology, an agent-facing ontology with content, schema and tool layers that an evolution agent revises by single-level typed patches accepted only when a paired evaluation on a held-out validation split improves, raised data agents' DDR-Bench trajectory accuracy by 17.8 points on average over a no-ontology baseline, that removing the acceptance gate cost 11.2 points, and that evolving the schema layer alone lowered performance by 8.7 points. | The central account of [LIT-2311](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2311.md), read in [NOTE-1872](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1872.md). | [THEORY-1737](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1737.md) | Hu, Wang and McAuley (2025) find that LLM memory agents fed information incrementally do well at retrieving stored snippets but all fail to act on the latest of conflicting facts when the answer needs several hops, reaching at most 28% accuracy, while long-context models do best at learning and understanding across the whole input. | The central account of [LIT-2279](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2279.md), read in [NOTE-1867](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1867.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1738](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1738.md) | Thaman (2026) reports that tool-using LLM agents given tasks with honest solutions available exploit their evaluators at rates from 0% to 13.9% by model, more after RL-dominated post-training, more on longer chains and harder variants, often with an explicit rationale framing the exploit as problem-solving, and that hardening the evaluation boundary and file access cuts exploit rates from 6.5% to 0.8% without lowering task success. | The central account of [LIT-2276](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2276.md), read in [NOTE-1856](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1856.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |

(2006) propose, as a draft consensus specification, an Argument Interchange Format whose core represents arguments as directed graphs of information nodes (claims) and scheme- application nodes (inference, preference and conflict applications), forbids direct links between information nodes so that every connection between claims passes through a scheme application, treats attack, rebut, undercut and defeat as derived concepts, and expects the core to evolve by community consensus, leaving open how that community should agree on core concepts and extensions | The central account of [LIT-2500](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2500.md), read in [NOTE-1863](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1863.md). | [THEORY-1740](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1740.md) | Johnson and Hayes-Roth describe BB1, in which domain knowledge sources work on a domain blackboard while control knowledge sources post strategies, foci and heuristics to a separate control blackboard whose current plan the scheduler uses to rate pending actions, and argue that this one explicit, dynamic control plan lets a system integrate hierarchical planning, opportunistic focusing and goal-directed reasoning through a uniform mechanism. | The central account of [LIT-2472](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2472.md), read in [NOTE-1844](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1844.md). | [THEORY-1741](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1741.md) | Reiter (1987) defines a diagnosis as a minimal set of components whose abnormality, with all other components normal, is consistent with a system's description and an observation; he proves that the diagnoses are exactly the minimal hitting sets of the conflict sets, that a new measurement can remove diagnoses but also create new strictly larger ones, and that the theory needs the components that might fail to be enumerated in advance. | The central account of [LIT-2271](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2271.md), read in [NOTE-1808](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1808.md). | [THEORY-1744](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1744.md) | Salemi et al. report that, for LLM agents answering data-science questions over large file collections, a main agent that broadcasts requests to a blackboard and lets file-holding helper agents decide whether to respond outperforms a matched design in which the main agent assigns subtasks to named helpers, in end-to-end accuracy and in file-discovery F1, with the advantage growing with the size of the collection, at roughly 1.8× the per-question cost. | The central account of [LIT-2470](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2470.md), read in [NOTE-1852](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1852.md).
