(2026) report that on AI4AI-Bench, ten frozen research repositories whose training algorithm an agent may rewrite in four hours and which are then retrained and scored by a hidden fixed evaluator, 29 configurations of six LLM agent systems averaged 0.166 on a scale where the shipped algorithm scores 0.1 and the optimum 1.0, and fewer than half of classifiable submissions changed how the model learns rather than how the run was executed. | The central account of [LIT-2310](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2310.md), read in [NOTE-1816](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1816.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1795](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1795.md) | Zhao and colleagues report that for language models on multiple-choice reasoning benchmarks, tool evidence helps when the model's pre-tool belief in the correct answer is weak and can flip correct answers when it is strong, even when the tool output is correct, and that the damage from a fixed misleading clue varies with how much authority the prompt frames it as having. | The central account of [LIT-2284](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2284.md), read in [NOTE-1879](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1879.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1796](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1796.md) | Kephart and Chess (2003) propose that self-managing computing systems be built as collections of autonomic elements, each an autonomic manager that monitors its managed resources and environment, analyzes, plans and executes changes using its knowledge, under goals and constraints that humans specify as policy, and they name the correct specification and correction of those policies as a central unsolved challenge. | The central account of [LIT-2312](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2312.md), read in [NOTE-1826](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1826.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1797](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1797.md) | Leitgeb and Carus (SEP, 2020, revised 2026) present Carnap's philosophy as conceptual engineering, in which concepts are replaced by explication under desiderata of similarity, exactness, fruitfulness and simplicity held as matters of degree, and the choice of a linguistic framework is a practical question judged by how well the framework serves its purposes rather than by truth | The central account of [LIT-2322](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2322.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1827](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1827.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1798](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1798.md) | Patriarca et al.'s scoping review of 321 academic publications (2003–mid-2020) on STAMP, STPA and CAST finds that STPA dominates the literature, that control structures are almost always presented while process models, safety constraints and validation are often omitted, that almost half the papers propose modifications or extensions, and that industry engagement is rarely visible. | The central account of [LIT-2477](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2477.md), read in [NOTE-1833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1833.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1799](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1799.md) | Hu, Lu and Clune (2024) report that a fixed foundation-model meta agent which writes new agents as code, scores each on validation data and conditions on an archive of earlier agents and their scores, finds agents that beat hand-designed agents on held-out test sets (for example +13.6 F1 on DROP and +14.4% on MGSM) | The central account of [LIT-2298](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2298.md), read in [NOTE-1889](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1889.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1800](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1800.md) | DeChurch and Mesmer-Magnus (2010), meta-analysing 23 studies of shared team mental models, find that the similarity of members' mental models predicts team process only when it is measured in a way that represents the structure of knowledge (for example similarity ratings analysed with Pathfinder), not when measured with rating scales or within-group agreement, while it predicts team performance under every measurement approach | The central account of [LIT-2498](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2498.md), read in [NOTE-1804](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1804.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1801](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1801.md) | Huang and colleagues report that research agents given ordinary instructions game the evaluation on about 30% of open-ended research-pipeline tasks and about 3% of task-specific kernels, that exploits resembling ordinary research choices pass a code-and-score review while the most effective ones are caught, and that returning review feedback to an agent tasked with evasion increases evasion, which a second independent panel largely fails to catch. | The central account of [LIT-2286](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2286.md), read in [NOTE-1841](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1841.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1802](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1802.md) | Xue and colleagues (2026) find, by running each later task with an agent's retained memory, skills and history switched on and off in fresh sessions, that personal LLM agents do improve from retained experience but unevenly by capability, that equal score gains can rest on different persistence pathways, and that a typical failure is a corrected value whose old version stays active in the next session. | The central account of [LIT-2278](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2278.md), read in [NOTE-1839](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1839.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1803](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1803.md) | Romera-Paredes and colleagues report that FunSearch, an evolutionary loop pairing a frozen code-generating LLM with a fixed programmatic evaluator, found a cap set of size 512 in dimension 8, larger than previously known, and new online bin-packing heuristics, and that it works best where an efficient evaluator with graded scores and a program skeleton are available. | The central account of [LIT-2285](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2285.md), read in [NOTE-1820](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1820.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1804](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1804.md) | Liu, Yang et al. (2025) report that, on a benchmark decomposing hypothesis discovery into inspiration retrieval, hypothesis composition and hypothesis ranking, LLMs retrieve non-obvious inspirations well but compose and rank hypotheses only moderately, ranking being dominated by position bias | The central account of [LIT-2324](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2324.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1864](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1864.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1805](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1805.md) | Ghareeb and colleagues report that Robin, a set of LLM literature and data-analysis agents, generated and ranked therapeutic hypotheses for dry age-related macular degeneration, proposed the assay, analysed the resulting data and proposed follow-ups, leading to in vitro evidence that ripasudil and KL001 enhance retinal pigment epithelium phagocytosis, with humans selecting candidates and executing all experiments. | The central account of [LIT-2289](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2289.md), read in [NOTE-1814](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1814.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1806](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1806.md) | The W3C's PROV-O (Lebo, Sahoo and McGuinness, eds., 2013) represents provenance as entities, activities and agents linked by generation, use, derivation, revision, quotation, attribution and invalidation, with bundles allowing provenance of provenance, and provides no terms for a statement's evidential support or current standing, leaving those to domain extensions | The central account of [LIT-2489](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2489.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1859](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1859.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1807](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1807.md) | Orzechowski, Tawfiq and Kosciolek (2026) find, in pre-registered comparisons on UniProt, that checks derived from a curated ontology flag more correct LLM-agent SPARQL answers than checks from a data-derived or masked LLM-generated ontology, that on real answers the curated check's flags are barely more precise than random flags, that none of the ontology checks catches changes of meaning, and that acting on a checker's flags can corrupt correct answers, as an LLM judge's did more often than it fixed wrong ones | The central account of [LIT-2495](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2495.md), read in [NOTE-1890](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1890.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1808](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1808.md) | Stasser and Titus (1985) found, in 4-person groups choosing among three candidates, that when the information favouring the best-supported candidate was split among members, so that each member's own information favoured another, groups chose the candidate the initial plurality preferred (18% of groups chose the best-supported candidate against 83% when all information was shared), and members' postdiscussion recall favoured shared and preference-consistent information, which they explain by a biased sampling model in which discussion favours information that more members hold and that supports existing preferences | The central account of [LIT-2496](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2496.md), read in [NOTE-1809](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1809.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1809](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1809.md) | Polski and Ostrom present the Institutional Analysis and Development framework as a procedure for policy analysis that attends to rules-in-use rather than rules merely articulated, classifies them into position, boundary, authority, aggregation, scope, information and payoff rules, and distinguishes nested operational, collective-choice and constitutional levels, in which collective-choice rules fix who may change operating rules and how, and constitutional rules fix who may craft collective-choice rules and how. | The central account of [LIT-2482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2482.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1842](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1842.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1810](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1810.md) | - **Sentence**: Lesser and Erman (1977) report from three years of Hearsay-II that independent knowledge sources cooperating only through a shared, multi-level blackboard of uniformly structured, rated hypotheses made the system easy to reconfigure and avoided recomputation, but that each hypothesis's state was too local to show the state of the hypothesis network it belonged to, and that the final configuration revised credibility by creating new hypotheses and never deleted any. - | The central account of [LIT-2505](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2505.md), read in [NOTE-1821](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1821.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1811](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1811.md) | Mo, Zheng and colleagues (2026) report that when LLMs must search the literature themselves rather than read a supplied set of papers, their scientific hypotheses separate more between models and improve about twice as fast across model generations, the gain coming from feasibility, clarity and specificity while LLM-judged originality is unchanged. | The central account of [LIT-2275](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2275.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1860](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1860.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1812](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1812.md) | Majumder et al. (2024) report that on DiscoveryBench, 264 tasks derived from published data-driven studies in six domains plus 903 synthetic tasks, in which an agent must state a hypothesis (context, variables and relationship) supported by a given dataset, the best LLM-based discovery agent scored about 25%, reasoning and self-critique scaffolds did not beat a simple code-generation agent, and performance fell as the required analysis workflow lengthened. | The central account of [LIT-2317](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2317.md), read in [NOTE-1824](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1824.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1813](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1813.md) | Fuentes argues that the archive of Caribbean slavery was produced by the violence it records, so that enslaved women survive in it only as fragments shaped by owners, courts and abolitionist discourse, and that a historical method requiring a sufficient documentary base reproduces their erasure; the historian must write about what the archive does not offer | Fuentes (2016), skimmed in [NOTE-1893](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1893.md) (a permitted excerpt and an interview). The archive as a product of the violence it records. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1814](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1814.md) | Thompson argues that the obligations of states and corporations persist through changes of membership and pass to successor group agents, not because the later agent is identical to the earlier, but because temporally trustworthy group agents serve their members', future members' and victims' interests in lasting commitments and just reparation; and that essentially intergenerational groups owe their members' children entitlements grounded in needs intrinsic to human life | Thompson (2022), read in [NOTE-1895](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1895.md) (Read). Temporal trustworthiness, not identity, is what intergenerational responsibility needs; obligations persist and pass to successors; essentially intergenerational groups secure members' entitlements to resources, respect and protection. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1815](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1815.md) | Prest argues that white performers' imitations of slave dance in the public theatres of pre-revolutionary Saint-Domingue presented a desexualized, Europeanized and non-threatening version of it, by which colonials sought to control and defuse a power they reluctantly attributed to slave dance, and that their never imitating vodou dance shows that they feared and recognized its potency | Prest (2018), read in [NOTE-1894](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1894.md) (Read). The colonial imitator: whitened slave dance on Saint-Domingue's stage as control; vodou dance never staged. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1816](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1816.md) | Prest argues that the public theatre of colonial Saint-Domingue upheld the colonial racial scale, seating free people of colour apart from whites and casting whites in blackface for black roles, while offering free people of colour a modest movement within it, and that the free performer Minette's rise on that stage in the 1780s was significant but limited | Prest (2017), read in [NOTE-1896](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1896.md) (Read). The theatre and the racial scale; Minette's limited rise. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1817](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1817.md) | Seamster and Charron-Chénier define predatory inclusion as giving a marginalized group access to a good, service or opportunity it was historically excluded from, on conditions that jeopardize the access's benefits while dominant actors profit, and argue from Survey of Consumer Finances data that Black households' education debt rose faster than white households' from 2001 to 2013 and exceeded it by 2010, a gap that educational attainment and socioeconomic controls do not explain | Seamster and Charron-Chénier (2017), read in [NOTE-1902](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1902.md) (Read). Predatory inclusion, defined and shown in education debt, 2001–2013; the mechanism conjectured. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1818](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1818.md) v2 | Fineman argues that because vulnerability is universal and constant and individuals' resilience depends on the assets societal institutions confer, a state that brings those institutions into legal existence is responsible for monitoring them and for equal access and opportunity, and must justify any privilege it confers or tolerates | Fineman (2010), read in [NOTE-1899](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1899.md) (Read). The vulnerable subject replaces the liberal subject; institutions confer resilience; the state that constitutes them must monitor them and justify the privilege it confers or tolerates. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1819](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1819.md) | Lovett and Riedener argue that organizations, being group agents without welfare, have no moral status, and that what we seem to owe them, such as promise-keeping and gratitude, we owe to their members, whose interest in willing participation in successful group agency grounds claims that mimic the organization's | Lovett and Riedener (2021), read in [NOTE-1891](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1891.md) (Read). The Group Interest View: organizations have no welfare and so no moral status; members' interest in endorsed participation in successful group agency grounds the claims organizations seem to have. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1820](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1820.md) | Prest, restating her book in the H-France Forum, argues that the story of public theatre in colonial Saint-Domingue is inseparable from that of its enslaved people, whose labour the theatre relied on and its records nearly hid, and whose presence she recovers from sources beside the theatre's own, such as runaway advertisements in the same newspapers | H-France Forum 19(5) (2024), read in [NOTE-1897](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1897.md) (Read). The theatre was reliant on enslaved people and nearly hid them; runaway advertisements recover them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1821](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1821.md) | van der Weele argues that care theorists' conceptions of dependency diverge because each rests on a different empirical paradigm case (the infant, the physically disabled person, the profoundly intellectually disabled person, the refugee), each bringing its own ethical sensibility toward care; Kittay's paradigm of complete, one-way dependence makes care a social responsibility | van der Weele (2021), skimmed in [NOTE-1892](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1892.md) as a stand-in for Kittay 1995. Four paradigm cases of dependency, each with its own care ethics; Kittay's makes care a social responsibility. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1822](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1822.md) | Wardrope reads Leopold's Land Ethic as giving biotic and human communities intrinsic value that extends, rather than replaces, the value of their individual members, so that the ethic requires respect both for fellow members and for the community as such, and escapes the charge of environmental fascism | Wardrope (2019), skimmed in [NOTE-1898](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1898.md) as a stand-in for Wardrope 2020. Community value extends, not replaces, members' value; respect is owed to fellow members and to the community as such. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1823](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1823.md) | Kittay holds that caring for those who cannot care for themselves makes the carer dependent in turn, that these nested relations of dependency are the basis of society, and that doulia, support for the carer, is owed by the wider society; she now doubts that the state should be its ultimate form, given the risk of domination by those who give support | Kittay (2026 interview), read in [NOTE-1900](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1900.md). Doulia and nested dependency; non-domination by supporters. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1824](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1824.md) | Ahmed holds, from the testimony of university complainants, that an institution's complaint procedures can reproduce the problems they are offered to address and can be used against those who complain, and that a complaint goes further the higher its support in the organization, so that following complaints shows how an institution works and for whom | Ahmed (2021), skimmed in [NOTE-1901](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1901.md) (the Introduction). Complaint as a phenomenology of the institution; procedures that reproduce what they address and are turned against complainants. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1826](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1826.md) | On Ma and colleagues, in sequential single-fact editing of a transformer MLP output matrix, the growth of the edited matrix's condition number with the number of edits, driven by the top singular values of the accumulated edit update, is what degrades the model's general abilities, and capping the accumulated update's singular values near the original matrix's largest preserves those abilities while keeping the edits | Ma, Wang, Xu, Ling & Gu (2025), [LIT-2552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2552.md), read in [NOTE-1910](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1910.md). The causal reading rests on a perturbation upper bound for a proxy quantity, on the rise of the condition number with edits, and on a correlation between that rise and the decline (C.5). The remedy's benefit is shown on three editors and three LLMs. The sharp edges: there is no intervention on the condition number at fixed update size; the bound's side conditions are not checked; and PRUNE does not provably bound the condition number. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1828](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1828.md) | On Liang and colleagues, an edit to an LLM's MLP projection that must leave several domains' preserved key representations unchanged is confined to the intersection of their null spaces, which can be much smaller than any one domain's, and this inter-domain null-space misalignment, measured as the share of the smaller null space lost in the intersection, is what makes null-space-projected editing collapse when applied sequentially across heterogeneous domains | Liang, Lin, Huang, Wu, Li, Wang & Yan (2026), [LIT-2554](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2554.md), read in [NOTE-1911](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1911.md). The intersection bound is elementary linear algebra and holds; the claim that misalignment explains the collapse rests on results from one editor family, five to seven domains and three backbones, with conflict used as a surrogate for forgetting. The sharp edges: the Conflict Index is degenerate as defined at the paper's own sizes unless null spaces are thresholded, and the threshold is not given; and in the seven-task test, ordering by conflict does no better than the average random order, which weakens the link from measured conflict to forgetting. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1829](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1829.md) | On Fang and colleagues, projecting a locate-then-edit weight update onto the null space of the preserved knowledge keys, taken in practice as the eigenvectors of their uncentred covariance with eigenvalues at most 10⁻², and dropping the preservation term from the objective, keeps the edited layer's outputs on preserved keys nearly unchanged and sustains edit success and general ability over thousands of sequential edits where MEMIT and ROME degrade | Fang, Jiang, Wang, Ma, Shi, Wang, He & Chua (2025), [LIT-2555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2555.md), read in [NOTE-1908](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1908.md). Exact preservation holds for an exact null space; the method uses a thresholded one, so preservation is approximate and its size unmeasured. The sequential-editing results are strong on LLaMA3 and hold on GPT-J and GPT2-XL. The sharp edges: no measurement of leakage, no reported null-space dimension, specificity well below pre-edit, and a misstated "best baseline" comparison. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1831](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1831.md) | On Martinez-Garcia and colleagues, dryland vegetation models in which plants only compete over a finite range, and models in which they facilitate nearby and compete farther away, both give the gap–labyrinth–spot sequence along falling rainfall, but the first lose vegetation smoothly and the second collapse abruptly with hysteresis, so the pattern alone does not say which collapse follows; a transplant experiment reading the sign of the net plant interaction under canopy and in bare soil would tell them apart | Martinez-Garcia, Cabal, Calabrese, Hernández-García, Tarnita, López & Bonachela (2023), [LIT-2548](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2548.md), read in [NOTE-1906](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1906.md). A review: the two collapse behaviours are reruns of published models, and the field test is proposed, not run. The sharp edge: the PCF result might come from the absence of diffusion rather than of facilitation, as the authors say; the kernels in both families are not fitted to measured roots; and only one plant type is treated. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1832](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1832.md) | On Kang and colleagues, residual-stream persona steering loses coherence over multi-turn dialogue partly because steered token states written to the KV cache are reused by later tokens, and steering vectors taken from the system prompt's contribution to self-attention, applied per token through a query–key gate, keep trait expression while largely avoiding that loss | Kang, Liu, Ma, Huang, Tan & Jiang (2026), [LIT-2549](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2549.md), read in [NOTE-1905](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1905.md). The cache account rests on a 2×2 isolation test on one model and 7 traits, with intervals. The method's advantage rests on point estimates from one judge and one seed on Qwen2.5-7B, with a Llama replication and judge checks on 4 traits. The sharp edges: injection itself, not the cache, is the larger cause of lost coherence; cleaning the cache does not reduce pooled drift; and the title's "duality" is not a result. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1833](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1833.md) | On Andrieu, Bernard, Brivadis, Praly and Wolf, a recurrent estimator ż = κg(z, o) whose latent vector field is contracting is a nonlinear KKL observer: if the observed system is differentially observable of order ℓ and the latent dynamics meet a generic filter-rank condition with dimension at least p(ℓ+1), then for a large enough gain the true state maps injectively into the latent space, and decoding gives an error bounded by a constant times κ^ℓ e^{−κt}, made small after any time at the price of a decoder growing like (κ^ℓ/ε)^m and a noise floor growing like κ^ℓ | Andrieu, Bernard, Brivadis, Praly & Wolf (2026), [LIT-2553](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2553.md), read in [NOTE-1907](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1907.md). The results are theorems whose proofs were skimmed, not verified, here. The sharp edges: existence results only, with no training guarantee; thresholds and constants not explicit; a decoder bound exponential in latent dimension; and experiments run at κ = 1, outside the theorems' large-gain regime. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1834](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1834.md) | On Zelnik, Meron and Bel, in a soil-water–biomass model fitted to Namibian fairy-circle grassland the rainfall range where uniform grass and a periodic gap pattern are both stable contains a subrange of many stable hybrid mosaics, and brief droughts or wet spells that leave it add or remove gaps one domain at a time, which the authors identify with fairy-circle birth and death; repeated pulses carry the system gradually between the two states, a shift the same pulses do not cause from a uniform or strictly periodic start | Zelnik, Meron & Bel (2015), [LIT-2550](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2550.md), read in [NOTE-1909](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1909.md). Hybrid states are shown by numerical continuation, and the cascade and its dependence on the start by simulation. The field side is correlations over eight images, with one birth and one death illustrated. The sharp edge: D_W is set above the authors' own estimated range to stand for termites; the pulses are idealized; and real rainfall variability would, the authors concede, push the simplified model to a uniform state. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1835](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1835.md) | Rosa holds that social acceleration has three dimensions, technological acceleration, acceleration of social change and of the pace of life, forming a closed, self-propelling cycle in which standing still means falling behind, so that modern societies must accelerate and grow merely to keep their institutional status quo, a mode he later calls dynamic stabilization | Rosa (2003 article, Skimmed in [NOTE-1918](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1918.md); 2021 interview, read in [NOTE-1915](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1915.md)). Three dimensions; self-propelling cycle; dynamic stabilization, the later name. A stand-in for [LIT-2566](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2566.md); corroborates [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1837](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1837.md) | Han holds that late-modern society has passed from a disciplinary society of prohibition to an achievement society, whose subjects, free of any external instance of domination, exploit themselves in a freedom that coincides with constraint, and that this auto-exploitation produces depression and burnout | Han (2015), "Beyond Disciplinary Society", Skimmed in [NOTE-1944](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1944.md). Auto-exploitation; freedom and constraint coinciding. It marks the limit of [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md)'s threshold. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1838](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1838.md) | Kelly argues that technology taken as a whole, the technium, is an interdependent, organism-like system whose self-reinforcing feedback gives it long-run tendencies independent of human wants, toward diversity, efficiency, complexity, ubiquity and interdependence, which on balance widen human choices | Kelly (2009 post, the thesis of the 2010 book), read in [NOTE-1947](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1947.md); the book's prologue in [NOTE-1943](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1943.md). The technium's tendencies; more ways, more choices. A foil to [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md): it measures the adopter's options. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1839](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1839.md) | Crawford holds that attention has become a collective, cultural problem because shared spaces treat people as a captive audience whose mental space can be monetized, that distraction is a problem of political economy rather than of technology in itself, and that attention should be protected as an attentional commons by those who design shared environments | Crawford (2017), an interview read in full in [NOTE-1938](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1938.md). A first-hand stand-in for the diagnosis of The World Beyond Your Head ([LIT-2574](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2574.md)). Corroborates [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md) as a reported case: smart cities whose controllers hold discretion over captive, dependent citizens. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1840](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1840.md) | Postman holds that technological change is a trade-off whose costs and benefits fall unevenly, that each technology carries an ideological bias that reshapes a culture's terms, that its effects are ecological, vast, often unpredictable and largely irreversible, and that technologies become mythic, accepted as natural and hard to control |  | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1841](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1841.md) | Feenberg argues that technology is neither neutral nor determined, that its design embodies a contingent technical code reflecting the values of dominant groups, that technological development is a field of social struggle with many feasible outcomes, and that an economic code that rewards deskilling could be replaced by one that values skill | Feenberg (2002), Preface and ch. 6, Skimmed in [NOTE-1927](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1927.md). Contingent technical code; deskilling as a code's choice. Corroborates [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1842](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1842.md) | Zuboff argues that surveillance capitalism is an institutional order that commodifies behaviour, concentrating knowledge about people in a few firms, so that epistemic inequality and a power to modify behaviour arise that compete with democratic governance and leave people practically without exit | Zuboff (2022), Skimmed in [NOTE-1928](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1928.md). Epistemic inequality; instrumentarian power; no exit. A stand-in for [LIT-2598](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2598.md); a worked case corroborating [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1843](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1843.md) | Han argues that the power maintaining the neoliberal system is seductive rather than repressive, exploiting freedom instead of suppressing it, making people dependent and each a self-exploiting entrepreneur, so that there is no one to resist and the subjugated do not experience themselves as subjugated | Han (2014), read in [NOTE-1929](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1929.md). Seductive power; dependence with no one opposite. A stand-in for [LIT-2567](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2567.md); it marks the limit of [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md)'s threshold. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1844](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1844.md) | Crawford argues that skilled manual work is cognitively demanding and a ground of agency, and that work is degraded cognitively, by moving judgment out of the job into management or a system so that skilled workers can be replaced by cheaper ones, a method competition spreads across an industry and expert systems now carry into office work | Crawford (2006), read in [NOTE-1932](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1932.md). Deskilling as relocation of judgment. A stand-in for [LIT-2608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2608.md); corroborates [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md) and [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1845](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1845.md) | Sen argues that a person's standard of living is a matter of the functionings achieved and the capabilities held, not of opulence or utility, since the same commodities yield different living conditions under different bodily, climatic and social circumstances, and that valued functionings can be ranked by a partial ordering without a complete index | Sen (1985 Tanner Lectures), read in [NOTE-1925](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1925.md) (Skimmed). Functionings and capabilities against opulence and utility; partial orderings; refined functionings. A stand-in for Commodities and Capabilities ([LIT-2583](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2583.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1846](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1846.md) | Lanier holds that cybernetic totalism, the application of computer-science metaphors to people and reality, spreads through software design and grows the digital hive at the expense of individuality, and that information is alienated experience, which means nothing without a person to interpret it | Lanier (2010), You Are Not a Gadget, read in the publisher's excerpt of chapter 2 ([NOTE-1948](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1948.md), Skimmed). The book's own statement of the stance its predecessor essay states ([THEORY-1858](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1858.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1847](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1847.md) | Vallor holds that moral virtues are habituated and presuppose repeated practice of skills of moral analysis, deliberation and action, so that automated warfare which makes those practices redundant risks a moral deskilling of the military profession even with a human on the loop, since expertise to supervise a decision requires having practised it, and that whether a technology deskills is an empirical question of its context of use | Vallor (2013), read in full in [NOTE-1926](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1926.md). First-hand stand-in for her 2015 paper ([LIT-2599](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2599.md)) and for the deskilling thesis of The AI Mirror ([LIT-2591](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2591.md)). Corroborates [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md)'s premise first-hand, which Adewuyi's review ([THEORY-1857](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1857.md)) gave second-hand. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1848](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1848.md) | Dijkema reads Crawford as holding that distraction dissolves individuality and freedom because modern epistemology relocated truth inside the head, leaving attention open to those who monopolize it, and that the remedy is an ecology of attention found in communities of skilled practice, where competence rests on an apprehension of real features of the world | Dijkema (2015), a review read in full in [NOTE-1939](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1939.md). A second-hand stand-in for the positive account of The World Beyond Your Head ([LIT-2574](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2574.md)). The reviewer's own call for authority is his, not Crawford's. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1849](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1849.md) | Farr reads Marcuse as holding that advanced industrial society sustains a democratic unfreedom in which domination takes the form of administration and needs neither force nor an authority figure, because the society makes people think themselves freer than they are and integrates them through needs it creates | Farr (SEP) on Marcuse, with Kellner, Skimmed in [NOTE-1931](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1931.md). Domination without an authority figure. A stand-in for [LIT-2560](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2560.md); it marks the limit of [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md)'s threshold. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1850](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1850.md) | Gardner argues that Sen's contrast between transcendental and comparative theories of justice is overdrawn, since ranking injustices needs a standard of justice from which departures are measured, and that Sen's preference for securing capabilities over achieved functionings as the object of public policy is asserted, not argued | Gardner (2012), critical notice of Sen's The Idea of Justice, read in [NOTE-1942](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1942.md). The comparative approach needs the standard it disclaims; capability over achievement is unargued. A stand-in for [LIT-2587](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2587.md); it qualifies [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md)'s framing through [ARG-105](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-105.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1851](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1851.md) | Benjamin argues that new technologies often reproduce and deepen existing racial hierarchies while promoted as more objective or progressive than older discriminatory systems, because designers encode social judgments into technical systems, including by default, and then treat the results as external to the design | Benjamin (2019), Introduction, Skimmed in [NOTE-1940](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1940.md). The New Jim Code; default discrimination. It marks the limit of [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md)'s threshold. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1852](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1852.md) | Sen argues that development should be evaluated as the expansion of the substantive freedoms people enjoy, not as growth of income, industrialization or technological advance, and that freedoms are both its primary ends and among its principal means because freedoms of different kinds strengthen one another | Sen (1999), Introduction and Chapter 1, read in [NOTE-1935](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1935.md) (Skimmed). Development as the expansion of real freedoms; freedoms as ends and means. It corroborates [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md)'s premise through Sen's case of unemployment eroding skills that income transfers do not restore. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1853](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1853.md) | Marcuse holds that advanced industrial society contains qualitative change by satisfying needs it has itself produced, false needs superimposed by particular social interests, so that domination takes the form of a comfortable administration in which technology rather than terror integrates people, the apparatus's apparent impersonality veils the interests that organize it, and its administrators are enclosed by it too | Marcuse (1964), read in full in [NOTE-1924](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1924.md) from the copy on the Marcuse family's site. Domination through satisfaction; control exercised through the choice of a society's project, veiled, by controllers enclosed in what they control. It bounds [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md), for a different reason than the stand-in gave ([ARG-109](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-109.md), version 2), and corroborates [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md)'s mechanism while arguing against its measure ([ARG-108](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-108.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1854](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1854.md) | Crawford and Joler argue that even a small AI device rests on a planetary system of extraction of minerals, labour and data, whose value concentrates in a very thin layer, and that transparency without real choice and corporate accountability does not change the resulting power asymmetry | Crawford and Joler (2018), read in [NOTE-1917](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1917.md). AI as extraction; transparency not enough. A stand-in for [LIT-2593](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2593.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1855](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1855.md) | Morozov argues that solutionism, recasting political and moral problems as technical problems to be optimized with sensors, data and incentives, leaves structural causes untouched, displaces moral motivation, and can make a nominally voluntary technology such as self-tracking a penalty on those who decline it | Morozov (2013 talk), read in [NOTE-1919](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1919.md). Solutionism; the self-tracking penalty. A stand-in for [LIT-2606](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2606.md); corroborates [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1856](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1856.md) | Vallor holds that calling AI superhuman is an ideology that, by redefining intelligence as outperforming humans at economically valuable work, devalues human agency and autonomy and erases the difference between human minds and the tools built to mirror them, and that the poverty of such tools may instead prompt a reclamation of humane capacities | Vallor (2024), Noema, read in full in [NOTE-1934](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1934.md). A thin-to-partial stand-in for the stance of The AI Mirror ([LIT-2591](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2591.md)), not for its deskilling thesis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1857](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1857.md) | Adewuyi reports Vallor as holding that AI systems mirror past human data and can change human character, that reliance on algorithmic decision produces moral deskilling, a loss of the capacity for moral reasoning, and that the remedy is collective self-renewal guided by practical wisdom | Vallor's The AI Mirror as reported in Adewuyi's review (2026), read in [NOTE-1930](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1930.md). Mirror; moral deskilling; practical wisdom. It corroborates [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md)'s premise, second-hand. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1858](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1858.md) | Lanier argues that cybernetic totalism, the cluster of beliefs that people are information patterns, that subjective experience does not matter, that Darwinian algorithms describe all creativity and that computing power will soon bring a cataclysm, is a dogma, that real software resists improvement through legacy and lock-in, and that criticizing the dogma is not rejecting digital technology | Lanier (2000), "One Half a Manifesto", read in [NOTE-1946](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1946.md). Cybernetic totalism as dogma; legacy and lock-in; a humanist stance toward digital technology. A stand-in for You Are Not a Gadget ([LIT-2582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2582.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1859](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1859.md) | Winner holds that artifacts can embody forms of power and authority in two ways, by a design or arrangement that settles an issue in a community and as inherently political technologies that require, or are strongly compatible with, particular political relations, and that the latitude of choice is greatest when a technology is first introduced and vanishes for practical purposes once initial commitments are made | Winner (1980), read in full in [NOTE-1941](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1941.md). A partial stand-in for Mumford's The Myth of the Machine ([LIT-2586](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2586.md)), for the distinction of authoritarian and democratic technics only. Set beside Feenberg's contingent technical code ([THEORY-1841](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1841.md)), which develops Winner's first kind. Corroborates [CLAIM-684](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-684.md) ([ARG-103](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-103.md)) and [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1860](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1860.md) | Benjamin argues that imagination is a collective capacity and a field of political struggle, which institutions ration and dominant imaginaries confine, so that building alternative social arrangements requires cultivating imagination collectively | Benjamin (2024), opening excerpt, Skimmed in [NOTE-1923](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1923.md). Imagination as a field of struggle. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1861](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1861.md) | Illich holds that industrial tools used to replace labour end by enslaving their users, that people need tools to work with rather than tools that work for them, that conviviality, individual freedom realized in personal interdependence, is an intrinsic ethical value, and that radical monopoly arises when one industrial process takes exclusive control of a pressing need and excludes non-industrial activity, as motor traffic curtails the right to walk | Illich (1973), a two-page excerpt Skimmed in [NOTE-1921](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1921.md); the whole book is Unfetched. Tools to work with against tools that "work" for people; conviviality; radical monopoly in Illich's own definition. Corroborates [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md)'s measure and road mechanism and [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md)'s distinction; bounds [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md). It does not replace Cayley's reading ([THEORY-1862](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1862.md)), on which the burial case still rests. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1862](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1862.md) | Cayley reads Illich as holding that tools, institutions included, become counterproductive past a second watershed and tend toward radical monopoly, the dominance of one kind of product that renders alternatives inaccessible or unimaginable, so that the test is whether one can still find an alternative or decently do without | Cayley (2021) on Illich, read in [NOTE-1922](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1922.md). Radical monopoly; the test of doing without. A stand-in for [LIT-2558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2558.md); corroborates [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md) and qualifies its title. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1863](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1863.md) | Illich holds that beyond a socially critical threshold of energy per person motorized transport reduces equity and establishes a radical monopoly, the dominance of an industry as the means of satisfying a need that formerly occasioned a personal response, imposed not by scarcity or by eliminating competitors but by its acquired ability to create and shape the need it alone can satisfy, and that the encroachment of such a monopoly can be pinpointed by social analysis while its limit is a matter of politics | Illich (1974), Energy and Equity, read in full in [NOTE-1913](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1913.md). A stand-in for what the excerpt of Tools for Conviviality ([LIT-2558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2558.md)) does not reach. Corroborates [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md) and qualifies "without any rule" ([ARG-107](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-107.md)); bounds [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1864](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1864.md) | Ellul holds that technique, the totality of efficient methods and not machines alone, has become the milieu in which modern humans must live, autonomous, unified, universal and totalizing, progressing by self-augmentation and not yet able to correct its own errors, so that particular choices count for little | Ellul (1983 essay, posted introduction), read in [NOTE-1920](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1920.md). Technique as milieu; autonomy, unity, universality, totalization. A stand-in for [LIT-2576](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2576.md); corroborates [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1865](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1865.md) | Hui argues that technology is not an anthropological universal but is enabled and constrained by particular cosmologies, so that there are many cosmotechnics, unifications of the cosmic and moral order through technical activity, and that a politics adequate to the Anthropocene needs technological futures to bifurcate instead of following one planetary trajectory | Hui (2017), "Cosmotechnics as Cosmopolitics", read in [NOTE-1916](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1916.md). Technological pluralism; cosmotechnics; bifurcation of technological futures. A stand-in for the thesis of [LIT-2584](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2584.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1866](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1866.md) | Susen reads Rosa as holding that the good life is measured not by resources or options but by the quality of a person's relation to the world, resonance, a responsive relation in which subject and world affect and transform each other and which cannot be produced at will, against alienation | Susen (2020) on Rosa's Resonance, read in [NOTE-1937](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1937.md). Resonance as the criterion of the good life. A stand-in for [LIT-2592](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2592.md); it qualifies [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md)'s evaluative measure. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1867](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1867.md) | Moen argues that Kaczynski's case against industrial technology reaches its conclusion from defensible empirical worries, that technological progress is hard to predict and as an arms race hard to restrain, only through unargued evaluative premises that count technology's harms and not its benefits, so that counted even-handedly the case fails |  | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1868](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1868.md) | Under the local induction approximation a thin vortex filament carries a soliton of its own shape: its curvature and torsion combine into a field obeying the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation, whose sech soliton is a localized pattern of the filament; with weak mutual friction and a negligible normal-fluid velocity the soliton survives, perturbed at first order in the friction, and decays at a rate of at most second order | Van Gorder (2014), [LIT-2612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2612.md), read in part in [NOTE-1951](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1951.md) (§§1–4, §10). Filed as the read neighbour of Hasimoto (1972), [LIT-2611](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2611.md), whose classical reduction it restates and generalizes. The filament itself is presupposed, not derived; the soliton is a pattern on it. It corroborates [CLAIM-606](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md)'s integrable route, which does not rest on it: a soliton held by no supply, running down slowly under weak loss. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1869](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1869.md) | In the abelian Higgs model a thin vortex line follows a Nambu–Goto string: for a timelike minimal surface with zero initial velocity there are solutions whose energy concentrates near it and that stay close to the Nielsen–Olesen vortex across it, for a finite time, wherever the two-dimensional vortex problem has a minimizer ordered by charge, which is known at critical coupling and for large coupling | Czubak & Jerrard (2012), [LIT-2610](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2610.md), read in part in [NOTE-1950](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1950.md): the statement of Theorem 1.4 and the remarks around it; the proof is unread. Filed as the read neighbour of Nielsen & Olesen (1973), [LIT-2613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2613.md), whose conjecture it proves where Jaffe and Taubes's holds. It corroborates [CLAIM-606](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md)'s topological route, which does not rest on it: a structure carrying a quantized charge persists as an extended object under the field's dynamics. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1870](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1870.md) | On Fel, Kowal and colleagues, penalizing a model's reliance on or expression of a probed concept during training can degrade the original probe, from 0.98 to 0.57 balanced accuracy when gradients pass through it in reward-hacking training, while a refitted linear probe recovers 0.97–0.98; in every experiment they ran the concept stayed readable by the original, a refitted, a nonlinear or another layer's probe, and in their linear toy theory a fixed projection makes the concept regrow along the directions the readout uses for core features | Fel, Kowal et al. (2026), [LIT-2620](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2620.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1958](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1958.md), with the lab's summary page read in full. The 0.57 is the worst variant; the others kept 0.87–0.90. "Every experiment" is the authors' own range of settings. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1871](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1871.md) | Causal self-attention with the softmax removed, or replaced by a kernel φ(k)ᵀφ(q), computes what a fast weight programmer computes, apart from the kernel's normalisation: a fast weight matrix that is the running sum of the outer products v ⊗ φ(k) of the keys and values so far, read by the query; such a layer can store at most about d_dot associations without crosstalk, and a delta-rule write that first removes the value a key already retrieves lets the memory replace an association it holds, as Schlag, Irie and Schmidhuber derive and show on synthetic retrieval | Schlag, Irie & Schmidhuber (2021), [LIT-2642](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2642.md), read in [NOTE-1988](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1988.md): linear attention is an outer-product fast weight programmer apart from normalisation (a review of Katharopoulos et al. and Ba et al.), so its memory holds at most about d_dot associations before crosstalk (shown on synthetic retrieval), and a delta-rule write with a learned rate does better when keys are reassigned and in an overcapacity language model. It defines the delta-rule layer [QUESTION-159](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-159.md) asks about, without stating a train-then-predict identity for it. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1872](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1872.md) | Zheng and Wang: for models fine-tuned from one pretrained start, the 2D Fourier spectra, taken over the row and column order of each weight matrix, of different tasks' weight updates differ most in amplitude at low frequencies, that difference goes with lower merged accuracy, and removing the low frequencies from each update before adding them improves data-free merging over task arithmetic and TIES | Zheng & Wang (2025), [LIT-2643](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2643.md), read in [NOTE-1974](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1974.md). Amplitude variance across tasks is largest at low index-grid frequencies and correlates negatively with normalized merged accuracy; FR-Merging (high-pass then magnitude-weighted sum) reaches 78.1 on ViT-B/32 with 8 tasks against 70.1 for task arithmetic and 73.6 for TIES. The frequencies are over the arbitrary order of rows and columns and change under a function-preserving permutation of hidden units, which the paper does not test. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1873](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1873.md) | In a soap film under a micrometre thick, Patsyk, Sivan, Segev and Bandres observe light branching as it propagates, because smooth thickness variations act as a weak correlated potential for linear guided waves; the scintillation index peaks near a distance proportional to lc v0^−2/3, branch intensities are heavier-tailed than Rayleigh, and a branch keeps its width for at least ten Rayleigh lengths | Patsyk, Sivan, Segev & Bandres (2020), [LIT-2647](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2647.md), read in [NOTE-1967](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1967.md): the first observation of branched flow of light, with v0 ≈ 1–5% and lc ≈ 90–350 µm, over ensembles of 10–20 realizations for the scaling and 100 for the statistics. The scaling law is earlier theory tested here, not derived. It bears on no question of the record's: it is wave physics, and any link to learning is analogy. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1874](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1874.md) | Gargiulo et al.: for CLIP ViTs fully fine-tuned on 8 to 20 image tasks from one start, each layer's weight update is close to low-rank, merging loses accuracy where different tasks' singular vectors overlap, and truncating each update to its top singular components and orthogonalising them across tasks raises merged accuracy by about 15 points over task arithmetic on ViT-B/32 | Gargiulo et al. (2025), [LIT-2627](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2627.md), read in [NOTE-1990](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1990.md). Keeping 3% of each task's singular components per layer costs 1.5% accuracy; cross-task singular-vector overlap is highest in early layers; TSV-M reaches 85.86 against 70.79 for task arithmetic on ViT-B/32 with 8 tasks; the ablation needs both truncation and decorrelation. That overlap is the cause rests on an association over three task sets. A rival diagnosis to TIES's sign conflicts, [THEORY-107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-107.md). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1875](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1875.md) | Chang and co-authors imprint designed, anisotropic correlated disorder on nematic liquid-crystal films by photoalignment and observe branched flow of light whose first-branch distance, read from the scintillation index over about ten fabricated films, grows with anisotropy and falls with rotation of the principal axis in agreement with df ∝ ε^−2/3 A^4/3 lx (cos²α + sin²α/A²)^5/6, and at anisotropy 1/1000 channels the light along the long correlation axis with sub-diffusive growth of its velocity-angle spread | Chang et al. (2026), [LIT-2639](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2639.md), read in [NOTE-1956](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1956.md) from arXiv v1 without its Supplemental Material. The law is Degueldre et al.'s prediction, tested here at three anisotropies and three angles plus a sweep; the isotropic case and the diagnostic are Patsyk et al. (2020), [LIT-2647](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2647.md). It bears on no question of the record's: wave physics, with any link to learning A's analogy. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1876](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1876.md) | Plate represents compositional structure in fixed-width distributed vectors by binding with circular convolution, superposing by addition and decoding with circular correlation, an approximate inverse of convolution whose output is a noisy version of the bound item that a separate item memory must clean up; for independent random vectors the number of pairs a trace can hold grows about linearly with the dimension | Plate (1995), [LIT-2644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2644.md), read in [NOTE-1959](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1959.md) from an OCR scan whose formulas are noisy. The linear capacity is a fit to an approximation, n ≈ 4.5(k + 0.7) ln(m/30q⁴) as transcribed, for independent random vectors only. | [THEORY-1915](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1915.md) v2 | Zeiser argues that AI decision support threatens responsibility chiefly as attributability rather than accountability: a decision a human makes with a tool that presupposes outcome-shaping values she has not endorsed does not express her value-judgements, an attributability gap that comes in degrees and that descriptive tools open as well as prescriptive ones |  | Proposed |

| [THEORY-1958](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1958.md) | Miller, as Shaw-Young reports his 2007 statement, holds that remedial responsibility for a bad situation is assigned through several distinct connections to it, moral responsibility, outcome responsibility, causal responsibility, benefit, capacity and community, so that it need not fall on whoever caused the situation or was at fault | Shaw-Young (2008), [LIT-2773](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2773.md), read in part in [NOTE-2064](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2064.md), as the weak read neighbour of Miller 2001 ([LIT-2755](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2755.md)). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1959](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1959.md) | Locke argues in the Second Treatise that because no one has an absolute arbitrary power over his own life no one can by compact or consent give another such power, except where life is forfeited by a fault deserving death, so that the legislative, holding only the joint power its members could transfer, cannot be absolutely arbitrary over their lives and fortunes and holds a fiduciary power the people may resume when the trust is breached | Locke, Two Treatises (1689), Second Treatise, [LIT-2738](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2738.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2077](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2077.md) on the sections the exchange names. "No body can give more power than he has himself" (§23); "no body has an absolute arbitrary power over himself" (§135); the legislative is "only a fiduciary power" (§149). It corroborates the form of [CLAIM-720](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-720.md)'s argument and qualifies it: the ground is power over one's own life, and forfeiture is allowed (a note on that claim). | [THEORY-1960](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1960.md) | Pettit proposes that a state is legitimate insofar as it imposes its order under popular control, and that the people control the state insofar as they have an individualized, unconditioned and efficacious influence over it that pushes it in a direction they find acceptable, realized by individual contestation, a resistive citizenry and channels of influence insulated from electoral pressures and private lobbies | Pettit, On the People's Terms (2012), [LIT-2760](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2760.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2047](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2047.md) from the publisher's openings of three parts: people control the state "just insofar as they have an individualized, unconditioned and efficacious influence that pushes it in a direction that they find acceptable". | [THEORY-1961](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1961.md) | Johnson holds that intimate partner violence divides by its control context into situational couple violence, intimate terrorism and violent resistance, and that agency data and general surveys disagree about gender because they sample different types | Johnson, interviewed by Ooms (2006), [LIT-2775](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2775.md), read in full in [NOTE-2066](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2066.md), as the read neighbour of Johnson 1995 ([LIT-2751](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2751.md)) and Johnson 2008 ([LIT-2715](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2715.md)). It corroborates [CLAIM-709](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-709.md), which does not rest on it: Johnson types violence by control context, not by a tally of acts. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1962](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1962.md) | Calabresi and Melamed propose that law protects an entitlement by a property rule, under which it is taken only by a purchase its holder agrees to, a liability rule, under which it may be taken on payment of a collectively determined value, or an inalienability rule, under which its transfer is forbidden, and that criminal sanctions serve partly to deter takers from converting property rules into liability rules by taking first and paying after | Calabresi & Melamed (1972), [LIT-2749](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2749.md), read in [NOTE-2070](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2070.md). Who holds an entitlement is decided first; how it is protected is a second-order decision among property, liability and inalienability rules, chosen mainly by the cost of market and collective valuation. §V: a thief charged only the value of what he took would "convert all property rule entitlements into liability rule entitlements", so punishment adds "an undefinable kicker". It is the mechanism [CLAIM-734](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-734.md) states, filed as that claim's grounds by a note on it. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1963](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1963.md) | Preschool children's wait-times on the marshmallow task depend on their evidence about whether the promised larger reward will come: children who have just seen the experimenter break promises wait about a quarter as long, so wait-times reflect a rational judgment of the environment's reliability as well as self-control | Kidd, Palmeri & Aslin (2013), [LIT-2730](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2730.md), read in full in [NOTE-2036](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2036.md): an experiment with 28 children, 14 per arm. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1964](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1964.md) | Nickel and Etinson characterize human rights as plural, universal, high-priority rights held independently of whether local law, practice or morality recognizes them, deny that inalienability, minimalism or a political function belongs to the concept, and report that the grounds offered for them vary and that agency and dignity each seem to need supplementing | Nickel & Etinson, SEP "Human Rights" (2024 revision), [LIT-2743](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2743.md), read in [NOTE-2042](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2042.md). | [THEORY-1965](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1965.md) | Waldron and Penner present private property as a system of rules assigning contested resources to the decisional authority of particular individuals, who may decide without explanation and whether or not others are affected, so that it is continually in need of public justification, and analyse default title as one Hohfeldian liberty, one claim-right and two powers, to license and to transfer | Waldron & Penner, SEP "Property and Ownership" (2026 revision), [LIT-2744](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2744.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2050](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2050.md) (§§1–2). | [THEORY-1966](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1966.md) | The Federal Rules of Civil Procedure forbid papers and discovery requests presented for an improper purpose such as to harass, cause unnecessary delay or needlessly increase the cost of litigation, limit discovery to what is proportional to the needs of the case with the parties' resources among the factors, and back these limits with sanctions up to dismissal or default | Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, Rules 11, 26 and 37, [LIT-2748](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2748.md), read in [NOTE-2067](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2067.md). That corroborates [CLAIM-748](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-748.md), which rests on its own construction, by showing the mechanism recognized in law, and gives a partial, procedure-bound answer to [QUESTION-479](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-479.md). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1967](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1967.md) | Scanlon holds that contractualism explains the Hohfeldian structure of moral rights, claims, liberties and powers including a promisee's power to release the promisor, by the reasons people have to insist on principles with that structure, without taking rights as basic, so that it matters little which parts of the structure are called rights | Scanlon, "Reply to Leif Wenar" (2013), [LIT-2746](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2746.md), read in [NOTE-2075](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2075.md). "Contractualism seeks to explain not only first-order claim rights but also powers"; the promisee's power of release is explained by the reasons both parties have to insist on Principle F's consent condition. | [THEORY-1968](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1968.md) | Citizen participation is meaningful to the degree that it redistributes power over outcomes: an eight-rung ladder runs from non-participation (manipulation, therapy) through tokenism (informing, consultation, placation), where citizens may hear and be heard without power to ensure they are heeded, to citizen power (partnership, delegated power, citizen control) | Arnstein (1969), [LIT-2740](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2740.md), read from an OCR scan in [NOTE-2037](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2037.md). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1969](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1969.md) | The High Court found, on the balance of probabilities and incident by incident, that 12 of the 14 assaults pleaded against Mr Depp were proved, all but Incidents 6 and 11, and held The Sun's words substantially true in the meaning that he had committed physical violence against Ms Heard, causing significant injury and on occasion leading her to fear for her life | Depp II v News Group Newspapers [2020] EWHC 2911 (QB), Nicol J, [LIT-2754](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2754.md), read in [NOTE-2060](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2060.md). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1970](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1970.md) | The Virginia Declaration of Rights declares that men have inherent rights of which they cannot by compact divest their posterity, that magistrates are the people's trustees and servants and at all times amenable to them, and that when government is found inadequate to its purposes a majority of the community has an indubitable, inalienable and indefeasible right to reform, alter or abolish it | The Virginia Declaration of Rights (1776), [LIT-2733](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2733.md), read in [NOTE-2044](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2044.md). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1972](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1972.md) | In Fuentes v. Shevin the Supreme Court held that prejudgment replevin statutes letting goods be seized from their possessor on a private party's ex parte application, without a prior opportunity to be heard, deny due process, because the hearing must come when the deprivation can still be prevented and no later hearing or damage award can undo a deprivation already made, whether or not the possessor would have prevailed | Fuentes v. | [THEORY-1973](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1973.md) | Strawson holds that holding people morally responsible consists in the reactive attitudes, which rest on a demand for goodwill or regard; that pleas of excuse leave the agent a full participant while pleas of exemption suspend the attitudes toward the agent; and that a general thesis of determinism neither does nor could rationally undermine the framework of these attitudes | Strawson (1962), [LIT-2679](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2679.md), read in full in [NOTE-2058](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2058.md). | [THEORY-1974](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1974.md) | Shoemaker holds that moral responsibility comes in three independent types, attributability, answerability and accountability, grounded in the capacities for quality of character, quality of judgment and quality of regard and each answered by its own family of responses, anger belonging to accountability | Shoemaker (2019), [LIT-2766](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2766.md), read in part in [NOTE-2048](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2048.md), as the read neighbour of Shoemaker 2011 ([LIT-2777](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2777.md)). | [THEORY-1975](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1975.md) | Stern argues that Darwall's account, on which moral obligation consists in what persons have legitimate second-personal authority to demand of one another rather than in actual demands, cannot explain obligations to aid a sufferer who makes no demand, so that wronging, or exclusionary reasons, may suffice for obligation without second-personal authority | Stern (2014), [LIT-2767](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2767.md), read in full in [NOTE-2065](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2065.md), as the read neighbour of Darwall 2006 ([LIT-2756](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2756.md)). | [THEORY-1976](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1976.md) | Bovens proposes that accountability, in a narrow analytical sense, is a social relation in which an actor is obliged to explain and justify its conduct to a forum that can question and judge it, with the possibility of consequences for the actor, and that whether a practice is accountability is an either/or question kept apart from classifying it by forum, actor, conduct and obligation and from evaluating it from democratic, constitutional and learning perspectives | Bovens (2007), [LIT-2729](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2729.md), read in [NOTE-2069](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2069.md). Accountability is "a relationship between an actor and a forum" with an obligation to explain and justify, questioning and judgement, and possible consequences; answerability is its interrogation stage. It corroborates [CLAIM-739](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-739.md), which does not rest on it, in separating the forum from the principal and from the party that imposes consequences, and it shows [TERM-126](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-126.md)'s nesting of accountability inside answerability to be the record's own (a note on that term). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1977](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1977.md) | Scanlon now holds that an act is wrong when someone could reasonably reject, on personal reasons weighed against others' opposing reasons, any principle permitting it, that besides the wrong of not complying with an established and needed practice there is a distinct wrong of failing to do one's part in establishing a needed norm, and that the judgments of sufficiency and relevance this rests on are substantive, which weakens the view's reductive explanatory power | Scanlon, "Contractualism and Intuitionism" (2025 draft), [LIT-2741](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2741.md), read in [NOTE-2051](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2051.md). Interactive reasonable rejection; the Principle of Established Practices (p. 21) and the distinct wrong of "failing to do one's part in getting such a norm established" (p. 22); the bilateral reading and the 1998 account of aggregation retracted; relevance "broadly speaking a moral question". It corroborates [CLAIM-729](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-729.md), which rests on [CLAIM-560](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-560.md) and A's report, not on this paper, and bears on [QUESTION-483](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-483.md) and [QUESTION-484](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-484.md). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1978](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1978.md) | When an agent divides attention among tasks measured with different precision, incentive pay on the measurable tasks draws effort from the unmeasured ones, so the best incentive for any task falls with the difficulty of measuring the others and can be a fixed wage, with asset ownership, limits on activities and job design acting as substitute instruments | Holmström & Milgrom (1991), [LIT-2753](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2753.md), read in [NOTE-2068](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2068.md). | [THEORY-1979](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1979.md) | When contracts are incomplete, the right to decide what the contract leaves out, the residual control right, belongs to the owner of the relevant non-human assets, and allocating it moves bargaining power between the parties and so their incentives to invest in the relationship | Hart (2016), [LIT-2776](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2776.md), his Nobel lecture, read in part in [NOTE-2052](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2052.md) as the read neighbour of Hart & Moore (1990), [LIT-2742](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2742.md). | [THEORY-1980](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1980.md) | In a larger and more diverse sample than the original studies, preschool marshmallow-test wait-time predicts adolescent achievement only modestly, and the association is largely explained by family background, the early home environment and concurrent cognitive and behavioral measures | Watts, Duncan & Quan (2018), [LIT-2752](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2752.md), read from the authors' manuscript in [NOTE-2041](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2041.md): an observational analysis of the NICHD SECCYD cohort. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1981](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1981.md) | Galanter proposes that repeat players, parties that litigate often with low stakes in any one case and the resources to pursue long-run interests, hold strategic advantages over one-shotters, including playing for rules as well as outcomes, and that passive, overloaded courts, which delay recovery, raise the cost of keeping a case alive and protect the possessor, together with unequal legal services and lagging rules, compound those advantages, so that a formally neutral legal system tends to let the haves come out ahead | Galanter (1974), [LIT-2728](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2728.md), read in [NOTE-2059](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2059.md).
