| [THEORY-1982](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1982.md) | Dirty hands are coherent, on Eggert's account: when two actual duties conflict, an act that is all things considered permissible, even required, can remain wrong, because the overridden duty survives as a moral remainder that makes remorse apt and can ground duties of apology or compensation | Eggert (2023; issue 2025), [LIT-2724](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2724.md), read in full in [NOTE-2040](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2040.md). | [THEORY-1984](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1984.md) | Hohfeld proposes that the word right in judicial reasoning covers several distinct legal relations, which reduce to eight fundamental conceptions, claim and duty, privilege and no-right, power and liability, immunity and disability, each with a correlative held by another party and an opposite, and that a legal power, volitional control over a change in legal relations, is distinct from the physical power to perform the acts that exercise it and from the privilege of performing them | Hohfeld (1913), [LIT-2762](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2762.md), read in [NOTE-2071](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2071.md). Eight conceptions in four correlative and four opposite pairs, "the lowest common denominators of the law"; a claim persists though the holder's own privilege is extinguished; legal power is distinct from "the physical power to do the things necessary" for its exercise. Filed as grounds of [CLAIM-722](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-722.md), whose separation of physical from normative power is A87's restatement of it, by a note on that claim; it corroborates [CLAIM-738](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-738.md), which does not rest on it, on the independence of normative positions. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1985](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1985.md) | Where contracts cannot specify in advance how assets will be used, ownership is the holding of residual rights of control over an asset, and allocating those rights to one party strengthens its incentive to invest in the relationship while weakening the other's, so integration is best when one party's investment matters much more than the other's | Grossman & Hart (1986), [LIT-2745](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2745.md), read in [NOTE-2063](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2063.md). | [THEORY-1994](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1994.md) | The Declaration of Independence asserts that all men are endowed with unalienable rights, that governments are instituted to secure them and derive their just powers from the consent of the governed, and that when a government becomes destructive of these ends the people have a right to alter or abolish it, though not for light and transient causes | The Declaration of Independence (1776), [LIT-2759](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2759.md), read in [NOTE-2057](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2057.md). | [THEORY-1999](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1999.md) | US law bars any part of an NTSB report of its determinations on an accident, probable cause included, from evidence or use in a civil action for damages arising from it, and NTSB regulation says its investigations are not conducted to determine anyone's rights, liabilities or blame: the Board's causal findings are fenced off from liability | 49 U.S.C. § 1154(b), [LIT-2782](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2782.md), read in [NOTE-2081](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2081.md) with 49 CFR 831.4, 835.2 and 835.3. | [THEORY-2000](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2000.md) v2 | Lunney and Lueder state Google's blameless postmortem as a review that records an incident's contributing causes and the follow-up actions to prevent recurrence without indicting any individual or team, on the ground that blame keeps people from bringing issues to light, so that correction is aimed at systems and processes rather than at people | Lunney and Lueder (2016), [LIT-2784](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2784.md), read in [NOTE-2082](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2082.md). | [THEORY-2002](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2002.md) | Neacsu and colleagues argue that, within active inference, structure learning is Bayesian model selection by model evidence over a supplied set of alternative models, done offline by refitting or by Bayesian model reduction or expansion, and that its open problem is not choosing among the alternatives but generating them | From the reading of [LIT-2835](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2835.md) in [NOTE-2092](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2092.md). Neacsu, So, Rutar, da Costa, Adams and Friston (2026), Minds and Machines 36:33, DOI 10.1007/s11023-026-09787-8 (open access). A conceptual review. It surveys what "structure learning" means across developmental, cognitive and machine-learning work, then defines Structure Learning in active inference as offline Bayesian model selection by model evidence, by refitting or by Bayesian model reduction or expansion. It names the open problem as generating the hypothesis space, not choosing within it. It reports no results. Here because the exchange called it the most useful single paper for what the free-energy literature covers. It maps that literature fairly but leaves active, data-choosing structure learning to [LIT-2815](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2815.md). It agrees with [THEORY-564](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-564.md)'s framing that reduction, not expansion, is the open half. Read in its NOTE (skimmed in part). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2003](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2003.md) | Geiger and colleagues define a high-level causal model as a constructive abstraction of a network when, under an alignment that partitions the network's variables into cells mapped onto high-level variables, translating the network's solutions under each aligned intervention gives the high-level model's solutions under the corresponding intervention, and they test this with interchange interventions that set aligned variables to the values a different source input would give, scored as interchange intervention accuracy | From the reading of [LIT-2800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2800.md) in [NOTE-2086](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2086.md). Geiger, Ibeling, Zur, Chaudhary et al. (2025), arXiv 2301.04709, published in JMLR 26 (2025). It sets out causal abstraction as a foundation for mechanistic interpretability. A high-level algorithm abstracts a network when, under an alignment partitioning the network's variables into cells mapped onto the algorithm's variables, intervening and then translating commutes with translating and then intervening. This is tested by interchange interventions that patch in values from a source input, distributed ones in rotated coordinates, and scored by interchange intervention accuracy. Interventions are generalized to "interventionals" so distributed features can be targeted, and many interpretability methods are recast in these terms. Here because A15 named it as the interventional criterion in [QUESTION-491](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-491.md); it complements the held approximate causal abstraction ([LIT-1310](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1310.md)) and DAS ([LIT-1551](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1551.md)), and [THEORY-1002](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1002.md)'s random-network control applies to it. Skimmed for its definitions; read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2004.md) | Carnap (1950) holds that logical probability is degree of confirmation, a relation between evidence and hypothesis whose statements are analytic, measured as partial entailment between ranges of state-descriptions relative to a language; that what holds for every admissible measure leaves every non-trivial value open, so one must be chosen by adequacy, provisionally; and that relevance under any such measure is symmetric but not transitive, with evidence positive singly able to be negative together | From the reading of [LIT-2818](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2818.md) in [NOTE-2110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2110.md): the book's account of probability, beside [THEORY-2017](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2017.md), its account of explication. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2005](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2005.md) | DeVille and Lerman show that a graph fibration between networks of continuous-time systems, a map lifting each incoming edge uniquely, induces a map of dynamical systems in the opposite direction for every modular vector field, so a surjective fibration (the quotient by a balanced relation) embeds the quotient's dynamics as an invariant synchrony polydiagonal and an injective fibration projects a network onto the subsystem that drives it | From the reading of [LIT-2792](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2792.md) in [NOTE-2130](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2130.md). DeVille and Lerman (2013), arXiv 1303.3907. In a coordinate-free framework of networks of control systems on manifolds, they prove that a graph fibration (Boldi and Vigna's unique lifting of incoming edges, equivalently input-tree isomorphism) induces a map of dynamical systems in the opposite direction for every modular vector field. Surjective fibrations, which include quotients by balanced relations, embed the quotient's dynamics as an invariant synchrony polydiagonal. Injective fibrations project a network onto the subsystem that drives it, which they call an abstraction. Only this direction is proved, and stability is not treated. Here because it is the fibration form of the balanced-partition result held as [THEORY-1065](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1065.md) and [THEORY-1059](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1059.md), which it generalizes in one direction. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2006](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2006.md) | Springer and colleagues show that, past an inflection point in pre-training length, language models degrade more under a fixed-size later modification (fine-tuning or weight noise), so that longer pre-training can leave a worse model after fine-tuning even though the base model keeps improving, and they attribute this mainly to forgetting of pre-trained capability that grows with pre-training ("progressive sensitivity"). | From the reading of [LIT-2829](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2829.md) in [NOTE-2119](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2119.md). Springer, Goyal, Wen, Kumar, Yue, Malladi, Neubig and Raghunathan (2025), arXiv 2503.19206. They name "catastrophic overtraining": past an inflection point, longer pre-training leaves a worse model after instruction or multimodal fine- tuning even though the base model keeps improving (OLMo-1B at 3T against 2.3T tokens; not seen at 7B up to 3T). In controlled small models and a deep-linear theory, they trace it to "progressive sensitivity": a fine- tune of fixed size destroys more pre-trained capability the longer the model was pre-trained. The cost shows up mostly as forgetting caused by the acquisition, and the new task itself gets worse only in some settings. It is here as the prime empirical case for overconsolidation ([CLAIM-758](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-758.md)) and the Pythia study ([CASE-294](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-294.md)), which it qualifies: the case is mainly about forgetting under modification, not a higher budget to acquire. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2007](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2007.md) | Sun and colleagues show that fine-tuning a jointly trained network's shared features on a self-supervised task formed from each unlabeled test image, before predicting, improves image classification under distribution shift without hurting the original distribution, that keeping the update across a stream of test images improves it further, and that the gain tracks the alignment of the self-supervised and main-task gradients | From the reading of [LIT-2821](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2821.md) in [NOTE-2128](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2128.md). Sun, Wang, Liu, Miller, Efros and Hardt (2020), ICML 2020, arXiv 1909.13231. The paper that named test-time training: before predicting, a jointly trained network fine-tunes its shared features on a self-supervised task (rotation prediction) built from the single unlabeled test image, then discards the update or, in the online version, keeps it for the next image. It improves classification under corruption, video and CIFAR-10.1 shifts without hurting the original test set, and the gain tracks the alignment of the two tasks' gradients (proved for convex losses). Here because the owner raised test-time training at U26: its discarded and kept updates are the two sides of [CLAIM-118](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-118.md), and its appendix prices the work moved to test time ([QUESTION-095](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-095.md)). Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2008.md) | Masumori and colleagues show that a growing neural cellular automaton trained to regenerate keeps its formed pattern not at a fixed point but on a recurrent attracting state sustained by persistent, spatially structured fluctuations, that damage displaces it from that state and it returns over hundreds of steps, and that suppressing small updates across most of the pattern impairs the return | From the reading of [LIT-2788](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2788.md) in [NOTE-2091](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2091.md). Masumori, Sato and Ikegami (2026), Entropy 28(8):893, DOI 10.3390/e28080893; read as the authors' arXiv preprint 2607.12403. In a growing neural cellular automaton trained to regenerate (Mordvintsev et al., [LIT-2798](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2798.md)), the formed pattern is kept not at a fixed point but on a recurrent attracting state, with persistent fluctuations concentrated in a few "fluctuation cores" near the shape's boundaries; damage displaces the system and it returns over hundreds of steps, and blocking small updates outside a disc holding less than about 74% of the cells impairs the return. Transfer entropy and information decomposition describe inward corrective and outward propagating predictive asymmetries during repair, which the authors do not read as causal flow. Here because A15 of the exchange "Topological protection explained" cited it beside Mordvintsev et al. for [CLAIM-566](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-566.md); it shows persistence and repair in this system as one precarious activity, not two mechanisms. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2009](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2009.md) | Chen, Kunin, Yamamura and Ganguli show that the symmetry-generated affine sets where a hidden neuron vanishes or two neurons in a layer are identical are invariant under SGD; that for a continuous model of SGD such a set attracts under a sufficient condition weighing the loss's curvature against gradient noise, which can hold at saddles and maxima; and that VGG-16 and ResNet-18 trained with SGD form clusters of near-identical neurons that grow with the learning rate | From the reading of [LIT-2793](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2793.md) in [NOTE-2127](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2127.md). The source Velarde and colleagues cite for covers attracting SGD; it supports less than they cite it for. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2010](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2010.md) | Omidvar, Bestler, Zahedi Fard, Zilberberg and Serra-Garcia show, in a chain of buckled polymer beams under a standing and a cyclic compression, that bits stored as buckling domains are moved one unit cell per load cycle, the domain wall advancing when a boundary mode localized at it, softened by the opposite domain's pressure, becomes unstable, a ratchet they distinguish from Chern-number pumping; logic gates built from such racetracks are shown in simulation only | From the reading of [LIT-2805](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2805.md) in [NOTE-2098](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2098.md). Omidvar, Bestler, Zahedi Fard, Zilberberg and Serra-Garcia (2026), Physical Review Letters, DOI 10.1103/jw9p-s3kk; read as arXiv 2509.01706 v1 (2025). In a chain of buckled polymer beams, bits stored as buckling domains are moved one unit cell per cycle of an applied compression pattern. The wall advances when a mode localized at it, softened by the opposite domain's pressure, goes unstable. The authors call this a topological ratchet and distinguish it from Chern-number pumping, which is ill- defined on their path. Logic gates are simulated only. It is here as information transport by boundaries without learning, against the learned defects of A15 ([LIT-2787](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2787.md)). Its mechanical neighbours are [THEORY-1893](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1893.md) (buckled bistable domains, also only under standing compression) and [THEORY-1408](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1408.md), whose index-protected modes it does not use. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2011](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2011.md) | Still shows that, for a partially observable information engine whose memory is formed at one temperature and used to extract work at another, minimising the lower bound on dissipation over the memory map is the information bottleneck: keep the information about the work-relevant variable, discard the rest, with the temperature ratio as the trade-off | From the reading of [LIT-2832](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2832.md) in [NOTE-2097](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2097.md). Still (arXiv 1705.00612, 2017; Physical Review Letters 124, 050601, 2020). The letter extends Szilárd's engine to partial observability and two temperatures. Forming a memory costs at least kT·I[M,X], and extracting work recovers at most kT'·I[M,Y], where Y is what the extraction device can manipulate. Minimising the resulting dissipation bound over the memory map is exactly the information bottleneck, with the temperature ratio as its trade-off. The agent's action never changes the next cycle's data, so the result is a no-feedback baseline. Here because the exchange made it the bridge between memory and thermodynamics: it is the nearest prior result for [QUESTION-494](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-494.md) and extends [THEORY-026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-026.md) to a cyclic engine. Read in its NOTE (arXiv v3). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2012](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2012.md) | Bardes, Ponce and LeCun show that in a joint-embedding objective the invariance term alone collapses all inputs to one vector, a covariance (decorrelation) term cannot prevent this, and a hinge keeping each embedding variable's batch standard deviation above a threshold does; with all three terms the method matches contemporary self-supervised methods on ImageNet without negatives, normalization, predictors or shared weights | From the reading of [LIT-2813](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2813.md) in [NOTE-2122](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2122.md). Bardes, Ponce, LeCun (2021), ICLR 2022, arXiv 2105.04906. The loss has three terms on the embeddings: invariance (mean squared distance between two views), a hinge holding each variable's batch standard deviation above 1, and a penalty on off-diagonal covariances, the last two applied to each branch separately. In the ablation the invariance term alone collapses everything to one vector, covariance cannot stop it, and the variance term does (57.5%, and 68.6% with all three, at 100 epochs; 73.2% at 1000). The hinge must be on the standard deviation: on the variance, its gradient vanishes and the embeddings collapse. That bears on [LIT-228](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-228.md)'s Laplacian-eigenmaps reading, which assumes a squared variance term. Here because A27 used it as a non-collapse mechanism ([CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md)'s note of 2026-11-19). Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2013](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2013.md) | Biderman and colleagues release Pythia, eight decoder-only language models from 70M to 12B parameters each trained once on the Pile and once on a deduplicated Pile in one fixed data order, with 154 public checkpoints per model (initialization, ten log-spaced early steps and every 1,000 steps to 143,000) and tools to reconstruct the exact batches seen up to each, and show with it that training order has little effect on memorization and that a link between term frequency and few-shot accuracy appears only late in training and only at 2.8B parameters and above | From the reading of [LIT-2841](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2841.md) in [NOTE-2136](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2136.md). Pythia is eight decoder-only language models, 70M to 12B parameters, each trained once on the Pile and once on a deduplicated Pile (about 1.5 epochs) in one fixed data order, with 154 public checkpoints per model (step 0, ten log-spaced early steps, every 1,000 steps to 143,000) and tools to reconstruct the batches seen up to each; one run per size, cosine learning-rate decay to a tenth of peak. Its case studies find training order has little effect on memorization and a term-frequency effect on few-shot accuracy that appears only late and only at 2.8B and above. Here because it is the testbed of [CASE-294](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-294.md), whose named models (70M- and 160M-deduped) and checkpoints exist as described, and because many THEORY entries use its models without an entry for the suite. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2014](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2014.md) | Gili and colleagues infer, for a literature-based eleven-region language connectome, the subnetworks whose coarsest balanced colourings equal the group-average fMRI synchrony clusters at rest (four fibres) and in two speech tasks (five, one partition for both); the inferred networks have only the identity automorphism and their rest and task partitions cross, so the reported fibration symmetry breaking is a change of balanced partition imposed by the observed clusters, not predicted from structure | Gili, Avila, Pasquini, Holodny, Phillips, Boldi, Gabrielli, Caldarelli, Zimmer and Makse ([LIT-2804](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2804.md)), read in [NOTE-2111](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2111.md). A mixed-integer program deletes the fewest tracts from a baseline connectome (five fibres, each an orbit) until each state's observed synchrony clusters are its coarsest balanced colouring. Rest gives four fibres, both tasks five, all with only the identity automorphism, and the rest and task partitions are not ordered by refinement. The account applies [THEORY-1065](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1065.md): synchrony classes without symmetry. | [THEORY-2015](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2015.md) | Han and colleagues show that, in Llama-2 and OLMo-2 language models of 0.5B-4B parameters pre-trained at 20 or 140 tokens per parameter, AdamW weight decay above the default 0.1 during pre-training yields models that score better on the fine-tuning task after fine-tuning, even where it leaves a worse pre-training loss, so that pre-training loss does not rank pre-trained models by their performance after further training. | From the reading of [LIT-2820](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2820.md) in [NOTE-2125](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2125.md). Han, Bordt, Zhang and Kakade (2026), arXiv 2602.11137, ICML 2026. They pre-train Llama-2 and OLMo-2 models (0.5B-4B, at 20 and 140 tokens per parameter) across AdamW weight decay values, then fine-tune on twelve tasks. Weight decay above the default 0.1 gives better fine-tuned performance even where it worsens pre-training loss (OLMo-2-1B at 140 tokens per parameter), so pre-training loss does not rank models by what they become. Plasticity is measured only as the fine-tuned score on the target task, and forgetting is not measured. It is here as a preventive training regime for overconsolidation ([CLAIM-758](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-758.md)) and an arm of [CASE-294](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-294.md), and it is the clearest case for [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md)'s point that present capability does not rank later capability. | [THEORY-2016](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2016.md) | Friston and colleagues show, in simulations of a three-ball rule-discovery task, that adding to expected free energy the expected information gain over a prespecified set of model structures, computed by Bayesian model reduction, lets an active-inference agent choose observations that identify the generating rule faster than when only information gain over states and parameters, or none, drives its choices | From the reading of [LIT-2815](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2815.md) in [NOTE-2105](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2105.md). Friston, Da Costa, Tschantz, Heins, Buckley, Verbelen and Parr (2026), Nature Communications 17:10125, DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-77209-5 (open access). The paper adds to active inference's expected free energy an expected information gain over model structures. It computes that gain by Bayesian model reduction over a hypothesis space fixed in advance by symmetry priors (81 rules in a three-ball task), so the agent chooses the observations that best discriminate rules. In 64 simulated games the rule was found in a modal 14 trials. Without information gain about half the games failed. It assumes the rest of the generative model is known. Here because the exchange named it as prior art for structure learning beside [THEORY-564](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-564.md). It qualifies that entry without meeting its promote_when, and it shows the mechanism [CASE-153](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-153.md)'s sentry would block. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2018](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2018.md) | Zbontar and colleagues show that a joint-embedding objective which standardizes each embedding unit over the batch and drives the cross-correlation matrix between two views' embeddings toward the identity learns ImageNet representations on par with contemporary self-supervised methods without negatives, predictors, stop-gradients or large batches, and that both the invariance (diagonal) and redundancy-reduction (off-diagonal) terms are needed | From the reading of [LIT-2795](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2795.md) in [NOTE-2129](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2129.md). Zbontar, Jing, Misra, LeCun, Deny (2021), ICML 2021 (PMLR 139), arXiv 2103.03230. The loss standardizes each embedding unit over the batch and drives the cross- correlation matrix between two distorted views' embeddings toward the identity. The diagonal makes the embedding invariant to the distortions and the off-diagonal decorrelates its units. It avoids collapse without negatives, predictors, stop-gradients or large batches, keeps improving with very wide embeddings, and both terms are needed: in the ablation, the off-diagonal term alone gives 0.1% linear accuracy, the diagonal alone 57.3%, the full loss 71.4%. The information-bottleneck reading rests on a Gaussian assumption and stated approximations, and there is no theorem. Here because A27 used it as a non-collapse mechanism ([CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md)'s note of 2026-11-19); [LIT-228](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-228.md) holds its CCA reading. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2019](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2019.md) | Nichol, Achiam and Schulman show that Reptile, which repeatedly trains on a sampled task for k steps and moves the initialization toward the result, matches MAML on few-shot Omniglot and Mini-ImageNet with first-order gradients only, and that to leading order its update and MAML's both combine joint training on the expected loss with a term that raises the inner product of gradients from different mini-batches of one task, a term that grows with the step size and the number of inner steps and vanishes at one step | From the reading of [LIT-2791](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2791.md) in [NOTE-2102](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2102.md). Nichol, Achiam and Schulman (2018), OpenAI, arXiv 1803.02999. Reptile meta-learns an initialization by repeatedly training on a sampled task and moving the initialization toward the result; it matches MAML on few-shot Omniglot and Mini-ImageNet with first-order gradients only, and a Taylor expansion shows its update, like MAML's, is joint training plus a term rewarding generalization between mini-batches of one task, a term that grows with step size and inner steps and is absent at one step. The authors suggest plain SGD does part of this already and that joint training plus fine-tuning stays a strong baseline; their RL results were negative. Here because A54 proposed it as the meta-trained arm of CASE- tmphsr99: the reading supports it as a cheap arm, with joint training on the same tasks as its control and the inner budget k fixed. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2020](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2020.md) | Javed and White show that a representation meta-trained by differentiating through online SGD updates on correlated streams (OML), then frozen beneath a small online-learned predictor, lets that predictor learn sequential regression and classification tasks with far less forgetting than pre-trained or sparsity-trained representations, and that such representations come out highly sparse with no dead units. | From the reading of [LIT-2828](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2828.md) in [NOTE-2106](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2106.md). Javed and White (2019), arXiv 1905.12588, NeurIPS 2019. OML meta-trains a representation by differentiating through online SGD on correlated streams, then freezes it beneath a small predictor that learns online. On Incremental Sine Waves and Split-Omniglot this gives far less forgetting than pre- trained or sparse representations, and learning faster than approximate IID training. The representation turns out highly sparse with no dead units. It is here because A54 named it for representations meta-trained against forgetting, bearing on overconsolidation ([CLAIM-758](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-758.md)). It bears mostly on forgetting: it secures retention and fast acquisition together by freezing the representation, and it says nothing on plasticity over long training. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2021](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2021.md) | Jacobs and colleagues show that recurrent networks with only local encoders and local recurrence learn to propagate travelling waves that carry whole-shape information to each pixel, so that a readout of each neuron's activity over time segments images needing global context, beating feed-forward networks of matched receptive field and, on Multi-MNIST, U-Nets of similar size | From the reading of [LIT-2836](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2836.md) in [NOTE-2133](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2133.md). Jacobs, Budzinski, Muller, Ba and Keller (2025), arXiv 2502.06034. Recurrent networks with only local encoders and local recurrence learn to propagate travelling waves that bring whole-shape information to each pixel; reading each neuron's activity over time, rather than its last state, lets them segment images that need global context, beating feed-forward CNNs of matched receptive field and, on Multi-MNIST, U-Nets of similar size. The motivation is Kac's "hearing the shape of a drum", and a wave RNN reproduces square drums' fundamental frequencies; even an unbiased convolutional LSTM learns waves. Here because A15 of the exchange "Topological protection explained" listed it beside Keller et al. as a way learned systems carry information ([QUESTION-491](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-491.md)), and [LIT-647](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-647.md) mentions it. The role of the waves rests on comparisons and a training- time correlation, not on intervention. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2022](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2022.md) | Teo and Kane show that a defect in a non-interacting gapped insulator or superconductor can be classified by the homotopy class of the Bloch or Bogoliubov–de Gennes Hamiltonian H(k, r) on a surface enclosing it, that this classification depends only on the symmetry class and on δ = d − D, and that in their examples a nontrivial class coincides with protected gapless modes bound to the defect, a correspondence they observe rather than prove | From the reading of [LIT-2797](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2797.md) in [NOTE-2124](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2124.md). Teo and Kane (2010), arXiv 1006.0690 (Phys. Rev. B 82, 115120). A unified classification of defects in non-interacting insulators and superconductors. It uses the homotopy class of the Bloch or Bogoliubov–de Gennes Hamiltonian H(k, r) on a surface around the defect, which depends only on the symmetry class and δ = d − D, together with a generalized bulk-boundary correspondence, observed in examples rather than proved, that pairs a nontrivial class with protected gapless modes bound to the defect. In the Jackiw–Rebbi kink, the Jackiw–Rossi vortex and the dislocation, the defect's structural charge fixes the mode invariant. In a disordered weak topological insulator the protected modes outlive the structure that produced them. It is here for the relation between defect topology and bound modes ([CLAIM-606](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md), [CLAIM-694](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-694.md)). It shows these are two topologies of different objects. What is protected is the hosted modes, not the defect's persistence. Skimmed in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2023](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2023.md) | Lu and Kankanhalli show that a policy trained to decide, per query, whether to answer directly, reuse a stored test-time-trained LoRA skill or build a new one with one of five test-time-training methods roughly doubles a 7B model's verified utility on a benchmark enriched for queries where adaptation helps, cuts adaptation compute by about 30% without loss of utility under a moderate compute penalty, and amortizes skill construction through reuse | From the reading of [LIT-2806](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2806.md) in [NOTE-2084](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2084.md). Lu and Kankanhalli (2026), arXiv 2610.12002. Five test-time-training methods become tools that produce reusable LoRA skills over a frozen backbone, and a policy trained by distillation and GRPO decides per query whether to answer directly, reuse a skill or build one, on utility gain minus a compute penalty. On a benchmark deliberately enriched for queries where adaptation helps, it raises Qwen2.5-7B's verified utility from 0.256 to 0.510, cuts adaptation compute by about 30% under a moderate penalty without losing utility, and amortizes skill construction through reuse (61 of 100 reuses help, 1 harms). Here because A58 cited it for learning when to update: its rule, build when gain amortized over expected reuse covers the compute, is [QUESTION-095](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-095.md)'s trade and [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s criterion for parameter skills. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2024](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2024.md) | Mordvintsev and colleagues show that a neural cellular automaton trained only to grow a target pattern from a seed grows it but does not reliably persist it, that training it to persist from its own outputs makes the pattern stable and often partly regenerative, and that adding damage during training gives robust regeneration, including from kinds of damage not seen in training | From the reading of [LIT-2798](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2798.md) in [NOTE-2135](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2135.md). Mordvintsev, Randazzo, Niklasson and Levin (2020), Distill, DOI 10.23915/distill.00023, CC-BY. A continuous cellular automaton with a small learned update rule shared by all cells grows an emoji from one seed; trained only to grow, the patterns die out, overgrow or are only almost stable; trained from a pool of their own outputs, the target becomes an attractor that persists and often partly regenerates; trained with damage, the patterns regenerate robustly, even from damage not seen in training. Here because A15 of the exchange "Topological protection explained" used it to separate persistence from regeneration, held as [CLAIM-566](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-566.md): the three training regimes do separate growth, persistence and regeneration, though persistence training brings some regeneration with it, and the regenerating rule is supplied from outside the pattern. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2025](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2025.md) | Raghu and colleagues show that on standard few-shot image-classification and RL benchmarks, MAML's fast adaptation comes almost entirely from reusing features already present in its meta-initialization rather than from rapid change of representations, so that freezing all layers but the head at test time, or never adapting the body during training (ANIL), leaves performance about unchanged. | From the reading of [LIT-2822](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2822.md) in [NOTE-2131](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2131.md). Raghu, Raghu, Bengio and Vinyals (2019), arXiv 1909.09157, ICLR 2020. On standard few-shot benchmarks, freezing MAML's network body at test time barely changes accuracy, and body representations hardly move during adaptation (CCA above 0.9). MAML's success is therefore "feature reuse", not "rapid learning", and ANIL, which adapts only the head, matches MAML. It is here because A54 used it to separate reusable structure from the capacity to acquire structure, a clause of [CLAIM-758](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-758.md). The paper supports that distinction between routes to fast adaptation but does not measure acquisition capacity over training or forgetting. It also warns that a low adaptation budget can measure reuse rather than plasticity ([CASE-294](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-294.md)). Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2026.md) | Kaschube, Schnabel and Wolf show that in a long-range-interaction pattern-formation model of orientation-map development the density of pinwheel defects per hypercolumn is exactly π in the limit of infinite interaction range, and stays close to π, with small variance between maps, for intermediate ranges | From the reading of [LIT-2807](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2807.md) in [NOTE-2109](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2109.md). Kaschube, Schnabel and Wolf (2008), arXiv 0801.3651. In a Swift-Hohenberg-type model of orientation-map development dominated by long-range interactions, the density of pinwheels (±1/2 point defects of the orientation map) per hypercolumn tends to exactly π as the interaction range grows and stays near π for intermediate ranges, while in rival models pinwheels annihilate or crystallize. Registered as a stand-in for Kaschube et al. (2010, [LIT-2812](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2812.md)), which is Unfetched: it restates that paper's model prediction, not its cross-species measurements. Here because A15 of the exchange "Topological protection explained" cited pinwheels as defect- like singularities that need not be functional units (QUESTION- tmpcb0bf); the paper treats them only as countable markers and assigns no function. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2027](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2027.md) | Dohare and colleagues show that networks trained by standard backpropagation on long sequences of new supervised tasks (Continual ImageNet, Permuted MNIST, class-incremental CIFAR-100) gradually lose the ability to learn each new task, down to about the level of a linear network, which is distinct from forgetting old tasks, and that methods which keep weights small while continually injecting fresh random units from the start of training, best of all their continual backpropagation, maintain that ability. | From the reading of [LIT-2810](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2810.md) in [NOTE-2137](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2137.md). Dohare, Hernandez- Garcia, Rahman, Mahmood and Sutton (2023), arXiv 2306.13812 (v3, "Maintaining Plasticity in Deep Continual Learning"), published with Lan as "Loss of plasticity in deep continual learning", Nature 632, 768-774 (2024), open access. On long sequences of new tasks (Continual ImageNet, Permuted MNIST, class-incremental CIFAR-100, ant locomotion with PPO), standard deep learning gradually loses the ability to learn new tasks, which the authors keep distinct from forgetting. On ImageNet it falls to about a linear network, and on CIFAR-100 below retraining from scratch with old classes still trained. Small weights with continual injection of randomness (Shrink and Perturb, and their continual backpropagation) maintain plasticity, but all are applied from the start, and none is tested as a late rescue. It is here for overconsolidation (CLAIM-758) beside [THEORY-1353](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1353.md), whose depletion reading it fits: plasticity is lost while the network keeps practising on varied tasks. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2028](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2028.md) | Rupe and Crutchfield define local causal states as classes of past lightcones with the same distribution over future lightcones, domains as regions where the resulting state field is invariant under a group of space and time shifts, and coherent structures as localized, persistent deviations from domains, and show on elementary cellular automata that the domains match the domain-particle decomposition exactly and its particles largely | From the reading of [LIT-2824](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2824.md) in [NOTE-2123](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2123.md). Rupe and Crutchfield (2018), arXiv 1801.00515 (Santa Fe Institute working paper). They define local causal states, classes of past lightcones with the same distribution over future lightcones; domains, regions where the resulting state field has a space–time shift symmetry group; and coherent structures, localized, persistent deviations from domains, "locally broken domain symmetries". On elementary cellular automata the domains match the earlier domain-particle decomposition exactly and its particles largely, but stochastic domains need extra hand-applied filtering. The authors stress that the states are predictive, not interventional. Here because it is the spatiotemporal form of the causal state held as [TERM-062](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-062.md) and the predictive criterion that QUESTION- tmpcb0bf compares. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2029](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2029.md) | Smith, Friston and Whyte show, in a tutorial simulation of an explore–exploit task with a costly hint, that an active-inference agent learning which option is better takes the hint early and less often as its Dirichlet counts grow, takes it less the more precisely it prefers the larger win, and returns to it after unexpected losses | From the reading of [LIT-2827](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2827.md) in [NOTE-2117](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2117.md). Smith, Friston and Whyte (2022), Journal of Mathematical Psychology 107, 102632, DOI 10.1016/j.jmp.2021.102632 (open access; PMC8956124). A practical tutorial on discrete-state active inference: building POMDPs, simulating with SPM's routines, Dirichlet learning and its novelty term, the neural process theory, hierarchical models, and fitting models to choices with recoverability checks and Bayesian model comparison. Its running example is an explore–exploit task with a costly hint. There information-seeking fades as Dirichlet counts grow, falls as the preference for the larger win sharpens, and returns after surprises. Here because the exchange recommended it as the first reading for U31. It is a ready template for the Bayesian baseline and the fitting of [CASE-153](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-153.md), though it has no second process with authority over action and no structure learning. Read in its NOTE (skimmed in part). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2030.md) | Ibrahim argues that collective capabilities, those that result from collective agency and that no individual alone could have or achieve, are intrinsically and instrumentally important for human capabilities, that their generation is good only when participation is free and voluntary and the agency empowering, and that the capability approach's evaluative space should therefore extend from the individual to the collectivity | From the reading of [LIT-2802](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2802.md) in [NOTE-2114](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2114.md). Ibrahim (2013), "Collective Capabilities: What are they and why are they Important?", Maitreyee no. 22 (HDCA e-bulletin), pp. 4–7, https://hd-ca.org/wp- content/uploads/2014/03/Maitreyee22_June20131.pdf. A short position piece. It defines collective capabilities, citing her 2006 paper, as capabilities that result from collective agency and that "the individual alone would neither have nor be able to achieve". It answers Sen's "socially dependent individual capabilities" and Alkire's heterogeneity objection, and sets conditions (free, voluntary, empowering participation) under which they are good. Registered as a stand-in for [LIT-2823](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2823.md), which is closed access. It restates that paper's definition but not its framework or its Egyptian case studies. Here for individual capabilities made possible by a collective, beside [CLAIM-352](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-352.md) and [CLAIM-760](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-760.md). Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2031](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2031.md) | Poole, Lahiri, Raghu, Sohl-Dickstein and Ganguli show, in the mean-field theory of wide random fully connected networks, that the slope of the correlation map at correlation 1 divides the weight and bias variances into an ordered phase, where nearby inputs converge, and a chaotic one, where they separate; that in the chaotic phase an input curve's length grows exponentially with depth while its curvature holds at a fixed point, so its global curvature grows exponentially with depth; and that a one-hidden-layer network can extend a curve's length only in proportion to its width | From the reading of [LIT-2842](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2842.md) in [NOTE-2099](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2099.md). The mean-field theory Schoenholz and colleagues build on. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2032](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2032.md) | Shankar, Souslov, Bowick, Marchetti and Vitelli review topology in active matter as two physically distinct classes of phenomena that share the mathematics of integer invariants: topological defects, whose winding number is protected under continuous deformation of the order parameter and which in active nematics self-propel and unbind through flows they themselves generate, and topologically protected edge modes, whose band invariant is protected under continuous change of the medium's parameters while the bulk gap stays open | From the reading of [LIT-2789](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2789.md) in [NOTE-2134](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2134.md). Shankar, Souslov, Bowick, Marchetti and Vitelli (2020; v3 2021), arXiv 2010.00364, published in Nature Reviews Physics 4, 380–398 (2022). A review of topology in active matter. It presents topological defects of the order parameter and topologically protected edge modes of waves as "two physically distinct classes of phenomena" that share the mathematics of integer invariants. In active nematics, flows the defects generate make +1/2 defects self-propel and unbind. In active fluids and metamaterials, activity can create the band topology that guarantees edge and interface modes. It is here for [QUESTION-490](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-490.md) and the record's split between defect topology and bound-mode topology. It corroborates that a winding number counts defects net ([CLAIM-694](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-694.md)), and it gives a case of one structure on both the charge route and the supplied route ([CLAIM-606](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md)). Skimmed in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2033](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2033.md) | Wang and Isola show that, as the number of negative samples grows, the normalized InfoNCE loss on the unit hypersphere converges to an alignment term, minimized exactly by encoders that map both members of every positive pair to the same feature, plus a uniformity term, minimized by encoders whose features are uniformly distributed on the sphere when such encoders exist; on a finite augmented dataset the two optima cannot both be met | From the reading of [LIT-2819](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2819.md) in [NOTE-2113](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2113.md). Wang, Isola (2020), ICML 2020 (PMLR 119), arXiv 2005.10242. As the number of negatives grows, the normalized InfoNCE loss on the unit hypersphere converges to an alignment term, minimized exactly when both members of every positive pair share a feature, plus a uniformity term, minimized by a uniform distribution of features on the sphere. On a finite augmented dataset the two optima cannot both be met, and weighting alignment far above uniformity maps every input to one vector. Across several hundred encoders, low alignment and uniformity losses go with good downstream accuracy, and optimizing them directly matches or beats the contrastive loss. Here because A27 used it for how self-supervised learning contracts some distinctions and keeps others ([CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md)'s note of 2026-11-19, [CLAIM-762](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-762.md)). It supports that split but is not spectral and says nothing of the classes kept. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2034](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2034.md) | Hospedales, Antoniou, Micaelli and Storkey characterize neural-network meta-learning as end-to-end optimization of an explicitly defined meta-objective over many learning episodes, so as to improve future learning, and order the field on three axes, what is meta-learned, how it is optimized and what objective it serves; they name meta-overfitting and generalization to task distributions other than the training one as open problems | From the reading of [LIT-2796](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2796.md) in [NOTE-2108](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2108.md). It also covers practical issues such as variable labelling costs, unknown model classes and stopping criteria. The constraints are there because the energy alone collapses every vertex onto a constant, and each connected component is treated separately. A recurrent network whose recurrence is a ring convolution initialised as a one-step shift (the Wave-RNN) carries travelling waves in its hidden state, and against a matched wave-free network (the identity-initialised RNN) it learns faster and keeps inputs far longer: more than five orders of magnitude lower loss on the copy task, the adding task solved at length 1000, and much more input information retained with the recurrence frozen. ([LIT-2838](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2838.md)) for [CASE-294](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-294.md): the reading supports the case's held-out task-generating processes, since learner overfitting survives shuffling, and adds two rules, several seeds and pre/post-update accuracy as the diagnostic. Larremore, Clauset and Jacobs (2014), arXiv 1403.2933. They formulate a degree-corrected bipartite stochastic block model, in which communities are pure-type groups with the same expected connection pattern to the other side's groups. It finds better partitions faster than the unconstrained SBM and recovers planted structure that one-mode projections hide. In their actor–movie example (IMDb, 1995–2000), five of six movie blocks were language groups and one was a genre (Adult), and the authors read the blocks as traces of "multiple mechanisms responsible for the existence of edges". Here because it is the standard method behind the owner's U10 genres example, [CASE-296](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-296.md): it supplies the joint people-and-items identification, but its own film blocks are mostly not genres, which bears on the case's confounds. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2055.md) | Velarde, Parra, Hashemi and Makse show that in layered networks a covering partition of units, units with equal colour-summed input and output weights, can only coarsen under gradient descent, and report that tolerance-defined quasi-covers grow during training of an MLP, a CNN and an LSTM agent and allow compression to 17–18% of size with little loss, while exact automorphisms are never observed | From the reading of [LIT-2843](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2843.md) in [NOTE-2085](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2085.md). Velarde, Parra, Hashemi and Makse (2026), arXiv 2609.01768 (v1, not peer reviewed). They carry graph fibrations to weighted layered networks as balanced colourings of units. They prove that a covering partition (equal colour- summed input and output weights) can only coarsen under gradient descent, and report that tolerance-defined quasi-covers grow during training of an MLP, a CNN and an LSTM agent, allowing compression to 17–18% of size; transformers are shown compressed, not tracked in training. Fibers here are computed with every input coordinate its own colour, so they are input-independent redundancies, not quotients of inputs, and the paper has no relational or rule task. Here because it is the evidence on the fibration side of the owner's U9 hunch, QUESTION- tmpex36a: it shows that balanced structure among units is learned without symmetry forcing it, and is silent on role abstraction. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |

Yin, Tucker, Zhou, Levine and Finn (2020), ICLR 2020, arXiv 1912.03820. They show that when meta-training tasks are not mutually exclusive, MAML and conditional neural processes can memorize one function that solves every training task without using its training data, with lower meta-training error than an adapting solution and poor performance on new tasks; ordinary weight regularization does not prevent it, while penalizing the information in the meta-parameters not used for adaptation does. Here because A54 used it for meta-overfitting, a design rule of CASE- tmphsr99: the reading supports the rule and adds pre-update accuracy on training tasks as its diagnostic. | [THEORY-2092](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2092.md) | He and colleagues find that in a parameter-sharing transformer on a synthetic two-hop fact-composition task, models that reach held-out compositions through a bridge-entity reasoning path, by grokking or by full compositional supervision, later compose new first-hop facts with old ones, while models that reach comparable held-out accuracy by a shortcut learn new facts without composing them, and no model composes new second-hop facts | From the reading of [LIT-2872](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2872.md) in [NOTE-2175](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2175.md). | [THEORY-2093](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2093.md) | Maennel and colleagues find that convolutional networks pretrained on images with random labels, rescaled and given a fresh head, usually learn a new labelling of fresh images faster than from scratch, a gain reproduced by first-layer filters sampled from the learned weight covariance, which aligns with the data covariance, while in other settings the same pretraining slows later learning as later-layer units go inactive | From the reading of [LIT-2878](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2878.md) in [NOTE-2173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2173.md). | [THEORY-2094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2094.md) | Kuhn holds that a scientific community's paradigm, learned from exemplary problem-solutions as a rule-free similarity relation, makes later puzzle-solving tractable and restricts which problems can be asked, that its rigidity makes anomalies visible until they bring crisis, and that a revolution changes the field's problems, standards and some learned similarity relations, with losses as well as gains | From the reading of [LIT-2884](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2884.md) in [NOTE-2176](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2176.md). | [THEORY-2095](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2095.md) | Kuhn holds that the exemplars of a science, shared concrete problem-solutions, teach a learned perception of similarity rather than rules, by which a new problem is seen as like one already solved so that its formalism follows and only manipulative difficulties remain, and that knowledge stored in that similarity relation differs from knowledge stored as rules | From the reading of [LIT-2883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2883.md) in [NOTE-2178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2178.md). | [THEORY-2096](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2096.md) | Kuhn, as Kindi reads his 1959 essay, holds that innovation in a mature science depends on convergent thinking as much as on divergent, because training that commits a scientist firmly to a tradition is what lets research recognize where the tradition fails and break with it | From the reading of [LIT-2885](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2885.md) in [NOTE-2177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2177.md). | [THEORY-2097](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2097.md) | Alexander holds that moral systems are in essence systems of indirect reciprocity arising from conflicts of reproductive interest, in which help seen by others pays through those observers' later choices, so that some indiscriminate altruism is social investment, idealized universal moralities misread it as self-sacrifice, and morality as practised is cohesion within groups that may be directed against others | From the reading of [LIT-2886](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2886.md) in [NOTE-2179](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2179.md), a stand-in for the book [LIT-495](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-495.md). | [THEORY-2098](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2098.md) | Solms argues that consciousness is generated in the upper brainstem and is fundamentally affective, feeling being the precision-weighting by which an organism that minimises free energy prioritises among its homeostatic needs in unpredicted contexts, so that rising uncertainty about a need is felt as unpleasure and falling uncertainty as pleasure | From the reading of [LIT-2891](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2891.md) in [NOTE-2186](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2186.md), a stand-in for [LIT-2916](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2916.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2099](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2099.md) | Recht argues that the mathematical rationality built with the first computers, which casts every decision under uncertainty as maximising expected utility under a probability model, is valid only in narrow settings such as regulation and engineering, so that outsourcing most decisions, political or value-laden ones above all, to computation built on it is itself irrational | From the reading of [LIT-2918](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2918.md) in [NOTE-2184](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2184.md), a stand-in for [LIT-2917](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2917.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2100](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2100.md) | Colman, Pulford and Lawrence find in asymmetric three-by-three and four-by-four games that level-1 cognitive hierarchy reasoning predominates, strong Stackelberg reasoning is frequent in the smaller games and team reasoning accounts for a larger share of choices in the larger games, most players considering several modes | From the reading of [LIT-2926](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2926.md) in [NOTE-2201](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2201.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2101.md) | Tomasello proposes that agency is feedback-control organization built up in grades over the human lineage, goal-directed agency in the first vertebrates, intentional agency with an executive tier monitoring and controlling action and attention in the first mammals, metacognitive or rational agency with a second tier monitoring and controlling the executive tier in the first great apes, and shared agency, joint then collective, with normative self-regulation in early humans | From the reading of [LIT-2899](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2899.md) in [NOTE-2191](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2191.md), a stand-in for [LIT-2912](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2912.md). | [THEORY-2102](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2102.md) | Tomasello proposes that great apes add a metacognitive tier of control to the executive tier common to mammals, monitoring their own executive decisions and uncertainty, and that they understand others as agents by attributing to them the goals, perceptions and knowledge they monitor in themselves | From the reading of [LIT-2913](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2913.md) in [NOTE-2195](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2195.md), a stand-in for chapter 4 of [LIT-2912](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2912.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2103.md) | Moll and Meltzoff argue that perspective-taking is founded on joint attention, developing from shared attention at about 12 months through knowing what others have experienced (14 months) and what they can see (2 to 2.5 years) to taking another's differing view by 3 and confronting two views of one object at about 4.5 | From the reading of [LIT-2919](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2919.md) in [NOTE-2188](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2188.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2104](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2104.md) | Tomasello and colleagues hypothesize that uniquely human cooperation evolved in two steps, first obligate collaborative foraging that made partners interdependent and selected, through partner choice by reputation as a good collaborator, for joint goals, commitment and helping, with reciprocity playing only a minor role, and then group growth and intergroup competition that scaled this into collective intentionality with conventions, norms and institutions | From the reading of [LIT-2921](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2921.md) in [NOTE-2192](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2192.md). | [THEORY-2105](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2105.md) | Tomasello argues that human communication is cooperative at base, pointing and pantomime working without conventions through an overt communicative intention, motives of requesting, informing and sharing, and common ground, on an infrastructure of shared intentionality evolved for collaboration, and that arbitrary conventions were built later on such natural gestures, which great apes lack | From the reading of [LIT-2910](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2910.md) in [NOTE-2210](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2210.md), a stand-in for [LIT-2903](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2903.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2106](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2106.md) | Tomasello argues that uniquely human thinking evolved in two steps from great apes' individual intentionality, first joint intentionality in dyadic collaboration and cooperative communication, yielding perspectival representation, recursive inference and social self-monitoring, then collective intentionality in cultural groups, yielding objective representation, self-reflective inference and normative self-governance | From the reading of [LIT-2889](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2889.md) in [NOTE-2200](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2200.md), with the reply [LIT-2887](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2887.md); stand-ins for [LIT-2930](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2930.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2107](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2107.md) | Tomasello argues that a participant can understand a social role only inside cooperation structured by shared intentionality, a joint goal with individual roles, and that taking part in such dual-level collaboration, which chimpanzees do not, leads young children to perspectival and objective thinking, role-based concepts, self-other equivalence and fairness, and a normative moral identity | From the reading of [LIT-2890](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2890.md) in [NOTE-2182](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2182.md). | [THEORY-2108](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2108.md) | Tomasello argues that infants and great apes pass implicit false-belief tasks by tracking what others see and know, a capacity evolved for competition, whereas children come to understand false belief at about four to five by coordinating conflicting perspectives, including an objective one, in the cooperative interaction and communication of shared intentionality | From the reading of [LIT-2915](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2915.md) in [NOTE-2211](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2211.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2109](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2109.md) | Tomasello and Vaish hold that human morality is a form of cooperation that arose in two steps, repeated in child development, first collaboration with particular partners giving a second-personal morality of helping, equal sharing and commitment, then group life giving an agent-neutral morality of mutually known norms enforced on others and, through guilt and shame, on oneself | From the reading of [LIT-2929](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2929.md) in [NOTE-2180](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2180.md), a stand-in for the 2016 book. A review. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2110](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2110.md) | Killen argues against Tomasello that cooperation and interdependence are a basis for morality but not sufficient for it, since from early childhood independent judgments of fairness coexist with group-minded cooperation and let children oppose group norms that treat others unequally, and peer conflict, not collaboration alone, drives moral change | From the reading of [LIT-2927](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2927.md) in [NOTE-2203](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2203.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2111.md) | McAuliffe, Blake, Steinbeis and Warneken argue that children show the signatures of fairness in order, refusing to get less than a peer by about four, punishing unfairness to self and others at a cost by six to eight and refusing advantageous inequality by about eight, varying by culture, and that three-year-olds already state equal division as a norm but do not follow it when it costs them | From the reading of [LIT-2920](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2920.md) in [NOTE-2206](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2206.md). | [THEORY-2112](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2112.md) | Rakoczy reviews theory-of-mind development as a perception–goal psychology from about nine months, which supports joint attention and joint intention, followed by explicit belief–desire meta-representation from about age four and a gradual later development of recursive mindreading, and reports that infant implicit false-belief findings have repeatedly failed direct replication | From the reading of [LIT-2911](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2911.md) in [NOTE-2205](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2205.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2113](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2113.md) | Grueneisen, Wyman and Tomasello show that six-year-olds use first- and second-order false-belief reasoning to coordinate with a peer without communication, choosing the option their partner falsely believes, or falsely believes they believe, to hold the larger reward, more often than when they choose independently | From the reading of [LIT-2900](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2900.md) in [NOTE-2209](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2209.md). | [THEORY-2114](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2114.md) | Cheng, Gao, Tomasello and Kushnir report that in a non-verbal coordination game human–human pairs show the highest joint commitment and coordination efficiency, that both fall when the partner is an AI optimizing an objective, and that children paired with an individual-reward partner are less efficient in proportion to their reduced joint commitment | From the reading of [LIT-2906](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2906.md) in [NOTE-2187](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2187.md), a poster standing in for [LIT-2898](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2898.md); values read off its layout and Study 2 unfinished. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2115](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2115.md) | Block argues that because we can attribute consciousness to other systems only by extrapolating from ourselves, and our consciousness may depend on our computational roles, on their subcomputational biological realizers, or on both, the major theories of consciousness are meat-neutral, and choosing roles favours conscious AI while choosing realizers favours conscious simple animals | From the reading of [LIT-2925](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2925.md) in [NOTE-2204](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2204.md). | [THEORY-2116](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2116.md) | Tomasello and colleagues propose that what is uniquely human in cognition is shared intentionality, an evolved motivation and capacity to take part in activities with shared goals and joint intentions, which emerges by about 14 months from a primate-general understanding of intentional action plus a uniquely human motivation to share, is absent in great apes, and from which language, belief–desire psychology and social norms derive | From the reading of [LIT-2902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2902.md) in [NOTE-2185](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2185.md). | [THEORY-2118](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2118.md) | Killen and Smetana hold that Piaget was right that peer relations foster concepts of fairness and that strict equality precedes equity, but wrong that early morality is heteronomous, since by about three to four children judge moral transgressions wrong independently of authority, take intentions into account and prefer equal distribution | From the reading of [LIT-2907](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2907.md) in [NOTE-2190](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2190.md). | [THEORY-2120](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2120.md) | Schelling holds that people who must coordinate without communicating can often do far better than chance by converging on a focal point that their shared situation makes prominent and unique, and that the same convergence of mutual expectations on conspicuous terms such as equal splits, round numbers, precedent and natural boundaries settles where explicit bargains and tacit limits in war come to rest, even against one party's interest | From the reading of [LIT-2894](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2894.md) in [NOTE-2193](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2193.md), a stand-in for chapter 3 of [LIT-2897](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2897.md). | [THEORY-2124](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2124.md) | Bohn, Kachel and Tomasello report that when speech is blocked young children create iconic gestural signs within one 30-minute reference game, that partners adopt them so that they become pair-specific and drift slightly toward the arbitrary as effort drops, and that six- and eight-year-olds combine signs into compositional sequences more often for complex relations, not in their native word order | From the reading of [LIT-2923](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2923.md) in [NOTE-2212](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2212.md). | [THEORY-2128](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2128.md) | Tomasello holds that agency is an organization of perception, goals and decision for acting where the environment is unpredictable, that learning serves it as a subprocess, that current machines lack its executive tier and the shared intentionality from which humans create conventions, so that artificial agents are better built up from coordination than down from language, and that markets and other emergent social regularities are not agents | From the reading of [LIT-2905](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2905.md) in [NOTE-2196](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2196.md). | [THEORY-2129](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2129.md) | Davidson argues that a creature has beliefs, and so any propositional attitude and any rationality, only if it has the concept of belief, which liability to surprise shows every believer must have, and that this concept, being the concept of objective truth, comes only from triangulating with another creature in communication, so that only communicators are rational animals | From the reading of [LIT-2901](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2901.md) in [NOTE-2199](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2199.md). | [THEORY-2135](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2135.md) | Chizat, Oyallon and Bach show that lazy training, in which a non-linear model trained by gradient methods stays close to its linearization at initialization, is produced by a choice of scale: multiplying the output by α makes the relative change of the model's differential per step small against that of the loss, so that as α grows the parameters move by order 1/α and the model and its linearization differ by order 1/α, and their experiments find networks in this regime generalize worse | The scale account of lazy training, read for [CLAIM-775](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-775.md): a separation of rates between a fast output and a slow parameter vector, readout included. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2136](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2136.md) | Bernstein and Newhouse construct a duality map for general networks by assigning each layer an operator norm and inducing a map recursively through the modular norm; for a linear layer under the RMS→RMS norm it sends a gradient UΣVᵀ to √(d_out/d_in)·UVᵀ, an update whose singular values all have the same magnitude, approximated by a Newton–Schulz iteration that converges to UVᵀ | The reading behind [CLAIM-774](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-774.md)'s update rule: modular dualization of a linear layer is the scaled polar factor, every singular direction moved by the same amount. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2137](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2137.md) | Bovier, Eckhoff, Gayrard and Klein hold that for a reversible Markov chain with generically separated metastable points, minus the logarithm of the capacity between them is an ultrametric up to an additive ln 3, the mean time to leave a point's valley is the valley's mass over that capacity up to a factor 1 + o(1), and each metastable point owns one low-lying eigenvalue equal to the inverse of that time, with an eigenvector near the valley's indicator | The sharp, large-N metastability result the record lacked beside its logarithmic Freidlin–Wentzell holdings ([THEORY-1366](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1366.md), [THEORY-1370](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1370.md)). It bears on the record's commute-time tree ([CLAIM-780](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-780.md)) by giving its general reversible counterpart with a size-independent slack. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2138](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2138.md) | Large, Liu, Huh, Bahng, Isola and Bernstein define a modular norm on a network's weights, built recursively from per-module norms, masses and sensitivities, in which each module's contribution to the linearized change in output is bounded by its share of the total mass, zero mass freezing a module; normalizing updates in it made learning rates transfer across width and depth in their experiments, and a 1/L residual construction has depth-independent sharpness | The modular norm read for [CLAIM-775](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-775.md): mass is a hand-set allocation of learning among modules, in ratios, with width handled by the atoms' norms. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2139](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2139.md) | Yang, Simon and Bernstein show that hidden features and their per-step changes stay of order one per entry at every width when each weight matrix and each of its updates has spectral norm of order √(fan-out/fan-in), that μP is the unique stable abc-parametrization meeting this condition, and that standard and neural-tangent parametrizations violate it | The spectral restatement of μP, bridging the width-exponent view ([THEORY-2133](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2133.md)) and the norm-based modular view ([THEORY-2138](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2138.md), [THEORY-2136](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2136.md)). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2140](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2140.md) | Belrose and colleagues show that in pre-LayerNorm transformer language models each layer's hidden state can be decoded by an affine translator into a next-token distribution whose perplexity falls smoothly with depth, that residual updates align with the negative loss gradient at every layer, as iterative inference predicts, and that decoding needs a separate translator per layer because hidden-state covariance drifts apart with layer separation | Depth as iterative refinement of a prediction, with the representation itself drifting ([CLAIM-771](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-771.md)); gradient-aligned updates as the systematic row of [CLAIM-767](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-767.md). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2141](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2141.md) | Bachas and Huberman show that a random walk among the leaves of an ultrametric tree, with rates set by the height of the common ancestor, relaxes by one exponential mode per branch point, so that on an infinite uniform tree with b offspring per node and per-pair rates falling by a factor g per level the autocorrelation decays as a power of time with exponent ln b/(ln(1/g) − ln b) when gb < 1, while on any finite tree it ends in exponential decay | Ultradiffusion, read as the stand-in for Ogielski and Stein. It is what a tree of rate differences ([CLAIM-780](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-780.md)'s limit) looks like from one state over time: a power law, not an exponential. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2142](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2142.md) | De Pasquale, Smith, Bullo and Valcher show that ergodicity coefficients are induced matrix seminorms and that projection and distance seminorms are dual, so one coefficient bounds both averaging and the flow of distributions, and that in systems leaving a seminorm's kernel or its complement invariant only the part off the kernel contracts, while differences along it may persist or grow | The discrete-time, Markov-side sibling of [THEORY-2143](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2143.md). It joins averaging and distribution flows in one seminorm framework, and confirms that semicontraction is a statement about forgetting off a kernel, not about what is kept on it. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
