| [THEORY-2143](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2143.md) | Jafarpour, Cisneros-Velarde and Bullo show that a continuous-time system contracting in a seminorm converges to a translate of the seminorm's kernel without fixing where on it each trajectory ends, and may diverge along it; that one also weakly contracting, with a kernel of equilibria, converges to a single equilibrium; and that in affine averaging that equilibrium is fixed by a conserved linear functional, not by the seminorm | The reading the record needed for [CLAIM-772](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-772.md)'s appeal to semicontraction. Semicontraction is the forgetting half of the record's picture only: it contracts what lies off the kernel. The keeping half comes from an exact invariant (vᵀx, as πF in [THEORY-960](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-960.md)). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2144](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2144.md) | Lad, Lee, Gurnee and Tegmark find that in GPT-2 and Pythia models deleting or swapping a single middle layer at inference leaves most top-1 predictions unchanged while first-layer interventions are catastrophic, and, from this and from probes, logit-lens and neuron statistics across 16 models in five families, hypothesize four ordered stages of inference: detokenization, feature engineering, prediction ensembling and residual sharpening | Ordered stages around a behaviourally robust middle, the second half specialized ([CLAIM-771](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-771.md)). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2145](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2145.md) | Sun, Pickett, Nain and Jones report that in frozen pretrained transformers the hidden states fall into a few beginning layers, a large middle and one or two ending layers, and that the middle layers share a representation space but do different work: skipping, reordering or running them in parallel degrades benchmarks gracefully, replacing them with copies of one layer is catastrophic, and math and reasoning tasks depend most on layer order | Evidence for a broad, robust middle in transformer depth, with the correction that it is uniform without being redundant ([CLAIM-771](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-771.md)). Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2146](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2146.md) | Bordelon, Noci, Li, Hanin and Pehlevan show, by a physics-level dynamical mean-field derivation and experiments on ResNets and ViTs, that a residual network with μP scaling and branches scaled by 1/√depth has a joint infinite-width and infinite-depth feature-learning limit in which each preactivation evolves over layer time as a diffusion from random contributions uncorrelated across blocks, each of order 1/√L, plus a drift from learned updates that skip connections correlate across blocks, each of order 1/L, with no depth factor in the learning rate | The second source for the record's two drift rows in depth ([CLAIM-767](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-767.md)), in DMFT and in so many words: diffusion from initialization, drift from learning, the skip connection as the correlating mechanism. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2147](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2147.md) | Reddy, Levine and Dragan propose that an assistive interface can be scored and trained, with no knowledge of the user's task, by the mutual information between the user's command and the state transition it induces, on the premise that a more intuitive interface makes commands less noisy; they find it ranks interfaces with task reward in four of five offline domains and learns usable interfaces online, with the time offset needing prior knowledge of the timescale of the user's desired influence | First Contact's central account, read locally on 2026-11-21 ([NOTE-2236](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2236.md)). The record's use of it is [CLAIM-788](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-788.md) (a channel formed to repair a failure of information) and [CLAIM-787](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-787.md) (the horizon as a level). Proposed until an independent replication. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2148](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2148.md) | Baik, Ben Arous and Péché prove that for complex Gaussian samples whose population covariance is the identity but for finitely many eigenvalues, with at least as many samples as variables, the largest sample eigenvalue leaves the bulk edge if and only if some population eigenvalue exceeds 1 + √(N/M), converging then to a stated outlier with fluctuations of order M^(-1/2) instead of the edge's Tracy-Widom M^(-2/3) | Baik, Ben Arous and Péché (2005), [LIT-2986](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2986.md), read in [NOTE-2241](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2241.md): the BBP transition. The record's spiked-matrix claims use its threshold and outlier, but for real data, eigenvectors, more variables than samples and several outliers they rest on Baik and Silverstein, Paul, and Benaych-Georges and Nadakuditi, which this paper corroborates ([ARG-145](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-145.md)). Proposed until a second reading confirms it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2149](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2149.md) | Baik and Silverstein prove that for real or complex samples with independent standardized entries of finite fourth moment and a population covariance that is the identity but for finitely many spikes, at any ratio of variables to samples c, each spike above 1 + √c gives its own sample eigenvalue converging almost surely to α + cα/(α − 1), and spikes at or below it leave the top eigenvalue at the bulk edge | Baik and Silverstein (2006), [LIT-2988](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2988.md), read in [NOTE-2245](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2245.md) (§1 only). The real, non-Gaussian, any-ratio, every-spike version of the BBP threshold and outlier, for limits. The record's spiked-matrix claims rest on it where BBP's complex Gaussian top-eigenvalue result does not reach ([ARG-151](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-151.md)). Proposed until the theorems are confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2150](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2150.md) | Mitzenmacher traces preferential attachment from Yule and Simon to the Web-graph models and Gibrat's multiplicative process to the lognormal, and shows that a lognormal can look straight on a log-log plot and that a lower reflecting barrier or an exponentially distributed observation time turns the multiplicative process's lognormal into a power law | Mitzenmacher (2004), [LIT-3003](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3003.md), read in [NOTE-2237](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2237.md). A survey: its results are other people's, given intuitively. What the record uses is the map of small changes (a floor, a random observation time) that turn multiplicative growth's lognormal into a power law, and the warning that one law has several mechanisms. Its floor is a reflecting minimum, not Kesten's additive term, and it treats only linear attachment kernels. Proposed until the reading is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2151](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2151.md) | Bialek, Nemenman and Tishby: the predictive information of a stationary series is the subextensive part of its entropy; when the data come from a model with K parameters drawn once from a prior it grows as (K/2) log N, with K replaced by a smaller dimension when the parameterization is degenerate, and when the density of models at small divergence from the target has an essential singularity exp(−B/D^μ) it grows, in the annealed approximation, as N^(μ/(μ+1)), as N^(1/2) for a smooth density under a field-theory prior | Bialek, Nemenman and Tishby (2001), [LIT-3008](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3008.md), read in [NOTE-2243](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2243.md). The source of the three regimes of predictive information the record's [TERM-141](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-141.md) carries. Their I_pred(T) has an infinite future. The power-law class is annealed and its essential singularity posited, then derived for one prior; the statements about criticality are asserted, not shown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2152](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2152.md) | Benaych-Georges and Nadakuditi show that a large Gaussian rectangular matrix plus a fixed-rank deterministic perturbation has an outlying singular value, and singular vectors correlated with the perturbation's, only for perturbation singular values above the fourth root of the aspect ratio, with closed forms for both above it | Benaych-Georges and Nadakuditi (2012), [LIT-2964](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2964.md), read in [NOTE-2246](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2246.md) (§3.1 only). The additive, signal-plus-noise form of the spiked transition: the model the record's two-class mixture ([CASE-301](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-301.md)) and mean-shift step ([CLAIM-827](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-827.md)) actually use, with the same formulas as the spiked covariance model ([ARG-135](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-135.md)). Proposed until §3.1 and the theorems behind it are confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2153](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2153.md) | Paul proves that for real Gaussian samples with a spiked covariance and fewer variables than samples, the sample eigenvector of a simple spike above 1 + √γ has a squared overlap with the population eigenvector tending to (1 − γ/(ℓ − 1)²)/(1 + γ/(ℓ − 1)), and that below the threshold the overlap tends to zero | Paul (2007), [LIT-3006](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3006.md), read in [NOTE-2238](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2238.md) (statements only). The eigenvector half of the spiked transition, for real Gaussian data with γ < 1, which [CLAIM-799](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-799.md) and [CASE-301](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-301.md) state and the BBP paper does not prove ([ARG-143](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-143.md)). Proposed until Theorem 4 is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2154](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2154.md) | Transtrum and colleagues (2015) characterize a sloppy model by Fisher eigenvalues roughly evenly spaced in log over many decades with no boundary between stiff and sloppy combinations, and, since those eigenvalues change under reparametrization, locate the invariant content in a bounded model manifold whose geodesic widths fall exponentially, the hyperribbon, approximated by the square roots of the eigenvalues in dimensionless parameters, argued from interpolation for one independent variable, and read through parameter-space compression as why coarse-grained theories predict well | Transtrum, Machta, Brown, Daniels, Myers and Sethna (2015), [LIT-2994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2994.md), read in [NOTE-2242](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2242.md). The programme's own statement of what sloppiness is: a spectrum as symptom, the hyperribbon as substance. It gives no quantitative criterion and draws no line from ill-conditioning or from singularity; its neural-network passage is about an autoencoder's code, not its weights. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2155](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2155.md) | Transtrum, Machta and Sethna (2011) argue from the interpolation error of analytic functions that a multiparameter nonlinear least-squares model's manifold is a bounded hyper-ribbon whose geodesic widths fall by a roughly constant factor; in natural or log units and from a central point the widths match the Jacobian's singular values for a sum of exponentials and a small tanh network, though not in magnitude for the PC12 model; and the manifold's boundaries are where the metric JᵀJ is singular, usually at parameters running to 0 or ∞ but also on finite fold lines such as equal rates | Transtrum, Machta and Sethna (2011), [LIT-3009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3009.md), read in [NOTE-2247](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2247.md). The geometry the record's [TERM-135](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-135.md) and [TERM-140](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-140.md) rest on. The widths are invariant where the Fisher spectrum is not, and match √λ only under conditions; the edges of the hyper-ribbon are where the metric is singular, which ties sloppiness to singularity at the boundary and leaves the interior regular. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2156.md) | Transtrum, Machta and Sethna (2010) argue that a nonlinear least-squares model's manifold of predictions is typically bounded and ribbon-like, its cross-sectional widths each thinner than the last by a roughly constant factor, from the error of polynomial interpolation for analytic models of one variable; in one eight-parameter model they observe the geodesic widths along the eigendirections of JᵀJ tracking the square roots of its eigenvalues over about four decades; fits fail where algorithms reach the manifold's boundaries, and adding geodesic acceleration to Levenberg–Marquardt raised its success on one four-exponential test from 33% to 65% | Transtrum, Machta and Sethna (2010), [LIT-2977](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2977.md), read in [NOTE-2240](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2240.md). The letter that named the hyper-ribbon. Its explanation of the width hierarchy (interpolation) and its link to the spectrum (an observation in one model) are separate, and neither is a theorem; the fuller treatment is [LIT-3009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3009.md) ([THEORY-2155](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2155.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2157](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2157.md) | Lau and colleagues define the local learning coefficient of a local minimum as the volume-scaling exponent of its low-loss set and estimate it as nβ*(E[Lₙ] − Lₙ(w*)) under a posterior tempered at β* = 1/log n and tied to w* by a Gaussian of precision γ, sampled by SGLD; that the estimate converges to the coefficient is conjectured, with the conditions on γ left open, and it is calibrated only in noiseless deep linear networks of 10² to 10⁸ parameters, where it tracks the exact values with relative errors mostly between 0 and 0.8, underestimates; elsewhere the authors claim only relative comparisons at fixed sampler settings | Lau, Furman, Wang, Murfet and Wei, [LIT-2995](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2995.md), read in [NOTE-2239](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2239.md). The estimator behind the record's learning-coefficient entries ([THEORY-1275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1275.md), [THEORY-975](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-975.md)). The estimate is a free-energy slope at effective sample size n/log n, cut off also by the localizer's γ; the paper fixes β*, sets γ per experiment, and calibrates only in noiseless deep linear networks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2158](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2158.md) | Dambre and colleagues show that for a dynamical system driven by independent identically distributed input and read out linearly from N observed variables, the capacities to reconstruct orthogonal functions of past inputs sum to at most N, and to exactly N over a complete basis when the system has fading memory and its variables are linearly independent, so that such systems differ in how they divide a fixed capacity between memory and nonlinear computation, not in its total | Dambre, Verstraeten, Schrauwen and Massar (2012), [LIT-2971](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2971.md), read in [NOTE-2244](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2244.md) with the supplement. The bound needs only i.i.d. input, a linear readout and infinite data; fading memory and full rank are the conditions for equality; unobserved noise is a further input and takes part of the total. The record uses it for [CLAIM-809](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-809.md)'s bound ([ARG-128](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-128.md)) and [CLAIM-814](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-814.md), which is an instance of Theorem 7 ([ARG-146](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-146.md)). Its edge is the undriven system's stability edge, and its sweep is input scaling. Proposed until the theorems are confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2159](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2159.md) | Acharya, Rimal and Dhakal find that in 17 decoder-only language models, word-level concept directions taken from final-layer activations put less of their Euclidean energy in the top eigendirections of the unembedding's regularized second moment, the unembedding's right singular basis, than a uniform-in-variance baseline, and more in its tail than norm-matched random directions in 13 of the 17, while differences of the same concepts' unembedding rows lean toward the top eigendirections | Acharya, Rimal and Dhakal, [LIT-2959](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2959.md), read in [NOTE-2251](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2251.md). Where concept vectors point in the logit metric's eigenbasis, from the activation side and the vocabulary side. A placement of directions, not a measure of information or of importance; the paper's own effect measures run with the metric. Its sign flip is what Park, Choe and Veitch's map predicts ([CLAIM-852](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-852.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2160](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2160.md) | Hoogland and colleagues find that in a two-layer attention-only language transformer of about 3.4 million parameters and a two-layer in-context linear-regression transformer of about 52 thousand, plateaus in SGLD estimates of the local learning coefficient over log training time divide training into five stages, four or five of which recur in each of five seeds, and most stages coincide with independently measured changes in behaviour or structure; the estimate rises in most stages and falls in three | Hoogland, Wang, Farrugia-Roberts, Carroll, Wei and Murfet, [LIT-2966](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2966.md), read in [NOTE-2248](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2248.md). Stages of transformer training read off pauses in the local learning coefficient, matched to behavioural and structural changes. Motivated by Bayesian singular learning, not derived from it; the coefficient's decreases are unexplained; the estimator is run at one fixed nβ and γ per setting. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2161](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2161.md) | Song, Ahn and Yun find that in small-learning-rate SGD on small MLP, CNN and Transformer classifiers the stochastic gradient lies mostly in the span of the training-loss Hessian's top-k eigenvectors, k the number of classes, yet projecting each update onto that span stops the training loss falling while projecting it onto the complement trains as fast as SGD; the alignment comes from gradient noise across a steep valley, or from self-stabilizing oscillation at the Edge of Stability, and vanishes under small-step full-batch gradient descent | Song, Ahn and Yun, [LIT-2973](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2973.md), read in [NOTE-2250](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2250.md). Gradient alignment with the dominant Hessian subspace is not where training happens: the loss falls along a steep valley's flat floor, in the complement of the top k. A weak instance of a model's rankings of directions disagreeing ([CLAIM-835](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-835.md)), within one metric. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2162](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2162.md) | Xu finds that in ten trained language models, replacing the final hidden state's component along the 5% of directions the centred, norm-folded unembedding amplifies least moves the logits less than equal-length random changes but changes the next-token distribution and the loss several times more; the prediction change per unit of logit distance stays near random over most of the spectrum and peaks at that bottom band, where the two leading candidate tokens differ disproportionately, while in total the top band's removal costs as much loss or more | Xu, [LIT-2967](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2967.md), read in [NOTE-2249](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2249.md). The logit metric WᵀW and the predictive Fisher pulled back to the final state disagree most along the unembedding's least-amplified directions, per unit of logit distance and against equal-length random changes; not a reversal, since the top band matters as much in total. The record's best evidence that [CLAIM-835](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-835.md)'s disagreement occurs in trained models. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2163](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2163.md) | Amari, Park and Ozeki show that in a multilayer perceptron or gaussian mixture the Fisher information degenerates on a continuum of finite parameter values, where a unit vanishes or two units coincide, which the map to distributions collapses to a cone-type singular point; and that near it ordinary gradient learning has fast and slow manifolds, so the state is drawn quickly towards the singular set and then moves slowly along it, the plateau, even when the truth is regular, while natural gradient is repelled from it | Amari, Park and Ozeki (2006), [LIT-2960](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2960.md), read in [NOTE-2255](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2255.md). Where network singularities are and what they do to learning: critical sets at finite parameters, cone apices in the space of distributions, a Milnor attractor for gradient flow, a slow manifold that makes the plateau, and repulsion under natural gradient. With the truth at the singularity, the gradient along the degenerate direction is cubic (Eq. 5.13), so the approach is algebraic, u ∝ t^(−1/2) (the reader's derivation; the paper states no rate). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2164](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2164.md) | Wei, Zhang, Cousseau, Ozeki and Amari show that in two-layer networks trained by averaged online gradient descent, the flow near an overlap singularity has to leading order a universal first integral whose constant decides whether an orbit reaches the line of overlapping units or passes on to the elimination singularity, as most orbits do; that the line is stable, saddle or split by the signature of a residual matrix, a Milnor-like attractor on which a noise-driven random walk is the on-singularity plateau; and that orbits passing near it cross a flat region where the loss changes only at fourth order, a shorter near-singularity plateau | Wei, Zhang, Cousseau, Ozeki and Amari (2008), [LIT-3000](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3000.md), read in [NOTE-2254](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2254.md). Orbits, not time courses: a conserved quantity of the averaged flow fixes where learning goes near coinciding units, and the long plateau on the singularity is a noise-driven walk along a line of equivalent models, not a slow decay along a degenerate direction. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2165](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2165.md) | Gutenkunst and colleagues find that in seventeen systems-biology models, with 9 to 234 parameters, the Hessian of a least-squares deviation of all time courses in log parameters has eigenvalues spanning many decades, all but one more than six, roughly evenly in log with no cutoff, along eigenvectors skewed from the bare parameter axes; and that in one of them a collective fit constrains a prediction that direct measurement would match only with all 24 relevant parameters measured to about 25% | Gutenkunst, Waterfall, Casey, Brown, Myers and Sethna (2007), [LIT-2999](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2999.md), read in [NOTE-2252](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2252.md). The empirical base of sloppiness: a two-part criterion (even spread over many decades, and skew from the bare axes), shown across a collection, and the argument that collective fits beat direct measurement for predictions, shown in one model. Across the collection the resolved span stays at 5–10 decades while the density of eigenvalues per decade grows with the number of parameters (the reader's computation from Dataset S1, recomputed by the filer). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2166](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2166.md) | Transtrum and Qiu reduce a sloppy model by following a geodesic along the Fisher metric's least sensitive direction until its smallest eigenvalue goes to zero at a boundary of the bounded model manifold, evaluating the limit found there to remove one parameter combination, refitting and repeating, so that the reduced model sits at a hypercorner; the method needs the manifold to have a hierarchy of edges and corners as well as of widths | Transtrum and Qiu (2014), [LIT-2979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2979.md), read in [NOTE-2253](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2253.md). The manifold boundary approximation turns the hyper-ribbon into a reduction algorithm: boundaries are where a parameter combination reaches a limit (0, ∞, or two terms merging), the reduced model is a hypercorner, and the method requires nested edges and corners, which an ellipsoid with a hierarchy of widths lacks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2167](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2167.md) | Quinn, Abbott, Transtrum, Machta and Sethna call a model sloppy, and its model manifold a hyperribbon, when its Fisher eigenvalues and geodesic widths are both hierarchical, roughly evenly spaced in log over several decades; they present the ubiquity of this shape as empirical, bound it rigorously only for least-squares models smooth in their control variables, hold that it gives a low-dimensional description only where many widths fall below the precision demanded, and say that its explanations in renormalizable physics and in least-squares fitting seem completely different | The 2023 review of the sloppy-model programme, [LIT-2958](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2958.md), read in [NOTE-2256](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2256.md). Its sharp edges: "sloppy" needs widths as well as eigenvalues to be hierarchical; ΛCDM is sloppy and yet fully determined, because sloppiness is low-dimensional only against a demanded precision; the rigorous bound is for smooth least-squares models, restated from the 2019 paper ([LIT-3029](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3029.md), Deferred); and the review offers no single account of why simple effective theories exist. It grounds [CLAIM-820](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-820.md) ([ARG-164](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-164.md)) and is drawn on by [TERM-135](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-135.md) and [TERM-140](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-140.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2168](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2168.md) | Azizpour, Priesemann, Zierenberg and Levina show, analytically in the limits and by simulation between them, that in a random network of stochastic spiking neurons with a branching (absorbing-to-active) transition at λ = 1, a leaky readout with finite integration time T makes both the number of ε-discriminable input rates and a fluctuation-aware dynamic range peak at a subcritical λ* < 1, at different λ* for the two measures, with λ* approaching the critical point as T grows, because critically slowed population fluctuations not averaged out within T blur the readout | Azizpour and colleagues, [LIT-2980](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2980.md), read in [NOTE-2259](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2259.md). "Criticality maximizes dynamic range" (Kinouchi and Copelli, [LIT-3027](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3027.md)) becomes "only for infinite integration time": every finite readout window has a subcritical optimum, different for the two measures. One transition (branching), one task family (discriminating stationary input rates); the paper itself says the side of the optimum depends on the task and the transition. Grounds [CLAIM-809](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-809.md)'s window- and task-dependence ([ARG-163](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-163.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2169](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2169.md) | Newman recommends measuring a power law by its cumulative distribution and a maximum-likelihood exponent rather than a least-squares fit to a log-log histogram, and holds that many mechanisms produce power laws, among them combinations of exponentials, inverses of quantities, random-walk first return times, the Yule process, critical phenomena and self-organized criticality, that different ones apply to different cases, and that most observed power laws are probably not the result of phase transitions | Newman (2005), [LIT-2976](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2976.md), read in [NOTE-2261](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2261.md). A tutorial review: its results are mostly other people's, with heuristic derivations the author flags. What the record uses is the catalogue of mechanisms with their exponents, which grounds items 2, 3, 6 and 7 of [CLAIM-795](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-795.md) and adds four mechanisms with no feedback (random typing, highly optimized tolerance, coherent noise, record dynamics), and its judgement that most observed power laws are probably not from phase transitions. It has no model comparison, and it calls the Yule process the most widely accepted theory for citations, cities and income. Proposed until the reading is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2170](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2170.md) | Dandi, Pesce, Cui, Krzakala, Lu and Loureiro prove that after one maximal-update gradient step on Gaussian single-index data a two-layer network's first-layer weights are a random bulk plus a rank-one spike along the target, and give the resulting feature covariance's asymptotic spectrum, whose bulk widens and lengthens its tails beside outliers of order d from the feature means, and the exact test error of the ridge-fitted readout, a functional of the whole deterministic equivalent | Dandi and colleagues, [LIT-2983](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2983.md), read in [NOTE-2258](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2258.md). The spike of one large gradient step is in the weights; in the features, learning shows chiefly as a reshaped bulk, with outliers from the means. Grounds [CLAIM-799](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-799.md)'s narrow point that the spiked picture of learned features is a theorem, and qualifies it ([ARG-166](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-166.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2171](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2171.md) | Park, Bocchi, D'Amico, Lucini and Aarts show, exactly for a linear rank-1 teacher–student model under full-batch gradient descent and heuristically for nonlinear, finite-data and stochastic extensions, that training shrinks the weight covariance's random bulk while growing a spike, so an outlier aligned with the teacher detaches by a BBP transition at a critical step size or a critical time set by the step size and the initial weight variance, while the student converges for every step size below one whether or not the outlier has yet appeared | Park and colleagues, [LIT-2990](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2990.md), read in [NOTE-2260](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2260.md). A dynamical reading of the BBP transition: the outlier's appearance in the weight spectrum is a matter of step size and time, while the signal is in the weights from the first step. Its UTKFace experiments find the leading first-layer directions tracking the data's principal components only in the large-step regime. Grounds [CLAIM-799](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-799.md) ([ARG-171](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-171.md)) and the rival reading [CLAIM-855](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-855.md) ([ARG-174](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-174.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2172.md) | Broido and Clauset, fitting a discrete power law to the upper tail of the degree sequences of 928 network data sets and comparing it by likelihood ratio with exponential, lognormal, Weibull and cutoff alternatives, find a power law plausible for 29% of data sets and strongly supported for 4%, and a lognormal at least as good for 88% of degree distributions, and conclude that a mechanism which necessarily yields power-law degrees has a limited role and that the degree distribution weakly discriminates between mechanisms | Broido & Clauset (2019), [LIT-2963](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2963.md), read in [NOTE-2263](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2263.md). The record's network-scale evidence that a power-law shape is weak evidence of mechanism, and a ground of [CLAIM-803](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-803.md). Its test is of a pure power law above k_min; the verdict is disputed by Voitalov and others ([LIT-3041](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3041.md), unread), who define a power law as a regularly varying tail, [TERM-142](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-142.md)'s sense 1. Proposed until the reading is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2173](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2173.md) | Clauset, Shalizi and Newman hold that a straight line on a log-log plot is necessary but not sufficient for a power law, replace least-squares fits with a maximum-likelihood exponent above a lower bound chosen by minimum Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance, a bootstrap goodness-of-fit test and likelihood-ratio tests against alternatives, and, applying them to 24 data sets, reject 7, find only word frequencies convincing and exclude the lognormal for only one, so that where the tests cannot decide the choice must rest on mechanism | Clauset, Shalizi & Newman (2009), [LIT-2987](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2987.md), read in [NOTE-2262](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2262.md). The record's standard for fitting a tail, and the ground of [CLAIM-803](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-803.md)'s "fit first" clause. Its empirical lesson is that a power law and a lognormal are seldom distinguishable at realistic sample sizes (US city sizes among the undecided), and it defers the choice to mechanism without supplying dynamical tests. Proposed until the reading is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2174.md) | Stringer, Pachitariu, Steinmetz, Carandini and Harris find that the stimulus-related responses of about 10,000 mouse V1 neurons to natural images have a cross-validated eigenspectrum close to a power law with exponent 1.04, fitted over ranks 11 to 500, and prove that in the many-neuron limit a code with finite expected derivative on a d-dimensional stimulus manifold has eigenvalues o(n^(−1−2/d)), a bound on the tail that lower-dimensional stimulus ensembles approach from above | Stringer and colleagues, [LIT-2972](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2972.md), read in [NOTE-2257](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2257.md). V1's code of natural images sits just on the smooth side of the critical exponent 1 + 2/d: a spectrum decaying more slowly would put so much variance in fine directions that the code would stop being differentiable. The bound is strict and asymptotic in rank. It grounds [CLAIM-848](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-848.md)'s premise in that corrected form ([ARG-169](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-169.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2175.md) | Corominas-Murtra, Hanel and Thurner prove that a process jumping uniformly to a lower state visits state i with probability exactly 1 over i, and that mixing its nested steps with uniform jumps gives occupation falling as i to the minus lambda | Corominas-Murtra, Hanel and Thurner (2015), [LIT-2997](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2997.md), read in [NOTE-2266](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2266.md). Sample-space reduction as a route to Zipf's law, with the exponent as the share of nested steps. Proved for uniform jumps only; a Markov chain with no reinforcement. Proposed until the derivation is checked independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2176](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2176.md) | Beck and Cohen define superstatistics as the Laplace transform of a slowly fluctuating inverse temperature's density, show that a gamma density gives Tsallis's q-exponential and that every superstatistics shares the same first correction at small variance, and leave the large-energy behaviour to the density | Beck and Cohen (2003), [LIT-2962](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2962.md), read in [NOTE-2265](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2265.md). A letter: the mixture-of-exponentials construction in physics, with a gamma density giving the Tsallis form exactly and a universality result at small variance. It never says "power law"; which densities give one is the assistant's [CLAIM-857](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-857.md). Proposed until the published text or a second source confirms it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2177](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2177.md) | Reed and Hughes show that a process growing exponentially in expectation and killed at a time with constant hazard has a power-law tail, a single Pareto for deterministic growth and a double Pareto set by a quadratic for geometric Brownian motion | Reed and Hughes (2002), [LIT-3007](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3007.md), read in [NOTE-2264](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2264.md). Killing exponential growth at a random time gives power-law tails; with noise the law is a double Pareto whose exponents solve a quadratic. Support for its applications is visual. Proposed until the general double Pareto is derived independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2178](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2178.md) | Merton names the Matthew effect, the accrual of disproportionate recognition for a given scientific contribution to scientists already eminent and its withholding from those not yet known, an inequity for careers that may raise the visibility of eminent scientists' work in science's communication system, and treats cumulative advantage, in which the rich get richer, as one institutional version of it, giving no model of either | Merton (1968), [LIT-3002](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3002.md), read in a scan of the AAAS reprint in [NOTE-2268](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2268.md). The source of the name the record's cumulative-advantage claims use ([CLAIM-817](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-817.md)), and of the sense [TERM-145](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-145.md) keeps apart from the formal one. The sharp edge: the Matthew effect proper is credit for a given contribution allotted by rank, not growth in proportion to size; Merton states no proportional rule, credits the growth implication to Price, and calls the communication side "a special application of the self-fulfilling prophecy". Proposed until a study that holds contribution fixed confirms the effect. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2179](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2179.md) | Bak, Tang and Wiesenfeld propose that spatially extended threshold systems in two or more dimensions relax to a critical state as an attractor, with no parameter tuned, because relaxation stops where clusters of minimally stable sites cease to percolate; in a sandpile automaton they find power-law cluster sizes (τ ≈ 0.98 in 2D, 1.35 in 3D) cut off by the system size, and spectra ω^(−1.58) and ω^(−1.1), and conjecture that this is the common mechanism of 1/f noise and fractals | Bak, Tang and Wiesenfeld (1987), [LIT-2992](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2992.md), read in full in [NOTE-2269](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2269.md). The founding letter of self-organized criticality: a critical point "reached by starting far from equilibrium", with the percolation-of-minimal-stability heuristic, the sandpile automaton, and power laws judged by eye over two decades. It states no slow-drive, time-scale or conservation condition. It corroborates [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s bullet that SOC reaches a critical point without outside tuning ([ARG-178](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-178.md)), and its finite-size cutoff, asserted without data, is reproduced in [CLAIM-858](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-858.md) ([ARG-181](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-181.md)). Proposed until the reading is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2180](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2180.md) | Barabási and Albert, growing a network one vertex at a time with links attached in proportion to degree, find a stationary power-law degree distribution with exponent near 3 by simulation and exactly 3 by a mean-field argument, an exponential distribution without preferential attachment, a non-stationary one tending to a complete graph without growth, and scaling only for a linear kernel, and propose growth and preferential attachment as the generic origin of the power-law tails they report in real networks | Barabási & Albert (1999), [LIT-3004](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3004.md), read in the arXiv preprint in [NOTE-2272](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2272.md). The record's source for the base case of [CLAIM-817](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-817.md) and the premise of [CLAIM-830](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-830.md), and for A3's sentence that attachment alone does not guarantee a power law ([ARG-179](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-179.md)). The sharp edge: the proposal that the mechanism is generic rests on four networks whose slopes were drawn by eye, the premise Broido and Clauset test ([THEORY-2172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2172.md)). Proposed until the print text and a replication confirm it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2181](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2181.md) | Krapivsky, Redner and Leyvraz, solving the rate equations of a growing tree whose new sites attach with probability proportional to a kernel A_k, find a stretched-exponential degree distribution for A_k = k^γ with 0 < γ < 1, a single site taking nearly all links for γ > 1, and a power law only at γ = 1, where an asymptotically linear kernel A_k → a∞k gives an exponent ν = 1 + μ/a∞ that can take any value above 2 | Krapivsky, Redner & Leyvraz (2000), [LIT-2974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2974.md), read in [NOTE-2267](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2267.md). The record's source for the regimes of the attachment kernel, which [CLAIM-817](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-817.md) and [CLAIM-806](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-806.md) state and [ARG-184](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-184.md) takes them from. The sharp edge: the power law is the borderline case, k^(−3) only for A_k = k exactly, and the authors themselves say that for 0.8 ≲ γ ≲ 1 a stretched exponential and a power law are hard to tell apart up to k = 1000. Proposed until an independent derivation confirms it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2182](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2182.md) | Alsmeyer and Mentemeier prove that the stationary solution of a random difference equation with invertible random matrices and a negative Liapunov exponent has a power-law tail in every direction, with index κ fixed by lim n^(−1) log E‖Π_n‖^κ = 0, a result they say Kesten stated in 1973 and Le Page proved | Alsmeyer and Mentemeier (2012), [LIT-3045](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3045.md), skimmed (introduction only) in [NOTE-2273](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2273.md) as a stand-in for Kesten (1973), [LIT-3005](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3005.md). Their Theorem 1.1 is the matrix form of the Kesten tail; their Remark 1 attributes the statement to Kesten "with one extra condition". The record's second-hand access to Kesten's matrix theorem. Proposed until the reading is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2183](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2183.md) | Kevei restates the Kesten–Grincevičius–Goldie theorem: the stationary solution of X = AX + B has a two-sided Pareto-like tail with index κ solving EA^κ = 1, given EA^κ log⁺A < ∞, a nonarithmetic log A, E\|B\|^κ < ∞ and non-degeneracy, a condition that forces E log A < 0; and, after Goldie, the max equation X = AX ∨ B has the same tail index | Kevei (2016), [LIT-3043](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3043.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2271](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2271.md) as a stand-in for Kesten (1973), [LIT-3005](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3005.md). Its introduction states the one-dimensional theorem with Kesten's hypotheses, its two-sided tail (c+ + c− > 0, so a tail may sit on one side only), the fact that EA^κ = 1 forces log-contraction, Grey's result that with EA^κ < 1 a regularly varying tail can come from B alone, and Goldie's Theorem 5.2 for the max form. It is the record's ground for [CLAIM-824](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-824.md)'s Kesten half, at second hand. Proposed until the reading is confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2184](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2184.md) | Barabási's Network Science chapter on the Barabási–Albert model derives a degree exponent of 3 from arrival at equal steps and the exact degree distribution 2m(m+1)/[k(k+1)(k+2)], shows that dropping growth or preferential attachment loses the scale-free property or stationarity, states after Krapivsky, Redner and Leyvraz that only linear attachment gives a pure power law, reports measured attachment exponents near 1, and reads link selection, copying and optimisation as routes that generate linear attachment | Barabási (2016), [LIT-2968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2968.md), read in the author's web edition in [NOTE-2270](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2270.md). A secondary source for the kernel regimes of [CLAIM-817](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-817.md) and [CLAIM-806](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-806.md) beside [THEORY-2181](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2181.md), and the record's source for the measured attachment exponents (α ≈ 1 for the Internet and citations, 0.9 ± 0.1 for co-authorship and actors). The sharp edge: its claim that preferential attachment is "necessary and sufficient", and that "all known models and real systems that are scale-free" have it, is a framing that reads geometric and optimisation models as generating attachment, which the record does not adopt ([CLAIM-817](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-817.md), [THEORY-188](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-188.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2185](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2185.md) | Yang, Steinhardt and Hu find that ResNet-18 trained on CIFAR-10 with labels merged into five two-class super-classes meets neural collapse on the coarse labels yet keeps the original classes as sub-clusters, recoverable without labels well enough that a linear probe on the recovered labels reaches over 93 per cent on the ten-class test set, and that the sub-clusters form before the label-driven merging, persist to 1,000 epochs and are absent in VGG | Yang, Steinhardt and Hu, [LIT-2957](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2957.md), read in [NOTE-2276](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2276.md). Neural collapse on coarse labels leaves the fine classes in the residual variation, linearly decodable after label-free clustering. Grounds [CLAIM-800](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-800.md)'s point that a geometric measure can saturate while finer information persists ([ARG-186](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-186.md)), and qualifies [THEORY-788](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-788.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2186.md) | Wang, Wu and Fan prove that in a deep network with random Gaussian weights at linear width and an odd-type activation a bounded input spike yields an outlier of a layer's conjugate kernel only if it passes a BBP-type test at every layer up to it, so the number of outliers and their alignment with the input cannot increase with depth, and that after a few gradient steps at unit-order step size a two-layer network's test-data conjugate kernel has a label-aligned outlier only above a threshold | Wang, Wu and Fan, [LIT-2984](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2984.md), read in [NOTE-2274](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2274.md). At random weights an input spike survives each layer only past a BBP-type test, and depth can only lose outliers and alignment. After training the rank-one weight update exists for any step size, but the weights' top singular value separates only above one threshold and the kernel's outlier needs a second condition. Grounds [CLAIM-799](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-799.md) as a third case of signal before outlier ([ARG-188](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-188.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2187](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2187.md) | Martínez-Sánchez, Arranz and Lozano-Durán find that decomposing the predictive information that the volume-averaged interscale energy fluxes at four inertial-range filter widths of a forced isotropic turbulence simulation carry about each other's futures gives unique terms only from each scale to the next smaller one, with any small-to-large dependence redundant and synergy minor, and read this as directed causality of the forward cascade | Martínez-Sánchez and colleagues, [LIT-2965](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2965.md), read in [NOTE-2275](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2275.md). SURD measures predictive information among time series of a physical flux, so it keeps transfer and dependence apart as objects; its "causality" is prediction. An instance of [CLAIM-335](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-335.md)'s point ([ARG-185](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-185.md)), and a fit to [CLAIM-810](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-810.md)'s turbulence row that does not test its separations ([ARG-187](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-187.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2188](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2188.md) | Cai, Zhang, Liu and Shi show that as the number of negatives grows InfoNCE and its gradient converge to a deterministic energy over the representation's distribution on a compact embedding manifold, which for one modality is a strictly convex free energy, alignment potential over temperature minus entropy, with a unique Gibbs minimizer, and for symmetric two-modality InfoNCE carries a negative symmetric KL divergence between the modalities that makes each one's density a barrier for the other | Cai and colleagues, [LIT-2975](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2975.md), read in [NOTE-2277](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2277.md). InfoNCE's large-batch limit is a passive, variational energy over the representation's law: one free energy with a Gibbs equilibrium for one modality, one joint energy with a repulsive cross-modal term for two. Grounds [CLAIM-798](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-798.md)'s weak reading and gives nothing toward its strong one ([ARG-189](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-189.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2189](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2189.md) | Ansuini, Laio, Macke and Zoccolan find that in trained image CNNs the TwoNN intrinsic dimension of a layer's representations is orders of magnitude below the layer's width, rises over the early layers and falls to about 12 to 25 in the last hidden layer, and is one to two orders below a 90 per cent variance PCA count, and that across architectures, not across seeds, its last-layer value correlates with test accuracy | Ansuini and colleagues, [LIT-2998](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2998.md), read in [NOTE-2278](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2278.md). Representations of trained CNNs lie near curved low-dimensional manifolds: a nonlinear estimate of their dimension is far below width and below a linear PCA count, which does not tell trained from random networks apart. [TERM-136](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-136.md) takes its intrinsic sense from this reading. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2190](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2190.md) | Bui and colleagues make an updated embedding model backward-compatible by lifting both models' embeddings into the Lorentz model and penalising each new embedding for leaving the entailment cone apexed at the same item's old embedding, beside an uncertainty-weighted contrastive loss, and on CIFAR100 and TinyImageNet this improves cross-model retrieval compatibility over Euclidean alignment baselines at little cost to the new model, most of all when the architecture changes | Bui, Yang, Chen, Neves, Ju, Ying, Shah & Zhao (2025), [LIT-2989](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2989.md), read in [NOTE-2281](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2281.md). Temporal cone restriction as a soft regularizer, and it works. The sharp edges: the hinge is weighted 0.3 and cone satisfaction is never reported; the cones are per item, between two separately trained models; one run per configuration; and the clipping radius must rise at every update, which the authors list as a limitation and which follows from the cone geometry ([CLAIM-860](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-860.md)). Proposed until replicated. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2191](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2191.md) | Lee, Smith, Adam and Hoogland find that the Bayesian influence of one training sample on another, estimated as a negative posterior covariance from sampling localized at each checkpoint, changes in sign and magnitude over training: in a two-layer linear network on a hierarchical dataset it flips sign and peaks as each level of the hierarchy is learned, in small language models token-class influences shift around induction-circuit formation, and upweighting induction tokens speeds induction heads in the window where that influence falls and delays them earlier | Lee, Smith, Adam & Hoogland (2025), [LIT-3001](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3001.md), read in [NOTE-2279](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2279.md). Influence as a susceptibility that changes at stage transitions. The sharp edges: the theory is for a Bayesian posterior split between two phases, and the link to SGD is the paper's "primary theoretical gap"; peaks are predicted only "under some conditions"; in the toy, the order of the peaks is the order of the modes' strengths. A.2 names the "Type-B" transition, equal loss with a falling LLC, without testing it. Proposed until reproduced. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2192](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2192.md) | Ghadimi Atigh and colleagues find that an image classifier with a class tree embedded as hyperbolic prototypes, trained on labels from any level of the tree with a coarse label as a uniform target over its leaves, an entailment-cone penalty toward the label's cone and a Busemann pull toward the label's boundary direction, reaches far higher leaf accuracy than one that discards the coarse labels, and recovers withheld fine labels, when most labels are coarse | Ghadimi Atigh, van Spengler, Long, Ayoughi, Kasarla & Mettes (2026), [LIT-2993](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2993.md), read in [NOTE-2282](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2282.md). Supervision as a region whose narrowness matches the label's specificity, with depth by radius. The sharp edges: coarsening is simulated uniformly at random; some leaf labels always remain; the prototypes are fixed, so nothing moves but the images; and the radial placement has to be enforced by a separate Busemann term, which hurts when few labels are coarse. Its "coarse-to-fine" names a label projection, not an order of learning. Proposed until replicated. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2193](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2193.md) | Yang finds that a detached Gaussian-mixture probe fitted to an encoder's output loses its collapsed state through a supercritical pitchfork at a precision equal to the reciprocal of the largest eigenvalue of the features' covariance, that the visible split can lag that crossing by orders of magnitude, so that in modular-addition grokking the crossing comes near step 40 and generalisation thousands of steps later, sooner with more weight decay, and that in sparse autoencoders an atom's part-of-speech purity early in training predicts its purity at convergence | Yang (2026), [LIT-2961](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2961.md), read in [NOTE-2280](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2280.md). Rose, Gurewitz and Fox's annealing threshold made dynamic, with the crossing separated from the visible split. The sharp edges: the pitchfork is the probe's, and the probe is detached ("the encoder's gradients never see the probe"); the bridge from the probe's split to the network's grokking plateau is a tilt the paper adds by hand and calls empirical; the per-atom choice is made by noise and cubic terms on a shared unstable subspace, not by small initial advantages compounding. Proposed until reproduced. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2194.md) | Gelfert and Nolting show that Mermin and Wagner's exclusion of ferro- and antiferromagnetic order in the one- and two-dimensional Heisenberg model rests on Bogoliubov's inequality reducing the order parameter's bound to the divergence of ∫d^Dk/k² in D ≤ 2, and report that Cassi, after Hattori, Hattori and Watanabe, extended the exclusion to fractal and disordered lattices of spectral dimension at most 2 | Gelfert and Nolting (2001), [LIT-3057](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3057.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2290](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2290.md) as a stand-in for Mermin and Wagner (1966), [LIT-2985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2985.md). The proof's outline and the graph version are both at second hand: the bounds are stated "as has been shown by Mermin and Wagner", and Cassi's theorem is reported in one paragraph. It is the record's ground for [CLAIM-842](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-842.md)'s d_s ≤ 2 criterion as a theorem of spin models ([ARG-200](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-200.md)). Proposed until the originals are read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2195](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2195.md) | Nachtergaele proves, by energy-entropy balance on equilibrium states, that a continuous symmetry is not spontaneously broken at finite temperature in one or two dimensions for quantum spin systems whose couplings have a finite second moment, with no need for translation invariance | Nachtergaele (2006), [LIT-3050](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3050.md), read in full in [NOTE-2289](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2289.md) as a stand-in for the statement of Mermin and Wagner (1966), [LIT-2985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2985.md). A general proof in course notes; it bears on [CLAIM-842](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-842.md) by showing the theorem does not need a regular lattice. Proposed until confirmed in a published source. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2196](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2196.md) | Gingrich, Horowitz, Perunov and England prove that for an ergodic Markov jump network with reversible transitions and local detailed balance, in its nonequilibrium steady state, the large-deviation rate function of any current that is a linear combination of edge currents lies below the quadratic (j_d − j^π_d)²Σ^π/(4(j^π_d)²), so current fluctuations are always at least as likely as linear response predicts, and that every such current therefore obeys the thermodynamic uncertainty relation ε²_d Σ^π ≥ 2, tightest for the dissipation current itself and in linear response | Gingrich and colleagues (2016), [LIT-2981](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2981.md), read in [NOTE-2291](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2291.md). The general proof of the thermodynamic uncertainty relation that Barato and Seifert ([LIT-1885](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1885.md), [THEORY-1268](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1268.md)) proved only in linear response and for unicyclic networks and otherwise conjectured: for every current of a Markov jump network, far from equilibrium included, and as a bound on the whole rate function, so on rare fluctuations as well as the variance. Long-time, steady-state, reversible transitions only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2197](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2197.md) | Drouin-Touchette's notes derive that the two-dimensional XY model's spin waves give correlations falling as r^(−k_BT/2πJ) at every low temperature, that below the Kosterlitz–Thouless temperature the vortex fugacity flows to zero on a line of fixed points, so the whole low-temperature phase has an infinite correlation length with nothing tuned, and that at the transition the correlation length diverges as an essential singularity, not a power | Drouin-Touchette (2022), [LIT-3055](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3055.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2295](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2295.md) as a stand-in for Kosterlitz and Thouless (1973), [LIT-2969](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2969.md). Standard results, derived at a student level and credited to Kosterlitz (1974) and José et al. (1977). Grounds [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s XY row with Kosterlitz's lecture ([THEORY-2206](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2206.md)) ([ARG-198](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-198.md)), and the BKT case of [CLAIM-862](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-862.md). Proposed until checked against the primary papers. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2198](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2198.md) | Le Doussal's retrospective holds that for d > 2 the KPZ coupling has an intermediate fixed point separating a weak-noise phase where the nonlinearity is irrelevant from the strong-noise KPZ phase, that the tilt symmetry fixes χ = 2 − z, and that the 1986 conjecture of dimension-independent exponents failed, with χ = 0.3869(4) in two dimensions | Le Doussal (2025), [LIT-3062](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3062.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2293](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2293.md) for one passage (p. 4). A summary by a specialist of results it cites, not derived here. Used to scope [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s KPZ row to d ≤ 2 ([ARG-195](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-195.md)) and for [CLAIM-862](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-862.md)'s higher-dimensional case. Proposed until the cited literature is read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2199](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2199.md) | In Toner and Tu's continuum theory of flocking, the ordered phase of a rotation-invariant, number-conserving flock without Galilean invariance scales anomalously throughout the phase, not only at its transition: below four dimensions convective nonlinearities replace diffusive transport, so that the long-range order the linearized theory loses in two dimensions survives, with exponents argued to be exact there, and density fluctuations whose structure factor diverges as q → 0; an explicit preferred direction removes the anomalous fluctuations | Toner and Tu (1998), [LIT-2970](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2970.md), read in [NOTE-2285](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2285.md) (§V.B's algebra and §VI skimmed). The linear theory's loss of order in d ≤ 2 and the relevance of the convective terms below d = 4 are calculations; the d = 2 exponents rest on a new symmetry argument and a flow the authors call "highly probable"; the equations are posited from symmetry. It grounds [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s ordered-active-matter row by the diverging structure factor ([ARG-197](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-197.md)), marks the equilibrium limit of [CLAIM-842](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-842.md)'s d_s ≤ 2 criterion, and is one case of [CLAIM-862](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-862.md). Proposed until the order and the structure factor are confirmed independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2200](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2200.md) | Crutchfield and Feldman show that for a stationary process on a finite alphabet the excess entropy, the summed excess of the finite-L entropy-rate estimates over the entropy rate, equals both the subextensive part of the block entropy and the mutual information between past and future, is bounded below by its finite-block estimates, and is finite for finitary processes, whose estimates fall faster than 1/L; that an observer who ignores it at block length L overestimates the entropy rate by E/L; and that it does not fix the structure of a process, which the transient information and the number of causal states can separate where the excess entropy cannot | Crutchfield and Feldman (2003), [LIT-3010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3010.md), read from the 2001 arXiv preprint in [NOTE-2286](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2286.md). One derivative-and-integral hierarchy of the block entropy gathers the entropy rate, the predictability gain, the excess entropy and a new transient information. Excess entropy is "one kind of memory": equal for processes the transient information tells apart, and small for a source whose optimal predictor has infinitely many states. Drawn on by [TERM-141](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-141.md); corroborates [CLAIM-805](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-805.md)'s separation of entropy from memory. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2201](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2201.md) | Takeuchi and Sano find that turbulent DSM2 clusters growing in nematic electroconvection, driven well above threshold, roughen with the 1+1-dimensional KPZ exponents and that their local-radius fluctuations follow the GUE Tracy-Widom distribution, with GOE and Gaussian ruled out by the parameter-free skewness and kurtosis, and Airy₂ correlations, which they attribute to strictly local growth, intrinsic noise and the absence of quenched disorder | Takeuchi and Sano (2010), [LIT-2982](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2982.md), read in full in [NOTE-2284](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2284.md). The exponents (α = 0.50(5), β = 0.336(11)) and the GUE Tracy-Widom skewness and kurtosis are measurements over 563 runs; the three factors that make this system show KPZ when most experiments do not are argued, not tested. Grounds [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s KPZ row with Kardar, Parisi and Zhang ([THEORY-2202](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2202.md)), and qualifies its "generically" for experiment ([ARG-195](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-195.md)). Proposed until confirmed independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2202](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2202.md) | Kardar, Parisi and Zhang propose ∂h/∂t = ν∇²h + (λ/2)(∇h)² + η, invariant under a shift of h and a small tilt, as the simplest local equation for a growing interface, and by a one-loop dynamic renormalization group find that any nonzero λ is relevant in one dimension and gives a class with χ = ½ and z = 3/2, exact by a fluctuation-dissipation theorem, that λ is marginally relevant in two dimensions, and that above two dimensions a small λ is irrelevant and the surface asymptotically smooth with z = 2 | Kardar, Parisi and Zhang (1986), [LIT-2978](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2978.md), read in full in [NOTE-2287](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2287.md). The equation is argued from locality and symmetry; the one-dimensional exponents are exact by a fluctuation-dissipation theorem the letter cites rather than shows; the two-dimensional conjecture of superuniversality later failed (Le Doussal, [THEORY-2198](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2198.md)). Grounds [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s KPZ row for d ≤ 2 ([ARG-195](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-195.md)) and is one of the three cases of [CLAIM-862](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-862.md). Proposed until confirmed by an independent derivation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2203](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2203.md) | Halperin holds that the Hohenberg–Mermin–Wagner theorem excludes, at T > 0 in one and two dimensions and in equilibrium, true long-range order breaking a continuous symmetry whose generator is a sum of local operators, for interactions with finite second moments, and that it says nothing about quasi-long-range order or T = 0 and does not exclude orientational order in a two-dimensional crystal | Halperin (2018), [LIT-3054](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3054.md), read in full in [NOTE-2296](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2296.md) as a stand-in for Mermin and Wagner (1966), [LIT-2985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2985.md). The theorem's scope and its exceptions, as an author close to it states them. Marks the limits of [CLAIM-842](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-842.md)'s criterion ([ARG-200](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-200.md)), and why [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s XY row does not rest on Mermin–Wagner. Proposed until a second source confirms the scope. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2204](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2204.md) | Natschläger, Bertschinger and Legenstein show, by an annealed mean-field theory and simulation, that random networks of binary threshold gates driven by a random binary input have an order-to-chaos line where a single flipped input bit flips on average one node (K·P_bf = 1), that a separation measure corrected for initial-condition and input-drive separation peaks near that line, that a trained linear readout performs best near it on delayed parity and random Boolean functions of recent inputs, averaged over many tasks, and that a local synaptic-scaling rule drives networks to the line | The NIPS 2004 companion ([LIT-3058](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3058.md)) of Bertschinger and Natschläger's Neural Computation paper ([LIT-2991](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2991.md), unreachable), read in its place in [NOTE-2288](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2288.md). The edge of chaos here is a damage-spreading line, K·P_bf = 1, crossing a wide range of mean activity; order is fading memory, and chaos fails because the state carries "spurious" information about initial conditions. The optimum is averaged over many tasks by design, with no per-task optima, so it qualifies rather than defeats [CLAIM-809](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-809.md) ([ARG-196](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-196.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2205](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2205.md) | Shalizi and Moore propose that, for a chosen set of observables of a system with Markov microdynamics, the macrostates are the causal states of the observed process, the coarsest partition of observation histories that predicts the observables as well as the whole history does and whose own dynamics is therefore Markov, so that which observables to start from is the observer's choice and the partition reached from them is fixed by the dynamics; and they call one causal description emergent from another when it is a coarse-graining of it and is predicted with higher efficiency E/Cµ, arguing both from examples rather than new theorems | Shalizi and Moore (2003), [LIT-2996](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2996.md), read in [NOTE-2294](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2294.md). Their answer to whether macrostates are objective or subjective is "both": the observables are the observer's, the causal states reached from them are fixed by the dynamics. "A different set of initial variables will, generally, lead to a different set of causal states"; "Nature has no preferred questions." Their emergence is a coarse-graining predicted more efficiently (argon: 0.87 against 0.5), held in [TERM-146](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-146.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2206](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2206.md) | Kosterlitz's Nobel lecture holds that the two-dimensional planar rotor and superfluid film have a finite-temperature topologically ordered phase without long-range order, in which winding-number sectors are separated by barriers growing as ln L, while the 2D Heisenberg model's invariant has a barrier of order unity and no ordered state; the phase ends when vortex pairs unbind at πK = 2, and a finite penetration depth, which cuts off the logarithmic interaction, frees vortices at any T > 0 | Kosterlitz (2016), [LIT-3053](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3053.md), read in full in [NOTE-2283](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2283.md) as a stand-in for Kosterlitz and Thouless (1973), [LIT-2969](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2969.md). The first author's restatement, with the 1973 paper's errors named. It grounds [CLAIM-841](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md)'s XY row with Drouin-Touchette ([THEORY-2197](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2197.md)) ([ARG-198](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-198.md)); it gives [CLAIM-694](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-694.md) the barrier condition; and it is one case of [CLAIM-862](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-862.md). Proposed until the primary papers are read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2207](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2207.md) | Rheinberg, Manig, Kliegl, Engeser and Vollmeyer find by experience sampling of 101 employees, with flow measured by all its components, that flow is higher at work and happiness/satisfaction higher in leisure, that across single reports the two correlate weakly positively, and that goal-directedness of the current activity raises flow in both contexts while leaving happiness unchanged at work and lowering it in leisure; they read the paradox of work as partly an effect of how often work is goal-directed | Rheinberg et al. (2007), [LIT-3071](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3071.md), read in [NOTE-2297](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2297.md). One of the record's two read in-episode studies of flow and affect, both found by [LEAD-054](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-054.md). Flow and happiness/satisfaction rated at each signal correlate r = .36 raw, .30 within-person, so some of flow's positivity is reported during the episode; it corroborates [CLAIM-441](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-441.md)'s premise that flow is reported as positive, against its third exit, weakly, since the correlation is pooled and flow is a continuous score. The sharp edge is the dissociation: goal-directedness lifts flow and not happiness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2208](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2208.md) | Engeser and Baumann find by experience sampling of 100 employees that flow goes with positive activation and, moderately, with valence at the same signal, that flow at one signal does not predict valence at the next once concurrent flow and prior valence are controlled, that leisure has better valence and less negative activation than work though flow is highest at work, and that perceived outcome importance raises flow and lowers valence | Engeser and Baumann (2014), [LIT-3070](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3070.md), read in [NOTE-2298](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2298.md). The more direct of the record's two read in-episode studies of flow and affect, both found by [LEAD-054](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-054.md). Within persons flow correlates .31 with valence and .59 with positive activation at the same signal, and does not raise valence at the next. It corroborates [CLAIM-441](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-441.md)'s premise that flow is positive during the episode, against the third exit that the positivity comes after it. The sharp edges: a continuous flow score with no enjoyment item, a two-hour lag, and a sample it appears to share with Rheinberg et al. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2209.md) | Vestring and colleagues report that in healthy adults ketamine, given 90 to 150 minutes before an approach-avoidance conflict task with experimenter-set threat probability and loss, raised approach, flattened its decline with threat probability and steepened its decline with loss, while lorazepam raised approach and flattened both | Vestring et al. (2026), [LIT-3079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3079.md), read in [NOTE-2300](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2300.md). The nearest design of a second kind that [LEAD-047](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-047.md)'s search found: a drug intervention on the arbitration of approach and avoidance with the objective threat fixed. The represented threat is not measured. Proposed until replicated with the session order counterbalanced. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2210](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2210.md) | Sridhar, Biagi and Wake report that a brief instruction to withhold avoidance in order to test one's threat expectancy left US expectancy and skin conductance unchanged, and propose that it reduced avoidance in more socially anxious people, a reduction their own tests give only as a non-significant exploratory trend | Sridhar, Biagi & Wake (2026), [LIT-3076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3076.md), read in [NOTE-2299](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2299.md). The nearest design [LEAD-047](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-047.md)'s search found to an intervention on what governs action with threat belief measured. Its expectancy null is clean; its avoidance effect is not. Proposed until the avoidance effect is shown confirmatorily. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2211.md) | Tatel finds that, with infrequent use, accuracy on laboratory motor tasks declines about three times faster than on real-world tasks, and little evidence that the real-world domains differ, though in the posted data only medical and dental tasks decline measurably | Tatel (2023), [LIT-2079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2079.md), and the coded data posted for Tatel & Ackerman (2025), [LIT-3080](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3080.md). For accuracy the decline is 0.16 SD a month on laboratory tasks and about 0.05 on real-world tasks; the dissertation finds "less evidence" that real-world domains differ from one another, and in the posted data medical and dental tasks decline by 0.04 a month while sports and military or transport tasks show no measurable decline over intervals of a year at most. Speed shows the same trend, not significant. Task type is confounded with complexity and with the range of intervals studied. Proposed: one synthesis, by the same author, and the article unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2212](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2212.md) | Simić, Sacchi and Perugini report that expecting one's national group to stay the same in the future lowers fear for its future and, through that, prejudice and anxiety toward immigrants, among those strongly attached to the group and not among the weakly attached | Simić, Sacchi and Perugini (2025), three Italian studies, the third a preregistered experiment (N = 252), read in full ([NOTE-2302](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2302.md)). The continuity is the group's with its own future, measured with future-self-continuity items; it correlated .14 with national attachment. The effects on prejudice and collective action needed a covariate outside the preregistration, and the moderation by attachment came from an analysis that left it. Nothing here concerns future people or legacy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2213](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2213.md) | Martela and Ryan (2021) find in three preregistered experiments that a small, instructed negative impact on a charity raises felt beneficence frustration but not self-reported ill-being, while an equal positive impact raises well-being, an asymmetry consistent with beneficence enhancing wellness without its frustration harming it | Martela and Ryan, read in [NOTE-2303](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2303.md) (Read). Three preregistered MTurk experiments randomise a small gain or loss to the Red Cross within a key-pressing task. The loss is noticed, raising beneficence frustration (meta-analytic d = 0.84), but negative affect, anxiety and depression do not rise; the gain raises well-being. Registered as a stand-in, in part, for [LIT-1980](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1980.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2214](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2214.md) | Martela and Ryan (2019) find that frustration of beneficence, measured as feeling one has harmed others, correlates with ill-being but adds no variance to it once autonomy, competence and relatedness frustration are controlled, and on that ground tentatively propose that beneficence is a basic wellness enhancer, whose satisfaction raises well-being but whose frustration has no unique cost, rather than a basic psychological need | Martela and Ryan, read in [NOTE-2304](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2304.md) (Read). Across three MTurk studies a new four-item beneficence-frustration scale correlates with every ill-being indicator but, entered after the three established frustration scales, adds no unique variance, and the three needs fully mediate it. The authors tentatively propose the category of basic wellness enhancer and call any conclusion about beneficence premature. | Proposed |
