| [THEORY-2215](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2215.md) | Čater, Čater and Ivašković (2026) find, in two surveys of European football fans asked how a hypothetical Super League entry would change their commitment and loyalty, that cognitive, affective and evaluative identification each predict a smaller imagined decline in commitment, cognitive most, and that imagined commitment change carries most of the imagined change in word-of-mouth and loyalty; they report that opposition to the decision moderates every identity–commitment link | Čater, Čater and Ivašković, read in [NOTE-2305](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2305.md) (Read). Two cross-sectional surveys (N = 172, 184) of fans recruited through fan clubs rate their commitment and loyalty now and, at once, if their club joined a Super League. All three identity dimensions predict a smaller imagined decline, cognitive most; commitment change carries loyalty change. The moderation by opposition is reported, but the simple slopes' signs do not plainly carry the authors' reading of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2216](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2216.md) | Mulgan (2018) argues that the only account of corporate agency that is temporally robust, giving people in credible broken and digital futures the concepts to resist domination by corporate groups, is moralised extreme collectivism: moral agency only for corporate groups reliably disposed to respond appropriately to moral reasons, full moral personhood open in principle to the sophisticated among them, and a group with no mechanism for moral reasons irredeemably psychopathic and without moral standing | Mulgan, read in [NOTE-2306](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2306.md) (Read). He sorts accounts of corporate agency into individualism and minimal, moderate and extreme collectivism, adds a "moralised" reliability condition, and argues from two imagined futures, broken and digital, that only moralised extreme collectivism is temporally robust. It reports Velasquez's individualism second-hand, enough to name its premises, not to assess them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2217](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2217.md) | Dorsch, Coeckelbergh and Vierkant (2026) argue, as an untested mechanism, that engagement-optimizing recommender systems threaten deliberative democracy not by isolating users from opposing views but by optimizing processing fluency, which inflates second-order confidence in one's own epistemic stance and makes rejecting opponents' views feel warranted, so that beliefs formed there carry reflective epistemic luck the user cannot detect from within | Dorsch, Coeckelbergh and Vierkant, read in [NOTE-2307](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2307.md) (Read). A theoretical paper, avowedly untested: since users of social media meet cross-cutting views, the harm of engagement optimization is not isolation but a recalibration of the metacognitive cues by which users judge their own beliefs, so that rejecting opponents feels warranted. The wording of the mechanism is the authors'; its central link, engagement as fluency, is assumed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2218](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2218.md) | Caliari (2026) shows that a welfare method satisfying Informational Responsiveness (one more choice of x over an indifferent y tips the ranking to x), with neutrality, choice non-negativeness and independence from menus lacking x and y, is exactly a weighted choice-count refinement of Bernheim and Rangel's Pareto relation and recovers the true preference for all preference-monotonic choice models; in a 145-subject experiment such methods cut expected false positives against subjects' reported rankings relative to the Pareto relation, while attention-type models, under which choice frequency and preference come apart, lie outside the guarantee | Caliari, read in [NOTE-2308](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2308.md) (Read). An axiom on welfare methods, Informational Responsiveness, with neutrality, choice non-negativeness and Connection, characterizes weighted count refinements of the Bernheim–Rangel Pareto relation, correct for preference-monotonic choice models. In an experiment with 145 St Andrews students most violate WARP, and such methods cut expected false positives against stated rankings. Every welfare method is "implicitly model-based". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2219](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2219.md) | Ivern and Carbonell (2026), scoping 72 empirical studies of 2017–2026, catalogue 136 loot-box design features that the literature treats as problematic, in six categories (obfuscation, psychological manipulation, social influence and promotion, value, data or engagement manipulation, self-regulation obstacles, gambling resemblance), and find that the separate and joint effects of these features on players are largely unstudied | Ivern and Carbonell, read in [NOTE-2309](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2309.md) (Read). A PRISMA-ScR scoping review: 72 studies, 136 features in 22 subcategories and 6 categories, grouped by the problem they cause players and ranked by how often the literature names them. The authors find the impact and interaction of the features largely unstudied, and place the risk in interacting features within monetization systems rather than in any single one. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2220](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2220.md) | Mossio and Moreno (2010) hold that a flame maintains itself through a single constraint acting on its own boundary conditions, while an organism maintains itself through organisational closure, the direct mutual dependence of several constraints; closure is necessary for an organism but not sufficient, which also needs templates and control between parts working at different time scales | Mossio and Moreno, read in [NOTE-2311](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2311.md) (Read). A flame is far-from-equilibrium self-maintenance through one constraint; an organism has organisational closure, a set of constraints each maintaining another that maintains it. Closure is partial, holds among constraints not processes, and is direct. It is necessary for an organism, not sufficient. A stand-in, in part, for [LIT-536](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-536.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2221](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2221.md) | Bich, Mossio, Ruiz-Mirazo and Moreno (2016) define biological regulation as second-order control by a subsystem the organism produces but which runs at its own rate and stoichiometry, is triggered by perturbations and switches the constitutive regime between viable states; feedback, network robustness and homeostasis belong instead to the constitutive regime | Bich, Mossio, Ruiz-Mirazo and Moreno, read in [NOTE-2310](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2310.md) (Read). Regulation is control exerted over the constitutive regime by a subsystem produced by it but dynamically decoupled from it, triggered by perturbations, that shifts the regime between viable states. Feedback depends on one constraint; closure is the mutual dependence of several. A stand-in, in part, for [LIT-536](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-536.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2222](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2222.md) | Metzinger (2021) argues that, since there is no theory of consciousness or of suffering, the risk of creating artificial suffering is incalculable and research that knowingly risks synthetic phenomenology should be banned until 2050; he holds that suffering requires four jointly necessary conditions, consciousness, a phenomenal self-model, negatively valenced states integrated into it and phenomenal transparency, so that a conscious system lacking a self-model, or identifying only with minimal phenomenal experience, could not suffer, which he offers as a route to ethics by design | Metzinger, read in [NOTE-2312](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2312.md) (Read). A moratorium until 2050 on research that aims at or knowingly risks synthetic phenomenology, on pathocentric and suffering-focused grounds; four necessary conditions of suffering (consciousness, self-model, integrated negative valence, transparency); and two designs that block suffering by blocking a condition. The conditions are stipulated from the author's self-model theory, not shown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2223](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2223.md) | Howard, Gagné and Bureau's (2017) meta-analysis of 486 samples finds that self-determination theory's motivation regulations follow a continuum-like (simplex) ordering that one dimension of self-determination accounts for almost entirely, but that integrated regulation is empirically indistinguishable from identified regulation (pooled r = .91), as are the three subtypes of intrinsic motivation from each other, so that no validated scale measures the most integrated rung of the continuum separately | Howard, Gagné and Bureau, read in [NOTE-2313](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2313.md) (Read). Pooled correlations among the motivation types from 486 samples and 13 scales form a simplex that one dimension explains (99.75%), with unexplained heterogeneity near 99%. Integrated regulation correlates .913 with identified regulation, with overlapping intervals; the authors call it "practically indistinguishable" and ask for the theory or the measures to change. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2224](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2224.md) | Burning Man's 10 Principles, written by Larry Harvey in 2004 and offered as an ethos rather than rules, state gifting as unconditional, ground decommodification in preserving the spirit of gifting, and state radical self-reliance only as reliance on one's inner resources, so that the ethos draws no line between what is self-provided and what is given | The 10 Principles, read in [NOTE-2314](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2314.md) (Read), from the organization's current page. Gifting "does not contemplate a return or an exchange for something of equal value"; decommodification is "In order to preserve the spirit of gifting"; Radical Self-reliance is only "discover, exercise and rely on their inner resources". The page has no revision date. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2225](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2225.md) | Across ten US studies, Syropoulos, Law, Coleman and Young find that continuity with one's own future self and consideration of one's own future consequences correlate with felt responsibility for future generations (meta-analytic r = .21 and .54), partly through identification with and efficacy toward future generations, but that writing tasks raising future-self continuity raised responsibility in one pre-registered experiment and not in its replication, and never raised identification, so the route from self to future others is shown as association, not cause | Syropoulos, Law, Coleman and Young, read in [NOTE-2315](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2315.md) (Read), from the 2024-05-21 manuscript. Self-oriented prospection correlates with responsibility for future generations across studies; mediation through identification is cross-sectional; and the two pre-registered experiments give a small effect on responsibility and then a null, with no effect on identification. The identification measure includes empathy and perspective-taking. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2226](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2226.md) | Two Winograd schemas joined in one story make a Bell-CHSH scenario over pronoun-and-word observables, and the one instance judged by crowd workers violates the inequality by about one standard deviation, with no-signalling imposed by an A/B-symmetric story and a response format that never elicits the pronouns' marginals | Lo, Sadrzadeh and Mansfield (2023), [LIT-3098](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3098.md), read in [NOTE-2316](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2316.md). The construction is theirs; that the response format leaves the marginals unobserved, so the test cannot see direct influences, is the reading's. The violation and its spread were recomputed from the paper's Table 1. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2227](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2227.md) | When binocular rivalry switches are made so inconspicuous that observers rarely detect them, fronto-parietal BOLD responses to the switches shrink in proportion to their reportability, so those responses reflect noticing a switch rather than causing it | Brascamp, Blake and Knapen (2015), [LIT-3089](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3089.md), read in [NOTE-2317](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2317.md). Rivalry between two dot fields identical except for the eye they reach: switches occur, by matched alternation statistics, but are detected at chance; the fronto-parietal switch response then matches an eighth of the conspicuous response, with no causal remainder. It is the inconspicuous contrast [THEORY-094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-094.md) names and supports that account's diagnosis for switch transients. Limit: BOLD and a switch transient, not percept-specific content, and six observers; it separates a perceptual change from awareness of the change, not experience from access. Proposed until confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2228](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2228.md) | In macaques viewing binocular rivalry without any trained report, ventrolateral prefrontal populations carry the perceived direction of motion, decodable on single trials and generalising from physical to rivalrous alternation, with the suppressed direction minimally represented | Kapoor, Dwarakanath, Safavi, Werner, Besserve, Panagiotaropoulos and Logothetis (2022), [LIT-3094](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3094.md), read in [NOTE-2318](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2318.md). 987 prefrontal units in two macaques, percept inferred from the optokinetic nystagmus, decoding up to 95%. It is report-free intracranial evidence that the content reaches prefrontal cortex. Limit: the switches were noticed ("unreported but clearly occurring"), so it does not remove post-perceptual cognition, and it neither promotes nor refutes [THEORY-094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-094.md). Proposed until confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2229](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2229.md) | After callosotomy, perception and attention are largely split between the hemispheres while detection, localisation and response selection stay largely unified, so access to a content can depend on the operation that uses it; whether the subject is split remains undecided on the evidence | de Haan et al. (2020), [LIT-3102](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3102.md), read in [NOTE-2319](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2319.md) as a stand-in for Pinto et al. 2017 ([LIT-3091](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3091.md)). "Perception appears to be more split, while responding remains largely unified"; "the body of evidence is insufficient" on the subject. It is independent evidence for the access half of [CLAIM-003](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-003.md) in a disconnected brain, argued in [ARG-202](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-202.md). Limit: a review, behavioural evidence, a lesioned brain, and no removal of post-perceptual cognition. Proposed until confirmed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2230](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2230.md) | Karnkowska and colleagues report that the genome of the oxymonad Monocercomonoides sp. PA203 encodes no hallmark mitochondrial protein, that its iron–sulfur clusters are made in the cytosol by a SUF system an ancestor shared with Paratrimastix took from bacteria by lateral transfer, and that the loss of the organelle is secondary, making it the first eukaryote known to lack any form of mitochondrion | Karnkowska, Vacek, Zubáčová and colleagues (2016), [LIT-1567](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1567.md), read in [NOTE-2320](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2320.md). Shown: none of 41 hallmark mitochondrial proteins and no credible candidate from broad searches, with Golgi proteins found as a control; SUF genes in the nucleus, with bacterial phylogeny shared with Paratrimastix. Not shown: that no organelle of wholly altered composition exists, which the authors say they cannot exclude. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2231](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2231.md) | Łukasik and colleagues report that in the cicada genus Tettigades a single ancestral Hodgkinia lineage has split at least six independent times in about 4 million years into complexes of two to six interdependent lineages per host, in distinct cells, which differ widely in abundance and gene content and together encode nearly the ancestral gene set | Łukasik, Nazario, Van Leuven, Campbell, Meyer, Michalik, Pessacq, Simon, Veloso & McCutcheon (2017/2018), [LIT-1586](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1586.md), read in [NOTE-2321](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2321.md). The authors also speculate, without testing, that splitting is nonadaptive for the host, begets more splitting, and makes the symbiont population harder to control; that reading is theirs and is not what this entry asserts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2232](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2232.md) | Campbell and colleagues report that in every periodical cicada species Hodgkinia exists as a complex of at least twenty circular molecules, with an order of magnitude more DNA than the ancestral genome and most of its genes, little synteny between species and gene dosages that differ between species groups, so that the splitting took a different course in each | Campbell, Łukasik, Simon & McCutcheon (2017), [LIT-1602](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1602.md), read in [NOTE-2322](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2322.md). The authors read the lack of convergence as evidence that the host does not dictate the splitting and that it is nonadaptive for the host; that reading is theirs. Not shown: whether the circles are separate cells. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2233](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2233.md) | Strand, Coffman and Burke review how parasitoid wasps transmit large DNA viruses to their hosts, from mechanical carriage to domesticated endogenized viruses integrated in the wasp germline; bracoviruses, which arose from a nudivirus about 100 million years ago, cannot replicate alone and produce particles that deliver virulence genes, some of wasp origin, which suppress the host's immunity and alter its development | Strand, Coffman & Burke (2026), [LIT-2395](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2395.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2323](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2323.md). The domestication history is the review's report of others' work. It does not say that the wasp's control of the virus is complete: a wasp polymerase and wasp-derived virulence genes are part of the system. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2234](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2234.md) | On Millikan's biosemantics, a sign has content because a producer and a consumer were shaped by selection or learning to cooperate through it: its content is the affair it must map onto, by a rule, for the consumer to perform its functions in the way that explains that shaping, and it can be true or false only by reference to that history, which natural signs lack | Millikan (2009), "Biosemantics", [LIT-3103](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3103.md), read in [NOTE-2324](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2324.md) from her pre-print. Her own short statement of the selection-based teleosemantics the record said it owed ([LEAD-018](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-018.md)). Teleology explains how a representation can be false; a mapping theory with producer and consumer explains what it represents. Corroborates [CLAIM-650](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-650.md) on its question (a), with a qualification argued in [ARG-204](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-204.md); grounds the objection [CLAIM-920](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-920.md) to [CLAIM-648](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-648.md). Proposed: one reading, of a compressed statement whose account of function is cited, not given. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2235](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2235.md) | Teleosemantic theories derive the norms by which a representation is correct or in error from functional norms, which they take to be descriptive and, in most versions, etiological: what an item or its type was selected for, by natural selection, learning or another selection process; they divide on whether the consumer's or the producer's function fixes content, and face objections from indeterminacy, from a replica with no history, from attributing representations to all living things, and from sophisticated concepts | Neander and Schulte (2004; rev. 2022), SEP, "Teleological Theories of Mental Content", [LIT-3104](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3104.md), read in [NOTE-2325](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2325.md). A survey by two proponents, one of whom is surveyed. It reports the field's shape and its objections and settles little; the title asserts only what the survey reports. Read for [LEAD-018](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-018.md) beside Millikan's own statement ([THEORY-2234](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2234.md)). Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2236](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2236.md) | Khan and Dhar find that knowing the same choice will recur lowers self-control in the present choice, which they explain by optimism about the next choice lowering the anticipated guilt of the present one, and that telling choosers the present choice is the best indicator of the next takes most of the effect away | Khan and Dhar (2007), [LIT-3113](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3113.md), read in [NOTE-2326](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2326.md) for [LEAD-078](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-078.md). A recurring choice is a licence unless it is seen as a precedent: the vice share rises from 46.6-57.5% in isolation to 70-90% when the same choice is announced for next week, and falls to 53% when the chooser is told this choice is the best indicator of the next. It bears on [THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md)'s first promotion condition, in part, and on [QUESTION-034](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-034.md)'s bargaining route. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2237](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2237.md) | Schuhr finds in a laboratory experiment with real money that intertemporal choices presented as a free series of two or three paired decisions, chosen at once, are more patient in their first choices than the same choices presented singly, and that forcing the paired decisions to match lowers patient choice, which he reads as reward bundling done by the chooser rather than imposed | Schuhr (2015), [LIT-3114](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3114.md), read in part in [NOTE-2327](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2327.md) for [LEAD-078](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-078.md). In eight one-session treatments of about thirty students each, a free series of decisions raised the mixture probability of exponential discounting by 0.307 (p = 0.019), forcing the decisions together lowered it by 0.330, and stake size did not explain it. Evidence for bundling in humans without an imposed bundle; not for bundling by self-prediction, since every decision in the series is made at once. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2238](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2238.md) | In Zaslavsky, Garvin, Kemp, Tishby and Regier's resurvey, Nafaanra colour naming in one village went from three terms in 1978 to seven in 2017, the three older terms now naming smaller categories, and both systems lie near the information-bottleneck efficiency bound | Zaslavsky, Garvin, Kemp, Tishby and Regier (2019), [LIT-3107](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3107.md), a CogSci abstract read in full in [NOTE-2329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2329.md), standing in for the unread journal paper [LIT-3106](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3106.md). 1978 World Color Survey: light, dark and red. 2017 resurvey in Banda Ahenkro: those three "now name smaller categories", with new terms for roughly yellow, green, blue and purple. Both near the efficiency bound of [THEORY-163](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-163.md). Stated without figures; later sources give 2018 and nine terms. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2239](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2239.md) | Adult Tsimane'-Spanish bilinguals use Tsimane' colour terms in narrower, less overlapping extensions than Tsimane' monolinguals, and split the shared green-blue term pair into green and blue, without borrowing Spanish terms | Malik-Moraleda, Mahowald, Conway and Gibson (2023), [LIT-3108](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3108.md), read in [NOTE-2330](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2330.md) (supplement unread). Against 71 monolinguals, 30 bilinguals' Tsimane' colour terms have lower average surprisal (4.42 against 5.16), cover fewer chips, and overlap less with their neighbours; shandyes and yụshñus, one green-blue category for monolinguals (KL 0.10), separate (1.18). No Spanish term is borrowed. Between-group and colour only; the bilinguals also live in a more industrialised town. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2240](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2240.md) | In five diachronic corpora, a sharply rising word's frequency gain is offset by losses among its nearest distributional neighbours more often when the frequency of its topic is stable than when it is rising, a significant association in each corpus explaining up to 11% of the variance beyond lexical controls | Karjus, Blythe, Kirby and Smith (2020), [LIT-3105](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3105.md), read in full in [NOTE-2328](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2328.md). The equalization range (how far out in LSA space the neighbours' frequency losses sum to a rising word's gain) correlates with topical advection (the mean log frequency change of the word's top context words) in COHA, DTA, Estonian, Czech and Scottish Twitter corpora, p < 0.05 in each. airplane took its rise from aeroplane while aviation's topic was stable; famed and famous rose together with interwar celebrity. The measure is frequency, not range of use. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2241](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2241.md) | Ge, Xie, Sun, Fan, Zhang and Liu find in a randomized trial that a week of brief smartphone mindfulness training combining monitoring and acceptance shortens Stroop and Go/No-go reaction times, without changing accuracy or delay discounting, and that no effect lasts two weeks; they attribute the effect to acceptance joined with monitoring | Ge et al. (2024), [LIT-916](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-916.md), read in [NOTE-2331](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2331.md) for [LEAD-078](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-078.md). In 70 students low in trait mindfulness, monitor-and-acceptance training sped conflict and inhibition responses at post-test, left accuracy and delay discounting unchanged, and had no effect at follow-up. A dissociation of speed from discounting, not a test of whether discounting mediates a change in self-control: [ARG-206](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-206.md) holds that it does not show [CLAIM-156](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-156.md)'s route. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2242](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2242.md) | Meckes, Cole, Gee and Lancaster report that, in one session of exposure for spider fear, an experimenter-supplied safety behaviour faded, kept or never offered made no detectable difference to outcome at post-treatment or one month, while it raised approach during exposure and acceptability after it | Meckes et al. (2025), [LIT-3123](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3123.md), read in [NOTE-2332](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2332.md). A randomized test of exposure held fixed with a safety behaviour cut or kept, the design [QUESTION-045](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-045.md) names, with a null on outcome at one month. Proposed until replicated beyond one session and one small sample; it says nothing about cutting a person's own maintaining safety behaviour. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2243.md) | de Jong, Ryan, van der Maas and Hamaker propose the hysteretic threshold autoregressive model to detect hysteresis in one person's time series, as two switching thresholds of a measured control variable against one, show by simulation that it recovers hysteresis from a depression symptom network, and report that no empirical psychological series had yet been analysed with it | de Jong et al. (2023), [LIT-3124](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3124.md), read in [NOTE-2333](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2333.md). The test [QUESTION-045](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-045.md)'s "individual data showing hysteresis" would need, with its conditions: a measured driver crossing an upper and then a lower threshold. Its depression case is simulated, and it reports no empirical psychopathology series. Proposed until its simulation results are reproduced or the paper is published as it stands. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2244](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2244.md) | Smit, Helmich, Bringmann, Oldehinkel, Wichers and Snippe report that in 37 formerly depressed people tapering antidepressants, rising autocorrelation and variance in momentary affect preceded recurrence in about a third of those who relapsed and appeared in about a sixth of those who did not, so that critical slowing down is detectable within persons before some transitions into depression, with low sensitivity | Smit et al. (2025), [LIT-3125](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3125.md), read from its preprint in [NOTE-2334](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2334.md). Within-person evidence, across 37 people, of the destabilization a tipping point predicts before entry into depression, in a minority of those who relapsed. Proposed until replicated in another sample; it is not evidence of hysteresis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2245](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2245.md) | Ko shows that two groups of phase oscillators with no coupling between them, each driven by a common noise plus independent local noise, synchronize their collective order parameters when the common noise is the same for both, from any initial state and down to a within-group noise correlation near 0.1, proved for uncoupled groups at large N and seen numerically with coupling inside the groups, which can weaken it | From the reading of [LIT-2245](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2245.md) in [NOTE-2335](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2335.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). A model in which synchrony between the collective variables of two groups is wholly exogenous. It does not say how to tell such synchrony from coupling in data. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2246](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2246.md) | Ocampo-Espindola and colleagues show, in a kinetic model and in nickel electrodissolution experiments, that one common open-loop periodic input designed from each unit's natural frequency and phase response curve entrains uncoupled oscillators with different responses into a prescribed phase pattern, including one-, two- and three-cluster states of four units, where a design from the mean response curve can lock them into the wrong pattern | From the reading of [LIT-2230](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2230.md) in [NOTE-2336](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2336.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). A demonstration that a pattern of synchrony, clusters included, can be imposed by a one-way common drive on units that are not coupled to one another. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2247](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2247.md) | Bačić and colleagues show that the phase-locked states of the topological Kuramoto model on a cell complex are the solutions of linear balance conditions that also meet nonlinear cycle conditions, sums of inverse sines around each independent cycle equal to 2π times a winding number, and that because a stable phase difference is below π/2 in size, coexisting stable states with nonzero winding need a boundary of at least five cells | From the reading of [LIT-2253](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2253.md) in [NOTE-2338](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2338.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). The unfrustrated, higher-order counterpart of the record's cycle-consistency results. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2248](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2248.md) | Manik, Timme and Witthaut show that the phase-locked states of Kuramoto and power-grid oscillator networks are the conserved edge flows that also meet the cycle condition, phase differences around every cycle summing to 2π times an integer, so locked states differing by cycle flows coexist, a ring of four or fewer nodes has only one stable such state, and raising one edge's capacity can destroy phase locking | From the reading of [LIT-2267](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2267.md) in [NOTE-2339](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2339.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). The graph case of Bačić and colleagues' cell-complex result ([THEORY-2247](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2247.md)), by an overlapping group. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2249](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2249.md) | Widder and Schilling show that the Dyson–Duhamel identity behind the generalized Langevin equation is proved only when PL is bounded, as for Mori's projection, and is an unsolved equation for Zwanzig's; that Mori's equation follows from Volterra equations alone and predicts nothing beyond the autocorrelation fitted to it; and that its memory term is a coupling between the kept and omitted subspaces, which vanishes when the omitted subspace is invariant | From the reading of [LIT-2250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2250.md) in [NOTE-2340](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2340.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). A's citation at A18, that memory terms depend on the projection and are not one physical timescale, is borne out and sharpened: memory is coupling. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2250](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2250.md) | Wang and Tang show that cells coupled through a shared dissipative signal begin a collective oscillation when loop gain and phase match, Nα₁R̃ₐ(ω)R̃ₛ(ω) = 1, and that because the medium lags the cells must lead in phase, which cells that adapt to a constant stimulus do in an active frequency window where energy flows from cell to signal, so quiescent adaptive cells oscillate together past a density where none oscillates alone | From the reading of [LIT-2256](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2256.md) in [NOTE-2341](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2341.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). A dynamical case of a capacity the composition has and no part has. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2251](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2251.md) | Stewart shows that on any coupled cell network of finite type the balanced equivalence relations, the patterns of synchrony invariant under every dynamics the architecture admits, form a complete lattice under refinement whose join is that of equivalence relations but whose meet is not intersection, with a unique coarsest element computable from input trees | From the reading of [LIT-2249](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2249.md) in [NOTE-2342](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2342.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). Structure on the candidates for robust synchrony; nothing on which of them attract. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2252](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2252.md) | Dörfler and Bullo survey synchronization of Kuramoto-type phase oscillators on networks: for identical oscillators on S¹-synchronizing graphs, complete and acyclic ones among them, the synchronized state is the only stable equilibrium; fixed points of heterogeneous networks are written through auxiliary edge variables whose homogeneous part lies in the cycle space; and the main analysis methods fail or become conservative for phase-shifted, directed or clustered cases | From the skimmed reading of [LIT-2232](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2232.md) in [NOTE-2343](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2343.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). The survey's landscape and cycle-space results, and its own list of what its methods do not cover. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2253](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2253.md) | Schultz, Spivak and Vasilakopoulou model open dynamical systems as spans of sheaves on time intervals, so that any wiring of such machines, feedback included, is again one, with totality, determinism and inertia each preserved by every wiring, while behaviour contracts that depend on history form presheaves that are not sheaves, since two valid behaviours can glue to an invalid one | From the skimmed reading of [LIT-2258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2258.md) in [NOTE-2344](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2344.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). Composition preserves the conditions of realizability the paper defines; history-dependent validity does not glue. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2254](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2254.md) | Bumpus and colleagues define time-varying data as narratives, sheaves or cosheaves on posets of time intervals valued in any suitable category, relate the persistent and cumulative views by an adjunction that can lose information, and show that a sequence of snapshots does not determine a narrative without the relations between successive times | From the skimmed reading of [LIT-2238](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2238.md) in [NOTE-2345](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2345.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). A language for temporal observation with gluing built in; the link to generating dynamics is left open by the authors. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2255](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2255.md) | Bosca and Ghrist show that on discourse sheaves with agents fixed in some opinion directions and some expression maps fixed, opinions settle by a sheaf Poisson equation, adapting maps converge to the Frobenius-nearest consistent sheaf, a conserved quantity excludes agreement by silence or vanishing opinions, and the ratio of expression to opinion rates bounds which of the two changes | From the skimmed reading of [LIT-2259](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2259.md) in [NOTE-2346](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2346.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). Extends Hansen and Ghrist's account ([THEORY-1088](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1088.md)) with selective rigidity and rate bounds. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2256](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2256.md) | Leal and colleagues model a multi-agent system with switching communication topology as a narrative valued in cellular sheaves, which records how agents' communication structure and sensing maps persist and accumulate across topology changes rather than as a sequence of graphs, with dynamics on such temporal sheaves left to work in progress | From the skimmed reading of [LIT-2262](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2262.md) in [NOTE-2347](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2347.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). A way to describe a changing correspondence structure over time; the change is given, not generated. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2257](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2257.md) | Battiston and colleagues report that phase reduction of oscillators with purely pairwise physical coupling yields nonpairwise phase interactions at higher order in the coupling, which capture indirect influence, so that the order of the physical and of the effective interactions can differ | From the skimmed reading of [LIT-2239](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2239.md) in [NOTE-2348](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2348.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). The review's account of where higher-order interactions come from; it reports others' derivations. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2258](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2258.md) | Schultz and Spivak model behavior types as sheaves on a topos of time intervals, which include families whose short-window compliance does not compose and families that are the solution set of no differential equation, and give a constructive temporal logic, sound but undecidable, in which a composed system's strongest contract is its components' contracts conjoined with the latent variables existentially quantified | From the skimmed reading of [LIT-2235](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2235.md) in [NOTE-2349](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2349.md), for [LEAD-023](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-023.md). A coherent behavior type need not be any ODE's solution set; composition of contracts eliminates latent variables. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2259](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2259.md) | Freeman and Pfenning propose refinement types for ML: subtypes of a datatype that the programmer declares as recursive types, closed under intersection and union into a finite lattice, and inferred by abstract interpretation only for programs already well-typed in ML, which keeps inference decidable and leaves the language of programs unchanged; an annotation is accepted only when the inferred refinement lies below it, and evaluation preserves the refinement type | Freeman & Pfenning (1991), [LIT-3127](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3127.md), read in [NOTE-2350](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2350.md) for [LEAD-215](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-215.md). The paper that introduced refinement types. For the record it is the reading on which [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md)'s correspondence of a descriptor with a refinement the entry inhabits can be tested ([ARG-209](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-209.md)), and on which its correspondence of the direction of fit with inferring against checking is found unsupported ([ARG-208](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-208.md), [CLAIM-965](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-965.md)). Proposed until the soundness theorem it states has a proof and the inference it describes an implementation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2260](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2260.md) | Davies and Pfenning: intersection types are unsound with effects unless intersection introduction is restricted to values and distributivity is dropped; inference being impractical, a bidirectional checker takes types from the programmer's ascriptions, checks terms against them and erases them, inserting nothing | Davies & Pfenning (2000), [LIT-3128](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3128.md), read in [NOTE-2351](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2351.md) for [LEAD-215](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-215.md). The paper that introduced bidirectional checking for intersection and refinement types. For the record it is the test, in a system where checking is a mode of its own, of [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md)'s correspondence of the direction of fit with synthesis against checking, which it bears out narrowly ([ARG-211](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-211.md)), and of its clause that the move fitting a term to a type is elaboration or coercion, which it does not ([ARG-212](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-212.md), [CLAIM-974](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-974.md)). Proposed until its theorems are checked independently and its checker implemented as described. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2261](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2261.md) | Optimal control of a system with unknown dynamics must probe it to learn, trading immediate performance for information, by acting on an extended state that adjoins an information state to the physical one; whether exploration must drive the system away from the optimal policy is set by closed-loop identifiability |  | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2262](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2262.md) | Rondon, Kawaguchi and Jhala's liquid types are dependent types {ν : B \| φ} whose predicates, wherever a type must be inferred, are conjunctions of qualifiers from a finite set the programmer supplies; inference refines Hindley-Milner types by weakening an assignment of every qualifier to the strongest conjunction that a conservative check in a decidable logic verifies, which keeps checking and inference decidable; the program is never changed, and one with no such type is reported, not repaired | Rondon, Kawaguchi & Jhala (2008), [LIT-3130](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3130.md), read in [NOTE-2353](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2353.md) for [LEAD-215](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-215.md). The predicate form of refinement types, made inferable by a finite qualifier vocabulary. For the record it is the reading on which [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md)'s descriptor as a refinement {x : A \| φ(x)} the entry inhabits is tested in the form the claim writes ([ARG-214](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-214.md)); on which inference is informative update and checking is not shown to be requirement ([ARG-213](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-213.md)); and which grounds [CLAIM-975](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-975.md), that a failed check does not show that the program fails. Proposed until its theorems' proofs are checked and its inference reproduced. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2263](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2263.md) | The Radner-Stiglitz nonconcavity of the value of information is an artifact of how the amount of information is measured: under a convex-divergence measure, the value of the efficiently acquired amount is concave with strictly positive marginal value at zero, while the value of the worst acquisition of each amount is almost never concave, and a max-min decision-maker's value of information is concave too |  | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md) | Anodal transcranial direct current stimulation over the left frontal lobe raises how much task-unrelated thought people report during a monotonous task, which its authors take as evidence that the frontal lobes, and executive control, play a causal part in mind-wandering | Axelrod, Rees, Lavidor and Bar (2015), [LIT-3135](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3135.md), read in [NOTE-2357](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2357.md). Two small experiments (n = 14 and 31). The causal clause is the authors' inference; the executive-capacity clause rests on a non-significant rise in target detection. The effect was replicated by the first author ([THEORY-2265](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2265.md)) and not in a pre-registered three-lab study ([THEORY-2266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2266.md)), so the two accounts rival. It does not say that the stimulation changed the agent's awareness of its own thought or control, which was not measured, and so it is not a test of Metzinger's H1, which the 2017 chapter ([LIT-1945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1945.md), p. 14) cited it for. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2265](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2265.md) | Frontal anodal transcranial direct current stimulation raises reported mind-wandering without changing rated meta-awareness of where attention is focused, so the stimulation effect on mind-wandering does not pass through a change in that awareness | Axelrod, Zhu and Qiu (2018), [LIT-3134](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3134.md), read in [NOTE-2355](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2355.md): a direct replication of [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md)'s experiment (n = 85) with a meta-awareness probe added. The second clause is the authors' inference, that "at least in some cases mind-wandering might not be regulated by meta-awareness". It rivals the pre-registered null of [THEORY-2266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2266.md). For the record it is the nearest the literature comes to Metzinger's H1, and it is not a test of it: the rated awareness is of attention's location, not of the capacity to end a thought, and it was not manipulated. It bears on [QUESTION-367](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-367.md) only as weak evidence that the rate of mind-wandering can move while the agent's self-rating does not. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2266](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2266.md) | Anodal transcranial direct current stimulation over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, with the montage of the original study, does not raise reported mind-wandering in a sustained-attention task, and the original positive result was most likely a false positive | Boayue and ten colleagues (2019/2020), [LIT-3133](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3133.md), read from the authors' preprint in [NOTE-2358](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2358.md): a pre-registered three-lab replication (n = 192) of [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md)'s experiment, with d = -0.11 (HDI [-0.38, 0.17]), BF 10.65 for the null against a positive effect, and a replication Bayes factor of 0.002. The false-positive clause is the authors' inference. It rivals [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md) and the first author's positive replication, [THEORY-2265](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2265.md), which it predates and does not discuss. Whether it corrects [THEORY-2264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2264.md) is left to the owner. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2267](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2267.md) | Frischmann and Benesch argue that state rules requiring friction with a functional purpose in digital code, architecture and interfaces can be content-neutral time, place and manner restrictions subject to intermediate First Amendment scrutiny; they justify such friction chiefly by the time it gives individuals to deliberate, report the line between friction that only imposes a cost and friction that blocks passage until a condition is shown and so opens a governance seam, and offer a framework and examples but no evidence of their own |  | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2268](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2268.md) | Leffler (2024) argues that of four inescapability proposals only Korsgaard's plight inescapability, reinterpreted as an agent's being continuously positioned to exercise its agency fully absent external limits, captures four necessary features of normative force, and that it then makes force relative to each agent's constitution, so that agents constituted differently, corporate agents included, are bound by different norms | Leffler, read in [NOTE-2360](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2360.md) (Read). Tested against invariance under desire change, ought-implies-can, ought-implies-can-fail and criticizability, only a reconstructed plight inescapability explains the force of norms constitutive of agency, and it makes that force relative to the agent's constitution: categoricity as constitution independence is out of its reach. The author calls the paper exploratory and defends none of the views as true. It is the adversarial test [LEAD-158](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-158.md) asked for; its application to organizations is [ARG-217](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-217.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2269](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2269.md) | Bourrat, Black, Rainey and colleagues hold that the Darwinian properties of a new level of individuality can be imposed first by an environmental scaffold, so that the puzzle of a transition is the origin of the scaffold and its endogenization, which needs a second, collective equilibrium in the unscaffolded environment that the scaffold lets the population reach, and that the line between what is internal and external to the collective shifts during the transition | Bourrat, Takacs, Doulcier, Nitschke, Black, Hammerschmidt and Rainey (2024), read in [NOTE-2362](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2362.md) (Read), a neighbour of [LIT-1940](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1940.md). A perspective piece: the two-peaks condition is borrowed from Doulcier et al. (2024) and the constructive route is proposed for future models. Its operative-cause definition assumes no feedback, which the constructive route is. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2270](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2270.md) | Bourrat proposes that collective properties imposed by an external ecological scaffold are only Darwinian-like, that a transition in individuality is complete only when internal mechanisms come to produce them so that they survive removal of the scaffold, and shows in an agent-based model that a pleiotropy coupling slow growth to staying on the patch keeps scaffolded collectives together after between-patch migration is reopened, for short propagule timescales and small patches | Bourrat (2022), read in [NOTE-2361](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2361.md) (Read). The criterion (§2, Table 1) grades collective properties as pseudo-Darwinian, Darwinian-like and Darwinian by the source of the mechanisms producing them; the model (§5-6) lifts one part of the scaffold, the migration ban, and leaves patches, their capacity and the periodic propagule generations in place. The author calls the result preliminary. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2271](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2271.md) | Shavit and Sharon read the southern Levantine shift to the Neolithic as an evolutionary transition in individuality on Griesemer's three stages, coordination in Epipalaeolithic bands, cooperation in the Natufian and collaboration in the PPNA and PPNB, and hold that farming became irreversible once group traits grew mutually dependent and group fitness decoupled from individual fitness, so that several causes could have produced it | Shavit and Sharon (2023), read in [NOTE-2363](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2363.md) (Read). An opinion paper: the stage assignments are made by fit with a published archaeological synthesis, and the authors say they do not examine how far the case meets ETI criteria. It is the application of [LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md)'s sketch, not a test of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2272](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2272.md) | Monnier, George, Guyard, Tarnec and Kountouris (2026) show that turning intersectional subgroup fairness measurements into one score requires a meta-metric, a choice of comparison, aggregation and weighting, and that different meta-metrics, which agree only when there is no disparity, can reverse the fairness ranking of the same distributions and models, increasingly so as subgroups multiply, so that the choice encodes which pattern of disadvantage counts as worse and needs its own justification | Monnier et al., read in [NOTE-2364](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2364.md) (Read). A taxonomy of meta-metrics, m = f_a ∘ f_w ∘ f_c (comparison, weighting, aggregation), with synthetic and UCI Adult evidence that they reverse fairness rankings, and guidelines that match meta-metrics to the disparity pattern a context most needs to avoid. It takes the subgroups as fixed by prior deliberation, so it bears on how identified demands are weighed, not on who counts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2273](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2273.md) | Wimsatt and Schank define the generative entrenchment of an element as the magnitude of what depends on it downstream in a directed causal graph of the organism and relevant environment, a graph that may contain cycles, and argue from network simulations under truncation selection that more entrenched, more strongly selected elements are preserved while weakly selected ones are lost, so that modular change is possible only rarely | Wimsatt and Schank (2004), read in [NOTE-2365](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2365.md) (Read), a neighbour of [LIT-1926](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1926.md). The definition is the paper's; the simulations mostly assign selection coefficients by class rather than compute entrenchment, so they bear on differential selection in general. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2274](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2274.md) | Massimi (2023, summarizing her 2022 book) holds that scientific knowledge is situated in the practices of historically and culturally placed epistemic communities and is still realist knowledge, because no community can certify its own claims by its own lights and reliability comes from many perspectives intersecting and interlacing over time, the reality so known being modally robust phenomena rather than hidden essences | Massimi's perspectival realism, read in [NOTE-2366](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2366.md) from her primer, a stand-in for the book [LIT-1228](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1228.md). On [QUESTION-129](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-129.md) it offers a procedural constraint on admissible perspectives, no self-certification and comparison across communities, for knowledge claims; whether it carries to normative standards is the question's. The primer states the view and gives none of the book's arguments, so the account is held only as stated. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2275](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2275.md) | Wilkins and Bourrat report Griesemer's reproducer as an entity that develops and overlaps materially with its progeny, reproduction being development plus progeneration, inheritance a system property acquired in development, and replication an evolved terminal form of reproduction, with no level of organization fixed in advance | Wilkins and Bourrat's SEP entry (2022 revision), §5.4, read in [NOTE-2367](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2367.md) (Skimmed), a neighbour of [LIT-1932](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1932.md) and [LIT-1937](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1937.md). A survey's report of Griesemer, not Griesemer; one of its page citations points to the wrong paper. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2276](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2276.md) | Ott and Antonsen show that for infinitely many phase oscillators whose phase velocity carries only the first harmonic of the phase, with a Lorentzian frequency distribution of nonzero width Δ, the order parameter is attracted at long times to the dynamics on their reduced manifold, by phase mixing at a rate of at least Δ and with no condition on any other rate, though the distribution itself need not converge; with Δ = 0, motion off the manifold can persist | Ott and Antonsen (2009), [LIT-3163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3163.md), read in full in [NOTE-2378](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2378.md), as a supplement to the 2008 paper ([THEORY-2295](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2295.md)), whose open question it answers for the order parameter. The closed law is reached from outside the manifold whenever frequencies are spread; it fails without spread ([QUESTION-391](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-391.md)). It is what makes the 2008 reduction a serious candidate defeater of [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md); the verdict is filed as alternatives ([CLAIM-1058](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1058.md), [CLAIM-1088](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1088.md)). Proposed until the attraction is confirmed independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2277](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2277.md) | Zidda and colleagues found that, freely viewing pictures in which a cue specific to their own trauma was set in a neutral background, 19 unmedicated people with PTSD made their first fixation on the background later than 18 trauma-exposed controls without PTSD, though they reached the cue as fast, and that latency to the background, with the earliest visual potential, predicted recognition of rearranged cue–background pairs the next day | Zidda, Steiger-White, Winkelmann, Ruttorf, Andoh, Nees & Flor (2025), [LIT-3174](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3174.md), read in full in [NOTE-2406](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2406.md). A gaze bias against the context of a trauma cue, specific to PTSD against trauma-exposed controls, measured only as the latency of the first look, and tied to poorer relational memory. The nearest study found to the first half of [QUESTION-303](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-303.md); it has no recall manipulation, and its background does not disambiguate. Proposed until replicated. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2278.md) | Arbona, Aimé and Elezgaray find, by UV-absorption melting of three-strand DNA constructions, that a staple's melting peak rises by 1.5 to 8.5 °C when a neighbouring staple is already folded and that the inner crossover position costs more than the outer, and that a local-equilibrium model with neighbour-dependent crossover penalties and no misfolds reproduces the annealing–melting hysteresis of four origamis of about 200 staples | In "small origamis" of one 64-base scaffold and two staples, a staple's melting peak rises when the other is folded (48.5 to 51.5 °C outer, 41.5 to 50 °C inner, 67 to 72 °C and +1.5 °C for a second pair), and the inner position, where the path between a crossover's ends runs through the staple, costs more than the bulge-forming outer one. A model of local equilibria conditioned on bound neighbours, with a strong-correlation closure and no misfolds or kinetics, fits the annealing and melting curves and the hysteresis (4 to 10 K) of four rectangular M13 origamis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2279](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2279.md) | Hancock and colleagues define metastability as a property of a dynamical system, not of data: an attractor landscape with regions that attract in some directions and repel in others, near which trajectories dwell and escape without noise, as against multistability, where noise drives switches between stable states; they find symmetry breaking a common enabler across its routes, from the ghost of a fixed point to cycles of saddles and chaotic itinerancy, and propose that dwell times, exponential for noise-driven multistability, may tell the two apart | Hancock, Rosas, Luppi, Zhang, Mediano, Cabral, Deco, Kringelbach, Breakspear, Kelso and Turkheimer (2024), [LIT-2266](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2266.md), skimmed from the accepted manuscript in [NOTE-2373](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2373.md). A review; the definition and the catalogue of routes are its own synthesis of the literature, the dwell-time test a proposal with computational support. It bears on [QUESTION-281](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md) by separating escape over a barrier by noise from passage near saddles. Proposed until the definition is confirmed in another source. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2280](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2280.md) | Lewis and colleagues report that, in families with a child conceived by assisted reproduction, mothers' and fathers' depression symptoms went with the child's depression and anxiety symptoms as strongly when the parent was genetically unrelated to the child as when related, and read this as environmental transmission not explained by shared adversity | Lewis et al. (2011), read in part ([NOTE-2370](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2370.md)). The same IVF cohort as Rice et al. 2010, used on the parenting side. It shows that the rearing route carries a parent's distress without genes or gametes, for depression symptoms. For [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md) it is the parenting route isolated from inheritance, for a non-traumatic exposure. Filed Proposed; the reading is the lead run's. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2281](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2281.md) | Frequency differences between remote clocks estimated by two satellite techniques agree with each other and with a simultaneous optical-fibre comparison within their combined uncertainties | Riedel et al.'s account, from a 26-day campaign over four European institutes: the frequency difference between two remote clocks, estimated over a satellite link by signal exchange between local masers, agrees between TWSTFT and GPS PPP ("compatible within a confidence level of 68 %", p. 11), and for LNE-SYRTE and PTB agrees with comparisons over optical fibre, one run simultaneously (pp. 12–13). The authors treat the two satellite techniques as "completely independent" and the comparison as a way to find systematic effects in either. For the record it is independent evidence for [CLAIM-510](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-510.md), that a measured correspondence can be checked against evidence the measurement did not produce. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2282](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2282.md) | Banerjee, Duflo, Glennerster and Kothari find, in a clustered randomized trial in 134 Rajasthan villages, that reliable monthly immunisation camps raised full immunisation of children aged 1-3 from 6 % to 18 %, that the same camps with small in-kind incentives raised it to 39 % at half the cost per fully immunised child, and that the incentive worked by stopping drop-out after the first injections | Seva Mandir ran monthly camps on fixed days in 30 villages, the same camps with 1 kg of lentils per immunisation and plates on completion in 30, and nothing new in 74. Full immunisation: 18 %, 39 % and 6 %. At least one injection did not differ between the camp arms (78 % and 74 %), so the incentive acted on completion. Cost per fully immunised child: $55.83 without incentives, $27.94 with, because the camp's fixed day served 13.4 immunisations instead of 4.5. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2283](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2283.md) | Leung, Chen, Yadav and Gallien find, from stock cards in 145 Zambian clinics and a validated simulation, that stock-outs of artemether-lumefantrine rose to about 20-30 % of clinics in early 2010 while the national warehouse held ample stock, caused by max-min replenishment targets set from past monthly issues, which miss seasonal demand and rainy-season lead times | During Zambia's 2009/10 supply chain pilot, with dedicated staff enforcing the max-min policy and central stock above 800,000 adult regimens, stocked-out clinics fell to 5 % or less late in 2009 and rose to about 20 % (30 % for one product) early in 2010. A discrete-event simulation of one clinic, validated out of sample, reproduces the rise: targets from the last three months' issues make the December order small and the larger orders arrive after peak demand. Raising the target buys service at roughly proportional extra stock; the recommended averaging changes help little. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2284](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2284.md) | Diotaiuti and colleagues' scoping review of 17 eye-tracking studies of PTSD published from 2010 to 2025 finds longer sustained gaze on negative or trauma-related material the most recurrent difference, with initial vigilance inconsistent and reduced exploration, shorter scanpaths and delayed attention to context each resting on one to three studies; no study it includes records gaze after the trauma is recalled or across treatment | Diotaiuti, Spica, Di Siena, Cavicchiolo, De Souza, Andrade & Mancone (2026), [LIT-3179](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3179.md), read in full in [NOTE-2382](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2382.md). A map of what the eye-tracking literature on PTSD has measured. For [QUESTION-303](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-303.md) it is a check on absence: no included study measures gaze after cued recall, and the use of gaze to track engagement with corrective context in exposure is called hypothetical. The last clause of the title is the reader's count from the review's Table 1, not a sentence of the review. The corpus misses at least two eligible studies. Proposed until an independent search agrees. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2285.md) | Google's example postmortem traces a fictional outage to a latent bug and a traffic surge, assigns every action item to an engineer of the responding teams, names no decision above them, and records a human error in its timeline without naming who made it | Appendix D of Google's Site Reliability Engineering (2016), [LIT-3175](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3175.md), read in [NOTE-2386](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2386.md). The template of a blameless postmortem, filled in. It bears on [QUESTION-476](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-476.md) as the practice's own picture of a finished review: blame withheld, correction kept. It is fictional and its causes are a bug and a surge, so it cannot show where a trace stops when an upstream decision was in play. The wording is the filer's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2286.md) | The Tempe operator, charged with negligent homicide, pleaded guilty to endangerment and was sentenced to three years of supervised probation, and prosecutors declined to charge Uber as a corporation | What [THEORY-2289](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2289.md) reports the Associated Press as reporting, stated as fact. Split off at the status review of 2026-11-23 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1; [ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md)), when the attribution went Active on its reading: the confirmation the old condition asked for belongs to this wider thesis, which keeps it word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2288.md) | Müller proposes that social interaction is self-organization in multilayer networks of neural, physiological and behavioral signals, in which circular causation across levels gives rise to dynamical and structural order parameters that in turn constrain the interacting individuals, and predicts that coordination emerges as coupling across layers increases, is most stable within an intermediate range of coupling, and shows bidirectional influence between order parameters and local dynamics | Müller (2026), [LIT-2252](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2252.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2402](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2402.md). A hypothesis with stated predictions, supported so far by examples. It reads Haken's enslavement causally, where Schmietendorf ([THEORY-2292](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2292.md)) cautions that the slaving principle supports by itself only a descriptive reading. Notes on [CLAIM-526](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-526.md) and [CLAIM-327](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md), no edges. Proposed until its predictions are tested; the promote_when asks for intervention evidence for the constraint it names. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2290](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2290.md) | Lippl and Lindsey find that rescaling a pretrained ResNet's weights by a factor below one before fine-tuning improves fine-tuning on small image classification tasks and gives the representation the signature of nested feature selection, lower dimension after fine-tuning with nearly all of it shared with the pretrained representation, while Vision Transformers show that signature unrescaled and are harmed by rescaling either way | From the reading of [LIT-3172](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3172.md) in [NOTE-2415](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2415.md), carrying out the lead that asked for it: the deep-network half of the paper, kept apart from the shallow theory ([THEORY-2305](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2305.md)) because it rests on experiment alone. That the best rescaling differs between architectures is a parallel to [CLAIM-754](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-754.md)'s point that no ranking holds without a declared context. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2291](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2291.md) | Caprioglio and Berthouze report that in simulations of identical phase-frustrated oscillators on three-layer hierarchically modular networks, mesoscale structure alone yields chimera and metastable states; the states of the upper layers follow the network Laplacian's slow modes, which reduce the network to the two-population model only when their gap to the fast modes is large, and the lowest-layer modules stay coherent, each acting as a single macro-oscillator, only while the spectral gap between the lowest two layers exceeds a threshold, below which they desynchronize and resynchronize metastably | Caprioglio and Berthouze (2024), [LIT-2241](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2241.md), read in [NOTE-2372](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2372.md) (appendices skipped). Numerical, one network family, N = 512. It corroborates [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md)'s first half with its version-5 condition, a gap between levels large against the spread within, and [CLAIM-157](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md)'s gap-isolated block as the unit; and it bears on [QUESTION-391](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-391.md), since the coarse-grained description fails as the gap closes. It also shows an Ott–Antonsen-based reduction of a network holding only with a large gap, which supports [CLAIM-1058](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1058.md). Proposed until reproduced independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2292](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2292.md) | Schmietendorf argues that the slaving principle of synergetics, on which near a critical point a separation of time scales lets a few slow order parameters describe the macro-dynamics while the stable modes follow them almost at once, supports by itself only a descriptive reading, that few variables suffice, and that a causal reading, the order parameter determining its constituents, needs further argument; weak emergence makes enslavement reducible and diachronic, downward causation through constraints makes it irreducible, and Synergetics alone does not settle between them | Schmietendorf (2026), [LIT-2231](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2231.md), read in [NOTE-2394](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2394.md). A perspective, reporting positions (Stephan, Bedau, Bishop) more than arguing one; the author finds the debate leaning reductionist. It restates Haken's account of slaving in brief, standing in for the unavailable review only that far. Bears on [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md)'s wording of constraint and on [CLAIM-526](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-526.md), as notes only. Proposed until the reading of the debate is confirmed by another survey. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2293](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2293.md) | Zhou and Ryan find, in a scoping review of human studies to mid-2023, that the evidence for intergenerational epigenetic transmission of stress and trauma is small, observational and mostly maternal, with two paternal-only studies and one measure of sperm, and hold that separating it from shared genes, environment and behaviour cannot easily be resolved | Zhou and Ryan (2023), read in full ([NOTE-2368](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2368.md)). The field's own survey, by authors open to the epigenetic route, reaches the scope that [CLAIM-644](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-644.md) takes from Horsthemke: no human design yet separates germline transmission from shared genes, environment and behaviour. That corroborates [CLAIM-644](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-644.md) independently of the sceptics' school. Filed Proposed; the reading is the lead run's. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2296](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2296.md) | Muralidharan and Sundararaman find, in a randomized evaluation in 500 Andhra Pradesh government primary schools, that bonuses paid to teachers on their students' test-score gains raised scores after two years by 0.27 SD (individual) and 0.16 SD (group), against 0.09 SD for an extra contract teacher or a block grant for materials calibrated to the same yearly spending, and that the incentive worked through effort while present rather than attendance | In AP RESt, five cells of 100 randomly assigned schools: control, group bonus, individual bonus, extra contract teacher, block grant. The bonus slope was set so that expected payouts matched the input arms' spending; in the event the inputs and the individual bonus cost Rs 10,000 per school a year and the group bonus about Rs 6,000. Two-year effects: 0.27, 0.16 and, for the pooled inputs, 0.09 SD. No difference in teacher attendance or observed classroom processes; teachers' self-reports show more homework, extra classes and practice tests. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2297](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2297.md) | Rice and colleagues report that, in children conceived by IVF, a mother's late-pregnancy stress went with lower birth weight, shorter gestation and more antisocial behaviour whether or not she was the child's genetic mother, while its link with ADHD symptoms appeared only when she was, and read the first as prenatal environmental and the second as inherited | Rice et al. (2010), read in full ([NOTE-2409](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2409.md)). It is the donor-gamete design at work in humans. The design compares related and unrelated carrier–child pairs, so it splits everything the gamete carries from everything the carrying and raising mother supplies. For [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md) it shows the design that can remove the womb and rearing from a germline comparison, and the limit of that design: a gamete-borne epigenetic mark falls with the genes. Filed Proposed; the reading is the lead run's. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2298](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2298.md) | Lee and colleagues report that mixtures of starfish embryos at two developmental ages, whose fluid-mediated interactions grow less nonreciprocal as they develop, pass abruptly from a traveling, flock-like collective state to a fluctuating, crystal-like one; weak nonreciprocity favours structural order and strong nonreciprocity fragments it, and at the passage both the rate of structural change and the estimated dissipation fall, while dissipation biases local rearrangements toward ordered motifs | Lee, Koskelo, Gokhale, Li, Fei, Liu, Lin, Dunkel, Skinner and Fakhri (2025), [LIT-2268](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2268.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2408](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2408.md) (sections I to III and the supplement skimmed past). One experimental system with a model and two analysis tools. It bears on [QUESTION-281](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md) as a measured, abrupt passage between collective states under a slowly drifting control parameter. Proposed until reproduced independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2299](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2299.md) | Mulligan and colleagues report that, among Syrian refugee families, grandchildren of women pregnant during the 1980 Hama violence differed at 14 DNA methylation sites from unexposed families, that directly exposed people differed at 21 other sites and prenatally exposed people at none, and read the first as a germline epigenetic signature of violence | Mulligan et al. (2025), read in full ([NOTE-2417](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2417.md)). It is the only human study found that names a germline exposure group for trauma, and it reports methylation differences there. The group is not separated from the uterine route of the middle generation, from family rearing or from the 1980 refugee community's history. For [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md) it is evidence of a difference between groups that the routes would all predict, not of one route. Filed Proposed; the reading is the lead run's, and how much it separates is set out in [CLAIM-1017](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1017.md) and its alternative, [CLAIM-1103](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1103.md). | Proposed |
