| [THEORY-2300](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2300.md) | Augustsson and colleagues report that identical phase oscillators coupled through slowly adapting product-form weights split by themselves into a synchronized cluster and a desynchronized group; while the cluster fraction stays fixed, the desynchronized group passes from stationary through breathing to chaotic dynamics without any change of membership, each such branch ends in a crisis-like jump that enlarges the cluster, and which sequence of cluster sizes occurs depends on initial conditions and on the direction of a parameter sweep | Augustsson, Cestnik, Wolfrum, Bick, Yanchuk and Martens (2026), [LIT-2244](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2244.md), read in [NOTE-2374](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2374.md) (supplement unread). Numerical, with exact reductions on invariant cluster subspaces. It bears on [QUESTION-281](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md) as a case of a distinction made at an instability, kept through changes of dynamics, and remade by crises. Proposed until reproduced independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2301](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2301.md) | Kaur, Jain and Berman report that representing animal posture across many time resolutions at once lets a transfer operator recover slow metastable behavioral states, one linear arm per basin around a central hub in its slow eigenvectors, which in flies persist for minutes against leg movements at tens of hertz and show heavy-tailed residences; where the gap between fast and slow rates is wide, a single-resolution operator finds no slow modes at all | Kaur, Jain and Berman (2026), [LIT-2257](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2257.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2399](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2399.md). A method validated on a driven Lorenz system and applied to worms and flies; the slow states are found, not shown to constrain. It bears on [QUESTION-281](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-281.md) as measured metastable states and transitions. Proposed until reproduced independently. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2302](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2302.md) | Google's blameless postmortem practice aims at what failed and not who, with action items that improve systems rather than people; leaders keep it blameless by recasting blameful questions, to managers and from executives, as questions about process; and questions about priorities set above the team are left to reviews of repeated incidents | What [THEORY-2294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2294.md) reports Rogers and colleagues as presenting, stated as Google's practice. Split off at the status review of 2026-11-23 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1; [ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md)), when the attribution went Active on its reading: the confirmation the old condition asked for belongs to this wider thesis, which keeps it word for word. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2303](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2303.md) | Tuulari, Bourgery and colleagues report that Finnish fathers who had suffered severe childhood maltreatment differed from fathers who had not in sperm DNA methylation at three regions and in the levels of dozens of sperm small RNAs, among them lower miR-34c-5p, and grant that transmission to offspring was not tested | Tuulari et al. (2025), read ([NOTE-2413](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2413.md)). In men, a childhood exposure goes with sperm marks decades later. That is the first step of a paternal germline route, at the level of association. For [QUESTION-297](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-297.md) it is the molecular half of a paternal design. The other half, the same men's children, with rearing removed, is missing. Filed Proposed; the reading is the lead run's. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2304](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2304.md) | Gallo, Lynch and Tomy find that firms under deferred or non-prosecution agreements that must take an on-site government-appointed monitor commit 18 to 25 percent fewer penalised violations than such firms without one while the monitor is on site, and not after the agreement ends, and that a measure of ethics and compliance norms in managers' speech rises and falls with it | Gallo, Lynch and Tomy (2023), [LIT-3157](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3157.md), read in [NOTE-2390](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2390.md): a difference-in-differences study of 193 deferred and non-prosecution agreements with listed US firms, 2001–2019. A monitor's effect on penalised violations lasts while it is on site; violations return to their pre-agreement level after, and an earnings-call measure of ethics and compliance norms moves with them. Mandated board changes are associated with fewer violations after the agreement ends. Used in [CASE-405](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-405.md) for [LEAD-101](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-101.md). Proposed until replicated. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2305](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2305.md) | Lippl and Lindsey show that in diagonal linear and one-hidden-layer ReLU networks both multi-task learning and pretraining then fine-tuning are biased to reuse pretrained features and to learn a sparse set of new ones, that the two biases trade off exactly, and that fine-tuning has a nested feature selection regime, reached by rescaling the weights after pretraining, which favours a sparse subset of the pretrained features | From the reading of [LIT-3172](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3172.md) in [NOTE-2415](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2415.md), carrying out the lead that asked for it. The theory Anguita and colleagues ([THEORY-2077](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2077.md)) extend. Its rescaling, which keeps the pretrained function when the readout is compensated, gives [CLAIM-1043](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1043.md)'s case of equal present function with different later learning. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2306](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2306.md) | On a strongly connected directed graph, diffusion wavelets extend to T = Π^{1/2}PΠ^{−1/2} by selecting columns of each restricted dyadic power as a non-orthogonal basis, compressing by the pseudo-inverse and squaring, which keeps the nested chain of spaces and trades orthogonality for localization at a large cost in conditioning | Sevi, Rilling and Borgnat (2023), [LIT-3194](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3194.md), skimmed in [NOTE-2414](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2414.md), §8.2–8.3.1. Their critically sampled transform on directed graphs, which they say has the scaling functions of the 2005 biorthogonal report ([LIT-3195](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3195.md)). The chain of spaces is nested by construction and the projector onto each is orthogonal; only the basis is non-orthogonal. It gives no error bound, does not read the levels as spectral bands, and reports conditioning on one example. | Proposed |
